The outermost ring is divided into numerical segments of 10, 20, and 30 for each sign, representing the degrees of the zodiacal circle.</image-desc>

### THE BOUNDS OF THE STARS in each sign of the zodiac. Chapter VI.

<margin>bounds <note>original Greek: ὅρια (*horia*)</note></margin>
Although the sign itself may be under the power of another, and possesses the proper domicile of a specific planet, its parts are nevertheless divided among the individual stars as if they were their own; these parts are called the "bounds" of the stars <term>fines</term> <note>Commonly known in astrology as "terms," these are five unequal subdivisions of each zodiac sign, each ruled by one of the five planets (excluding the Sun and Moon).</note>. The Greeks call these bounds *horia*; but we must gather this through subtle inquiry. For when a star is found in its own bounds, it is just as if it were established in its own domicile. So that the whole matter may be more clearly understood, we must explain it specifically, so that the secrets of birth charts <term>geniturae</term> <note>From the Latin for "birth" or "origin," referring to the natal horoscope.</note> may be known from these bounds.

<margin>Bounds of Aries.</margin>
The lord of **Aries (♈)** is, as we have said, **Mars (♂)**, but its bounds are divided among the individual stars as follows: from the first up to the sixth part, **Jupiter (♃)** possesses; from the seventh up to the twelfth, **Venus (♀)**; from the thirteenth up to the twentieth, **Mercury (☿)**; from the twenty-first up to the twenty-fifth, **Mars (♂)**; from the twenty-sixth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn (♄)**. And these are the parts of Aries, divided by this system.

**Taurus (♉)** is ruled by **Venus (♀)**, and the bounds of this sign are divided as follows: from the first part up to the eighth, **Venus (♀)** possesses; from the ninth up to the fourteenth, **Mercury (☿)**; from the fifteenth up to the twenty-second, **Jupiter (♃)**; from the twenty-third up to the twenty-seventh, **Saturn (♄)**; from the twenty-eighth up to the thirtieth, **Mars (♂)**. And the stars possess these bounds in Taurus.

**Gemini (♊)** is ruled by **Mercury (☿)**, and the bounds of this sign are divided as follows: from the first part up to the sixth, **Mercury (☿)** possesses; from the seventh up to the twelfth, **Jupiter (♃)**; from the thirteenth up to the seventeenth, **Venus (♀)**; from the eighteenth up to the twenty-fourth, **Mars (♂)**; from the twenty-fifth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn (♄)**. And these are the bounds of Gemini.

### BOOK TWO.

The mistress of **Cancer** (♋) is the **Moon** (☽), but the bounds <note>Latin: *fines*. In ancient astrology, these are sub-divisions of a zodiac sign, often called "terms," where a specific planet exerts influence.</note> of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree <note>Latin: *pars*.</note> of **Cancer** (♋) up to the seventh, **Mars** (♂) possesses; from the eighth to the thirteenth, **Venus** (♀); from the fourteenth up to the twentieth, **Mercury** (☿); from the twenty-first up to the twenty-seventh, **Jupiter** (♃); from the twenty-eighth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn** (♄). And these are the bounds of **Cancer** (♋).

The master of **Leo** (♌) is the **Sun** (☉), but its bounds are divided thus: from the first degree up to the sixth of **Leo** (♌), **Jupiter** (♃) possesses; from the seventh up to the eleventh, **Venus** (♀); from the twelfth up to the eighteenth, **Saturn** (♄); from the nineteenth up to the twenty-fourth, **Mercury** (☿); from the twenty-fifth up to the thirtieth, **Mars** (♂). And these are the bounds of **Leo** (♌).

**Mercury** (☿) is the master of **Virgo** (♍), but its bounds are divided thus: from the first degree up to the seventh of **Virgo** (♍), **Mercury** (☿) possesses; from the eighth up to the seventeenth, **Venus** (♀); from the eighteenth up to the twenty-first, **Jupiter** (♃); from the twenty-second up to the twenty-eighth, **Mars** (♂); from the twenty-ninth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn** (♄). And these are the bounds of **Virgo** (♍).

The mistress of **Libra** (♎) is **Venus** (♀), but the bounds of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the sixth of **Libra** (♎), **Saturn** (♄) possesses; from the seventh up to the fourteenth, **Mercury** (☿); from the fifteenth up to the twenty-first, **Jupiter** (♃); from the twenty-second up to the twenty-eighth, **Venus** (♀); from the twenty-ninth up to the thirtieth, **Mars** (♂). And these are the bounds of **Libra** (♎).

The master of **Scorpio** (♏) is **Mars** (♂), but the bounds of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the seventh of **Scorpio** (♏), **Mars** (♂) possesses; from the eighth up to the eleventh, **Venus** (♀); from the twelfth up to the nineteenth, **Mercury** (☿); from the twentieth up to the twenty-fourth, **Jupiter** (♃); from the twenty-fifth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn** (♄). And these indeed are the bounds of **Scorpio** (♏).

The master of **Sagittarius** (♐) is **Jupiter** (♃), the bounds of which sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the twelfth of **Sagittarius** (♐), **Jupiter** (♃) possesses; from the thirteenth up to the seventeenth, **Venus** (♀); from the eighteenth up to the twenty-third, **Mercury** (☿); from the twenty-fourth up to the twenty-seventh, **Saturn** (♄); from the twenty-eighth up to the thirtieth, **Mars** (♂). And these are the bounds of **Sagittarius** (♐).

The master of **Capricorn** (♑) is **Saturn** (♄), but the bounds of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the seventh of **Capricorn** (♑), **Mercury** (☿) possesses; from the eighth up to the fourteenth, **Jupiter** (♃); from the fifteenth up to the twenty-second, **Venus** (♀); from the twenty-third up to the twenty-sixth, **Saturn** (♄); from the twenty-seventh up to the thirtieth, **Mars** (♂). And these are the bounds of **Capricorn** (♑).

The master of **Aquarius** (♒) is **Saturn** (♄), but the bounds of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the seventh of **Aquarius** (♒), **Mercury** (☿) possesses; from the eighth up to the thirteenth, **Venus** (♀); from the fourteenth up to the twentieth, **Jupiter** (♃); from the twenty-first up to the twenty-fifth, **Mars** (♂); from the twenty-sixth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn** (♄). And these are the bounds of **Aquarius** (♒).

The master of **Pisces** (♓) is **Jupiter** (♃), but the bounds of this sign are divided thus: from the first degree up to the twelfth of **Pisces** (♓), **Venus** (♀) possesses; from the thirteenth up to the sixteenth, **Saturn** (♄); from the seventeenth up to the nineteenth, **Mercury** (☿); from the twentieth up to the twenty-seventh, **Mars** (♂); from the twenty-eighth up to the thirtieth, **Saturn** (♄). And these are the bounds of **Pisces** (♓).

## THE DAYTIME OR NIGHTTIME JOYS OF THE STARS. Chapter 7.

<margin>Which planets rejoice by day.</margin>
**H**aving set out and shown the bounds of the stars, we must now explain which stars rejoice by day and whose condition they follow, and which rejoice by night and whose condition they similarly imitate. By day, therefore, the Sun (☉), Jupiter (♃), and Saturn (♄) rejoice. Thus, Jupiter and Saturn follow the condition of the Sun. For this reason, in daytime <term>genitures: birth charts or nativities</term>, if they are placed in favorable locations, they possess greater power and, for the most part, decree good fortune and happiness. 
<margin>Which rejoice by night.</margin>
By night, however, the Moon (☽), Mars (♂), and Venus (♀) rejoice. Thus, Mars and Venus follow the condition of the Moon. As for Mercury (☿), since it accommodates itself to either nature, it is sometimes diurnal (day-oriented) and sometimes nocturnal (night-oriented). When it is "Oriental" <note>Rising in the East before the Sun.</note>, it is diurnal, but when it is "Occidental" <note>Setting in the West after the Sun.</note>, it is nocturnal. It is stronger in the latter position than the former, though it sits between the two natures when mixed with other stars. Furthermore, the "superior" stars <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—the planets further from the Sun than Earth is.</note>, according to their various mutual radiations, decree sometimes happy fortune and sometimes unhappy or evil fortune. For if Venus (♀) or Mars (♂) receives a waning Moon in a nocturnal birth chart, they decree all things to be prosperous and happy. But if the Moon is full of light or waxing, and Venus or Mars joins it by some radiation,
<margin>Venus is contrary to the waxing Moon.</margin>
then the greatest calamities and misfortunes are stirred up. Venus is contrary to the waxing Moon because they disagree with one another with a certain natural "shriek" of envy <note>original: "inuidiæ sibi stridore dissentiũt." This refers to a mythological or harmonic dissonance between the two feminine influences.</note>. Let it suffice that we have said these things summarily in this book of instruction; for we shall explain all things most fully, both concerning the Moon and the other stars, specifically in the following books.

## THE RISINGS AND SETTINGS OF THE STARS, AND THEIR CONDITION. Chapter 8.

<margin>Vanishing and synodic, or acronychal.</margin>
**T**he five stars—namely Saturn (♄), Jupiter (♃), Mars (♂), Venus (♀), and Mercury (☿)—become morning stars, evening stars, Occidental (Westward), or hidden (which are called <note>original: "ἀφανίσται καὶ συνοδικαὶ" (aphanistai kai synodikai)</note> "vanishing and synodic" by the Greeks), or <note>original: "ἀκρονύκται" (akronyktia)</note> "acronychal" <note>Rising in the East exactly as the Sun sets in the West.</note>. By what logic they become such, or for what reason they take these names, let us now explain. They are "morning stars" at their rising when they precede the Sun's disk; they are "evening stars" at their rising when they follow the rising Sun. They are "hidden" when the Sun's disk covers them. They are "acronychal" when they rise at the moment the Sun sets. When these planetary configurations help and when they harm, we shall explain in later books; for we have not said this without cause. In summary, however, it must be said 
<margin>Proximity to the Sun harms all stars.</margin>
that proximity to the Sun harms all stars <term>Combustion: the weakening of a planet's influence when it is too close to the Sun's light.</term>. Some, however, maintain that Mars (♂) falls prosperously when it is oppressed by the Sun's rays, for out of respect for the Sun, it loses its natural malice. We must also know with which stars the "morning" position rejoices and with which the "evening" position. For they are protected whenever they precede the Sun with a favorable radiation. Indeed, the other stars rejoice when positioned in a morning rising, and then the Sun's divine power is protected by the best radiation whenever it is adorned by the morning rising of the stars. But the stars become ineffective whenever they follow the Sun's disk in an evening rising. In the light of the Moon, however, they are greatly protected by its radiations, or when they precede its disk by some radiation. We must also show what the mixture of stars produces in birth charts: when they are made morning stars and when evening stars—that is, how many degrees away from the Sun the stars must be to become morning stars.

## THE DEGREES OF THE MORNING AND EVENING STARS. Chapter 9.

**W**e have explained more than enough by what logic stars become evening or morning stars. Now it must be known that the star Saturn (♄), when it has receded 12 degrees from the Sun—that is, when it has risen preceding the Sun—will be a morning star. In a similar way, Jupiter (♃) makes itself a preceding morning star when receding by 11 degrees; Venus (♀) by 8 degrees; Mars (♂) also becomes a morning star when preceding and positioned at the 8th degree; Mercury (☿) likewise is a morning star when preceding and positioned at the 8th degree. They are evening stars when, positioned at these same degree numbers, they follow after the Sun.

## THE GOVERNANCE OF ALL THE WANDERING STARS. Chapter 10.

We shall now explain the planetary "governances" <term>ducatus: the leadership or influence a planet exerts over a life</term> to you, Mavortius, our great honor, so that nothing pertaining to this divine discipline of **Mathematics** <note>original: "Matheseos" — here meaning the science of astrology</note> should seem to have been overlooked by us. Starting, therefore, with Saturn (♄), we will attempt to uncover in a brief exposition what each of the planets decrees by its own fate.

<margin>The nature and signification of Saturn.</margin>
**Saturn (♄)** is by nature cold and dry, though occasionally moist by accident. He is dark, harsh, heavy, foul-smelling, voracious, and grasping. He is a planet of much reflection and deep memory. His signification <term>significatio: what the planet represents or "rules" in a person's life</term> covers the cultivation of the fields, dwelling upon the waters, the measurement of things, weights, and whatever pertains to rustic affairs. Likewise, he rules those crafts performed by hand, such as masonry, digging, carpentry, and the like. Furthermore, he signifies extreme poverty, a long and difficult life, exile, dangers, deceits, wickedness, betrayals, and solitude. Yet, in deliberation, he grants a very sharp intellect, certain speech, stable friendship, long-term foresight, and kingly counsel. He also signifies violence, captivity, condemnation, stubbornness, treachery, anger, and every hatred of the good, as well as fear, distress, pain, repentance, funerals, mourning, and bereavement. He also indicates ancient inheritances and such things as wicked old men, but also slaves, bondsmen, hired laborers, eunuchs, vile and infamous men, thieves, sorcerers, and those who carry or prepare the dead for burial <note>original: "vespillones pollinctoresq"</note>. He also signifies the magic arts, long-winded thoughts in a man, rare speech, but a high intellect and a profound knowledge of things.
<margin>Which body parts he governs.</margin>
Regarding the parts of the body, he governs the right ear, the spleen, and **melancholy** <note>one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids thought to control health and temperament</note>.

**Jupiter (♃)** is by nature hot and moist, but so temperate that his particular power is suited by the stable decree of the Fates to nourishing the bodies of mortals and propagating them through many generations of offspring. Truly, his signification is dignity of form, nobility of mind, sound wisdom, intellect, and the interpretation of dreams. Furthermore, he rules justice, laws, established religion, as well as piety, modesty, grace, faith, and whatever the fair mind of a well-instructed man can conceive. Truly, by accident sometimes, perhaps due to excessive self-confidence, he signifies an ill-advised approach to affairs, and sometimes a difficult outcome of works for such a reason. He also signifies a patient mind, yet one eager for vengeance, and usually a victor in every contention. He also signifies high priests, petty kings, leaders, tribunes, and the authors of every most worthy magistracy. Furthermore, he brings hope, joy, self-control, liberality, the bringing together of men, public benefit, mature counsel, and speech that is weighty, pleasant, festive, and always suited to the public advantage.
<margin>Body parts.</margin>
Of the parts of the body, he governs the left ear and the liver.

**Mars (♂)** is by nature hot and dry, wrathful, violent, and often headstrong with incited anger. His signification is betrayal, battle, slaughter, audacity, rashness, arrogance, sedition, controversy, plunder, snares, and banditry. Furthermore, he signifies wounds, captivities, fear, and difficulty in flight. Then treachery, obscenity, reckless love, easy offense, wandering thoughts, and no counsel. He also signifies violent princes—fierce, inhuman, always lusting for the slaughter of others, perjurers, deceitful, inconstant, slanderers, disorderly, contaminating everything, polluting everything, and holding things divine and human in indiscriminate contempt. Yet they are clever, and ready for all their attempts with a certain wonderful shrewdness. He also signifies the deformed, the shameless, the ungrateful, and is harmful to births, and for this reason perhaps hateful to women.
<margin>The Arts.</margin>
Of the arts, he signifies Surgery, and whatever bloody or blood-letting...

...is completed with a certain pleasure. Of the parts of the human body, Jupiter (♃) rules the liver <margin>Body parts.</margin>, and Venus (♀) rules the nostrils. But when associated with Saturn (♄) or Mars (♂), it indicates a bitter death.

---

<margin>The Sun (☉)</margin>
**The Sun (☉)** is by nature fiery, hot, and dry, but tempered in a marvelous way; for this reason, it occupies the middle of the habitable zone. Its signification <term>significatio: the specific areas of life or character the planet governs</term> represents the most honorable gathering of men, ambitious reputation, the desire for gold and honors, the long-sought revenge against enemies, strength of mind, physical integrity, magnificence, victory, clear purity, and an incredible expectation among all people—indeed, whatever seems to belong to the royal heights. It also signifies kings and princes, not those who are cruel, difficult, or unjust, but those who are just, affable, approachable, mild, and honored by every kind of virtue—though they are sometimes inflated with a small spirit of pride. It also signifies grave eloquence, mature counsel, severe judgment, and a splendid and thoroughly magnificent way of acting in every matter; it likewise represents all brightness, clarity, and royal equipment. <margin>Body parts.</margin> Of the parts of the body, it possesses the head of the universal living being, the spirit <note>original: "spiritum" — referring to the vital breath or life force</note>, and the right eye.

---

<margin>Venus (♀)</margin>
**Venus (♀)** is by nature cold and moist; yet she is so tempered that, especially at her morning rising, she pours forth a generative dew upon mortals, by which not only are living beings suited for various kinds of reproduction, but green plants are also disposed toward various fruitfulness. Her signification represents all beauty and all grace, adorned garments, dress worked with gold thread, and those honored with silver or the purple of Tyrian dye. Furthermore, she rules baths, pigments, scented balsams, grace, humor, the Muses <note>the goddesses of the arts and inspiration</note>, and rich applause in the dance. She also signifies, above all, the forms of young maidens, their playful betrothals, loves, elegies, amorous resentments, snares, complaints, and then peace and the renewal of love. She also signifies banquets, morning treats, sweet delicacies or candies, and whatever is sweet and pleasurable to the taste; she rules both lawful and unlawful sexual unions, debaucheries, incests, adulteries, and others of that kind. She also signifies mutual love among men, piety, faith, trust, and the greatest humanity toward all. From the condition of the body, she signifies fatness rather, but adorned with a charming beauty; yet she often indicates a weak constitution, fatigued by poor health. <margin>Arts.</margin> Of the arts, she rules painting, the trade of perfumes, and whatever is practiced with wonderful and subtle skill. <margin>Body parts.</margin> But of the parts of the body, along with Mars (♂), she rules the nostrils.

---

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
**Mercury (☿)** is of a mixed nature, and he adheres without difficulty to whichever planet he is mixed with or joined to by some radiation, following the general agreement of the mixture; yet by nature he is rather cold and dry. His signification represents childhood, talent, reason, eloquence, pleasant deception, and playful theft. Furthermore, he rules logical arguments <note>original: "enthymemata, syllogismi, sophismata"</note>, poetry, music, and the scrutiny of the stars and the whole of **Mathematics** <note>original: "Matheseos" — in this context, the science of astrology</note>. He signifies faithful men, prophets, soothsayers, augurs <note>priests who interpret the will of the gods from the flight of birds</note>, and those graced with the divine interpretation of fates; also merchants, ambassadors, and orators, though these are often ones who deceive with fraudulent cunning. He also signifies the late-night study of every most sharp art, the invention of hidden and secret things, charming speech, sound counsel, delights, pleasures, ambitions, gains, and treasury taxes—indeed, whatever is sought for the sake of glory rather than utility. Furthermore, he rules feigned reconciliation, a doubtful and entangled affection, yet a mild compassion of the soul, and an ungrateful tone of voice; but in every sharp workmanship of any art, he provides a skillful hand and a most suitable talent, both for the wonderful invention of hidden things and for their swiftest perfection. <margin>Parts of the body.</margin> Of the parts of the body, he possesses the mouth, the tongue, and the hands that assist human speech.

---

<margin>The Moon (☽)</margin>
**The Moon (☽)** is by nature cold and moist; yet occasionally, by accident, she is heated by the rays of the sun, declining toward a certain warmth. Her signification represents form, joy, and the pursuit of glory; yet she also represents weak senses, a thin memory, lies, denunciations, flatteries, much greediness, but little sexual desire. She signifies traders of light goods, and especially aquatic things, the beginnings of business, and the rewards earned from them; she rules various resources and honors...

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...followers: diligent cultivators of the laws and fine arts, and most worthy explorers of all the most excellent things. She <note>Referring to the Moon (☽), continuing the description from the previous page</note> also signifies mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters. Furthermore, [she governs] works of water, the cultivation of the earth, and the affairs of princes and leaders; and in early youth, a great sense of religion, but one that is minimally constant or firm in its perseverance. <margin>Body parts.</margin> Of the parts of the body, specifically of the rational living being, she possesses the left eye.

->THE LORDS OF THE TRIGONS, AND<-
->their qualities. Chapter 11.<-

Now for you, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work</note>, our pride, we shall arrange the lords of the trigons <term>trigoni: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element, often called "triplicities"</term>, so that nothing belonging to the condition and height of these stars may seem to be left out. For since the twelve signs represent four natures <note>The four elements: Fire, Earth, Air, and Water</note> divided through three intervals, it is necessary that there be three signs of the same nature. For since the figure of an equilateral triangle is equal and consistent in itself, and the zodiac <note>original: "signifer"</note> marks three boundaries of the circle—that is, Aries (♈), Leo (♌), and Sagittarius (♐)—it will also divide its twelve parts into four trigons. From this kinship of nature, it will be possible to add something to the dignity of the stars. <margin>Fiery Trigons.</margin> For the diurnal <term>diurnal: belonging to the day</term> and masculine trigons shall be presided over by divine and masculine stars; <margin>Earthy.</margin> while the nocturnal <term>nocturnal: belonging to the night</term> and feminine trigons shall be presided over by nocturnal and feminine stars, because they have the testimony of greater harmony in that knowledge. <margin>Airy.</margin> Therefore, of the **Fiery Trigons**—that is, Aries (♈), Leo (♌), and Sagittarius (♐)—which are diurnal, masculine, and Northern, the first of the lords by day is the Sun (☉), the second is Jupiter (♃); but in the night it is the reverse; yet Saturn (♄) shares in both. Of the **Earthy Trigons**—that is, Taurus (♉), Virgo (♍), and Capricorn (♑)—which are nocturnal, feminine, and Southern, the first of the lords by day is Venus (♀), the second is the Moon (☽); but in the night it is the reverse; yet Mars (♂) shares in both. Next, of the **Airy Trigons**—that is, Gemini (♊), Libra (♎), and Aquarius (♒)—which are diurnal, masculine, and Eastern, the first of the lords by day is Saturn (♄), the second is Mercury (☿); but in the night it is the reverse; yet Jupiter (♃) shares in both. <margin>Watery.</margin> Finally, of the **Watery Trigons**—that is, Cancer (♋), Scorpio (♏), and Pisces (♓)—which are nocturnal, feminine, and Western: the first of the lords by day is Venus (♀), the second is Mars (♂); but in the night it is the contrary; yet the Moon (☽) shares in both. These are all the powers of the stars, which, if you compare them well and consider them carefully, you will be able to unravel with no small skill in divination what they have decreed by their fatal law in every birth chart <term>genitura: a horoscope or birth chart</term>.

### THE NATURE, FORMS, AND QUALITIES OF THE SIGNS. Chapter 12.

We have spoken of the purpose and categories of the signs. Now we must explain their nature, forms, quality, subjects, and rising times <term>anaphoris: the rising of signs above the horizon, used to calculate planetary strength</term>, so that we may impart the knowledge of this entire art to you most fully through the clearest explanations.

<margin>The nature and quality of Aries.</margin>
Aries (♈) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, equinoctial <note>original: "aequinoctiale"</note>, royal, fiery, strong, truthful, four-footed, and semi-corporeal <term>semicorporale: having characteristics of both human and animal, or partial bodies</term>. It has languid eyes and is wandering. It is called *Krios* <margin>Krios</margin> <note>original: "$\kappa\rho\iota\acute{o}\varsigma$"</note> by the Greeks. It is untamed, harmonious, impure, and lustful. It is the house of Mars, the setting of Venus; the exaltation <note>original: "altitudo"</note> of the Sun is around the 19th degree, and the depression <note>original: "deiectio"</note> of Saturn is around the 20th degree. Its triplicity <note>original: "trigonum"</note> is ruled by the Sun by day and by Jupiter by night. It is called "equinoctial" because in this sign the Sun balances the hours of night and day in equal measure; for this reason, it is called by the Greeks the "equinoctial tropic" <margin>isēmerinon</margin> <note>original: "$\tau\rho\omicron\pi\iota\kappa\grave{o}\nu$ $\iota\sigma\eta\mu\epsilon\rho\iota\nu\grave{o}\nu$"</note>. For when the Sun is in Aries, it balances the diurnal and nocturnal hours equally, such that the day has 12 hours and the night likewise has 12. It is called *Krios* [the Ram] because <unclear>like goats</unclear> <note>original: "$\alpha\iota\gamma\grave{\iota}\delta\epsilon\varsigma$"</note> when the Sun is in it, it judges between day and night, as "to judge" is called *krinein* <margin>krinein</margin> <note>original: "$\kappa\rho\acute{\iota}\nu\epsilon\iota\nu$"</note> in Greek; and because, being positioned between winter and summer in that sign, the Sun itself is judged again. It is called "Tropic" because the Sun, situated in that sign, creates the springtime. For spring begins <margin>The beginning of Spring.</margin> when the Sun has entered the first degree of that sign. It is called "Fiery" because whoever has this sign as their ascendant <note>original: "horosc."</note> in their birth chart will lean toward a fiery and choleric nature. This sign is positioned in the North Wind.

<margin>Taurus (♉)</margin>
Taurus (♉) is a sign in the heavens that is feminine, Northern, earthy, melancholic, fixed, of a single body, four-footed, domestic, flawed, having few children, lustful, and of a diminished voice. It flourishes in the South, is oblique, heavy, of a single business, odd, irrational, easy, and with cut-off limbs. It is the house of Venus, the setting of Mars; the exaltation of the Moon is around the third degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus by day and the Moon by night. This sign is positioned in the South Wind. It also signifies a bitter taste, the colors green and white, four-footed animals with cloven hooves, the fifth climate <term>clima: ancient latitudinal zones of the Earth; the fifth climate was typically associated with the Mediterranean</term>, cultivated lands, mediocre men, and all ailments of the neck.

<margin>Gemini (♊)</margin>
Gemini (♊) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, common <note>original: "commune," also known as mutable</note>, bicorporeal <term>bicorporeum: "two-bodied," represented by twins</term>, two-footed, rational, of a beautiful voice, winged, sterile, flourishing in the West, and midway between light and heavy. It is of two businesses, even, Northern, and both acquiring and emptying. It is the house of Mercury, the setting of Saturn. Its triplicity is ruled by Saturn by day and Venus by night. This sign is positioned in the East Wind <note>original: "Subsolano"</note>. It also signifies a sweet taste, a mixed and tempered color, rational animals, the ape, and all songbirds. It signifies the sixth climate, all high and sunny places where bird-catching is especially practiced, as well as primates <note>original: "Primates," meaning those of first rank</note>, astronomers, and all troubles and ailments of the shoulders.

<margin>Cancer (♋)</margin>
Cancer (♋) is a sign in the heavens that is feminine, movable <note>original: "mobile," also known as cardinal</note>, semi-corporeal, irrational, many-footed, wild, voiceless, flawed, and having many children. it is nocturnal, flourishing in the North, watery, phlegmatic, of one business, and midway between light and heavy. It is odd, Northern, solstitial <term>solstitiale: marking the summer solstice</term>, lowly, untruthful, and weak. It is the house of the Moon, the setting of Saturn; the exaltation of Jupiter is around the 15th degree, and the depression of Mars is around the 28th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus by day and Mars by night. This sign is positioned in the Southwest Wind <note>original: "Aphrico"</note>. It also signifies a sharp and salty taste, the color white and milky-white <note>original: "leucotheum"</note>, aquatic and creeping animals, the seventh climate, stagnant or flowing waters, mediocre men, and all ailments of the heart and midriff.

<margin>Leo (♌)</margin>
Leo (♌) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, fixed, of a single body, four-footed, irrational, midway between domestic and wild, and lustful. It flourishes in the East, and is fiery, choleric, of a medium voice, light, of one business, even, diurnal, Northern, direct, truthful, and strong. It is the house of the Sun, the setting of Saturn. Its triplicity is ruled by the Sun by day and Jupiter by night. This sign is positioned in the North Wind. It also signifies a bitter and sharp taste, a saffron color leaning toward red, wild and ferocious animals, the fifth climate, and all dignified places such as difficult ascents, military camps, headquarters <note>original: "praetoria"</note>, and palaces. It also signifies princes, leaders, the powerful, and wealthy men, as well as all ailments of the chest and stomach.

<margin>♍</margin> Virgo (♍) is a sign in the heavens that is feminine, common <term>commune: also known as a mutable sign, occurring at the end of a season</term>, double-bodied <note>original: "bicorporeum"</note>, rational, two-footed, having a beautiful voice, winged, sterile, and powerful in the South. It is heavy, concerned with two affairs, earthy, melancholic, odd-numbered, northern, honest, beautiful, generous, easy-going, direct, nocturnal, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Mercury (☿), the setting of Jupiter (♃); the exaltation <note>original: "altitudo"</note> of Mercury is around the fifteenth degree, and the depression <note>original: "deiectio," also known as the "fall"</note> of Venus (♀) is around the twenty-seventh degree. Its triplicity <term>trigonum: a group of three signs belonging to the same element</term> is ruled by Venus by day and by the Moon (☽) by night. This sign is situated in the South wind. It also signifies a styptic <note>original: "stypticum," meaning astringent or mouth-puckering</note> taste, and the colors white, purple, and pale-white <note>original: "leucotheum"</note>. It represents rational animals and birds, the fifth climate <note>clima: ancient geographical zones based on the length of the longest day</note>, and all cultivated and flowering places. It indicates wise and industrious men, as well as jesters, and governs all ailments and sufferings of the belly.

<margin>♎</margin> Libra (♎) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, movable <term>mobile: also known as a cardinal sign, marking the start of a season</term>, semi-corporeal, rational, domestic, two-footed, and having a beautiful voice. It produces few children and is powerful in the West. It is medium in weight between light and heavy, airy, sanguine, concerned with one affair, even-numbered, southern, equinoctial, direct, diurnal, strong, and truthful. It is the house of Venus (♀), the setting of Mars (♂); the exaltation of Saturn (♄) is around the 20th degree, and the depression of the Sun (☉) is around the 19th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Saturn by day and by Mercury (☿) by night. This sign is situated in the East wind <note>original: "Subsolano"</note>. It also signifies a sweet taste, the colors green and pale-white, and flying animals—especially large ones. It represents the fifth climate and all places on mountain peaks, as well as sown and cultivated lands. It also indicates merchants, judges, diviners, and obedient men, and governs all ailments of the kidneys and vertebrae.

<margin>♏</margin> Scorpio (♏) is a sign in the heavens that is feminine, fixed, single-bodied, irrational, wild, many-footed, and produces many children. It lacks a voice and is powerful in the North. It is watery, phlegmatic, concerned with one affair, odd-numbered, southern, direct, nocturnal, heavy, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Mars (♂), the setting of Venus (♀), and the depression of the Moon (☽) is around the third degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus by day and by Mars by night. This sign is situated in the Southwest wind <note>original: "Aphrico"</note>. It also signifies a salt-like and insipid taste, and the colors green, red, and pale-white. It represents crawling and poisonous animals, as well as marine and aquatic ones. It governs the third climate and places that are sometimes garden-like <note>original: "cepurica"</note>, and at other times foul-smelling and deserted. It indicates doctors (though often fake and unlearned) and mediocre men, and governs all ailments of the groin.

<margin>♐</margin> Sagittarius (♐) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, common, and double-bodied—of which the first part is rational and the second part is irrational <note>Firmicus refers here to the Centaur's form: half-man, half-horse</note>. It has a beautiful voice, is four-footed, lustful, and produces few children. It is powerful in the East, though its second part has a diminished voice. It is light, fiery, choleric, strong, concerned with two affairs, even-numbered, southern, direct, diurnal, and truthful. It is partly domestic and partly wild. It is the house of Jupiter (♃), the setting of Mercury (☿); its triplicity is ruled by the Sun (☉) by day and by Jupiter (♃) by night. This sign is situated in the North wind <note>original: "Aquilone"</note>. It also signifies a bitter taste, the colors red or saffron, and represents rational animals, horses, birds, and serpents. It governs the second climate and all well-watered places, mountains, gardens, and whatever contains some pleasantness. Finally, it indicates judges, worshippers of God, merciful men, interpreters of dreams, and prophets, and governs all ailments of the thighs.

<margin>♑</margin> Capricorn (♑) is a sign in the heavens that is feminine, movable, semi-corporeal, irrational, four-footed, domestic, flawed, and produces few children. It is chaste, has a diminished voice, is oblique <note>original: "obliquum," referring to its manner of rising on the horizon</note>, earthy, and melancholic. It is powerful in the South, heavy, concerned with one affair, odd-numbered, southern, solstitial, easy-going, nocturnal, false-speaking, and weak. It is the house of Saturn (♄), the setting of the Moon (☽); the exaltation of Mars (♂) is around the 28th degree, and the depression of Jupiter (♃) is around the 15th degree. Its triplicity is ruled by Venus (♀) by day and the Moon (☽) by night. This sign is situated in the South wind. It also signifies a bitter and styptic taste, the colors black or pale-white, four-footed animals, and some aquatic ones. It governs the first climate, garden-like and irrigated places, springs, rivers, as well as pastures, animal stalls, and the dwellings of obscure people. It indicates men who are unrefined and of low status, yet some of deep genius, as well as melancholics, and governs all ailments and sufferings of the knees.

<margin>♒</margin> Aquarius (♒) is a sign in the heavens that is masculine, fixed, single-bodied, rational, two-footed, having a beautiful voice, and producing few children. It is powerful in the West, medium between light and heavy, even-numbered, concerned with one affair, southern, oblique, diurnal, truthful, strong, airy, and sanguine.

This sign is situated in the Africus <note>The Southwest wind</note> wind. It governs the seventh climate, ruinous and damp places, and signifies fishermen, sailors, and all ailments of the feet.

### THE RISINGS OF THE SIGNS ACCORDING TO
-> different climates. Chapter XIII. <-

Having explained the types and forms of the signs, and having described their nature with diligent reasoning—just as the teachings of the wisest Greeks have handed down to us—we must show in the following section in which year each sign rises in a birth chart <note>Firmicus is referring to "ascensional times," a technical calculation used to determine the length of life and planetary periods</note>. We shall demonstrate the purpose of this through a brief definition. The signs rise at various times and days, according to the climates. Therefore, we demonstrate by this reasoning which signs rise in which climates and at what time.

<margin>First and second climates.</margin>
In the first climate, which is that of Ethiopia, and in the second climate, which belongs to Babylon, and in all other regions lying within these climates, the signs rise in this course of time: Aries (♈) rises in the fourteenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-fourth; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-eighth; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-sixth; Virgo (♍) in the fortieth; Libra (♎) similarly in the fortieth; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-sixth; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-second; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-eighth; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-fourth; and Pisces (♓) in the twenty-fourth year.

<margin>The third.</margin>
In the climate that passes through Alexandria and the other regions lying within this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the nineteenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-third; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-seventh; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-sixth; Virgo (♍) in the fortieth; Libra (♎) in the fortieth; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-sixth; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-second; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-seventh; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-third; and Pisces (♓) similarly in the nineteenth year.

<margin>The fourth.</margin>
In the climate of Athens and the other regions lying within this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the eighteenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-third; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-seventh; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-sixth; Virgo (♍) in the forty-first; Libra (♎) in the forty-first; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-sixth; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-second; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-seventh; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-third; and Pisces (♓) similarly in the eighteenth year.

<margin>The fifth.</margin>
In the climate of the City <note>Referring to Rome</note> and other regions lying within this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the seventeenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-second; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-seventh; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-seventh; Virgo (♍) in the forty-second; Libra (♎) similarly in the forty-second; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-seventh; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-second; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-seventh; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-second; and Pisces (♓) in the seventeenth year.

<margin>The sixth.</margin>
In the climate of the Hellespont <note>The narrow strait in northwestern Turkey, connecting the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara</note> and other regions lying within this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the sixteenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-second; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-seventh; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-seventh; Virgo (♍) in the forty-second; Libra (♎) similarly in the forty-second; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-seventh; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-second; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-seventh; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-second; and Pisces (♓) indeed in the sixteenth year.

<margin>The seventh.</margin>
In the climate of the North and other regions lying within this climate, Aries (♈) rises in the fifteenth year; Taurus (♉) in the twenty-first; Gemini (♊) in the twenty-ninth; Cancer (♋) in the thirty-second; Leo (♌) in the thirty-septimum; Virgo (♍) in the forty-first; Libra (♎) similarly in the forty-first; Scorpio (♏) in the thirty-first; Sagittarius (♐) in the thirty-third; Capricorn (♑) in the twenty-seventh; Aquarius (♒) in the twenty-first; and Pisces (♓) similarly in the fifteenth year. These are the risings of the signs, by which individual stars are moved toward their own efficacy.

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS ON THE ASSIGNMENT OF THE SIGNS TO THE WINDS. Chapter 14.

**I**t is also fitting for us to know which signs are subject to which winds; for this knowledge is especially necessary for us in the casting of horoscopes <term>apotelesmatis: the study of the effects or outcomes of planetary positions</term>. To the North Wind <note>original: "Aquilo"</note> are subject the signs Aries (♈︎), Leo (♌︎), and Sagittarius (♐︎). To the South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note>, Taurus (♉︎), Virgo (♍︎), and Capricorn (♑︎). To the East Wind <note>original: "Apeliotes," which we call "Subsolanus"</note>, Gemini (♊︎), Libra (♎︎), and Aquarius (♒︎). To the Southwest Wind <note>original: "Aphricus," which is called "Lips" (λὶψ) by the Greeks</note>, Cancer (♋︎), Scorpio (♏︎), and Pisces (♓︎).

*The morning rising times <note>original Greek: Ἀναφοραὶ ἑωρινοὶ (Anaphorai heōrinoi)</note> are reported differently by different people. Therefore, reader, do not be surprised if other authors vary from the tradition presented here. See Georgius Valla <note>A 15th-century Italian humanist and translator of scientific texts</note>, Book 4 on Astrology, chapter 62.*

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS.
# TWELFTH-PARTS. CHAPTER XV.

I shall now briefly show the method by which you may investigate the twelfth-parts <note>original: *duodecatemoria*. These are micro-zodiac divisions where each 30-degree sign is divided into twelve 2.5-degree segments, each associated with a sign of the zodiac.</note>. For some believe they can discover the entire substance of a birth chart <note>original: *genitura*</note> through them, and they suggest that whatever is hidden in the celestial decree can be brought to light from these twelfth-parts. What these twelfth-parts are is taught by this example: whichever star’s twelfth-part you wish to find, multiply its degree by twelve; divide the resulting sum and assign them to the individual signs, 30 degrees to each. You begin from the very sign in which the star is located whose twelfth-part is being sought; in whichever sign the final number falls, that sign will show you the location of the twelfth-part. 

But so that you may understand more clearly, we shall also provide an example of this. Suppose the **Sun** (☉) is in **Aries** (♈) at 5 degrees and 5 minutes. Twelve times 5 degrees makes 60; likewise, twelve times 5 minutes makes 60 minutes, and these 60 minutes make 1 degree; through this, the total becomes 61 degrees. From these, give 30 to **Aries**, in which we said the **Sun** was located, and 30 to **Taurus** (♉). The **Sun's** twelfth-part is found in the 1st degree of **Gemini** (♊). 

Therefore, investigate whether the full **Moon** (☽) sends its twelfth-part into the terms <note>original: *fines*. The "terms" or "bounds" are specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet.</note> of **Mars** (♂) during the day; or whether, when waning—that is, deficient—it sends it into the terms of **Saturn** (♄); or whether **Mars** is at its setting, or **Venus** (♀) is in the sign of **Mars**, or **Mars** is in the sign of **Venus**. Look to see how they receive power to help or harm from the terms, the decans <note>original: *decanis*. 10-degree subdivisions of a sign.</note>, and their specific conditions. For the benevolence of **Jupiter** (♃) fails when its kindness is hindered by the weakness of the sign, the degrees, the decan, or a change in condition. But the malice of **Saturn** grows more powerful when it receives a stronger power for harming, provoked by the quality of its place, the terms, the decan, the sign, or the condition of all these together. The other stars act in a similar way. Yet one thing must be known: although the star of **Jupiter** is benevolent, it cannot resist the attack of **Mars** and **Saturn** alone if they constrain it with violent radiation <note>referring to astrological aspects or "rays" cast by the planets</note>.

<margin>The wonderful benevolence of the planet Jupiter.</margin>
Indeed, humans would be immortal if the benevolence of **Jupiter** were never overcome in their birth charts. But because God the Craftsman <note>original: *artifex Deus*</note> made man so that his substance would dissolve after a certain span of life, it was necessary that—while **Jupiter** (through whom life and a healing defense are granted to men) is held back—the malicious and destructive power of the malevolent stars should remain with an increase in malice during the extinguishing of a human, so that the framework of the body, attacked by malevolent radiations, might be dissolved.

## THINGS TO BE CONSIDERED CONCERNING THE HOROSCOPE. CHAPTER XVI.

Now, let our attention be turned to the explanation of the angles <note>original: *cardines*. The four pivotal points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven.</note> and all the "places." Once we have diligently found all these, we must then discover the individual decrees of a man, by which the entire substance of his life is divided—but for now, we do so "platically" <note>original: *platicè*. From the Greek *platys*, meaning "broadly." This refers to interpreting by whole signs rather than exact degrees.</note>. A little later, when we come to the books on *Apotelesmata* <note>The Greek term for "astrological effects" or "outcomes."</note>, we will show the "partile" <note>original: *partiliter*. Examining the chart by specific degrees and minutes.</note> method by which individual places can be gathered through secret inquiries. For he who is being instructed must first be instructed platically; so that, having been composed and shaped by these clearer and lighter things, he may then more confidently follow the more hidden aspects of the birth chart. For when the place itself has been found partilly, one must consider its nature, what sign it is in, whose terms it is in, and which stars are there to provide testimony. It must also be especially considered where the "Lord of the sign" <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign in question.</note> is positioned, in what sign, or in what terms it sits. This matter must be sought with great diligence: whether it is adorned by the testimonies of benevolent stars, or whether it is beaten by the attack of malevolent ones. Now, let us return to the platic definition of the places, so that we may explain the order of the angles and the other places.

## THE ANGLES AND THEIR SUCCESSORS. CHAPTER XVII.

One must read carefully concerning the eight places. The definition of the eight places is this: Platically, the "Place of Life" is in the sign in which the horoscope <note>original: *horoscopus*. In ancient astrology, this refers specifically to the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> is established; the "Place of Money or Hope" is in the second sign from the horoscope; the "Sign of Siblings" in the third; the "Place of Parents" in the fourth; the "Place of Children" in the fifth; the "Place of Health" <note>often referring to illness or the physical condition</note> in the sixth; the "Place of the Spouse" in the seventh; the "Place of Death" in the eighth. All of these, beginning from the horoscope, we have shown by this definition of names: Life, Hope, Siblings, Parents, Children, Health, Spouse, and Death. But as we said above, let it suffice to have spoken platically to inform the beginnings of the learner.

# BOOK TWO.

<margin>What is said of men is to be understood similarly for women.</margin>
...should suffice. Later, however, we shall take care to explain how these places are shown by a precise definition of their parts. Certainly, you ought to know this: that those things we say regarding the birth charts <note>original: *genituris*</note> of men, these same things also operate in the birth charts of women—knowing this: that **Venus** (♀) indicates the wife, and the star of **Mars** (♂) indicates the husband.

### THE PIVOTS OF THE BIRTH CHART. CHAPTER XVIII.

<margin>The four pivots.</margin>
<margin>The Rising.</margin>
<margin>The Setting.</margin>
<margin>Midheaven.</margin>
<margin>Lower Midheaven.</margin>
In birth charts there are four pivots <note>original: *cardines*. These are the most powerful points in an astrological chart, representing the four directions.</note>: the Rising, the Setting, the Midheaven, and the Lower Midheaven. These places are usually called by these names by the Greeks: *anatole*, *dusis*, *mesourania*, and *hupogeion* <note>original: "ἀνατολὴ, δύσις, μεσουράνια, ὑπόγειον"</note>. The Rising <note>original: *ortus*</note> is the part of the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*</note> which, at the time of any birth, first emerges from the eastern part and is drawn out through the next 30 degrees; this is called *anatole* <note>original: "ἀνατολὴ"</note> by the Greeks. The Setting <note>original: *occasus*</note> is the part of the sky exactly opposite, in the seventh place from the Ascendant, which is called the *western diameter* <note>original: "διάμετρον δυτικὸν"</note> by the Greeks. So that you may understand this more easily, calculate from the degree of the Ascendant through the other signs for 180 degrees; in whatever sign the 181st degree is found, the Setting of the birth chart is established in that sign or degree. The Midheaven <note>original: *Medium Coelum* or MC</note> is the tenth sign from the Ascendant; but sometimes the Midheaven is also found exactly in the eleventh sign from the Ascendant. So that you may understand this more clearly, calculate from the degree of the Ascendant through the signs that follow for 270 degrees; in whatever sign the 271st degree is found, this has obtained the Midheaven, which is called *mesourania* <note>original: "μεσουράνια"</note> by the Greeks. The Lower Midheaven <note>original: *Imum Coelum* or IMC</note>, which is called *hupogeion* <note>original: "ὑπόγειον"</note> by the Greeks, is established in the fourth place from the Ascendant. To understand this easily, calculate from the degree of the Ascendant in order for 90 degrees; where the 91st degree falls, there the place of the Lower Midheaven is positioned. These are the four pivots of birth charts and decrees, which we must always gather by diligent reasoning so that we may explain the entire substance of fate with the truest pronouncements.

### THE FOUR SECONDARY PLACES. CHAPTER XIX.

After these four pivots—that is, after the Rising, Setting, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven—there are four other places in birth charts which have a following and secondary power: these are Goddess, God, Good Fortune, and Good Spirit <note>original: *dea, deus, bona fortuna, & bonus dæmon*</note>. To this point, they are named by the Greeks as *Thea, Theos, Agathe Tyche,* and *Agathodaimon* <note>original: "Θεὰ, Θεὸς, ἀγαθὴ τύχη, ἀγαθοδαίμων"</note>. Goddess is the third place from the Ascendant—that is, the third sign from the Ascendant; this place, as we said, is called *Thea* by the Greeks. God is that sign which is established directly opposite this sign, that is, the ninth sign from the Ascendant; this place is called *Theos* by the Greeks. Good Fortune is located in the fifth sign from the Ascendant, which place is called *Agathe Tyche* by the Greeks. The Good Spirit is located opposite this sign, that is, in the eleventh place from the Ascendant; this place is called *Agathodaimon* by the Greeks.

### THE IDLE AND CAST-DOWN PLACES OF THE FIGURE. CHAPTER XX.

The remaining four places are said to be idle and cast-down for this reason: because they are joined by no association with the Ascendant <note>In traditional astrology, houses that do not "aspect" (see) the 1st house are considered weakened or "blind."</note>. Among these remaining four places, the first is that which is established in the second sign from the Ascendant; this place is called the Infernal Gate, or *anaphora* <note>original: "ἀναφορὰ", meaning a rising up</note>. Whichever place is opposite this sign—that is, in the eighth sign from the Ascendant—is called *epanaphora* <note>original: "ἐπαναφορὰ"</note>, or the Celestial Gate. The very last places are those of Bad Fortune and the Bad Spirit. Bad Fortune is established in the sixth sign from the Ascendant. The Bad Spirit is positioned in the twelfth sign from the Ascendant. The Greeks call Bad Fortune *Kake Tyche* <note>original: "κακὴν τύχην"</note>; but the Bad Spirit—that is, the place in the twelfth sign from the Ascendant—the Greeks call *Kakodaimon* <note>original: "κακοδαίμονα"</note>.

### THE ORDER OF THE PLACES IN THE FIGURE. CHAPTER XXI.

Now we ought to know which of these twelve places take precedence and which follow—that is, which places are primary and which are secondary—so that we can gather everything by diligent reasoning. The Ascendant precedes the Setting; the Midheaven is placed before the Lower Midheaven; the eleventh place, which is the Good Spirit, is preferred over Good Fortune; the ninth, which is God, is placed before the third place, which is Goddess; the *epanaphora* <note>the 8th house</note>, that is the eighth place from the Ascendant, is placed before the *anaphora* <note>the 2nd house</note>; Bad Fortune, the sixth place from the Ascendant, is placed before the Bad Spirit, which is the twelfth place from the Ascendant. All these things must be known so that when we come to the astrological outcomes <note>original: *apotelesmata*</note>, by mixing and tempering all factors, we may strengthen our judgments with a faithful account of the truth.

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS ON THE POWERS OF THE TWELVE HOUSES. CHAPTER XXII.

Now we must explain the specific meanings of the twelve houses, beginning with the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopo*. In ancient astrology, the "horoscope" refers specifically to the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth, now commonly called the Ascendant.</note>. Once all have been set out in order, the obscurity of confusion may be illuminated, and the things that follow may be more clearly understood.

<margin>First House.</margin>
The **First House** is that part in which the Ascendant is established. In this place, the life and spirit of humans are contained; from this place, the very foundations of the entire birth chart <note>original: *geniturae*</note> are known. This place extends its powers from that degree in which the Ascendant is found through the remaining 30 degrees. Moreover, it is the first pivot <note>original: *cardo*. These are the four "hinges" or "angles" of the sky—the most powerful points in a chart.</note>, the framework and substance of the whole birth chart, which provides the entry point for all the rest.

**II.** The **Second House** from the Ascendant is established in the second sign; it begins at the 30th degree from the Ascendant and extends its power through the next 30 degrees. From this sign, the growth of hope and possessions are known. It is, however, an "idle" house <note>original: *piger locus*. Houses that do not "aspect" (see) the Ascendant were considered weak or sluggish because they could not easily transmit their influence to the life of the individual.</note>, being estranged from the Ascendant. For this reason, it is also called the **Lower Gate**, because it is joined to the Ascendant by no ray of light nor mixed with any aspect.

**III.** The **Third House** is that which is established in the third sign from the Ascendant, taking its beginning at 60 degrees from the Ascendant and ending at 90. From this place, we shall speak of everything regarding brothers and friends. The name for this place is **Goddess** <note>original: *dea*</note>. This is also the first house of the traveler; it is joined to the Ascendant in a slender partnership, for it is seen to look back at the Ascendant from a hexagon <note>original: *hexagono*. This refers to a "sextile" aspect, a 60-degree angle, considered a minor but harmonious connection.</note>.

**IIII.** The **Fourth House** from the Ascendant—that is, the **Lower Midheaven** <note>original: *imum coelum*</note>—is established in the fourth sign from the Ascendant. Its beginning starts from the 90th degree and reaches to the 120th. This place shows us parents, patrimony, substance, foundations, movable goods, and whatever pertains to the hidden or stored wealth of one's inheritance. This is also a pivot of the birth chart. It is called the Lower Midheaven because it is established diametrically opposite the Midheaven (MC). But this place is joined to the Ascendant in the greatest partnership because it looks toward the Ascendant from a square <note>original: *quadrato*. A 90-degree angle, considered a strong and challenging connection.</note>, and is seen by the Ascendant through a square aspect, as is clear to the investigator.

**V.** The **Fifth House** from the Ascendant is established in the fifth sign, because beginning from 120 degrees from the Ascendant, it extends to 150 degrees. From this place, the number of children and the quality of one's lineage are found. It is called **Good Fortune**, because it is the house of **Venus** (♀). This place is also joined to the Ascendant in the greatest partnership; sometimes the Midheaven (MC) is established in the diameter of this sign <note>original: *in diametro huius signi MC pars constituitur*. A reference to different house-calculation systems where the Midheaven might fall in the 5th house depending on the latitude.</note>. It is associated with the Ascendant in a most powerful union because it sees from a trine <note>original: *trigono*. A 120-degree angle, the most harmonious aspect in astrology.</note> and receives its rays.

**VI.** The **Sixth House** is established in the sixth sign from the Ascendant, which, beginning at 150 degrees, extends to 180. In this sign, we shall find the cause of defects and health; this place is called **Bad Fortune** because it is the house of **Mars** (♂). This place is also "idle" because it is joined by no partnership to the Ascendant. However, sometimes the malice of the place itself is relieved if a star is located there while other stars, found in the tenth house from the Ascendant, are joined to it by a prosperous radiation that might help it.

**VII.** The **Seventh House** is established in the seventh sign from the Ascendant; starting from 180 degrees, it extends to 210 and ends there. Its beginning is fixed at the 180th degree. In this place is another pivot of the birth chart. It is called the **Setting** <note>original: *occasus*</note> by us, but by the Greeks, as we said above, it is called ***Dysis*** <note>original: "Δύσις", meaning the setting or the West.</note>. This pivot is positioned directly opposite the pivot of the Ascendant. From this place, let us seek the quality and quantity of marriages. This place is also joined to the Ascendant in a powerful partnership and is seen by the Ascendant from a diameter <note>original: *diametro*. An "opposition" aspect of 180 degrees.</note>.

**VIII.** The **Eighth House** is established in the eighth sign from the Ascendant, because starting from 210 degrees, it extends to 240 and ends there. This place is called ***Anaphora*** <note>original: "ἀναφορὰ", meaning a "rising up" or "succession."</note>. It is an "idle" house, because it also is joined by no partnership to the Ascendant. From this place, the quality of death is found. It is fitting for us to know that no star rejoices in this place except the **Moon** (☽) alone, and then only in nocturnal birth charts. For if in a nocturnal chart, the waxing Moon is found in this place, and while so positioned—without the partnership or radiation of malevolent stars—**Jupiter** (♃) looks upon her from a hexagon or trine...

->BOOK TWO.<-

<meta>catchword: first</meta>

...[if the planet] has looked into its own house, or the house of Venus ♀, or the house of Jupiter ♃, or the house of Saturn ♄, or within the bounds <note>original: *finibus*. These are specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign, each ruled by a different planet, which refine the planet's influence.</note> of those stars we have mentioned, it decrees the greatest resources, wealth beyond measure, magnificent glories of power, and promises the clear ornaments of nobility.

**IX.** The **Ninth House** is established in the ninth sign from the Ascendant; its measurement extends from the 240th degree for the 9th section up to the 270th degree. Moreover, it is the place of the Day and of the Sun ☉. In this place, we find the schools of human thought <note>original: *sectas*</note>; it also concerns religions and foreign travels. This place is joined to the Ascendant by a very strong aspect <note>original: *radiatione*, literally "beaming."</note>: for it is seen from a trine <note>original: *trigono*. An aspect of 120 degrees, considered the most harmonious and supportive relationship between signs.</note> relative to the Ascendant and receives its rays.

**X.** The **Tenth House** is established in the tenth sign from the Ascendant: taking its beginning at the 270th degree, it extends to the 300th degree and ends there. This place is principal and more sublime in power than all the other angles <note>original: *cardinum*</note>. This place is called by us the **MC** <note>original: *M C*, abbreviation for *Medium Coeli* or Midheaven.</note>, and by the Greeks **Mesourania** <note>original: *$\mu\epsilon\sigma ov\rho\alpha\nu\acute{\iota}\alpha$*, literally "the middle of the sky."</note>: for it is situated in the middle part of the entire world. In this place, we find life, spirit, all actions, the fatherland, the home, and one's entire social life; also the arts, and whatever is granted to us by the support of the arts. From this place, we may perceive the vices of the soul with easier reasoning. The power of this place is joined in partnership with the Ascendant, because it is seen from a square <note>original: *quadrato*. A 90-degree aspect, often indicating tension or dynamic activity.</note> relative to the Ascendant.

**XI.** The **Eleventh House** is established in the eleventh sign from the Ascendant: this place begins at the 300th degree and is established up to the 330th degree. This place is called by us the **Good Spirit** or **Good Genius**; by the Greeks it is called **Agathos Daimon** <note>original: *$\alpha\gamma\alpha\theta\text{ò}\varsigma$ $\delta\alpha\acute{\iota}\mu\omega\nu$*</note>. In this place, the exact degree of the MC is frequently found. It is the place of Jupiter ♃ and is joined to the Ascendant in no small partnership: for it sees the Ascendant from a sextile <note>original: *Hexagono*. A 60-degree aspect, considered friendly and helpful.</note> and is seen by the Ascendant from a sextile, and it captures its rays.

**XII.** The **Twelfth House** is established in the twelfth sign from the Ascendant: starting from the 330th degree, it is established up to the 360th degree. This place is called **Kakodaimon** <note>original: *$\kappa\alpha\kappa\text{o}\delta\alpha\acute{\iota}\mu\omega\nu$*</note> by the Greeks, and by us the **Bad Spirit**. From this place, the quality of enemies and the substance of slaves are shown to us by an easy indication; we also find vices and illnesses in this place. But this is also an "idle" house, because it is joined to the Ascendant by no partnership <note>Signs that are adjacent to the Ascendant cannot "see" it via a standard aspect, making them "blind" or disconnected from the life-force of the individual.</note>. It is the place of Saturn ♄. Indeed, it shows the father through Saturn ♄ in the birth chart of both a man and a woman; the mother through Venus ♀, the wife through Venus ♀, and the husband through Mars ♂.

## THE NAMES AND EFFECTS OF THE TWELVE HOUSES. CHAPTER XXIII.

Now, because we have stated the qualities, names, and substance of the twelve houses, we ought to show these same places through a brief summary of their meanings. Let our beginning, therefore, be the Ascendant, whose starting point the other places follow. It is fitting that these places be called by these names: **Life** (1), **Hope** (2), **the Goddess or Brothers** (3), **Parents** (4), **Children** (5), **Health** (6), **Spouse** (7), **Death** (8), **Religion or God** (9), **MC** (10), **Good Spirit** (11), **Bad Spirit** (12). Through these names and these places, the substance of the entire birth chart is sought. 

When you have inspected these things diligently and grasped them in your mind, and joined everything together in that partnership, observe which stars possess those very places; you will also diligently inspect the conditions of the daytime and nighttime stars. Furthermore, you must see what kind of testimony the benefic stars <margin>Benefic stars.</margin> provide to each place, and which places the malefic stars strike with their rays. For whatever place the benefic stars have looked upon—either being situated in that same place, or from a trine, or from a sextile—all those things which we said should be sought will turn out fortunately. 

<margin>Malefic [stars].</margin> If, however, without the testimony of benefic stars, the malefic stars alone—either situated there, or from a square, or from an opposition <note>original: *diametro*</note>—should infect these same places, then according to the quality of each house, all the things we touched upon and described in the earlier part of our discourse as being seen in each place, will be burdened by frequent calamities of misfortune. 

<margin>Mixed [stars].</margin> If, indeed, both benefic and malefic stars look upon a place with equal rays, then the good fortune is diminished and the misfortune is mitigated, and the whole substance of the place is composed by a moderate reckoning of equality, so that they are liberated from the harmful malefic stars by the salutary protection of the benefic stars. 

<margin>The place of the star must be considered.</margin> Inspect also which star is situated in which place, and whose star's domicile or bounds it possesses; and if it should be situated in another's house, inspect its ruler <note>original: *dominũ*</note>, what place of the birth chart it occupies, and whether in...

[whether it is] in the first cardinal points <note>The "cardines" or angles: the 1st, 10th, 7th, and 4th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart.</note> of the birth chart, or in secondary places, or in "black" places <note>original: *nigris*. This refers to houses that are "dark" because they do not "aspect" or see the Ascendant, often considered unlucky or weak.</note>, and whether it is in its height <note>Exaltation.</note> or its depression: and whether it is in signs where it rejoices, or in those where it is saddened by a certain natural grief. For if the **lord of the sign** <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign where another planet is currently located; often called the "dispositor."</note> is well placed, even the star we are examining borrows a portion of happiness from the joy of its host. But if the lord of that sign is debased for any reason, even if the star we are examining is placed in favorable areas of the chart and is naturally inclined to provide something good, it is hindered by the shared debasement of the star that is the mistress of the sign. You can easily understand this through an analogy of our own actions: if you enter the home or dwelling of a friend or host for the sake of hospitality, and the master of the house is buoyed by happy successes, you also become a sharer in that happiness; for you borrow the joy of gladness from the successes of your host. If, however, your host is disfigured by wretched squalor and entangled in the dejected accidents of misfortune, the shared torments of grief and misfortune will affect you as well. In this way, the stars that are lords of the signs uplift others when they are well placed; they arrange the inhabitant and guest of their house according to the condition of their own status through a balanced partnership, and they shape the power of the guest to their own whim.

<margin>Observations of the birth chart.</margin>
Search also to see, if it is a **diurnal** birth chart <note>A chart for a birth that occurred during the day.</note>, to what extent the stars that rejoice in diurnal charts are placed, and to what extent those that harm diurnal charts are present. For if the stars that rejoice by day possess the principal places in a diurnal chart and are found in the first cardinal points, they decree the greatest increases in happiness. But if the stars which we said rejoice by night possess the principal places or the first cardinal points in a diurnal chart, they indicate infinite misfortunes with continuous calamities. We must also observe this in **nocturnal** charts, but with the order of power reversed. For if, in a nocturnal chart, the stars or the forms of the celestial images <note>Signs of the Zodiac.</note> which we said rejoice by night possess the principal places or the first cardinal points, they likewise decree the greatest increases in happiness. But if, in nocturnal charts, those which we said rejoice in diurnal company possess the principal places or the first cardinal points, they cause the entire ornament of happiness to be entangled in the falling accidents of misery.

<margin>The use of Astrology <note>original: *Matheseos*.</note></margin>
If all these things are collected by diligent reasoning, and if you combine the mixtures of benevolent and malevolent stars, the power of the places, and the authorities of the signs and degrees through a balanced comparison of their conjunction, you will be able to designate the whole man—from his first to his final day—and his entire life, his hope, his brothers, parents, children, health, spouse, death, his school of thought <note>original: *sectam*</note>, his actions, honors, travels, his home, his foundations, his substance, and the accusations and dangers of friends and enemies, all through a clear explanation of your definition. We have said enough of these things for now in this book of instruction; but when we come to the **predictions** <note>original: *apotelesmata*, a Greek term for the outcomes or results of astrological configurations.</note>, we shall first speak of everything broadly, and then with subtle interpretation, showing everything by designation so that no trembling of doubt may hinder the science of pronouncement.

### THE QUALITIES OF BIRTH CHARTS, WHICH 
### are called noble or mediocre. Chapter XXIV.

It is also fitting for us to know that a **mediocre** birth chart is one which has only one star (besides the Sun ☉ and Moon ☽) established in its own domicile <note>The sign that the planet rules.</note> and located in the principal places of the chart. One who has two stars placed in their own domiciles in favorable places of the birth chart is buoyed by **moderate** happiness. He who has three will be **happy and powerful beyond measure**. One who has four stars established in their own domiciles will approach the **happiness of the gods**. Beyond this number, the substance of the human race does not allow. But he who has no star established in its own domicile will be unknown, ignoble, and always entangled in miserable actions.

# BOOK TWO. ALL THE ASPECTS OF THE STARS. CHAPTER XXV.

<margin>The Diameter.</margin>
First and foremost, we must teach what is a diameter, what is a trine, what is a square, what is a sextile, and what is "cast off"; also, what is a right trine and what is a left, and what is a right sextile and what is a left. The diameter <note>original: *diametrum*; in modern astrology, this is called an "opposition," where two signs are 180 degrees apart.</note> is of Aries ♈ and Libra ♎; the diameter of Taurus ♉ is Scorpio ♏, and so on for all other signs in a similar fashion. But so that you may find this not only by sight but also by calculation, we teach it with a brief example: from one sign to another, the seventh sign is the diameter. This is always a harmful and threatening radiation <note>original: *radiatio*; the ancient belief that stars "see" each other by casting beams of light.</note>.

<margin>The Trine.</margin>
The trine <note>original: *trigonum*; a "triangle" aspect where signs are 120 degrees apart.</note> is the fifth sign from the one we start with. This is shown by this example: from Aries ♈ to Leo ♌ is a trine, and similarly from Taurus ♉ to Virgo ♍, and so through all the signs; whichever is in the fifth sign is the trine.

<margin>The Right and Left Trine.</margin>
We must also know what a right trine is and what a left one is. The "right" <note>original: *dextrum*.</note> is that which is behind the sign we start from; the "left" <note>original: *sinistrum*.</note> is that which is ahead. <note>In ancient astrology, "behind" means moving against the order of the zodiac signs, following the daily rotation of the sky.</note> For example, the right trine of Aries ♈ is Sagittarius ♐, while the left is Leo ♌. In the same way, for Leo ♌, the right trine is Aries ♈, and the left is Sagittarius ♐. For Sagittarius ♐, Leo ♌ is the right trine, and Aries ♈ is the left. Thus you shall seek trines in all other signs; and this is a prosperous and happy radiation.

The square <note>original: *quadratum*; a 90-degree aspect.</note> is the fourth sign from the one we begin with, as shown by this example: the square of Aries ♈ is the sign Cancer ♋, of Cancer is Libra ♎, of Libra is Capricorn ♑, and of Capricorn is Aries ♈. But which is the right square and which is the left, you will find by the same reasoning we stated for trines. For whichever is behind is the right square—such as Capricorn ♑ for Aries ♈—and the left is Cancer ♋. Thus in all other squares, what is behind is the right, and what is ahead is the left. This is a threatening radiation, composed of malicious power and full of the bitterness of enmity.

<margin>The Sextile.</margin>
Sextiles <note>original: *hexagona*; a "six-sided" aspect where signs are 60 degrees apart.</note> are the same as trines, but of lesser power. A sextile is the third sign from the one we start with; for example, Gemini ♊ is the sextile of Aries ♈. You will find which is the right sextile and which is the left just like the others. But lest there be any controversy, we give examples of this too: the right sextile of Aries ♈ is Aquarius ♒, and the left is Gemini ♊. Thus in the other signs, what is behind is the right, and what is ahead is the left. But those sextiles are more powerful which have "tropical" <note>Cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which mark the change of seasons.</note> or "double" <note>Mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces, which have a "dual" nature.</note> signs between them; those that are divided by "solid" <note>Fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius.</note> signs are ineffective.
