# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS: THE AFFINITY OF THE SIGNS AMONG THEMSELVES. Chapter XXVI.

We have already discussed, by means of radiation <note>The ancient concept that planets "see" each other by casting beams of light across the zodiac.</note>, the reasoning that joins the horoscopus <note>original: *horoscopus*; the Ascendant or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> to trines, squares, diameters, and sextiles. Now we must briefly explain why we have shown that certain places are joined to the Ascendant by the fellowship of radiation, while others are turned away from the Ascendant and are in some way foreign—which we have rightly called **idle**. We must explain all these things so that this book of instruction may be fortified with the full substance of the Mathematical Art <note>original: *Matheseos*; in this context, "Mathesis" refers specifically to the divine science of astrology.</note>. All signs are joined together in mutual obligation to one another. Briefly learn why we say this: we have said that all signs have 30 degrees <note>original: *p.*, abbreviation for *partes*.</note>. Therefore, if you take these 30 degrees twelve times over and make them into one sum, you will complete 360 degrees, which are divided through the bodies of all twelve signs. From this, the proximity of the connection associates all signs with one another. Therefore, whichever signs are joined by a whole number of degrees that results in 360, these are joined to one another by the radiation of equality and fellowship.

<margin>The Sextile.</margin>
Regarding the **Sextile** <note>original: *Hexagonum*; an aspect where signs are 60 degrees apart.</note>, we have spoken before, and now we indicate it degree by degree. From the degree of the Ascendant, whatever is at 60 degrees marks the side of the Sextile. Therefore, if you combine 60 six times, it makes the whole number of 360 degrees. Thus, that which fills the total sum of 360 degrees by the joining of six whole parts is united in a balanced fellowship.

<margin>The Trine.</margin>
Regarding the **Trine** <note>original: *Trigonum*; a "triangle" aspect where signs are 120 degrees apart.</note>, which is the fifth place from the Ascendant and from the others—whether it be a right trine or a left one—we have said it is joined to the Ascendant or others in the greatest fellowship. Let us briefly explain by what reasoning this happens. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, if we triple 120 degrees, we will complete the first whole number of 360 degrees. By this radiation of connection, this place is joined to the Ascendant; indeed, all trines are joined to one another by this radiation of fellowship.

<margin>The Square.</margin>
We have also said that the **Square** <note>original: *Quadratum*; an aspect where signs are 90 degrees apart.</note> is joined to the Ascendant by a very strong fellowship of radiation. I shall briefly show the reasoning for this connection as well. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, we establish this place at 90 degrees. Thus, by quadrupling 90 degrees, we complete the whole number of 360 degrees. See how appropriately the Square is a worthy "side," because the number 90 quadrupled completes the entire substance of 360 degrees; for this reason, it received the name "Square." This is the reasoning in all squares.

<margin>The Diameter.</margin>
We have said that **Diameters** <note>original: *Diametra*; in modern astrology, the "opposition," where signs are 180 degrees apart.</note> are joined to the Ascendant by the fellowship of radiation, and I will explain the reasoning for this connection. Starting from the first degree of the Ascendant, we establish this place at 180 degrees. Therefore, if we double 180, we will make the whole number 360. Because two whole numbers—that is, 180 joined twice—render the full substance of 360 degrees, these places are joined to one another by the greatest radiation of fellowship. This radiation exists in all diameters. However, those places which are so positioned that their degrees cannot complete the whole number of 360 by doubling, tripling, or quadrupling, are joined by no reasoning of fellowship with the Ascendant, nor with any other sign that falls in such a way. Because of this, whatever sign is found outside of this numerical logic is called **idle** and **abject**.

---

### THE DOMINION OF THE SIGNS OVER THE HUMAN BODY. Chapter XXVII.

We must explain which parts of the human body the twelve signs hold. This is extremely useful for predictions <note>original: *apotelesmata*; the interpretive outcomes or effects of the stars.</note>, especially when we wish to find the location of a health condition or a physical defect. The head of a human is in the sign of **Aries** ♈, the neck in **Taurus** ♉, the shoulders in **Gemini** ♊, the heart in **Cancer** ♋, the chest and stomach in **Leo** ♌, the belly in **Virgo** ♍, the kidneys and vertebrae in **Libra** ♎, the reproductive organs <note>original: *natura*.</note> in **Scorpio** ♏, the thighs in **Sagittarius** ♐, the knees in **Capricorn** ♑, the shins in **Aquarius** ♒, and the feet in **Pisces** ♓. In this way, all the members of a human are divided through these signs.

## THE GIVER OF HUMAN LIFE. CHAPTER XXVIII.

Now we must explain which star <note>Astrologers of this period used "star" to refer to both planets and the luminaries (the Sun and Moon).</note> decrees how many years: more years if well-positioned, and fewer if poorly situated. When you have carefully examined the Giver of Life <note>original: *dator vitae*; often called the *Apheta* or *Hyleg* in other traditions, this is the planet or point in the chart that determines the length of the native's life.</note>, that is, the Lord of the Nativity, and you have seen in what place it is positioned, in which sign, and in which degrees <note>original: *p.*, abbreviation for *partes*.</note>; and if you have likewise observed by the same method the ruler of the sign in which the Giver of Life is located—noting its place, sign, and degrees—and also the Moon, and to what extent they and the benefic stars aspect the Giver of Life, you will be able to easily define the whole substance of the lifespan.

For if the Giver of Life itself is positioned in a good place, a good sign, and in good degrees, a full number of years is decreed, especially if Jupiter (♃) in a daytime birth, or Venus (♀) in a nighttime birth, supports the Giver of Life with a favorable radiation <note>The favorable "rays" or aspects from benefic planets.</note>. 

Therefore, if **Saturn (♄)** is the Giver of Life and decrees a full number of years, it decrees 57 years; if in a middle state, 42 years and six months; but if it decrees poorly, it decrees 30 years, or 20 months, or 30 days and 12 hours. 

If **Jupiter (♃)** is the Giver of Life and decrees well, it decrees 79 years; if in a middle state, 45 years and six months; if poorly, 12 years, or 12 months, 12 days, 12 hours, [or] 15 days. 

If [**Mars (♂)**] <note>The name is omitted in the Latin but implied by the symbol ♂ and the context.</note> is the Giver of Life and decrees well, it decrees 66 years; if in a middle state, 40 and six months; if poorly, 15 years, or 15 months, [and] 12 hours. 

If the **Sun (☉)** decrees well, it decrees 120 years; if in a middle state, 69 and 6 months; if poorly, 19 years, or 19 months, 19 days, [and] 12 hours. 

If **Venus (♀)** decrees well, it decrees 82 years; if in a middle state, 45 and 6 months; if poorly, 8 years, or 8 months, [and] 12 hours. 

If **Mercury (☿)** decrees well, it decrees 76 years; if in a middle state, 48 and 6 months; if poorly, 20 years, or 20 months, [and] 12 hours. 

If the **Moon (☽)** decrees well, it decrees 108 years; if in a middle state, 66 and 6 months; if poorly, 29 years, or 29 months, 2 days, [and] 12 hours. 

Thus, if the Lord of Life or the Giver of Life (that is, the Lord of the Nativity) is in its own house, or its own exaltation <note>original: *altitudine*.</note>, or its own bounds <note>original: *finibus*; specific segments of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets.</note>, and the stars of its own condition bear good witness to it—that is, they look upon it with good radiation—and those stars which bear witness are themselves well-positioned, a greater number of years is decreed. However, they decree a middle age especially if the Giver of Life is indeed in its own bounds, its own domiciles, its rising, or its dignity, yet is hindered by malefic radiations, or is positioned in an neglected place, or is fortified by the testimony of no other star.

## THE LORD OF TIME. CHAPTER XXIX.

The Greeks called the <term>Chronocrator</term> <note>original: *Chronocratorem*; literally "Time-ruler."</note> the "Lord of Times." In daytime nativities, the Sun (☉) takes the beginning of the times and divides them among the others; in nighttime nativities, the Moon (☽) does so. You should not admit any other method, because this one is approved by everyone. 

Therefore, when the Sun is the Lord of Times, it holds dominion for 10 years and 9 months. In the same way, when the Moon is the mistress of time, she will hold 10 years and 9 months. Thus, in a daytime nativity, the Sun takes the first decade; the second is taken by whichever planet is found in the second place following the course of the signs in the nativity; the third by whichever is after the second, and so on for the rest. 

To understand this more clearly, we teach by this example: if in a daytime nativity the Sun is found in Aries (♈), it will be the lord of the decade; and so it is in whatever other sign it may be. Therefore, whichever planet is in Taurus (♉) will be in the second place; whichever is after Taurus will be third; and so on for the others in this manner. We shall do the same in nighttime nativities, starting from the Moon. But whoever is allotted the decade, although they are the lord of the whole time, they nevertheless divide the entire substance of the decade among all the stars, starting from themselves and handing it over to those who follow in order: first handing it over to whichever planet is found second in the chart <note>original: *themate*; the birth chart or "theme".</note>.

### THE DIVISION OF TIMES. CHAPTER XXX.

We shall briefly demonstrate how great the distribution of time periods is. The **Sun (☉)** receives nineteen months, the **Moon (☽)** twenty-five, **Saturn (♄)** thirty, **Jupiter (♃)** twelve, **Mars (♂)** fifteen, and **Mercury (☿)** twenty. <note>Venus (♀) is omitted from the sentence in the original Latin but assigned 8 months in the table and traditional chronocrator systems.</note> What actually happens during this distribution of times we shall discuss in the books on *Outcomes* <note>original: *Apotelesmatum*; refers to judicial astrology, the study of the effects of planetary movements on human life.</note>, showing what each star decrees when it takes over a period of time from another star. For all things that happen to us, whether good or bad, we gather from this calculation of times. Even the end of life is found this way, as is the entire substance of the birth chart <note>original: *geniturae*</note> and everything that the order of the stars has decreed. We find the annual division by very easy methods: for it always takes its beginning from the **Ascendant** <note>original: *horosc.*, an abbreviation for *horoscopus*; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>. The first year will be that in which the Ascendant is located, the second year in the second sign, the third in the third sign, and so on for the others in order. Others do this same thing from the **Sun (☉)** in a daytime birth, but from the **Moon (☽)** in a nighttime birth, and this method has its own logic.

### THE DIVISION OF THE YEARS BY DAYS. Chapter XXXI.

The days of the entire year are also divided among the individual stars. I will take care to show to what extent they are divided and from where they take their beginning—showing when illnesses, when weaknesses, when profits, when losses occur, and when joys or sorrows arise. For when the benefic stars have received the days, we are liberated from every evil; but when the malefic stars receive them, then sudden cases of misfortune attack us. Therefore, in whatever sign the year falls, the ruler of that sign receives the first days, and after that ruler, the others follow according to how they are each positioned in the birth chart. I will also teach how many days each star is allotted. 

The **Sun (☉)** has fifty-three days, the **Moon (☽)** seventy-one, **Saturn (♄)** eighty-five, **Jupiter (♃)** thirty, **Mars (♂)** thirty-six, **Venus (♀)** thirty-three, and **Mercury (☿)** fifty-seven. <note>These figures total 365 days, comprising a full solar year.</note> Within this space of days, we can find everything that happens to us, provided we have first looked into the quality of the signs and the "places" <note>The twelve "houses" or sectors of the sky that govern different areas of life.</note>. For if a star is well-placed and has received either a long period, or months, or days, and is a benefic, it decrees all good things. But if a malefic star has received a period, or months, or days, and is poorly placed, it decrees misfortunes according to the quality of the places. Thus, by examining everything with prudent inquiry, you will be able to explain the whole substance of a most true nativity.

### THE OUTCOME OF THE ANTISCIA. Chapter XXXII.

Following all these instructions—and because we deferred the treatise on the **antiscia** <note>original: *antisciorum*; these are "shadow-points" or reflections, pairs of points in the zodiac that are equidistant from the solstice points (Cancer/Capricorn). They were thought to exert a hidden influence on each other.</note> a little while ago—we ought to explain this topic now, so that nothing in this instruction seems to have been overlooked by us. The knowledge of the antiscia has been handed down to us by the mastery of the Greeks; for I do not want anyone to suspect that this treatise does not exist among the Greeks. Indeed, **Ptolemy** follows no other logic than that of the antiscia; and **Antiochus**, when he says that Libra cannot see Aries because of the earth that is in the middle, touches upon the logic of the antiscia as if through a mirror. Furthermore, **Dorotheus of Sidon** <note>A famous 1st-century astrologer who wrote a foundational instructional poem on astrology.</note>, a most prudent man who wrote about the outcomes of the stars in the most truthful and eloquent verses, explained the logic of the antiscia in clear maxims, specifically in his fourth book. Now I shall briefly explain by what logic the antiscia are gathered. We begin the starting point of the antiscia either from **Gemini (♊)** and **Cancer (♋)**, or from **Sagittarius (♐)** and **Capricorn (♑)**. Therefore, following our own instruction, we begin from **Gemini (♊)** and **Cancer (♋)**.

# BOOK TWO

->**THE CALCULATION OF ANTISCIA**<-

**Gemini (♊)** casts an antiscium <note>original: *antiscium*; literally "opposite-shadow." This refers to a point in the zodiac that is the mathematical reflection of another sign or degree across the solstice axis (the Cancer-Capricorn line).</note> into **Cancer (♋)**, and **Cancer** into **Gemini**; **Leo (♌)** into **Taurus (♉)**, and **Taurus** into **Leo**; **Virgo (♍)** into **Aries (♈)**, and **Aries** into **Virgo**; **Libra (♎)** into **Pisces (♓)**, and **Pisces** into **Libra**; **Scorpio (♏)** into **Aquarius (♒)**, and **Aquarius** into **Scorpio**; **Sagittarius (♐)** into **Capricorn (♑)**, and **Capricorn** into **Sagittarius**. If we begin again from **Sagittarius** into **Capricorn**, it ends in the same manner at **Gemini** and **Cancer**. Therefore, we must always handle all these matters with wise investigation, lest such an honorable profession <note>The author refers here to the "profession" of astrology.</note> be overshadowed at any time by the false lies of outcomes <note>original: *apotelesmatum*; refers to the specific predictions or "effects" of planetary positions.</note>. 

But what we have said regarding the antiscia is not enough, unless the specific degrees <note>original: *partes*; here meaning the 30 individual degrees of a zodiac sign.</note> are also explained: which degree casts into which part, and which degree receives the antiscium in return. Among other things, it is necessary to know that no degree is cast into the thirtieth degree of a sign, and that the thirtieth degree itself sends no antiscium into any part. <margin>The thirtieth degree of each sign.</margin> Therefore, this example which we have made concerning **Gemini** and **Cancer** will pertain to the antiscia of all signs.

The 1st degree of **Gemini** casts an antiscium into the 29th degree of **Cancer**; in turn, the 29th degree of **Cancer** casts an antiscium into the 1st degree of **Gemini**.
The 2nd degree into the 28th, the 28th into the 2nd;
the 3rd into the 27th, the 27th into the 3rd;
the 4th into the 26th, the 26th into the 4th;
the 5th into the 25th, the 25th into the 5th;

the 15th into the 15th, and so on conversely. 

And you should do this in this manner until you have numbered through the number of degrees...

Thus Leo is in Taurus, and Taurus likewise in Leo; thus Aries in Virgo, and Virgo back in Aries; thus Pisces in Libra, and Libra back in Pisces; thus Scorpio in Aquarius, and Aquarius in Scorpio; thus Sagittarius in Capricorn, and Capricorn in Sagittarius. If, therefore, any stars <note>In ancient astrology, "stars" referred to both the fixed stars and the seven planets.</note> in the arrangement of a birth chart do not "see" each other <note>i.e., they do not form a standard aspect like a trine or square</note>, one must ask whether they are joined by a shared radiation through an **antiscium**. For when they have sent an **antiscium** in such a way that they join through a trine, square, opposition, or sextile radiation <note>original: *trigonica, quadrata, diametra, uel hexagona radiatione*. These are the four major geometric relationships in astrology.</note>, they decree results just as if they were composed in a simple arrangement; and thus all these things are fulfilled by the mixing of radiations. When you have done this, you will be able to find everything sought in the fates of men very easily. This is a hidden ratio, confirmed by the natural consensus of the **antiscia**, which I shall take care to explain at another time. However, you will be able to learn from this birth chart, which I set forth below, how much the power of the **antiscia** prevails and how much their logic operates.

<margin>This birth chart does not correspond to reason or astronomical calculation. For Venus cannot be in Taurus while the Sun is in 15 degrees of Pisces, to say nothing of Venus for the moment. <note>This marginalia likely comes from a later Renaissance editor/reader noting that Venus and Mercury never travel that far away from the Sun in the sky.</note></margin>

In the birth chart of this man, the Sun was in Pisces, the Moon in Cancer, Saturn in Virgo, Jupiter in Pisces (in the same degree as the Sun), Mars in Aquarius, Venus in Taurus, and Mercury in Aquarius. With the Sun at the same degree as the **Horoscope** <note>The Ascendant or rising sign.</note> in Scorpio, the father of this birth was sent into exile after a double ordinary consulship. But the man himself was similarly sent into exile on the charge of adultery. Yet, eventually snatched from exile, he was first appointed to the administration of Campania, then to the proconsulship of Achaia, and afterwards he was promoted to a similar proconsulship of Asia. Finally, by the consensus of all the Senators, he was promoted to the Prefecture of the City of Rome; and he turned his previously bitter and adverse fortune into a prosperous and successful one.

### THE BIRTH CHART OF LOLLIANUS.

For any man who is ignorant of the logic of **antiscia**, seeing the Sun with Jupiter in the same degrees in the fifth place from the **Horoscope**—that is, in **Good Fortune** <note>original: *bona fortuna*. The traditional name for the 5th house.</note>—would pronounce that his father was blessed, happy, and powerful, and other such things. But concerning his exile and the constant plots against him, he could pronounce nothing unless he turned his attention to the logic of the **antiscia**. You remember that we said that Pisces sends an **antiscium** into Libra, and Libra back into Pisces. Therefore, the Sun and Jupiter, being equally established in Pisces, send an **antiscium** into Libra—specifically into this sign in which the Sun is humbled and cast down <note>original: *humiliatur atq; deijcitur*. The Sun is in its "fall" in Libra, where its power is considered weakest.</note>, and into the twelfth house of the birth chart, which is the **Cacodemon** <note>From the Greek for "Evil Spirit," the 12th house was associated with enemies, hidden burdens, and exile.</note>. This revealed that the father's lineage was ignoble and decreed a famous exile for the father himself. Indeed Jupiter—whose force and power the ray of the **antiscium** transferred from the sign of Pisces to the sign of Libra—acted as if he had been established in the twelfth house (the **Cacodemon**) through the **antiscium**. This stirred up many enemies for both him and his father, and caused those enemies to be superior. Behold also another thing, which for the father

decreed exile. For Saturn, positioned in Virgo, sees the Sun by diameter <note>original: *de diametro*; in astrology, this refers to an "opposition," an aspect of 180 degrees usually signaling conflict.</note>, and its reflection <note>original: *antiscium*</note> looked back at the Sun's reflection from a diametric radiation. For being positioned in Virgo, it sent a reflection into Aries. Thus its reflection, positioned in Aries, and the Sun's reflection, which was sent into Libra, were made contrary to each other through the diameter; by a decree of the highest order <note>Likely referring to the Roman Senate or the Emperor's council.</note>, they caused him to be sent into exile, because the reflections of Saturn and the Sun, positioned in the cosmic signs, saw each other by diameter. 

Truly, the reason why he became an exile, or the reason why he was an adulterer (for this was the crime charged against him), is shown by this logic. We said that Gemini sends a reflection to Cancer: therefore, Jupiter positioned in Cancer sent its reflection into Gemini: whose reflection Mars, positioned in Aquarius, looked upon from the right side. Mars is destructive whenever he receives the light of the waxing Moon from any side. For the earlier effect, along with many bodily vices, finally made this same man an exile. 

But Mars itself, positioned in Aquarius, sends a reflection into Scorpio, in which sign the part of the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> had been situated. First, it struck the part of life—that is, the Ascendant—positioned in Taurus with a violent radiation. Then, it looked upon the full Moon (its reflection being positioned in Scorpio) by a trine radiation <note>original: *trigonica radiatione*; a harmonious 120-degree aspect.</note>. Third, it fouled its reflection in the part of the Ascendant. Fourth, the Moon, positioned in Cancer, saw the reflection of Mars, which it had sent into the Ascendant, from a trine. Therefore, from all sides, the waxing Moon, struck by the rays of Mars, oppressed him with many illnesses and finally made him an exile. And unless Jupiter, positioned in Cancer, had seen the Ascendant from a trine, he would never have been freed from exile; and unless the Moon had similarly seen the Ascendant from a trine while in its exaltation <note>original: *altitudine*; Cancer is the sign where Jupiter is traditionally most powerful.</note>, he would have died a violent death <note>original: *biothanatus*; one who dies by execution, suicide, or accident.</note>. 

But we said in the earlier parts that Jupiter’s benefits of this kind fail because on the third day, the Moon, positioned in Leo and full of light, collided with the rays of Mars by diameter. For this day—that is, the third—operates in a very great way in birth charts <note>original: *genituris*</note>.

<margin>The third day is to be observed in birth charts.</margin>

As for which radiation made him an adulterer, I will take care to explain this as well. Mars, positioned in Aquarius, sent its reflection into Scorpio. Thus, it found Venus placed in the setting <note>original: *occasu*; the Western horizon or Descendant of the chart.</note> of the birth chart. For Venus is miserable and entangled in many calamities if, placed in the setting, she is struck by the violent radiation of Mars. And again, the reflection of Venus, sent into Leo, looked back at Mars (positioned in Aquarius) by diameter at the Bottom of the Sky <note>original: *I M C* or *Imum Coeli*; the lowest point of the chart representing roots and endings.</note>. But Saturn, from the Bottom of the Sky, is joined to Aquarius by a square radiation <note>original: *quadrata radiatione*; a 90-degree aspect of tension.</note> without the logic of a reflection. Therefore, by all calculations—through themselves and through their reflections—in the principal angles <note>original: *cardinibus*; the four most powerful points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart, Venus and Mars attack each other as enemies in their type of association, either by square or diametric radiations.

This logic made him guilty of the charge of adultery. Truly, Mercury positioned in Aquarius, without the testimony of Saturn—that is, in the house of Saturn, and Saturn in the house of Mercury, having exchanged houses <note>original: *commutatis inuicem domibus*; a concept known as "mutual reception," where two planets stay in each other's signs, creating a strong bond.</note>—makes him an initiate of secret 

<margin>Saturn and Mercury in exchanged houses.</margin>

writings. And the Moon, positioned full of light in her own house in the ninth place, decrees the greatest honors for him; especially because in a nocturnal birth chart, having followed the power of her condition, she held the leadership in decreeing honors. Saturn and Mercury, through their exchanged houses, also decree such great learning and knowledge of literature that his speech and style are compared to the ancient authors. But because Venus sent a reflection of Mars into Leo—that is, into the house of the Sun and into the Midheaven <note>original: *M C* or *Medium Coeli*; the highest point of the chart, representing career and public reputation.</note>—the Emperor pronounced the sentence against him regarding those crimes. 

You know best, Lollianus <note>Mavortius Lollianus, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work.</note>, our glory, whose birth chart this is. Thus, having treated all these things, you will find how great is the power of the reflections; if anyone pursues this with diligent discipline, the intent of his conjecture will never fail him when he treats the fates of men.

### THE CONDITION OF THE ASTROLOGER.
### Chapter XXXIII.

Now you, whoever you are who attempts to read these books: when you have received all the knowledge of divinity, and when you have been imbued with the secrets of nature and initiated into the discipline of this sacred work, shape yourself into the image and likeness of divinity, so that you may always be adorned with the heraldry of truth. For it is necessary for him who speaks daily about the gods and with the gods to so form and instruct his mind that he always approaches an imitation of the divinity. Therefore, learn and practice all the ornaments of virtue. When you have instructed yourself in these, be easy of access, so that if anyone wishes to inquire anything of you, they may approach with no fear or trembling. Be modest, and among the sober, be content with a small livelihood and small means, lest the glory of this divine science be [stained by] ignoble...

<meta>This page transitions from the technical details of the birth chart to the ethical and professional code of conduct required of an astrologer. The author emphasizes the sacred nature of the profession, framing the astrologer as a priest of the celestial bodies.</meta>

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATHERNUS

...lest the greed for money defame you. Take care that, by your principles and your purpose, you surpass the principles and purpose of good priests. For it is necessary for the priest of the Sun ☉ and Moon ☽ <note>original: *antistitem... Solis et Lunae*; Firmicus views the astrologer as a religious official serving the planetary deities.</note>, and the other gods through whom all earthly things are governed, to always prepare his mind so that he is proven worthy of such great ceremonies by the testimony of everyone. Give your answers publicly, and say this beforehand to those who are about to ask: that you will speak with a clear voice about all things they ask you, so that nothing is asked of you that is not permitted to be either asked or said. 

Take care that you never respond to anyone inquiring about the state of the Republic or the life of the Roman Emperor. For it is not right, nor is it permitted, that we say anything about the state of the Republic out of wicked curiosity. But he is also a criminal, and worthy of every punishment, who, when asked, speaks about the fate of the Emperor—because you will neither be able to say anything about him, nor find it. 

<margin>Nothing is to be answered regarding the Emperor.</margin>

For it is proper for you to know that the haruspices <note>original: *aruspices*; traditional Roman diviners who interpreted the will of the gods by inspecting the entrails of sacrificed animals.</note>, whenever they have been asked by private citizens about the state of the Emperor and have wished to respond to the seeker, find that the entrails designated for this purpose, and the patterns of the veins, are thrown into a tangled confusion. Indeed, no astrologer <term>mathematicus<gloss>In the late Roman Empire, this term referred specifically to astrologers rather than general mathematicians.</gloss></term> has been able to define anything true about the Emperor’s fate. For the Emperor alone is not subject to the courses of the stars, and he is the only one in whose fate the stars have no power of decree. 

Since he is the lord of the whole world, his fate is governed by the judgment of the Supreme God. And because the earthly space of the whole world is subject to the Emperor's powers, he himself is also ranked among the number of those gods whom the primary divinity established to create and preserve all things. This reason also disturbs the haruspices: for whatever deity might be invoked by them, because it is of a lesser power, it cannot explain the substance of the greater power that exists in the Emperor. To him all talents, all social classes, all the wealthy, all the noble, all honors, and all powers serve; having obtained the power of divine and immortal freedom, he is placed among the primary ranks of the gods. 

Therefore, if anyone asks anything about the Emperor, I do not want you to disturb him with a fierce and severe response; rather, persuade him with gentle speech that no one can find anything regarding the life of the Emperor, so that, warned by your persuasions, he may set aside this madness of recklessness and correct the error of his mind. But I do not want you to denounce <note>original: *deferre*; to act as an informer to the authorities.</note> him if someone asks something wickedly, lest when he is subjected to a capital sentence because of the illicit desires of his mind, you appear to have been the cause of his death—which is foreign to the purpose of a priest. 

Let there be for you a wife, let there be a home, let there be an abundance of honorable friends, let there be constant access to the public. Be separated from all contentions, undertake no harmful business, and let no increase in money ever tempt you. Be removed from every fire of cruelty; never rejoice in the quarrels of others or in capital and deadly enmities, but let quiet moderation please you in every conversation. Flee from seditions, flee always from turbulent struggles; bind the loyalty of friendship with strong ties. Take care that in all your actions your faith remains incorruptible; never pollute your conscience with false testimonies. Never practice the lending of money for interest, nor let a miserable increase in wealth be gathered by you from the needs of others. Neither promise nor demand an oath <note>original: *iusiurandum*; Firmicus warns against the religious weight of legal oaths, especially in financial matters.</note>, especially if it is demanded because of money, lest the divine protections of the gods seem to have been implored for the sake of a miserable fee. 

To men who are wandering—especially those joined to you by the bond of friendship—show the right way of living, so that, formed by your instruction, they may be freed from the errors of their past life, and so that you may be able to restrain the ruined desires of men not only with your answers but also with your counsel. Never be present at nocturnal sacrifices, whether they are called public or private. Do not share stories in secret with anyone, but practice the discipline of this divine art openly, as I have stated above, in the sight of all. 

I do not want you to explain the vices of men too clearly when interpreting their birth charts; but whenever you come to such a point, withhold your answer with a certain trembling of a blush, lest you seem not to speak of, but to mock, what the bad course of the stars has decreed for a man. Separate yourself always from the allurements of the public shows <note>original: *spectaculorum*; referring to the gladiatorial games, chariot races, or theater, which were often seen as sites of moral corruption or demonic influence.</note>, lest anyone think you are a supporter of any faction...

<meta>catchword: met:an</meta>

<summary>Julius Firmicus Maternus outlines the strict ethical code for astrologers, emphasizing their status as "priests of the stars" who must avoid greed, maintain a public and moral life, and strictly refuse to cast horoscopes for the Roman Emperor, who is considered above the influence of the planets.</summary>

<keywords>astrological ethics, Roman Emperor, divinity of the Emperor, haruspices, mathematicus, priesthood of the stars, nocturnal sacrifices, social conduct, late antiquity astrology</keywords>

--- Page 66 ---
<meta>This page transitions from the ethical requirements of an astrologer—specifically the need for a pure and disciplined mind—into the opening of Book 3. The author begins by establishing the philosophical foundation of astrology: the human being as a microcosm created from the four elements in the image of the universe.</meta>

...it is fitting that the high priests of the gods be separate and distant from the wicked allurements of pleasures. When you have adorned your mind with these ornaments and protections of virtue, approach this work: and learn the subsequent books, which we have written concerning the astrological outcomes <note>original: *apotelesmatis*; the predicted effects or results of planetary positions</note>, with a fearless boldness of mind. But if you turn your mind away in any part from these teachings which we have stated concerning morals, see that you do not come to the secrets of this discipline by the instinct of perverted desire or the sacrilegious heat of rashness. Do not entrust the secrets of this religion to the wandering desires of the mind; for it is not right for the ruined minds of men to be initiated into divine ceremonies. Nor can the discipline of this venerable science ever take hold in a soul that is preoccupied and polluted by ruined greed; instead, he who defiles it with the wicked will of a practitioner <note>original: *professoris*; here referring to one who professes or teaches the art</note> always suffers the greatest loss. 

Therefore, be immaculate, pure, and chaste. If you have separated yourself from all nefarious acts which are accustomed to ruin the soul, and if the vow of right living has freed you from all the envy of crimes, and if you carry a purified mind mindful of the divine seed, approach this work and commit these later books to memory. Let them hand over to you the complete knowledge of divinity, so that your mind may secretly approach that prophetic majesty. Having attained the true knowledge of divinity, you may be instructed in defining the fates of men and in explaining the course of life—not only by your readings, but by the judgments of your own mind—so that more may be granted to you by the divinity of your own soul than by the teaching of the text.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS THE
## YOUNGER, OF SICILY, OF SENATORIAL RANK, TO MAVORTIUS
### Lollianus, the Third Book of the Mathematical Art <note>original: *Matheseos*; at this time, "Mathematics" often specifically referred to the study of astrology</note>.
#### PREFACE.

<margin>Man is made of four elements.</margin>
<margin>Petosyris and Necepso.</margin>
Let the whole discourse of the Mathematical Art, which was relevant, be transferred into the definition of astrological outcomes <note>original: *apotelesmatum*</note>. Once all things have been revealed and demonstrated which the divine seers have published, the discipline of this wisdom may be most fully introduced through us to those men who are students of this kind of art. Therefore, Lollianus, our glory, it is necessary for us to know in the first place that the God who is the fabricator of man, with nature as His guide, perfected the form of man, his posture, and his entire substance according to the image and appearance of the world <note>original: *mundi*; the cosmos or universe</note>. For He composed the body of man, like that of the world, from a mixture of the four elements—namely fire, water, air, and earth—so that the tempered union of all these might adorn a living being in the form of divine imitation. He set forth man with the skill of divine craftsmanship so that nature, by necessity, might bring together the power and substance of all elements in a small body. He did this so that for that divine spirit, which descended from the celestial mind for the sustenance of the mortal body, He might prepare a dwelling—fragile, yet similar to the universe. For this reason, the five stars, as well as the fiery Sun ☉ and Moon ☽, sustain man as a sort of "lesser world" <note>original: *minorem mundum*; the concept of the human being as a microcosm</note> by their eternal motion, so that a living being made in imitation of the world might be governed by a similar substance of divinity. Wherefore those divine men, worthy of all admiration, Petosyris and Necepso <note>legendary Egyptian founders of the astrological tradition</note>, whose wisdom approached the very secrets of divinity, also handed down to us the birth chart of the world through the divine mastery of science. They did this to show and demonstrate that man, formed according to the nature and likeness of the world, is sustained by those same principles by which the world itself is ruled and contained, through the eternal companions of perpetuity.

## THE BIRTH CHART OF THE WORLD. CHAPTER I.

<margin>Perhaps Anubis.</margin>
They wished this to be the birth chart of the world, following Aesculapius and Anubius <note>original: *Anubium*; likely referring to a legendary sage associated with the Egyptian god Anubis</note>, to whom the most powerful deity committed the secrets of this science. For they positioned the Sun ☉ in Leo ♌ at the fifteenth degree, the Moon ☽ in Cancer ♋ at the fifteenth degree, Saturn ♄ in Aquarius ♒ at the fifteenth degree, Jupiter ♃ in Sagittarius ♐ at the fifteenth degree, Mars ♂ in Scorpio ♏ at the fifteenth degree...

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...fifteenth, Venus in Libra at the fifteenth degree, Mercury in Virgo at the fifteenth degree, with the Ascendant <term>horoscopo; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> in Cancer at the fifteenth degree. According to this birth chart <term>genituram; a map of the heavens at a specific moment, used to predict fate</term>, then, and according to these conditions of the stars, and according to the testimonies which they provide to this birth chart, and according to these principles, the ancients maintain that the fates of men are arranged. This is just as it is contained in that book of Aesculapius which is called *Myriogenesis* <note>original: *μυριογένεσις*; a Greek title meaning "Ten Thousand Births" or "The Origin of Infinite Beings"</note>: so that nothing in the individual birth charts of men should seem alien to this birth chart of the world. 

Let us see, therefore, which star provided testimony to the "luminaries," to what extent, and by what method of its radiation—for the luminaries <term>lumina; the Sun and the Moon, the two brightest bodies in the sky</term> are the Sun and the Moon. Saturn, however, first joins itself to the Moon, for it has followed the condition of the Moon. Now, it follows the condition of the Moon for this reason: because, being situated in a feminine sign, it received the rays of the Moon (which was also situated in a feminine sign) through an opposition <term>per diametrum; an aspect of 180 degrees, where planets are positioned directly across from each other in the zodiac</term>. 

But when this same Saturn, in this particular birth chart, made its transit to the sign of Aquarius, it joined itself to the Sun again with a similar radiation: and it is again adapted to the condition of the Sun. For being situated in a masculine sign, it associates itself with an equal testimony of radiation, since it regarded the Sun through an opposition <note>original: *per diametrum*</note> with a radiation similar to that of the Moon. 

By this same principle, Jupiter also was situated in Sagittarius, and providing testimony through a trine <term>per trigonum; an aspect of 120 degrees, forming a triangle; usually considered a harmonious and supportive connection</term>, it first joined itself to the Sun's condition. For this reason, being situated in a masculine sign and associated with the Sun (which is situated in a sign of the same gender), it first follows the Sun's power. But when it has made its transit to Pisces, it will join itself again to the Moon in an equal condition. For in a similar manner, being placed in a feminine sign, it will have regarded the Moon (situated in a sign of the same gender) through a trine with a balanced radiation of condition. 

In a similar way, the star of Mars, situated in Scorpio, because it is in a feminine sign, provides testimony to the Moon through a trine. But when it comes to Aries, making testimony to the Sun while placed in a masculine sign, it will join itself to the Sun by a trine radiation. 

But this principle is changed in the case of Venus: for though situated in Libra, which is itself a masculine sign, it nevertheless provides testimony to the Moon through a square <term>per quadratum; an aspect of 90 degrees, often associated with challenge or friction</term>. However, when it has made its transit to Taurus, being situated in a feminine sign and regarding the Sun with a square radiation, it will again provide testimony to the Sun. 

Mercury, however, the ancients wished to be "common" in this birth chart, because it provides testimony to neither the Sun nor the Moon through a square, a trine, or an opposition: nor does it join itself to either the Sun or Moon by radiation. But it is indeed delighted by the Sun during the day, if it is a "morning star"; but by the Moon during the night, if it is an "evening star." 

They maintain that all these things we have mentioned must also be observed in the birth charts of men: and they believe that they cannot discover the fate of a human being unless these radiations have been gathered by a wise investigation. But lest the fabulous stories of men deceive you, and lest anyone...

### BOOK THREE

...might think that this birth chart was composed by the wisest men without cause, every detail must be specifically explained by us, so that the most prudent reasoning of this secret may be made known through all diligent expositions. This was not the actual birth chart of the world:
<margin>The uncertain origin of the world.</margin>
for the world did not have a certain day of its own beginning, nor was anything present at that time when the world was formed by the reasoning of the divine mind and provident divinity. Nor could the focus of human frailty extend itself so far that it could conceive or explain the origin of the world by easy reasoning—especially since the greater <term>apokatastasis; the restoration of the universe to its original state</term> <note>original: ἀποκατάστασις</note> of three hundred thousand years is completed in that space of time through <term>ekpyrosis; a great conflagration or purification by fire</term> <note>original: ἐκπύρωσιν</note> or through <term>kataklysmos; a great flood or cataclysm</term> <note>original: κατακλυσμὸν</note>. For the restoration is accustomed to happen by these two types:
<margin>The restoration of the world.</margin>
for a flood follows a burning—that is, a <term>kataklysmos</term> follows an <term>ekpyrosis</term>. For by no other thing could burned things be reborn, nor by any other thing could they be recalled to their former face and form, unless the mixtures and the combined dust of the ashes conceived the gathered fertility of all generative seeds. But so that there would be an example for astrologers to follow in the birth charts of men, the divine men fashioned this "birth chart of the world" through prudent reasoning. It is pleasing, therefore, to explain the inventions of this divine composition, so that the reasoning of this admirable conjecture may be opened by the study of mastery. They wished, therefore, to establish the Moon <term>☽</term> so that she first joined herself to Saturn <term>♄</term>, and to him she handed over the leadership of the ages. Nor was this indeed without merit.
<margin>The ages as they followed one another.</margin>
For because the first origin of the world was uncultivated and rough, and wild with rustic interaction—and because crude men, having entered the first footsteps of light unknown to them, lacked the system of established humanity—they wished Saturn <term>♄</term> to be this rustic and rough time. This was so that, in imitation of this star, at the beginnings of life, the established quality might endure through wild interaction and the harshness of inhuman ferocity. After Saturn <term>♄</term>, Jupiter <term>♃</term> received the power of the ages.
<margin>♄</margin>
<margin>♃</margin>
For to him in the second place the Moon is joined; so that with the horror of the former squalor abandoned, and the ferocity of rustic interaction set aside, a more cultivated life of men might be returned with purified morals. In the third place, Mars <term>♂</term> joining himself to the Moon <term>☽</term>, she handed over the power of the ages to him;
<margin>♂</margin>
so that mortality, having entered the right path of life and being composed by a certain moderation of inhumanity, might conceive all the ornaments of the arts and fabrications. After Mars <term>♂</term>, Venus <term>♀</term> received the time of ruling; so that the discipline of men, growing by degrees, might also conceive the ornaments of wisdom.
<margin>♀</margin>
They wished this time—in which learned speech cultivated the morals of men, and in which men were formed in the natural freedom of individual disciplines—to belong to Venus <term>♀</term>, so that, protected by the majesty of a joyful and health-giving divinity, they might govern their wandering acts by the mastery of providence. They thought the final time should be given to Mercury <term>☿</term>, to whom the Moon <term>☽</term> joins herself last. What can be found more subtle than this arrangement? For once the rustic pursuits were purged, the arts discovered, and the disciplines organized, the focus of the human race sharpened itself through various acts. And because a noble character in man cannot keep to a single course of life, from various institutions and confused morals the boldness of malice grew; and at this time, the race of men both invented and handed down the disgraces of life's crimes through wicked machinations. For this cause, they thought the final time should be handed to Mercury <term>☿</term>,
<margin>☿</margin>
so that in imitation of this star, the race of men might conceive power once full malice was discovered. From these things, therefore, which were carried out in order, and from these things—whichever men created the change of succeeding times—the birth chart of the world was composed by a divine interpretation of conjecture, and thus both the origin and the course of the human race are handed down to us. This was done so that it might be the example we follow in the birth charts of men. However, lest anything seem to be omitted by us, everything must be explained which proves that man was formed in imitation of the world and in its likeness. Indeed, we have said—and it is proven by everyone—that the restoration <note>original: ἀποκατάστασιν</note> happens through conflagration <note>original: ἐκπύρωσιν</note> and through flood <note>original: κατακλυσμὸν</note>. The substance of the human body, once the course of life is completed, is dissolved by a similar reasoning. For whenever the body of a man, excessively loosened by the natural heat of warmth, evaporates through inundations of humors, it is always either cooked away by fiery heat or dissolved by excessive sweating. Not otherwise do the most prudent interpreters of the medical art pronounce the substance of the human race to be dissolved at its natural end, unless either moisture dissolves the fire, or heat again dominates...

...with the spark extinguished, the fire deep within the marrow withers. In this way, nature the master-craftsman composed man in every respect as an imitation of the world: so that whatever either dissolves or forms the substance of the world, this same thing should both form and release man.

## THE FIRST OF THE SIGNS. CHAPTER II.

<margin>Perhaps broadly.</margin> <note>original: "fortè platicè"; This refers to an astrological calculation based on the whole sign rather than specific degrees.</note>
We must now explain why they wished the beginning of the twelve signs to start from Aries. I did not explain this in the book of *Institutions* <note>Referring to an introductory volume of this work</note> because that question could not have been clarified unless the <term>genitura mundi; the birth chart of the world</term> had first been shown. I ought not to have explained it in that book, lest that exposition disturb the unrefined minds of students with an obscure interpretation. Therefore, reconsidering the birth chart of the world, which we have said was most prudently composed by the wisest men, I found the <term>Medium Coeli; the Midheaven or the highest point in the sky</term> <note>original: MC</note> of that birth chart was positioned in Aries. For this reason—because the Midheaven frequently, or rather always, holds the primary position in all birth charts, and because this place is first above the summit of the sky, and because we gather the foundations of the entire birth chart from this place—it was appropriate that the beginning was given to all signs from this sign. This is especially true since the majority of the stars, as well as both "luminaries" (that is, the Sun and the Moon), sent their rays into this sign. From this, it was agreed among all nations that the beginning of the stars should start from this sign. Now that these things have been said and shown, we must define what each individual star decrees when positioned in the various houses of the birth chart. And although some might think this arrangement is <term>platica; broad or general</term> <note>original: "platicam"</note>, it nevertheless settles the student’s mind with an easy mastery of instruction, lest the astrologer, as if placed in darkness, be disturbed by the falling confusion of error. But although these things may be thought by some to be defined in a <term>Platonic</term> <note>Possibly a scribal error for "platicè" (broadly), though the text says "Platonice"</note> manner, many things in this book are stated <term>partiliter; by exact degree</term>. For the stars will only have their full efficacy if they are positioned in their individual places by their exact degrees.

## THE DECREES OF SATURN THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER III.

<margin>The first place of Saturn in birth charts.</margin>
If Saturn is positioned by exact degree in the <term>horoscopus; the Ascendant or the 1st House</term> during a daytime birth—that is, in that specific degree where the Ascendant is—he will cause the birth to be announced with a great shout. Furthermore, the one who is born will be the eldest of all his brothers; or, if anyone was born before him, that child will be separated from the parents. Indeed, this god <note>Ancient astrologers often referred to the planets as gods.</note> always causes those born during the day with him in any of the four <term>cardines; the angles or pivot points of the chart</term> to be the first-born or the first-nourished, or causes those brothers born before them to pass away. He also makes people puffed up and uplifted by a spirit of pride. However, if Saturn is positioned in the Ascendant by day, or occupies another angle of the birth chart, or is in the <term>anaphora; the house following an angle</term> of an angle, it signifies the arrival of many evils. For he will cause the greatest dangers and the ruin of the family inheritance. Frequently, if no benevolent star positioned in a good place of the birth chart joins him with a strong radiation, and if he receives the rays of a waxing Moon, he creates <term>biothanatos; those who die a violent death</term> <note>original: βιοθάνατος</note>. But if Saturn is positioned in the degree of the Ascendant by night, the one who has him so will be hindered by the greatest ailments and always weighed down by great labor. For some, he will give activities around water, but in such a way that they are always worn down and oppressed by laborious lifestyles.

**II**  In the second house from the Ascendant, Saturn causes grave illnesses and the greatest upheavals. He is also a destroyer of wife and children, and a stirrer of great and frequent crowds; he also dissipates the paternal and maternal wealth. He makes the one who is born slower in all actions, and for some, he ordains perpetual physical infirmities. If, with Saturn so positioned, Mars is in any angle of the birth chart and looks upon the Sun via a <term>quadrate; a 90-degree angle</term> or <term>diameter; a 180-degree opposition</term>, or regards a waxing Moon in a similar way, it will produce miserable, poor, and destitute people who must commit their bodies to daily labor. But if he is in this place during the day, he will give increases to the inheritance slowly and step by step. He renders these people hidden, reclusive, and poor in spirit, always denying that they possess anything. For some, however, he grants the means of life from aquatic activities or from businesses involving liquids.

**III** In the third house from the Ascendant, Saturn makes people lazy, slow, and seeking no inheritance of wealth. If he is in this place with Mercury and the Moon, he makes people malicious in their foolishness, tossing out sacrilegious words against divinity, and always losing their inheritance,

### BOOK THREE.

...but these are people whom no prosperous outcome will follow in the future. If, however, with Saturn positioned this way, <term>Mars; ♂</term> <note>original: "♂ ratione"</note> joins him by any calculation, he will create accusers, sycophants, and those who are evil, malevolent, envious, and malicious, and who always perish by a wretched death.

<margin>IV</margin> In the fourth place from the <term>horoscopus; the ascendant or rising sign</term>, if Saturn is positioned <term>partiliter; specifically by degree</term>—that is, in the <term>I M C; the Imum Coeli or "Bottom of the Sky"</term> <note>The lowest point of the chart, representing foundations, home, and the father.</note>—and if he holds this place during a daytime birth, he will make men greedy for money and keepers of gold and silver. However, if he is in this place during a nocturnal birth, he dissipates the paternal inheritance and causes the early death of the father; he will also cause severe illnesses, cold shivers of the body, and make the person always infamous in their weak old age. But if the <term>Moon; ☽</term> looks upon him from a square or diameter <note>A "square" aspect is 90 degrees; a "diameter" or opposition is 180 degrees. Both were considered stressful or difficult alignments.</note>, or if she herself is in the same part where he is positioned, he will cause sterility of children and force the native to adopt the children of others, or make him a guardian of orphans; and from hidden pains, he deforms the person with the vice of perpetual ill-health. He quickly makes the mother of the native a widow, and through women, he inflicts heavy ailments upon the native, and causes the stomach to be exhausted by perpetual pains and many anxieties.

<margin>V</margin> In the fifth place from the ascendant, if Saturn is there during a daytime birth, he will create kings and leaders, and bestows the greatest insignias of power. If, with Saturn so positioned, the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is found in the degree of the ascendant, and Saturn receives the conjunction of a waxing Moon, he grants perpetual happiness and decrees the ornaments of the highest powers. If, however, with Saturn so positioned, it is not the Sun but <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> in the ascendant, he will make magistrates of lesser rank, and those to whom the governance of individual cities is entrusted; he will make them masters of a very great inheritance, so that they can sustain others from their own wealth. But if neither the Sun nor Jupiter is in the ascendant, but Saturn only receives the conjunction of a waxing Moon while positioned in the fifth place, he will give substance and inheritances; yet these men will frequently be without a wife, or joined in marriages unworthy of them. If Saturn holds this place of the birth chart by night, in the progress of age, he assigns a portion of happiness to the man through some small lordship, but makes his youth inconsistent; he also demonstrates the man to be slow and lazy in all his acts. For some, however, if a waning Moon joins him, he causes them to lose their inheritance and to waste away whatever was previously acquired through a miserable tearing-apart of their resources.

<margin>VI</margin> In the sixth place from the ascendant, Saturn positioned there dissipates the entire inheritance. For he is always badly positioned in that place. He also causes illnesses, especially if a waning Moon joins him, or if a waning Moon regards him through a diameter, or if she is square to him while waning. For he will make men unhappy, infamous, and wanderers—those, namely, who can never stay in one place. If Mars looks upon Saturn so positioned, either from a square or diameter, or if he is in the same sign with him, he will cause hidden bodily pains, or make them <term>phthisical; suffering from consumption or tuberculosis</term>, or dysenteric; and if the radiation of no benevolent star mitigates them so positioned, he will cause those who are born to perish unhappily from these ailments.

<margin>VII</margin> In the seventh place from the ascendant—that is, positioned specifically in the <term>occasus; the setting point or descendant</term>—if he is a morning star, namely in a daytime birth, he will be good and decrees the greatest substance for men; but only then, when they have entered the threshold of old age. For so positioned, he bestows the greatest length of life and makes them keepers of money, but he indicates hidden pains of the bodies. For he makes <term>hemorrhoidals; those suffering from hemorrhoids</term>, or those contracted by the pain of the nerves. If, however, he is an evening star in this place, he causes fistulas around the anus, and in a similar way, hemorrhoids; especially if Mars looks upon him so positioned by any radiation. He also makes men <term>rheumatic; suffering from fluid imbalances or joint pain</term>, and those in whom abscesses frequently grow, and whom the misfortunes of wives always strike, crushed by the heavy bitterness of grief.

<margin>VIII</margin> In the eighth place from the ascendant, if Saturn is placed there by day, with the passage of time, he bestows increases of inheritance; for some indeed, if positioned in this place in a sign of Mars, or in the <term>bounds; specific degree-subdivisions</term> of Mars, he decrees money from the deaths of others. If, however, he is positioned in this place by night, he will cause the overthrow of the inheritance, especially if the Moon looks upon him with a square or diametrical radiation. It is also bad if, with Saturn so positioned, the Moon is positioned in his house <note>The signs of Capricorn or Aquarius</note> and looks upon him with preceding radiations. But if the Moon is so positioned with Saturn, and Mars looks upon them from any part by any radiation, he will create <term>biothanatos; those who die by violence or unnatural means</term>. If similarly, Jupiter, <term>Venus; ♀</term>, the Moon, and Saturn, are positioned as we have said and look upon each other with favorable radiation, he will make them good men of good life and reputation; but...

->JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS<-

...always makes the wife's affections unstable; however, a good trine <note>original: "radiatio trigonica" — an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> or sextile <note>original: "hexagona" — an aspect of 60 degrees, also considered favorable.</note> radiation is beneficial.

<margin>IX</margin>
If <term>Saturn; ♄</term> is positioned in the ninth place from the <term>horoscopus; the Ascendant</term> during a daytime birth, he will create famous magi <note>In this context, "magi" refers to practitioners of high magic or esoteric wisdom.</note>, or renowned philosophers, or priests of temples who are always highly distinguished in the study of magic. Depending on the nature of the zodiac signs, he also creates <term>haruspices; diviners who read entrails</term>, prophets, and astrologers <note>original: "mathematicos" — in the Roman world, this term specifically referred to those who calculated horoscopes.</note> who always shine with true interpretations, and whose responses are given as if by the very authority of the divine. He makes some persist forever in the worship of temples, and sometimes makes them leaders of religions and divine interpreters of dreams; he also frequently produces "long-haired" philosophers <note>original: "philosophos capillatos" — a reference to the traditional ascetic appearance of certain Greek philosophical schools.</note>. But if he is positioned in this place during a night birth, he will cause the anger of the gods and the hatred of emperors, especially if the <term>Moon; ☽</term> brings her waning light <note>original: "minuto lumine"</note> toward him by any calculation. The gods or the Emperor decree even greater evils for one born this way if <term>Mars; ♂</term> looks upon Saturn and the Moon from any direction. However, these effects are mitigated if a ray from <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> reaches him from a favorable place, and if Saturn is in his own <term>bounds; Egyptian terms</term>, or in the house of Jupiter or the <term>Sun; ☉</term>, or in his own <term>exaltation; height</term>, or if he is joined by a trine radiation from Jupiter.

<margin>X</margin>
If Saturn is positioned in the tenth place from the horoscopus—that is, specifically in the <term>M C; Medium Coeli or Midheaven</term>—he will create Emperors, generals, and praetorian prefects. If Saturn is thus positioned in the places where he is exalted, and the Sun is positioned in the degree of the horoscopus while Saturn (as we said before) is in the Midheaven during a daytime birth, he will make men honorable and of upright character: farmers, but wealthy ones, whose possessions always lie near the sea, rivers, or forests. He will also grant the greatest wealth, great glory, and inheritances from elder persons—especially if, with Saturn so positioned, the Sun joins him with no radiation. But if Saturn looks back while so positioned with a very strong conjunction, he will provide these things we mentioned to a lesser degree. However, if he is found in the Midheaven during a night birth, he decrees misfortunes and causes the loss of the paternal inheritance; he will deny marriage and children, especially if he is found in a malevolent sign, place, or bounds. But if a benevolent star looks upon Saturn so positioned at night with a good radiation—that is, Jupiter or <term>Venus; ♀</term>—he grants to some extent those things we just said were denied.

<margin>♄ by night in the angles.</margin>
But specifically, the star of Saturn positioned during a night birth in any of the <term>angles; cardines</term> <note>The four most powerful points of the chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> decrees the greatest evils for the nativity. For he destroys the wife, strikes down the children, and always imposes the bitter pains of bereavement. If, when so positioned, he receives a conjunction from a waning Moon, the one who has Saturn thus will be so burdened by the weight of poverty that he will scarcely have the nourishment for daily life—especially if the Moon, positioned in a feminine sign and failing in light, joins herself to Saturn. But if Saturn, so positioned, receives the rays of a waxing Moon, he decrees an inequality of life, so that the course of life for the one who has Saturn thus is not consistent, but always turns with changing diversity. If, however, the star of <term>Mercury; ☿</term> associates with Saturn when so positioned, he will give the greatest sharpness of heart and a long substance of life—especially if Mercury is the lord of the birth chart <note>original: "dominus geniturae"</note> or the giver of life. But if he is opposed to the lord of the birth chart or the giver of life, he subtracts thirty years from the years that were decreed. He also decrees even greater evils whenever he is placed against the lord of the birth chart, whom the Greeks call the <term>oikodespotes; οἰκοδεσπότην</term> <note>The "ruler of the house" or the planet that governs the entire chart.</note>; that is, if he is positioned against the giver of life—especially if the Sun looks upon him from a square or diameter radiation. For if he is so placed, he will create paralytics, the ridiculed, hunchbacks, dwarfs, the bent-over, hermaphrodites, and whatever is similar to these. He decrees these things according to the nature and substance of the zodiac signs. But if, with Saturn so positioned, the Moon moves away from him and joins with Mars—specifically in nocturnal charts—he will create the insane, lunatics, melancholics, and the weak. If Saturn is so positioned in a nocturnal birth and the Moon departs from him at the very tip of her waning horn, he will create consumptives <note>original: "phthisicos" — those suffering from wasting diseases like tuberculosis.</note>.

<margin>XI</margin>
If Saturn is positioned in the eleventh place from the horoscopus, he decrees moderate goods. When he has granted something malignant, he will place the native in the same status and order in which his father was previously placed, but only after the thirtieth year of age; for before that time, whatever he seeks, he will lose. Nor will he be able to attain dignity or inheritance unless the first thirty-year span has passed.

<margin>XII</margin>
If Saturn is positioned in the twelfth place from the horoscopus, he decrees tumults, dangers of speech, or dangers on account of slaves, and he constrains with servitude anyone who has him so placed in their birth chart. He will also cause the greatest illnesses and significant health problems—especially if, with Saturn so positioned, the Moon joins him from any direction, and if even...

->BOOK THREE.<-

...even if a benevolent star <note>A "benevolent star" refers to the "benefic" planets, Jupiter or Venus, which were believed to bring good fortune.</note> has been positioned in the <term>angles; cardines</term> <note>The "angles" or "pivots" are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart. For if <term>Saturn; ♄</term> is so positioned, and a benevolent star is found in any angle of the birth chart, these evils we have mentioned are mitigated to some extent. All these things will be milder and lighter if Saturn is found in this way during a daytime birth; however, they will be stronger and more intense if he occupies this place in a nocturnal birth chart. But in all these places where Saturn is positioned, diligently inquire after his "portion," so that you may find in which place and in which borders his <term>dodecatemorion; twelfth-part</term> <note>original: "δυοδεκατημόριον" — a calculation that divides each zodiac sign into twelve 2.5-degree segments to find a more specific planetary influence.</note> is located, so that from that and its borders, you may find the full power of Saturn.

## THE DECREES OF JUPITER THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL CELESTIAL STATIONS. Chapter IV.

<margin>The first station of Jupiter.</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is specifically positioned in the degree of the <term>horoscopus; the Ascendant</term> <note>The "horoscopus" is the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, especially in those signs in which he rejoices, or in his own houses, or even in his own borders, or in his <term>exaltation; altitudo</term>, he will always make men noble, glorious, and great, such as governors of cities. According to the scale of the birth chart, he makes them good, charming, benevolent, joyful, and wealthy—especially if he is found in the degrees of the Ascendant during the day, and if no malevolent star <note>A "malevolent star" refers to the "malefic" planets, Saturn or Mars.</note> regards him from any side while so positioned. For if malevolent stars regard Jupiter in this position with a hostile radiation <note>original: "radiatione" — an aspect or geometrical relationship between planets.</note>, everything that Jupiter has decreed is for the most part diminished. If, however, he is found in the degree of the Ascendant during the night, he will cause the person to be the first-born among brothers, or those born before him will die in the meantime; or he will separate and establish the person in distant regions and places, so that he himself may have the leadership in the paternal house. He also causes the person to be well-nourished and places the parents in the greatest happiness. But if, with Jupiter so positioned at night, a malevolent star resists him, it dissipates all the paternal and maternal substance. However, Jupiter placed in the angles of the birth chart will always either cause the person to be the first-born, or will cause the death of the elder brothers so that he himself (as I said above) may alone have leadership in the father's house. If, while Jupiter is in the Ascendant by day or night, the waxing <term>Moon; ☾</term> joins him by any radiation, he will make the greatest administrators, rulers of cities, and those often put in charge of the greatest affairs.

<margin>II</margin>
In the second place from the Ascendant, Jupiter decrees inheritances from strangers, and will cause the person to be adopted by outsiders. He will grant the lordship of great noble estates and vast possessions if, with Jupiter so positioned, <term>Mercury; ☿</term> is also well-placed and joins him with a good radiation. But if, with Jupiter so positioned, he is in the company of Saturn <note>The Latin text here mentions Saturn twice ("in societate ♄ scilicet ♂ uel ♄"), likely a scribal error or emphasizing Saturn's restrictive influence alongside Mars.</note>—that is, if <term>Mars; ♂</term> or Saturn regards him from any part—the person will frequently change his status, and will be transferred from good circumstances to bad. And whoever has Saturn thus will be changeable with various diversities throughout his entire life, such that at one moment he abounds in riches, and at another he is weighed down by the burden of poverty.

<margin>III</margin>
In the third place from the Ascendant, Jupiter is neither good nor bad, but is always composed with an even moderation; so that sometimes the patrimony of such persons is dissipated, and yet at other times unexpected riches are bestowed upon them.

<margin>IIII</margin>
In the fourth place from the Ascendant during a daytime birth—that is, in the <term>Midheaven; M.C.</term> <note>original: "Medium Coeli" — although traditionally the 10th house, Firmicus here aligns the fourth "angle" with high-status careers.</note>—Jupiter makes the greatest of men: judges, lawmakers, interpreters of the law, or legal experts. He also makes lovers and breeders of livestock (depending on the quality of the signs), messengers of kings, generals, or judges, and those to whom the care and anxiety of the first public postal services <note>original: "cursus publici" — the state-run courier and transportation system of the Roman Empire.</note> are mandated; those who, by public order of princes, generals, or judges, are sent here and there with frequent travel. He will also make them known to princes, assigned to public acts, and those who commit themselves to the protection of the gods and seek remedies from the gods, and who demonstrate the direct path to others by frequent signs. Furthermore, many who have Jupiter thus can foresee the future, and they frequently hold the greatest honors in temples. Others, according to the quality of the signs, find treasures. For Jupiter positioned in this way always decrees a happy old age until death. If, however, Jupiter is so constituted and is placed in diameter <note>An "aspect" of 180 degrees, known as an opposition.</note> to the <term>Sun; ☉</term>, he makes the person noble and glorious, but his patrimony will be dissipated around the middle of his life, only to be gathered again later. Moreover, he who has this placement will be slower regarding sexual intercourse with women and separated from the affections of his children. If he is found thus during a night birth, he will make men of mediocre substance, though he will render them even happier through the passage of time.
