V. When <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the fifth place <note>The 5th House, traditionally called the "Place of Good Fortune," was associated with children, creativity, and pleasure.</note> from the <term>horoscopus; ascendant</term>, he decrees great increases in prosperity. For he makes whoever is born under this sign honored in public magistracies, especially if he is found in his own <term>houses; domicilia</term>, his <term>borders; fines</term> <note>These are specific degrees within a zodiac sign that belong to a particular planet, also known as "terms."</note>, his <term>exaltation; altitudo</term>, or in the house of the <term>Sun; ☉</term> <note>The house of the Sun is Leo.</note>. But if, with Jupiter so positioned, <term>Mars; ♂</term> joins him with a favorable <term>aspect; radiatione</term> <note>Astrologers believed planets influenced each other by "beaming" light at specific angles (aspects).</note>, he will create leaders who possess the power of life and death. If Jupiter is positioned this way without Mars, but <term>Venus; ♀</term> and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> join him from any direction, he will create financial stewards for kings. But if, without any of these, Venus joins him alone from any direction, he will make people wealthy and adorned with graceful success. For if, as we said above, he is positioned with Mars, the person who has this will always be distinguished by royal power, and his judgments will be carried out as if divine teachings were being brought forth by the men joined to him. Furthermore, the person with this placement will have a strong body and sturdy bones. And if he receives the conjunction of a waxing Moon in her <term>course; uecto</term>, he will produce men of an almost divine and immortal substance. 

However, it will always be necessary to observe, when Jupiter is so placed, in what course the Moon is moving toward him. For this calculation is difficult to gather. If the Moon—leaving the South and moving toward the North—joins Jupiter with a waxing and full light while Jupiter is in the fifth place from the ascendant and in those signs in which he <term>rejoices; gaudet</term>, or in his own houses, or in his exaltation, and provided it is a daytime birth, he will create unconquered Emperors who hold the steering oars of the entire world. This is especially true if, with Jupiter so positioned in signs where he rejoices or is exalted, the Sun joins him in a <term>trine; trigonica</term> aspect <note>A trine is a harmonious aspect of 120 degrees.</note>. For during the day, Jupiter rejoices when adorned by the Sun's light, especially if he is positioned in his <term>morning rising; matutino ortu</term>. 

But if Jupiter, so positioned as we described, receives a waning Moon, he will make men of honorable character, raised up by the grace of moderate dignity, upon whom the burden of poverty never falls. If Jupiter is so positioned, and without any conjunction of the <term>winds; uentorum</term> <note>This refers to the planetary latitude or the "inclination" of the planet's path.</note> we mentioned, the waxing Moon joins him by a simple aspect, he will make administrators, consulars, and frequently even regular <term>consuls; consules ordinarios</term> <note>The highest elected political office in Rome; "ordinary" consuls were those who gave their names to the year.</note>, especially if it is a daytime birth. 

If <term>Mercury; ☿</term> joins him in a partnership of light, he decrees long years and a very long lifespan; he will also grant children of both sexes, or twins, especially if he is the <term>Lord of the Birth; dominus geniturae</term> <note>The planet with the most influence over the entire chart.</note>, or the lord of the part of the ascendant, or the lord of that sign in which the Lord of the Birth is positioned. But if, in a nocturnal birth, he is positioned opposite the <term>Giver of Life; datore uitae</term> <note>The Hyleg, or planet responsible for determining the length of life.</note> (<margin>Jupiter does not rejoice in nocturnal births.</margin> for Jupiter does not rejoice in nocturnal births), he takes away twelve years from whatever lifespan was decreed. 

Furthermore, if in a nocturnal birth, Mercury, Venus, or the Moon show themselves to him in an adverse course, he will cause the person born then to be entangled in the greatest vices, according to the nature and substance of the signs. For if positioned in <term>human signs; humanis signis</term> <note>Signs depicting humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius.</note>, he will make them lustful and perverse with insane desire regarding their loves, doing things that women are accustomed to doing. But in <term>four-footed signs; quadrupedibus signis</term> <note>Signs depicting animals: Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, and Capricorn.</note>, he will make them hunters and lovers of wild beasts, whom the wilderness of the woods always delights, and who are entangled in constant labors. In <term>earthy signs; terrenis</term>, he will make them herbalists and those wishing to know more than the substance of human nature allows. In <term>watery signs; aquosis</term>, he will make them fishermen and those whose livelihood depends on rivers, the sea, or marshes—certainly hard-working men, often living by these crafts. 

But if Jupiter is so positioned in a nocturnal birth and those we mentioned are resisting him, and the Moon moves away from him, he will make an unstable life, for the person who has this will fall into frequent miseries. But he will be tempered from this evil to some extent if, while the Moon moves away, Venus joins with a favorable aspect. But if Jupiter is so positioned and the Moon moving from him has no conjunction with any star, he decrees the greatest misfortunes, labors, and miseries. However, if with Jupiter so positioned, the Moon moves away and, as if fleeing, throws herself into the rays of Mars by a <term>square; quadratum</term> <note>A challenging aspect of 90 degrees.</note> or <term>opposition; diametrum</term> <note>A challenging aspect of 180 degrees.</note>, he will create those who die a violent death <note>original: "biothanatos"</note>, according to the natural form and substance of the sign. For if Mars regards the Moon moving away from Jupiter by the opposition aspect we mentioned in a nocturnal birth, he will cause brawls, dangers, and always great contests with inferiors. Whence, by night in this sign, Jupiter frequently decrees bad hardships and calamities.

For he will cause the newborns to frequently be <term>exposed; exponi</term> <note>A reference to the Roman practice of "exposure," where unwanted infants were left in public places.</note>, especially if, being positioned in the sixth place, he is himself the lord of that sign in which the ascendant is located, or in which the <term>Midheaven; M C</term> <note>original: "Medium Coeli," the highest point in the sky at the time of birth.</note> is positioned; especially if it is a nocturnal birth, and if he regards the Sun, <term>Saturn; ♄</term>, or Mars by an opposition; and if, so positioned, the Moon is waning from a square aspect...

### BOOK THREE

<margin>The sixth place is destructive.</margin>
...if he sees the <term>Moon; ☽</term> in a <term>square aspect; quadrato</term> <note>A square aspect (90 degrees) was traditionally considered a stressful or challenging relationship between two planets.</note>, or if he is in the same <term>zodiac sign; signo</term> with a waning Moon. But if he is positioned so that he does not receive the light of a waxing Moon through the harmful <term>aspect; radiatione</term> of some malefic star, the things we have mentioned are mitigated to some extent. In such cases, he produces goldsmiths, or those who decorate garments with woven gold, and sometimes silversmiths. Nevertheless, even if he has bestowed these arts, he destroys them through frequent and sudden reversals. For the sixth place possesses its own inherent quality of malice; whatever star is in that place will always borrow the greatest strength from the vice of the location to decree evils.

<margin>VII</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the seventh place from the <term>ascendant; horosc.</term>—that is, in the <term>descendant; occasu</term> <note>The seventh house represents the setting sun, partnerships, and open enemies.</note>—equally in a day-birth <term>chart; genitura</term>, he will make people affluent and wealthy, and he decrees the spans of a long and blessed old age. However, in a night-birth, he mostly troubles the area of children and the spouse. For in that case, it is necessary that the individual loses a most dear and obedient wife, and sees a miserable death for a beloved son or daughter. If, however, he is found in that place in a birth chart by night, the one who has him thus will obtain increases in his inheritance as he grows older; he will be of moderate means, yet with enough resources so that nothing is lacking for living well.

<margin>VIII</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the eighth place from the ascendant, he frequently undermines the inheritance and creates the greatest enemies; he often stirs up seditions among the people and makes individuals occupied with malicious ages of life. He also makes people ignoble, rejoicing in foolish animosity, and perverted—those whose madness even proceeds all the way to insanity—especially if, with Jupiter so positioned, a malefic star occupies any <term>angle; cardinem</term> <note>The "angles" (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses) are the strongest points in a chart.</note> of the birth chart. But if, while positioned in that place, he either has <term>Mercury; ☿</term> with him or Mercury regards him with a <term>trine aspect; trigonica radiatione</term>, and a waxing Moon joins him with a good aspect, he will make either governors for kings, or accountants, or those to whom the power of making proclamations is granted; however, these people always die in their early years.

<margin>IX</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the ninth place from the ascendant, and if it is a day-birth, he will make the person born one who foretells whatever is to come, and he always renders them an interpreter of the gods. Some even obtain priesthoods. For others, he causes some gift to be conferred from the temples; but occasionally he also causes losses and fevers of the body and mind. If, however, he is positioned in that place by night, he always makes people who dream entirely false things; those who frequently lie about the gods, and those who promise themselves some hope from the "flowers of the gods" <note>This may refer to specific ritual offerings or botanical omens.</note>, and who consider themselves to be especially tormented in their lives because of this.

<margin>X</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the tenth place from the ascendant—that is, in the <term>Midheaven; MC</term> <note>The 10th house (Medium Coeli) is the highest point in the chart, representing career, reputation, and public standing.</note>—equally by day, he will make leaders of public business, the ten foremost of the greatest men, and those upon whom the highest honors are conferred by the people. He makes them famous, and those who always wish to exert themselves for the sake of display, though it renders them luxurious in their lives. He makes some handle the affairs of great men or emperors. Others he will make "crowned" throughout their whole lives <note>This likely refers to winning athletic or civic crowns, symbols of high achievement.</note>. He decrees the greatest strokes of luck when positioned thus, provided no malefic star positioned in the Midheaven resists him. But if a malefic star does resist Jupiter while he is in the Midheaven, whatever dignity, honor, or wealth was bestowed on them in their early age is all diminished, scattered, and utterly overturned in later life, unless the descendant (the seventh place from the ascendant) is protected by the omen of another benevolent star. If, however, he is positioned in the tenth place by night, he makes them indeed honorable in character, but those who are quickly deceived, and whose inheritance perishes and flows away through frequent and swift dissipation.

<margin>XI</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the eleventh place from the ascendant by day, he decrees the greatest happiness and bestows large riches. He also gives the most famous powers: he decrees the <term>fasces; fasces</term> <note>Bundles of rods symbolizing the power of Roman high magistrates.</note> and proconsular command, if the <term>Sun; ☉</term> and <term>Venus; ♀</term> join him with a good aspect; and if the Moon, moving away from the South while Jupiter is positioned in the North, joins him while full—that is, if she is carried toward him in such a course as we described in the fifth place. However, all these things are diminished and lose their efficacy if he is so positioned in a night-birth. But if <term>Mars; ♂</term> or <term>Saturn; ♄</term> is contrary to him when so positioned, placed in a strong location of the birth chart, he will make them rejoice in great and powerful successes and be refined with the greatest riches; but everything—whatever honors or dignities were conferred upon them—he will change through the incursion of miseries and unhappiness.

<margin>XII</margin>
If <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is positioned in the twelfth place <note>The 12th house was traditionally the "Place of Bad Spirit," associated with hidden enemies and imprisonment. Firmicus Maternus uniquely suggests Jupiter can overcome these themes here.</note> from the ascendant, he decrees the greatest happiness. He makes them powerful over their enemies and those who deter them with frequent power, especially if a malefic star occupies the ascendant to the degree. # THE DECREES OF MARS THROUGH EACH
->house; Chapter V.<-

<margin>
The first house
of Mars.
</margin>
<term>Mars; ♂</term> positioned exactly in the <term>ascendant; horosc.</term> <note>The first house, representing the self, physical appearance, and vitality.</note> in a night-birth and in masculine signs will create military men. However, if he is positioned exactly in the ascendant as a morning star <note>Rising before the sun.</note> without the <term>aspect; radiatione</term> of Jupiter, he will create overly generous men, wishing to give away more than the substance of their inheritance allows, so that they appear wasteful; but they always make all their actions known through public reasoning. But if by night the ascendant is located in the <term>domicile; domicilio</term> of Mars <note>A sign ruled by Mars, such as Aries or Scorpio.</note>—specifically in a masculine sign—and Mars is found in that same sign (the ascendant) with Jupiter exactly in the same sign or looking upon him with a solid aspect, he will create leaders of wars to whom the entire army is committed. He will render them masters of life and death, whose arrival cities or provinces always greatly dread; they will be happy, brave, and serious, and their anger will always be expressed with great indignation. Yet such a placement does not permit one to love a spouse or children with dear affection. By day, however, if he is found exactly in the ascendant, he creates cunning, bold, furious, and wandering people, but unstable in all things: whatever they dare to do, they can complete by no reason; rather, whatever they have obtained always slips from their hands. They also dissipate the inheritances of those who have Mars so placed. They lose all the substance of life, even wives and children, and nothing of the paternal substance is reserved for them, but these things perish in the first stage of life. If, however, Jupiter looks upon Mars—who is himself positioned in his own domicile, or in his <term>exaltation; altitudine</term>, or in his <term>bounds; finibus</term>—through a <term>trine aspect; trigonica radiatione</term> <note>A favorable 120-degree aspect.</note>, or if he is exactly with him, his evils are mitigated from every side. But I also know, as I have found in many birth charts, that with Mars positioned in the ascendant, many who were given into exile administered the republic well and strenuously and were well-deserving of it.

<margin>II</margin>
Mars positioned in the second house from the ascendant, if found in this place by day, decrees the greatest evils and great misfortunes, especially if he is positioned in a morning rising. For he will cause one to be alienated from parents and from one's own home, and to always wander in foreign lands. But sometimes they will not have the necessities of life. If, however, he is found so by night, he makes soldiers or athletes; but he is accustomed to easily deceive even these through a continuation of dangers. Dangers will be present in a similar way unless Jupiter and Venus join him in a good aspect, as we said above.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

<margin>Mars does not overturn his own house.</margin>
But if <term>Mars; ♂</term> is positioned in his own house at the setting <note>The 7th House, or "Occasus," which represents the western horizon where stars set.</note> and looks upon it by diameter <note>In opposition, or 180 degrees apart.</note>, he will not cause a <term>violent death; biothanatos</term> <note>original: "biothanatū"; from the Greek for "violent death."</note>. For though Mars normally overturns his own house, in this case he merely makes them <term>short-lived; oligochronios</term> <note>original: "ὀλιγοχρονίους"</note>, provided the <term>Ascendant; horosc.</term> and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> have not been protected by the guard of <term>Jupiter; ♃</term>. If, however, the Ascendant is not in the house of Mars, he renders them short-lived, especially if the Moon—established in her full light—has looked upon the Ascendant or the <term>Midheaven; MC</term> by a square or diameter aspect. But generally, Mars established in the seventh place from the Ascendant—that is, in the setting, by both day and night—causes violent deaths; and this varies according to the quality of the zodiac signs. However, he decrees this evil more strongly and more clearly in foreign signs <note>The Latin text here reads "lignis" (woods), likely an OCR error for "signis" (signs), which is standard for astrological houses.</note>. For if he is found in this place, then he causes pains and lacerations of the body, and either casts the person down from heights or kills them; or he crushes those placed in prison and chains with perpetual and deadly calamities. In nocturnal births, however, he will cause pains and fevers arising from all activities; he frequently inflicts wounds from iron, and causes those very wounds to be cured by the fiery burning of <term>cauteries</term> <note>Hot irons used in ancient medicine to sear wounds or prevent infection.</note>. He also causes hidden and immense bodily pains, especially when he himself is the Lord of Times, or has possessed the time-periods divided for him by the full Moon. But if, with Mars established in the seventh place, <term>Saturn; ♄</term> is likewise in the Ascendant or the Midheaven, and the full Moon carries light to Mars, or the waning Moon to Saturn, misfortunes of great evils and deadly calamity are decreed. For then come accusations, then chains, then prisons, then condemnations, and then capital sentences are brought against the person. For they are either thrown to wild beasts, or cast from precipices, or crushed by a building collapse, or torn apart by domestic plots, or killed by bandits, or perish in a shipwreck. But these things are decreed according to the nature and quality of the signs. For if Mars is established in earthly signs, he will cause one to be thrown to wild beasts; in solid signs, to be crushed by a collapse or cast from precipices; in watery signs, to be submerged in a shipwreck; but established in human signs <note>Signs depicting humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius.</note>, he causes one to perish by the sword. If the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is in diameter to him, or with him, or in another angle of the birth chart, the person is to be burned alive; so that in every way, established in this place, Mars destroys the person with miserable calamity and the mournful atrocity of life. But before 
<margin>Mars in the 7th persecutes the place of the spouse and children.</margin>
the final day of life, whoever has Mars in the seventh house of their birth chart will have their actions driven by fire, iron, violence, torments, or homicides. Moreover, Mars established in the seventh house most vehemently persecutes the place of the spouse and children.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the eighth house from the Ascendant, Mars either denies the resources of inheritances, or for those who possess an inheritance, he causes it to be lost through a miserable <term>proscription</term> <note>The public identification and condemnation of enemies of the state, whose property was then confiscated.</note>. But if he has the Sun and Moon in diameter, he decrees blindness with the eyes extinguished. Established alone in this sign, he will cause poverty, distress, fevers, turmoils, seditions, and dangers. But if, with Mars thus established, the Moon is in the <term>succession; anaphora</term> <note>The house immediately following an angle; here referring to the 2nd House.</note> of the Ascendant—that is, in the second place from the Ascendant—and Jupiter joins himself to them by no radiation but is instead distant from them and does not see the Ascendant, Mars causes a violent death, according to the nature and substance of the signs. For in human signs, as we said, if he is established, the person will be killed by men with a sword, or will be cut off by pirates, or bandits, or household enemies. Therefore, whoever has Mars thus will either kill or be struck by the sword by the sentence of a judge, having been convicted of various diverse crimes. Frequently, however, when positioned thus with the Moon, as we said, without the testimony of Jupiter or Saturn, he creates gladiators—but those who perish in the sight of the people with a cruel atrocity of death. In earthly signs, he will cause death in desert places; [in watery] signs, with this radiation of the Moon we mentioned, he causes one to be submerged in rivers, ponds, or the sea, or causes those killed by pirates to be dispersed by the waves and surges. In solid signs, he kills those who have fallen from precipices. In fiery signs, he causes them to be burned. By night, established in this sign—that is, in the eighth house from the Ascendant—he will make people cunning, dangerous, and sharp-witted. He places those who have Mars thus in public or illustrious roles; but he nonetheless decrees a violent death, or a sudden one, just as those with apoplexy are accustomed to perish. But if Jupiter looks upon Mars so positioned by any radiation, or if he is with him, these evils we mentioned are for the most part mitigated. But if Jupiter is likewise found in the Ascendant, and the Ascendant itself is in the house of Jupiter or <term>Venus; ♀</term>—which prosperous star joins itself to the radiation of Jupiter and stands against Mars as he rages with the radiation we mentioned—all these deadly calamities are for the greatest part changed. For the mournful falls and the always miserable inconveniences of misfortunes in this and other places, decreed through Mars, are changed and [grow mild].

### THE DECREES OF THE SUN THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL
### STATIONS OF THE HEAVENS. CHAPTER VI.

The <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned in the degree of the <term>Ascendant; horoscopus</term> will give difficult brothers. However, in a masculine sign, in his own house or <term>exaltation; altitudine</term>, and joined by the radiation of a benevolent star and protected by benevolent ones, he grants the insignia of great nobility. But if malevolent stars approach near the rays of the <term>Sun; ☉</term> established in the Ascendant, they mostly take away the sharpness of the eyes. 

But because we have said that he decrees the greatest happiness, we must explain everything specifically. Therefore, when the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is positioned in the degree of the Ascendant, in those parts we mentioned, he will make <term>Emperors; Imperatores</term> and Kings by day; but if his power is slightly hindered, he will make Consuls and Proconsuls, and he gives ordinary magistrates. 

If, however, <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> regards the <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned as we said, or if he is placed with him, he decrees empires and powers granted with the greatest envy and with great dangers, hindrances, fights, and difficulties. But if the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is in the Ascendant by day, established exactly in the signs we mentioned, and <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> possesses another angle of the birth, while <term>Mars; ♂</term> is exactly in the <term>Midheaven; M C</term>...

### BOOK THREE

...found, specifically in a masculine sign <note>The "masculine" signs are Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius.</note>, and if the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is also in any <term>angle; cardine</term> <note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the birth chart, full of light, or in the <term>houses following the angles; anaphoris</term> <note>Also called "succedent" houses (the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses).</note>, it will make the one who is born rule the whole world. Or, it will place him in such administration of power that his authority, even if he is not the lord or king, is nevertheless directed through the reaches of the whole world. 

But if <term>Mars; ♂</term> is in the <term>Midheaven; MC</term> <note>The highest point in the chart, representing career and public standing.</note> or in the <term>setting house; occasu</term> <note>The Descendant or 7th house.</note>, with the <term>Sun; ☉</term> and <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> positioned as we have said, and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is found with <term>Mars; ♂</term> either in the Midheaven—provided she is full of light—or in the eighth house of the birth chart, it makes those born under this sign leaders, kings, or administrators who will meet <term>violent deaths; biothanatos</term> <note>From the Greek 'biothanatos,' referring to those who die by execution, accident, suicide, or combat.</note>. Or, if they are captured for some reason, it will cause them to be laid low by an evil death, according to the nature and substance of the signs. It will also sometimes cause one to be deposed from his honors and cast down from all power. 

Even if <term>Mars; ♂</term> is not joined with the <term>Moon; ☽</term> as we described, but is found alone in the angles of the birth, or in the houses falling away from or following them <note>original: "cataphoris, aut anaphoris"</note>, with the <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned in the <term>Ascendant; horosc.</term> <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> as we said before, nonetheless those born will be leaders, kings, or administrators who will be captives, die violently, or be deposed from power with the greatest disgrace. 

But if the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is found in the degree of the Ascendant and <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> likewise possesses the Midheaven, it similarly produces kings, leaders, and very powerful administrators. If, however, with the Sun so placed, <term>Saturn; ♄</term> or <term>Mars; ♂</term> is found in the second house from the Ascendant or in the eighth, and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is found full of light in other angles, or in the second house from the Ascendant, or in the eighth with <term>Mars; ♂</term>, it makes those who are born kings, leaders, or administrators who die violently, or become exiles and captives. 

If the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is found alone in the degree of the Ascendant in the signs we mentioned (for it is proper that you remember this), and <term>Mars; ♂</term> is found in the house following the Moon, and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is established in the other angles or their following houses, it will similarly make those born kings, leaders, or administrators who die violently, or it will force them to be deprived of that honor. 

If the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is found in the degree of the Ascendant, and the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is found in the other angles of the birth, or in the houses following or falling from the angles, and <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> joins them with no <term>aspect; radiatione</term> <note>Astrological 'rays' or angles between planets.</note>, yet the star of <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> is either positioned with the <term>Sun; ☉</term> in the degree of the Ascendant or found in the other angles (or their following or falling houses), those born will possess the helm of the whole world as kings, overturning some cities and raising others. 

But if <term>Mars; ♂</term> <note>The OCR reads ♃ (Jupiter) here, but the context of "evil deaths" and the surrounding technical formulas suggest Mars is intended.</note> is so positioned and aspects <term>Jupiter; ♃</term>, or is positioned with them, or found in the angles, or established in the houses following or falling from the angles, it will cause evil deaths for those we have mentioned. It also decrees vices and illnesses according to the nature of the signs and those parts of the body which we have said are divided among the signs. 

If, with all these things arranged as we have said, <term>Saturn; ♄</term> is found in the houses following them or falling from the angles, they will not have as much empire as we described; nevertheless, it will make them men of the greatest power, or famous judges, or commanders of great legions, or tribunes—effective and terrible. However, they will not persevere in these dignities and powers; it will either make them captives, or cause them to be driven into exile, or die easily as a <term>violent death; biothanatos</term>. 

Broadly speaking <note>original: "Platicè," an astrological term meaning an aspect that is not exact by degree but occurs within the same sign.</note>, the <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned in the sign of the Ascendant will make people free-born and noble. Also, if the <term>Sun; ☉</term> is positioned broadly in the sign of the Ascendant and <term>Jupiter; ♃</term>, <term>Venus; ♀</term>, and <term>Mercury; ☿</term> are in the other angles of the birth, it will make great men whose parents experience the greatest happiness of goods, and who grow up from their earliest age in good and prosperous circumstances, so that they are always far removed from the onset of poverty. 

But if, with all these so positioned, <term>Saturn; ♄</term> aspects them from a <term>trine; trigono</term> <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered very harmonious.</note> or a <term>sextile; hexagono</term> <note>An aspect of 60 degrees, also considered favorable.</note>, or even if he is positioned alongside them, perpetual happiness is decreed for them. 

If, however, with all these positioned thus—that is, the <term>Sun; ☉</term> in the sign of the Ascendant, <term>Jupiter; ♃</term>, <term>Venus; ♀</term>, and <term>Mercury; ☿</term> in the angles, and <term>Saturn; ♄</term> in trine, sextile, or the same place with them—if he aspects <term>Mars; ♂</term> with this radiation, or is positioned with them, or sees them all from a <term>square; quadrato</term> <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, considered tense or difficult.</note> or from an <term>opposition; diametro</term> <note>An aspect of 180 degrees, the most confrontational.</note>, and joins himself to this mixture of stars, he will make the greatest judges, powerful men having the power of life and death; but also thieves, plunderers, and those who seize the property of others by the instinct of greedy desire. Nonetheless, after the greatest predations, robberies, and immense crimes, this makes them exiles or victims of a violent death.

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...if the Sun has joined with these planets, it indeed destroys the older brothers, and dissipates the substance of the individual's life, all their inheritance, and all their actions with a fatal perversion. However, the <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned in any of the <term>angles; cardinibus</term> <note>The four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the <term>birth chart; geniturae</term> will always weaken all older brothers; or whoever has this placement will be the firstborn among all his brothers, or the eldest among them.

<margin>II</margin> In the second <term>house; loco</term> <note>The 2nd house traditionally relates to wealth and personal resources.</note> from the <term>Ascendant; horoscopo</term>, the Sun positioned there makes those who seek inheritances through their own efforts, and who are pleasant and good throughout their lives. But it also makes these same people sickly and short-lived, easily hindered by various setbacks, and who are always anxious in their lives with various fears and trembling. If, however, when the Sun is positioned in this place, <term>Venus; ♀</term> or <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> look upon it with a favorable <term>aspect; radiatione</term>, either from a <term>trine; trigono</term> <note>An angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> or a <term>sextile; hexagono</term> <note>An angle of 60 degrees, also considered harmonious.</note>, or if they are placed in the same sign with it, the Sun will grant some sudden good and a significant increase in happiness. For it causes lowly and abject men to be brought to a public increase of dignity. But this is decreed for them with great labor and with the maximum of hindrance, and with a voluntary loss of inheritance. Therefore, whoever has the Sun positioned thus should desire nothing and dare nothing, knowing that with the Sun so placed, he will be unhappily hindered in all his actions.

<margin>III</margin> In the third house from the Ascendant, the Sun positioned there decrees a bad death for the father, and will make those who have it thus weak of body, but good and grave in counsel. They may be governors of cities, or those who handle public accounts, or those placed over the <term>imperial treasury; fisco</term>, or advocates for the treasury, provided that Jupiter and Venus join the Sun with a good aspect. However, they will obtain a wife and children later in life. If, indeed, in the third house of the birth chart the Sun is placed in its own <term>zodiac sign; domo</term>, or if Jupiter, Venus, or <term>Mercury; ☿</term> are there, or if the Sun is in its <term>exaltation; altitudine</term> <note>The sign where a planet's power is most highly "exalted"; for the Sun, this is Aries.</note>, or in the exaltation of Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury, it will make them religious people and worshippers of the gods. These are people who dedicate statues to the gods and perform religious consecrations, and who oversee the construction of temples by the order of princes or judges. But if placed in other signs, as we have said, the Sun results in ignoble offices in temples or some servile ministry. If, however, in the third house from the Ascendant, <term>Saturn; ♄</term> or <term>Mars; ♂</term> should join the Sun by any aspect, or if they are with it, it will make them perjurers, treacherous, and miserable due to frequent denunciations; they will be gluttons who always seek out filthy and hidden places, and who utter irreligious words against the divine, yet always burning with constant mental exhaustion.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the fourth house <note>The 4th house represents the home, family roots, and the end of life.</note> from the Ascendant, specifically <term>by degree; partiliter</term>, if the Sun is struck by any aspect from Mars and Saturn, it first decrees death for the father and makes for the overthrow of the entire family line or the ruin of the whole inheritance. For the person who has it thus, it decrees many interruptions, troubles, setbacks, and hindrances for the most part. But it will make for a good old age, such that at this stage of life, the greatest profits are conferred; but concerning his feelings for his wife, he will be unstable.

<margin>V</margin> In the fifth house <note>The 5th house relates to children, pleasure, and creativity.</note> from the Ascendant, the Sun positioned there makes people lovable, honored, and those who easily obtain everything, and to whom all things are granted through the protection of friends. But if, with the Sun thus placed, the star of Venus is present in the same sign as a companion, or joins it from a sextile, it bestows the insignia of crowns, and will decorate the person born under such a star with the <term>purple-bordered toga; prætexta ueste</term> <note>The *toga praetexta* was worn by high-ranking Roman magistrates, symbolizing political power.</note>; indeed, the greatest honors are conferred upon him by the people. Even if malevolent stars are with the Sun in the same place, they will be able to decree or perpetrate nothing evil because of the natural goodness of this house, though it will harm the children. If, however, the Sun is found alone in that place, these happinesses we mentioned will be smaller, and it will also harm the children, indicating <term>perpetual childlessness; orbitates</term>, or it decrees the greatest torments of grief from the death of children.

<margin>VI</margin> In the sixth house <note>The 6th house is traditionally associated with illness, service, and misfortune.</note> from the Ascendant, the Sun positioned there decrees many evils: for it will always cause harm and produce serious and long illnesses. But if, with the Sun so placed, Mars is found in the Ascendant, it will indeed create public roles, but it will frequently inflict wounds from iron; it will cause the father to either perish by an evil death or be condemned to an early death for some reason. But it also causes the whole substance of wealth to be lost in various ways, if, with the Sun placed in the sixth house, no star is found in the tenth house from the Ascendant—that is, in the <term>Midheaven; MC</term>. For if, with the Sun in the sixth house, any star occupies the tenth house (the Midheaven), it will make them wealthy, rich, and affluent, and those to whom the greatest happiness is conferred through paternal succession. If, however, with the Sun in the sixth house, no star is positioned in the Midheaven, but Jupiter and Venus are found with that same Sun in the sixth house, whatever...

<margin>VII</margin>
In the seventh <term>house; loco</term> <note>The 7th house, or Descendant, traditionally governs marriage, partnerships, and open enemies.</note>, the <term>Sun; ☉</term> positioned away from the <term>Ascendant; horoscopo</term> decrees the greatest vices and illnesses, especially if <term>Mars; ♂</term> and <term>Saturn; ♄</term> look upon the Sun so positioned with any <term>aspect; radiatione</term>, or if they are situated with it. For according to the nature of the malevolent star <note>In ancient astrology, Saturn and Mars were considered "malefics," or planets that naturally bring challenge.</note> that is placed with it, the Sun indicates vices and ailments. If it is Saturn, the illnesses are cold; if Mars, they are hot and fiery <note>This reflects the ancient medical theory of humors, where Saturn was associated with cold melancholy and Mars with hot bile.</note>. But if the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is found with it in the seventh house, or if with the Sun in the seventh, the Moon is positioned <term>exactly; partiliter</term> in the Ascendant or in the <term>Midheaven; M C</term> <note>The highest point of the chart, representing career and public standing.</note>, they will make men who are great, powerful, and noble, to whom the greatest powers are committed; especially if the Sun is in its own <term>house; domo</term> or its <term>exaltation; altitudine</term> <note>A sign where a planet's influence is most harmoniously amplified.</note>, or situated in the house of <term>Jupiter; ♃</term>. And if the <term>Lot of Fortune; locus fortunae</term> holds an angle, they will make emperors and kings—but ones who are good and benevolent.

They will also make leaders, powerful men, the wealthy, and strong, temperate, and effective administrators who subjugate provinces and cities. But if, while all these are positioned as we said—namely the Sun, Moon, Jupiter, and Fortune—Mars and Saturn are situated in the second house or the eighth from the Ascendant, such men lose their empires, and are deposed from their honors or administrations with a loss of dignity; or they are oppressed by enemies, adversaries, and rivals.

They may even cause these same men to bring death upon themselves with their own hands, or make them captives or exiles. If, however, in the seventh house of the <term>birth chart; geniturae</term>, or in any other angle, <term>Mercury; ☿</term> joined with <term>Venus; ♀</term> is found in that same place—whether appearing in the morning or evening—they will make learned people who achieve a great and varied knowledge of literature.

But if, with the Sun and Mercury thus positioned, Saturn joins them, they will make men who are malicious, malevolent, and very wicked; those who wish to have knowledge of "difficult" literature <note>Likely referring to occult, cryptic, or forbidden texts.</note>, or who produce such difficult writings themselves.

If, however, Mercury, Venus, and Saturn are found in a night chart, they will make stonemasons, <term>embalmers; pollinctores</term>, or undertakers, or those to whom the care of tombs is mandated. They also make cattle-drivers, ox-herds, shepherds, horse tamers, swineherds, and those similar to these, according to the nature and power of the <term>zodiac signs; signorum</term>.

And if in a nocturnal birth chart the Sun and Saturn are positioned in the seventh house, and Venus and Mercury are found in that same place, or in the twelfth or the sixth house, they will make <term>eunuchs; eunuchos</term> and <term>viragoes; uiragines</term> <note>Women who display masculine traits or take on traditionally male roles.</note>, and women who never join themselves in masculine coitus; or if they should ever join with a man, they will never conceive or give birth.

<margin>Hermaphrodites.</margin>
If, while these are thus positioned, Mars joins them by some aspect or is found with them, he will make <term>hermaphrodites; hermaphroditos</term> in whom a double nature is joined. But if, while all these are so situated, the Moon joins by some aspect or is found with them, they will make <term>archigalli; archigallos</term> <note>High priests of the goddess Cybele who famously castrated themselves in religious ecstasy.</note> and those who amputate their own virility with their own hands. They also make pimps, and those who wish to place prostitutes under their own management.

But in the sixth house, these same placements will produce the same effects when the Sun is positioned there, provided no star positioned in the Midheaven breaks the atrocity of this malice. For if any planet is found in the Midheaven while all those are situated in the sixth house, all the things we have mentioned are mitigated.

In the second house of the birth chart, or the fifth, or the eleventh, if Jupiter is found with Saturn and the Sun is positioned with them in that same place, it makes men who are malicious, malevolent, and the worst in all their actions; yet they may be advocates, legal experts, scribes, shorthand writers, or those in charge of gardens or distributors of water.

But if, with these planets positioned in the places we mentioned, Mars joins in some association or is found with them, they will be overseers of public executions and the recorders of those sentences which are brought against the lives of men; or they will be <term>military clerks; cornicularij</term> or <term>legal registrars; cōmentarienses</term> to whom the care of the condemned is committed; or jailers, guards of prisons, those entrusted with the care of public chains, or those in charge of executioners, or the executioners themselves, and those who are accustomed to tear apart condemned men with whips, and other things similar to these.

If, however, with all these things positioned as we said, Jupiter and Venus join by some aspect, or if they are found with them, they will do none of those things which we mentioned before. For no evils are decreed from this benevolent aspect of the Sun.

But joined with Jupiter and Venus, they will make <term>sacrificial priests; sacerdotes uictimarios</term>, and those who preside over sacred rites, or those who graze the sacred herds destined for religious ceremonies, or those who perform some office in the temples, or who obtain the greatest gifts from the temples. But all these stars which we have mentioned, even if positioned exactly in the twelfth house, by a similar reasoning...

<margin>VIII</margin> The Sun positioned in the eighth house from the <term>Ascendant; horoscopo</term> will cause the father to die quickly. If indeed <term>Mars; ♂</term> or <term>Saturn; ♄</term> are found with it, or are diametrically opposite to it, or joined in a <term>square aspect; quadrato</term>, they will make people who are mentally disturbed, delirious, suffering from heart ailments, or <term>frenzied; phreneticos</term>; however, these defects of health are decreed according to the nature of the <term>Signs; signorum</term> <note>The zodiac signs (Aries, Taurus, etc.) would color the specific expression of the illness.</note>. But if, with the Sun placed in the eighth house, the <term>Moon; ☽</term> is positioned diametrically opposite it, not yet having moved away from the <term>opposition; coniunctione</term> <note>original: "nondum soluta coniunctione," referring here to the full moon aspect</note> but full of light, or if it is found in a <term>conjunction; synodica</term> with the Sun in the eighth house, while Saturn and Mars are positioned diametrically opposite, either together or joined to them by a square radiation, it will cause the greatest illnesses and weaknesses. For it loads the head with malicious <term>humors; humoribus</term> <note>In ancient medicine, health was determined by the balance of four "humors" or bodily fluids.</note>, and from the persistent stagnation of these humors collected around the head, it will make people <term>epileptic; caducos</term> and <term>moon-sick; lunaticos</term>, or those who faint with constant loss of consciousness. They also cause people to utter strange words and weaken the shoulders of others with heavy loss; they inflict spots, leprosies, skin eruptions, kidney diseases, <term>consumption; phthisim</term>, and <term>dropsy; hydropem</term> upon others. Some they make <term>leperous; elephanticos</term>, others lame, others hunchbacked, others paralyzed, and for others they cause the amputation of major parts of the body. But all these things they decree according to the differences and nature of the Signs. For they cause similar things when positioned in the second house from the Ascendant, and in the sixth, the twelfth, and the eighth, as we have said.

But if, with all things positioned as we said, <term>Jupiter; ♃</term> and <term>Venus; ♀</term> join them by some radiation, or are with them, or look upon them with a <term>trine aspect; trigonica</term>, or if they join the Moon, then all these illnesses we mentioned will be of such a kind that they can be healed and cured. But even if, with the benevolent stars so placed—namely Jupiter and Venus—a malevolent star intercepts the conjunction of the approaching Moon, the defect and sickness will indeed be lifelong, but by the providence of some divinity, the bitterness of the illness will be mitigated. 

If, with all these positioned as we said, a star joins the Moon, either placed with it or in a <term>sextile aspect; hexagono</term>, it will check those illnesses we mentioned either with some remedy or with incantations, or it will free them in every way from the onset of these illnesses by these remedies, especially if the waxing Moon, or the Moon with diminished light, joins Jupiter or Venus. But if in that arrangement of stars we have explained, the Moon joins the star of Venus, and being placed with her, is radiated by benevolent stars either from a trine or sextile, they will flee to the gods for help; and they will remain there, requesting remedies from them. 

But if the Moon joins the star of Venus while Saturn, Mars, and the Moon are positioned as we said, and Jupiter and Venus are found in adverse and <term>debilitated; deiectis</term> places, they will make people insane, moon-struck, and <term>demon-possessed; dæmoniacos</term>, and those who are entangled in perpetual calamities from these vices, so that they perish by a <term>violent death; biothanata morte</term> <note>original: "biothanata morte," a Greek-derived term meaning a death by violence, execution, or suicide rather than natural causes.</note>.

<margin>IX</margin> The Sun positioned in the ninth house from the Ascendant makes makers of gods, or worshipers of divine images, or decorators of the gods, or builders of temples; or hymn-singers, and those who sing the praises of the gods with boasting and ostentation, from which they will nevertheless have honor and glory. The Sun so placed also makes the father happy, but it decrees for both them and their father various and manifold changes of life. And if a benevolent star is found in the <term>rising house; anaphora</term> <note>The house following the one mentioned, in this case, the house following the Midheaven.</note> of the Midheaven while the Sun is so positioned, the person who has this will achieve the greatest increases of happiness while situated in foreign places. But if a malevolent star is found in this place, he will suffer many inconveniences in travel, and will die abroad, removed from his fatherland with the greatest grief.

<margin>X</margin> The Sun positioned exactly in the tenth house from the Ascendant in a daytime birth—that is, in the Midheaven in its own house, or in the house of Jupiter, or in that part in which it is <term>exalted; exaltatur</term>—will make kings to whom power is handed down from the father, or leaders to whom this honor is conferred in a similar way through inherited paternal honors, or administrators, consuls, and proconsuls:

But if the Sun is positioned as we said, and Mars (♂) is absent from these locations, while Jupiter (♃) is found in the angles or in the <term>cadent houses; cataphoris</term> <note>original: "cataphoris"; these are houses that "fall away" from the powerful angles, specifically the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses.</note>, and the Moon (☽) occupies any angle of the nativity and joins herself to the rays of Jupiter while she is full of light, this will make these same kings or dukes extend their power across the breadth of the whole world.

The Sun positioned generally in the sign containing the Midheaven will make the parents noble and respectable, especially if a benevolent star regards the Sun so positioned with any ray. Even if a benevolent star is found with the Sun in that place, it will nonetheless produce great ignobility. But if a malevolent star is found in this place with the Sun, it decrees perpetual illnesses, great defects, and perpetual slavery. You must also diligently seek the Sun’s <term>twelfth-part; δυοδεκατημόριον</term> <note>original: "δυοδεκατημόριον"; a technique where each zodiac sign is divided into twelve 2.5-degree sections to refine a planet's influence.</note> and its boundaries, so that the discipline of this work does not fail you in any way.

For if positioned in <term>cardinal; tropicis</term> or <term>double; duplicibus</term> signs, she decrees widowhood and losses and lawsuits because of women, or stirred up by women. # THIRD BOOK. 67

This star <note>Venus (♀)</note> has various powers of determination, though they are difficult to fully discover. For just as an artist painter marks out the various features of limbs in images with a diversity of mixtures, and with tempered colors creates a specific bodily form by changing the physical likeness: so the combined radiation of Venus (♀) and the other stars, equally tempered by the consensus of their association, borrows a certain force in turn from the powers joined to it. It depicts the fates of men in the manner of a painting, adjusted by the moderation of this partnership, and using the substance brought to it from the heat of different fires. That what we say is true is proved by these reasons:

If Venus (♀) is positioned as we have said, and Saturn (♄) joins her by any radiation <note>original: "radiatione," referring to an astrological aspect or beam of influence</note>, she causes minds to be entangled in perverse vices and rendered useless for any necessary actions—especially if this conjunction of Venus (♀) and Saturn (♄) is found in a nocturnal <term>nativity; genitura</term> <note>A birth chart cast for a birth occurring at night.</note>. 

But if, when so positioned, favorable Jupiter (♃) joins her by aspect, the person is liberated from the onset of the preceding malice. It also bestows the greatest goods upon men; for they will achieve increases in their inheritance through their own actions, and they will be set apart from every stain of vice. This is true if, while Venus (♀) is so constituted with Jupiter (♃), the Moon (☽) does not aspect her from the <term>opposition; de diametro</term> <note>original: "de diametro," an aspect of 180 degrees.</note> by any radiation. 

But if she <note>the Moon</note> is found in opposition to Venus, she will make them infamous, lustful, or lovers of boys. Because of dishonest intercourse with women, they are usually struck by the disgrace of heavy infamy; and from incest and debauchery, grave infamies are decreed from that mixture. For they are forced to have intercourse with sisters, or stepmothers, or daughters, or brothers; yet nonetheless, from this incest, the greatest profits will come to them, or some merit of dignity is conferred. 

But always Venus (♀) placed together with the Moon (☽), or joined from a <term>square; quadrato</term> <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful.</note>, decrees the allurements of love, or the stain of infamy with a tendency toward luck, or she will involve them in bitter vices of the mind. She either makes them impure, or preposterous with lustful desire, or strikes them with heavy infamy from incestuous loves. For either, as we said above, they have intercourse with sisters, or with those outside their family, or they join two sisters to themselves in debauchery, or they will have intercourse with daughters, or with mothers, or with daughters-in-law, or with the wives of their stepsons; or they will burn with the vice of lustful desire for the wives of their brothers; or they will be joined with stepmothers, or female relatives, or sisters, or the daughters of sisters. 

If a woman has Venus (♀) positioned this way, she will be lustful and one who is entangled in promiscuous loves and pleasures. She will always be possessed by the stain of infamy and burning with incestuous loves; for she will have intercourse with her own brothers, or with her sons, or parents, or with the sons of her paternal uncles, or with the husbands of her daughters, or with paternal uncles, or stepsons, or female relatives; or she will be called to the lust of one bed with two brothers. It also makes other women desire to perform masculine acts. 

But she <note>Venus</note> does these things more strongly if, joined to the Moon (☽) by this aspect, she is in <term>tropical; tropicis</term>, <term>mutable; erraticis</term>, <term>scaly; ſquamofis</term> <note>Water signs, like Pisces or Cancer.</note>, or <term>double-bodied; biformibus</term> <note>Signs like Gemini or Sagittarius.</note> signs. These things are also stronger and more vehement if Saturn (♄) sees both of them (that is, the Moon and Venus) as we described, or even just one of the two, by opposition or square, or if he is positioned with one of them. Or if, joined in this partnership, the Moon (☽) and Venus (♀) are both positioned in the house of Mars (♂) or Saturn (♄); or if they are together in the signs of Mercury (☿), or if one of the two is placed in a sign of Mercury (☿) and aspects the other with the radiation we mentioned. 

When Venus (♀) is positioned in her evening rising, if in a nocturnal birth she joins Mars (♂) with a favorable aspect in a good sign, she decrees good increases of happiness. For she makes them powerful and glorious, and bestows the greatest insignia of power and honors, as well as the riches of wealthy estates. But if during the day Mars (♂) joins her by any aspect, he decrees the misfortunes of many and great evils. 

She rejoices by night if she joins the Moon (☽), Mars (♂), and Mercury (☿); then she ennobles men with the greatest happiness whenever she is joined with them by a good aspect in a nocturnal birth. But if Venus (♀) is with the Sun (☉) in this place of which we speak, it is established by the responses of all the wise that she will be most unjust. For Venus (♀) is badly positioned if she is placed with the Sun (☉), for she does not rejoice when associated with the [greater] luminary; instead, whatever seems evil and miserable in human affairs, she decrees all of this for men when so placed. 

However, she rejoices when positioned behind the Sun (☉), that is, as a morning star. For then, whatever good she has decreed when placed with good planets, it will grow with a more powerful increase of happiness. But if she is found to be the <term>Lady of the Horoscope; dña horoſ.</term> <note>The planet ruling the Ascendant or the entire chart.</note> and she is the mistress of the entire nativity, or if she has decreed the length of life, being positioned in good signs and favorable places of the birth chart, she bestows a very long life. ### THE DECREES OF MERCURY THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE SKY. Chapter VIII.

<margin>The first house of Mercury in the nativity.</margin>
Mercury (☿) positioned exactly in the degree of the <term>horoscope; Ascendant</term> <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, in those signs in which he rejoices in a day birth, will produce philosophers, masters of the art of grammar, geometers, and those who often treat of celestial matters: or those who are so inclined that they are able to behold the presence of the gods, or he makes experts in sacred literature. He also frequently makes orators and advocates, especially if he is found in this place, or in his own signs <note>Gemini and Virgo</note>, or in other local signs. If the Sun (☉), Saturn (♄), or Jupiter (♃) aspect Mercury (☿) so positioned in a day birth, they will produce great men, whom they crown with sacred and glorious lineages; they also produce such men to whom the greatest business of emperors may be entrusted. But if Mars (♂) aspects Mercury (☿) so positioned from a <term>square; quadrate</term> <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful.</note> or <term>opposition; diameter</term> <note>An aspect of 180 degrees.</note>, such that he is found exactly in the horoscope with him, he will cast down the one so born with a manifold continuation of evils. <margin>The ruinous conjunction of Mercury (☿) and Mars (♂).</margin> For the evils which arise from that conjunction of Mercury (☿) and Mars (♂) can neither be defined nor described. If, however, the Sun (☉) aspects Mercury (☿) so positioned from a <term>trine</term> <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very favorable.</note>, he will cause the person to be occupied with good and prosperous actions. But if Mercury (☿) is found exactly in the horoscope in a nocturnal nativity, he will make them divine in their senses, and people who always achieve everything they wish by the easiest of reasons. He will also render them honorable and serious in character; he will place them in charge of accounts, or of contracts, or of grain, or of taxes, or of businesses, or of banks, or of money-lending, or those who handle business of this sort. Thus positioned at night, he also frequently produces interpreters for emperors or for the most powerful judges; but he decrees all these things according to the difference and quality of the signs.

II. Mercury (☿) positioned in the second house from the horoscope, if he is found in a morning rising, will make men obscure, of a wicked mind, strangers to the knowledge of literature, and who are destitute of every support of life. But if in this place he is an evening star, and in a nocturnal birth, he will make money-lenders, businessmen, or those who undertake the care and management of others' affairs. If, however, he is found thus in a day birth, he will make philologists, or experts in laborious literature, and those who do not wish to compare their own nature to other men, and who even affect all things which no discipline of teaching has handed down to them; yet he makes them miserable in life, and people who are always worn out by various kinds of distress. But if some radiation of Jupiter (♃) aspects Mercury (☿) so positioned, or if he is found with him, and Jupiter (♃) joins them in a good conjunction, he causes them to be placed over great and famous positions; but they will be those who do not have principal power, and in their very actions they are subject to the power of another. He also makes them overseers of great accounts, and such men who sustain the royal resources with prompt disposition, and who have all the royal revenues and treasures committed to their trust and management. But this happiness of theirs will be ended in a short space of time, and will quickly perish as a fleeting thing.

III. Mercury (☿) positioned in the third house from the horoscope will make great priests, chief physicians, and <term>mathematicians; astrologers</term> <note>original: "mathematicos." In the 4th century, this term specifically referred to those who cast horoscopes.</note>, but those who discover by themselves and learn whatever was not demonstrated to them by the teaching of another. He will also make them sensible, happy, and those who join themselves to all actions with easy reasoning. But if Jupiter (♃) aspects Mercury (☿) so positioned from a trine or a <term>sextile; hexagon</term> <note>An aspect of 60 degrees.</note>, or if he is found with him, he will produce men of great mind and of great and divine counsel. If, however, Mars (♂) should bind himself by some radiations to Mercury (☿) and Jupiter (♃) thus positioned, he will make agents of kings, famous leaders, powerful administrators, and those to whom royal resources are entrusted: and he will render them so sharp in mind and strength that they can happily overcome all things by the virtue of their own spirit.

But if, while Mercury (☿) is so positioned, the Sun (☉) and Saturn (♄) possess the other cardines <note>The four "angles" or pivot points of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> of the nativity, and

### BOOK THREE.

[...If Mercury] looks toward [the horoscope] from a **square** or **opposition** <note>original: "de quadrato aut diametro"—aspects of 90 and 180 degrees respectively.</note>, he will produce accusers, jailers, and frequent judges. But if he is found as an **evening star** <note>original: "vespertinus"—rising after the Sun.</note> in this place, he will make goldsmiths, or gold-miners, or masters of certain hidden arts, or those who appear trained in calculation or accounting; or he will produce leaders of the wrestling schools.

<margin>V</margin>
In the **fifth house** from the horoscope <note>Known as the House of Good Fortune.</note>, if Mercury is found as a **morning star** <note>original: "matutino ortu"—rising before the Sun.</note>, he will make finders of gold and riches, and those who by their own foresight create a very great abundance of property; he also makes them overseers of the great wealth of others, and those who appear to possess divine character. Moreover, for those with Mercury so positioned, the greatest substance of life and a fertile abundance of children is decreed. But if he is found as an **evening star** in this place, the person will be able to save money by no means: rather, whatever money, gold, silver, or other noble goods are set before him, he will cause to be scattered through lavish expenditures. He will also produce businessmen and those put in charge of public accounts in any administration. Sometimes also, according to the quality of the signs, he makes teachers, geometers, or **astrologers** <note>original: "astrologos"—in this period, the term referred to both astronomers and judicial astrologers.</note> who find the course of the stars through the wisdom of calculation. He will also produce overseers and leaders of wrestling schools. But if Mercury, positioned in this place, receives a conjunction of the **increasing Moon** (☽), he causes the whole body of the man, though healthy, to be mottled with spots or entangled in diseased health, according to the nature and quality of the signs. But if the **waning Moon** joins itself to Mercury so positioned, he will entangle the man in shameful illnesses and cause him to frequently wander from the right order of living through perverse falls into madness.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the **sixth house** <note>Known as the House of Bad Fortune or Illness.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury will cause one to acquire a very great fortune for oneself, either from a learned facility of speech or legal advocacy, or from business, or from the revenues of the gods <note>Likely referring to temple management or priestly income.</note>; especially if, with Mercury so positioned, another star is found in the **tenth sign** from the horoscope <note>The Midheaven or Medium Coeli.</note>. But if in a nocturnal birth he is found as a morning star in the sixth house, he makes interpreters, fishermen, bird-catchers, or sculptors, provided that another star is found in the tenth house of the birth chart. But if he is a morning star in a nocturnal birth in the sixth house and the tenth house from the horoscope has no star, he will make them spiteful, malicious, authors of evil counsels, and thieves, and those who always desire the property of others with an envious fire of the mind, and those who rejoice in the misfortunes of others, informers, and those who pursue their own kin and neighbors with bitter hatreds—lazy, mentally blind, and those upon whom all kinds of malice are heaped. But if he is found as an **evening star** in this place, he will make them wise, serious, and critics of accounts, put in charge of banks, granaries, storehouses, tools, or businesses, from which occasions great profits are brought to them. But if, so positioned, he receives a conjunction of the **approaching Moon** (☽), he will make scribes, or those belonging to the judges, or the senate, or those who, being stationed with Emperors, have some power of speech; or those who undertake to govern the acts of their prince by their own arrangements: especially if, with the Moon so positioned, Jupiter (♃) or another star possesses the tenth house of the birth chart.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the **seventh house** from the horoscope, that is in the **setting** <note>The Descendant; the point of the western horizon.</note>, in a day birth, Mercury causes one to be entangled in heavy vices and to boil with the desires of wretched lusts. They will be excessive lovers of either boys or virgins; but these men are allotted defiled women as wives, and frequently undertake the care and protection of infant males. But this too is decreed according to the quality of the signs. For if he is found in this place in those signs in which he does not rejoice—that is, in the house of **Mars** (♂) or **Saturn** (♄), or in others in which he is humbled—he will make overseers of prostitutes and pimps, and those who are filthy with the squalor of such infamy. But if he is found in **opposition** to Mars (♂), or in the **Midheaven**, or in the setting (the seventh house) with Mars, he will cause a short life, and produce those who are consumptive, fugitives, exiles, and the condemned. But if Mercury is found in the setting with Saturn (♄) at night, he will make procurers of women, and those to whom the greatest happiness is granted from such occasions. He also makes inventors of calculation, music, shorthand, or difficult literature; he also renders the associate in this place to have frequently made **deceptive ambushers** <note>original: "Pseudenedros"—from the Greek ψευδένεδρος, meaning one who lies in wait or a treacherous person.</note>.

In the **eighth house** from the horoscope <note>The house associated with death and inheritance.</note>, if he is found as an evening star during the day in this place, he will make them sluggish, and those who dare or wish to do nothing, always hindered by laborious acts—foolish, malicious, and fit for no necessary actions. #### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

[...If Mercury] is positioned in the **house of Saturn** <note>The zodiac signs of Capricorn or Aquarius.</note>, or in those degrees, he will make the person deaf: especially if **Saturn** (♄) regards <note>original: "respexerit"—an "aspect," or geometric relationship between planets.</note> Mercury while so positioned by some radiation. But if he is found as an **evening star** <note>original: "vespertinus"—rising after the sunset.</note> in this place during a night birth, he will make them heirs to the estates of others, and those who find hidden wealth by chance. They will also be equally fortunate and blessed: yet they will be prone to vice and easily exhausted by constant illnesses. If positioned as a **morning star** <note>original: "matutinus"—rising before the sunrise.</note> in this place, he will make those born under this sign seek money and great deeds without limit; or he will make them faithful and stable authors of anxieties, commendations, acts, or legal instruments, and frequently also the possessors of others' estates.

<margin>IX</margin> In the **ninth house** <note>The "House of Journeys" or "House of God."</note> from the **horoscope** <note>The Ascendant or first house.</note>, if Mercury (☿) is positioned without the radiation of any other star, he will make the person contentious, contradictory, a **dialectician** <note>A practitioner of logical debate or philosophy.</note>, and one who professes to know things that were never taught to them by any master; they will be malicious, but unable to complete anything with effective reasoning. But if he is found as a **morning star** in this place, he will make priests, diviners, **haruspices** <note>Priests who predicted the future by inspecting the entrails of sacrificed animals.</note>, **augurs** <note>Priests who interpreted the will of the gods through the flight of birds.</note>, mathematicians, **astrologers**, and physicians, who seek their livelihood from these arts and institutions. But these effects will be stronger if he is protected by the radiation of a **benefic star** <note>original: "beneuolae stellae"—usually Jupiter or Venus.</note>; for then he will make them happy, blessed, great, powerful, and those upon whom all the insignia of happiness are conferred. But if **malefic stars** <note>original: "maleuolae stellae"—Saturn or Mars.</note> regard Mercury so positioned, or if they are found in **opposition** or **square** <note>original: "diametro aut quadrato"—aspects of 180 and 90 degrees.</note>, they will make the person irreligious, sacrilegious, temple-robbers, damnable, and condemned: those who always wander as fugitives in foreign lands, or who are oppressed by the exile of their condemnations. However, Mercury positioned as an **evening star** in this place makes priests, **magi** <note>Practitioners of magic or Persian wisdom.</note>, physicians, and craftsmen who prepare their life's livelihood from these arts; they will also have such a character that they learn for themselves what no discipline or mastery has handed down to them.

<margin>X</margin> In the **tenth house** from the horoscope, which is the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" (Medium Coeli)—the highest point of the chart, representing career and public life.</note>, if Mercury is a **morning star** in this place, he will make the person admirable and great in their actions. But if **Jupiter** (♃) regards Mercury so positioned from any side, by a **trine** or **sextile** <note>original: "trigono, uel hexagono"—harmonious aspects of 120 and 60 degrees.</note> in a daytime birth, they will be great, powerful, and handle the business of the greatest cities, emperors, or powerful men; they will be faithful, benevolent, wise, and grave. But in a nighttime birth, if **Venus** (♀) regards Mercury so positioned by any radiation, she will do the same as we showed Jupiter does in a daytime birth. If, however, **Mars** (♂) regards Mercury so positioned from any side—that is, by **square** or **opposition**—coming promotions are repelled by various kinds of offenses; and because of this, they will frequently be exiles or bear the burdens of some condemnation. But if the **Moon** (☽) joins Mercury by some radiation, he will even produce those who die a **violent death** <term>biothanathos</term><note>A technical term for a person destined for a violent or unnatural death.</note>. Mercury positioned as an **evening star** in the tenth house from the horoscope produces travels and constant changes of location; he also makes them **tax collectors** <note>original: "publicarios"—officials who managed public contracts and taxes.</note> in all their actions. But if **Saturn** (♄) regards Mercury so positioned from any side, either by **square** or **opposition**, he will cause the person to be always involved in water-based activities, and establishes their duties near the sea, rivers, or pools. He also decrees vices and health problems stemming from an abundance of **humors** <note>The bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—believed to control health and temperament.</note>.

<margin>XI</margin> In the **eleventh house** from the horoscope <note>The "House of the Good Spirit."</note>, Mercury (☿) will make the person ingenious and necessary in all actions, and those to whom the management of great accounts is committed; but he decrees even greater duties if **Jupiter** (♃) is joined by a favorable radiation.

<margin>XII</margin> In the **twelfth house** <note>The "House of the Bad Spirit," often associated with enemies and misfortune.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury (☿) will make people ingenious if they are placed in great affairs, or if they are contractors of public business in which others might be endangered unless they achieve prosperous outcomes. Mercury as an **evening star** in this house will make those who stir up much business and the inventors of many affairs. For not without cause did the most prudent men mark this place and assign the time of childbirth or the laboring woman to this house; for here the mother is positioned when about to bring forth offspring. The **sixth house** <note>Another difficult house, associated with illness and slaves.</note> also relates to the twelfth. Although all other stars positioned in these places produce sluggish actions, Mercury found in this place makes scholars, **grammarians**, orators, geometers, and those who sell by constant trade, or those who are accustomed to help men in labor by the protection of their speech, defending them and liberating them from dangers. For such people will be judged to be more prudent than all others, and those to whom the advancements of all learning are granted. But he does this only when either **Jupiter** (♃) is joined to him, or when he is struck by no radiation from **malefics**. But if **Mars** (♂) regards him either by **opposition** or **square**...

# BOOK THREE

[...in a] **square** <note>An aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart, usually considered stressful or challenging.</note>, or if he is together with him <note>referring to Mars (♂)</note>, he will create informants, people who are hidden, subtle, malicious, evildoers, and moneylenders, or those through whom the false crafts of malice are perfected: or those who, due to the malice of these crimes, incur heavy legal condemnations. For they will be condemned as either evildoers or forgers, and having been condemned through tablets or public acts, they are forced to perish by miserable deaths. He will also cause them to incur the greatest condemnations and dangers either by means of slaves or because of slaves. But if, with **Mercury** (☿) and **Mars** (♂) thus positioned, the **Moon** (☽) joins them while her light is increasing, he will create those who die by violence <note>original: "biothanatos"—a term for those who die an unnatural or premature death</note>; specifically those who are executed by judicial sentence.
