All these things are determined according to the quality of the signs. But because I have said that <margin>The varied nature of Mercury.</margin> **Mercury** joins himself to all with an easy radiation, and is good with the good and equally evil with the evil: we must therefore now explain what he decrees in the charts <note>original: "genituris"—birth charts</note> in the company of each planet. For by day, when positioned with **Jupiter** and the **Sun** in opportune places of the birth chart, he decrees the greatest happiness. But if by day he is found with **Saturn** (♄), he will cause the greatest calamities of misfortune: by night, he is changed by a similar logic. For with **Jupiter** and the **Moon**, he is good; but with the **Sun**, he decrees the greatest evils and unhappiness. So that we may teach this more clearly, we must explain everything specifically. But first, diligently seek the <gloss>twelfth-part</gloss> <note>original: "duodenariam" / δωδεκατημόριον—a subdivision of a zodiac sign into twelve parts of 2.5 degrees each.</note> of **Mercury** and its bounds, so that you may reach all the secrets of the birth chart.

### MERCURY WITH THE SUN THROUGH THE TWELVE
#### stations of heaven. Chapter IX.

<margin>The place of Mercuries with the Sun</margin>
**Mercury** with the **Sun** (☉) by day, positioned exactly <note>original: "partiliter"—degree for degree</note> in the **horoscope** <note>The Ascendant, or the First House.</note>, will create kings, leaders, and the powerful: but by night, he will render the father degenerate and ignoble. These people will be learned in the public arts, but hidden and miserable, yet according to the quality and nature of the signs.

<margin>II</margin>
In the **second house** <note>Associated with personal wealth and assets.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope decrees an increase in inheritance, and designates the leadership of certain actions by a happy radiation.

<margin>III</margin>
In the **third house** <note>Associated with siblings, communication, and short travels.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope makes soothsayers <note>original: "aruspices"—priests who interpreted omens from entrails.</note>, interpreters of dreams, doctors, diviners, augurs, astrologers, mathematicians <note>In antiquity, "mathematici" often referred specifically to astrologers.</note>, and those who always predict the future, and whose art and purpose is very easily brought to the knowledge of all.

<margin>IV</margin>
In the **fourth house** <note>Associated with family, the home, and the father.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope will make people ignoble and skilled in hidden or illicit arts: but honest and serious. If they are thus positioned in the fourth house of the birth chart, it must be greatly considered in which sign they are positioned, and who the master of that sign is. For it is dangerous, especially if **Mercury**, positioned in this place, is found in the **house of Saturn** with the **Sun**.

<margin>V</margin>
In the **fifth house** <note>Associated with children and pleasure.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope will make people noble and those who complete all things easily: but they are dangerous, and those who do not have perpetual happiness, but deceive and trick many men by easy reasoning.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the **sixth house** <note>Associated with health, labor, and servitude.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope will make people ignoble, slaves, hardworking, and lazy, and those whose fathers are unknown, orphans, slow in actions, and those who can achieve nothing: and this occurs if no star is found in the tenth house from the horoscope. If, however, some star is found in the **tenth house** from the horoscope, signs of divine nobility and glory are conferred: and especially if a benevolent star is also positioned in that same place.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the **seventh house** <note>The Descendant; associated with marriage and open enemies.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope—that is, in the setting <note>The west horizon.</note>—if found in this place by day, he will cause the greatest affairs and powers to be committed to those so born, but he will eventually cause them to perish by a violent death. But if by night he is positioned exactly in this place, he will cause them to endure many evils while toiling, seeking food by daily work, and always occupied in evil and filthy acts. For their trades will be either filthy, or squalid, or of a heavy odor, from which perpetual vigils are demanded of the workers: such as tanners, fullers, wool-workers, painters, cooks, and those similar to these: yet he will make them underdogs <note>original: "hettematicos"—from the Greek for "losers" or those who are perpetually bested.</note>, and indeed always prone to vice in their early age.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the **eighth house** <note>Associated with death and inheritance.</note>, **Mercury** with the **Sun** positioned exactly from the horoscope will make people weak, prone to vice, and those who are easily deceived, also those who die violently, and those who frequently run into danger in infancy.

->**MERCURY WITH THE MOON, THROUGH THE TWELVE**<-
->**STATIONS OF THE SKY, CHAPTER X.**<-

<margin>The first station of Mercury with the Moon.</margin>
**I.** **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree in the part of the horoscope <note>the Ascendant or 1st house</note>, will make scribes, merchants, and those who seek the daily supports of life through the service of kings or princes. They will be sensible indeed, and intelligent, and their words and reasoning will be approved by all. Such people will also be those who, involved in many businesses, acquire not only an abundance of riches for themselves but also the favor of the people.

**II.** In the **second house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, will make those born quite happy in their trades, and they will acquire great means from them. Many people, admiring their industry and talent, will be joined to them in an intimate bond of love. For this reason, they will confer many increases in utility upon them, with which they may frequently enrich their inheritance.

**III.** In the **third house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, will make men happy in their journeys, from which they will obtain the greatest profits. They will be useful to their brothers and relatives, from whom they also receive many supports for life. It also bestows many friends during short journeys, through whose kind favor they obtain both honor and chief glory.

**IV.** In the **fourth house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, will make men who receive a happy inheritance of property from their parents. They will be lovers of their parents, whom they will also see established in some dignity of honor, from which the greatest profits are prepared for them. This is especially true if a kind radiation <note>a favorable "glance" or aspect</note> from **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon them while so positioned.

**V.** In the **fifth house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, decrees joy and gladness in the celebration of banquets. For he will make men who are always enriched with the greatest happiness in procreating children, who not only grant desired joys to their parents, but having been raised to some degree of honor, they grace them with no small reputation and glory.

**VI.** In the **sixth house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, decrees gains and profits of wealth from humble and base persons. For he will make men who, although they are involved in various businesses involving the proceeds of cattle <note>original: "beluarum" - often referring to large animals or livestock</note>, will nevertheless accomplish this through the service of slaves and low-born men. They themselves, however, preparing the greatest supports of life for themselves from there, will always aspire to higher things.

**VII.** In the **seventh house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, decrees useful gains and the greatest wealth from marriage. For such men will be those for whom even the method of doing business is found by their wives, whence not only power and riches, but also great marks of honor are prepared for them. However, various obstacles from such causes will sometimes happen to them.

<margin>The Moon (☽) rejoices in the eighth.</margin>
**VIII.** In the **eighth house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, decrees inheritances from the deaths of others, through which many useful trades may be practiced and some marks of honor obtained. But if **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon this place with a benevolent radiation, he certainly decrees the greatest riches and wealth from the inheritance of the dead. For this is the place in which the **Moon** (☽) especially rejoices <note>original: "gaudet" — a technical term for when a planet is in a house that suits its nature</note>.

**IX.** In the **ninth house** from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) with the **Moon** (☽) positioned exactly by degree, decrees good and useful travels abroad, from which not only trades of the greatest profit are sought, but...

# BOOK THREE

...and many badges of dignity are prepared for them. It will also make men who are religious, and who, in their own religion, search out many sharp and subtle things with a sagacious stirring of the mind, from which they obtain the greatest honor for themselves.

<margin>X</margin> In the **tenth house** <note>The Midheaven, the peak of the chart representing career and public life.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an astrological term meaning at the same degree, intensifying the effect</term> with the **Moon** (☽), will make men sharp in their life, spirit, and actions; they will be wise, intelligent, and those who seek out many things with a perceptive character. Because of this, they illuminate not only themselves but their entire fatherland with an honorable rank of dignity. For such people will be those whom everyone loves and venerates together, and upon whom they confer the rewards that their virtues deserve.

<margin>XI</margin> In the **eleventh house** <note>The house of friends, luck, and social support.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with the **Moon** (☽), will make men not only industrious and skillful in seeking friends, but also fortunate and happy. Relying on the goodwill of these friends, they seek the greatest support for their resources and frequently acquire the badges of honors—especially if **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon them with a benevolent "aspect" <note>an "aspect" is a geometric relationship between planets that transmits influence</note>.

<margin>XII</margin> In the **twelfth house** <note>The house of hidden enemies, constraints, and losses.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with the **Moon** (☽), will make men who obtain the greatest benefits and profits from their enemies, and who come to the highest expectations among the people through the liberation of captives. They will certainly be powerful over their enemies; from their victory over them, they will bring back the greatest praise and triumph for themselves, to the extreme admiration of everyone.

->**MERCURY WITH SATURN THROUGH THE TWELVE**<-
->**STATIONS OF THE SKY. CHAPTER XI.**<-

<margin>Mercury with Saturn in the horoscope.</margin>**Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree in the part of the horoscope <note>the Ascendant or 1st house, representing the self and physical body</note>: in a **daytime birth**, this will make hiders of money <note>original: "pecuniarum absconditores"</note>, advocates, legal experts, or scribes, but they will be sluggish and those who fail quickly. If, however, they are positioned in this place in a **nighttime birth**, they will make slaves or captives out of free men, and will hand them over to powerful men to serve as captives. But if they are found in a feminine sign in a nighttime birth, they will make eunuchs, or men without seed who cannot perform sexually; they will also be shameful, infamous, unchaste, and gender-nonconforming <note>original: "cinaedos," a Roman term for men who did not follow traditional masculine sexual or social roles, often used as an insult</note>.

<margin>II</margin> In the **second house** <note>The house of wealth and personal assets.</note>, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree from the horoscope in a daytime birth, will make herbalists, doctors, and those through whom health is provided to men; but it also makes them wealthy and famous in their actions. They will frequently be orators or agents for powerful men, depending on the nature of the zodiac signs. If, however, they are found in this place in a nighttime birth, they make beggars, the insane, those who are naked, or temple-slaves. They will frequently cause people to be accused and placed in custody; they will always be mournful, childless, weak in some part of the body, or entangled in certain crimes and vices.

<margin>III</margin> In the **third house** <note>The house of siblings and travel.</note>, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree from the horoscope, will make divers <note>original: "urinatores," specialist free-divers who recovered goods from the sea or worked on harbors</note>, those who lift water from deep wells, gardeners, managers of small estates, or embalmers and undertakers, guards of dead bodies, or porters of tombs.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the **fourth house** <note>The house of family, land, and the "hidden" depths of life.</note>, **Mercury** (☿) and **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree from the horoscope, will make masters of illicit and hidden arts, or those who are accomplices to them, and those who seek their daily life from evil arts. But some having Mercury with Saturn in this way will either be in custody or be condemned for some reason; however, all actions are found according to the nature and quality of the signs, and according to the logic of the other stars.

<margin>V</margin> In the **fifth house** <note>The house of children and pleasure.</note>, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree from the horoscope, will make those who frequently change their dwellings; but it also makes overseers of the grain supply or of crops, or of certain places, and prefects of gems, pearls, spices, or metals, and carvers of sacred objects.

<margin>VI</margin> In the **sixth house** <note>The house of illness and service.</note>, **Mercury** (☿) with **Saturn** (♄) positioned exactly by degree from the horoscope: if found in this place by day, it will make those who are knowledgeable in many teachings, and powerful in the doctrine of hidden arts, and who want to know everything that exists in human affairs; but they will certainly be ambitious and envious, and entangled in many vices and illnesses. In a nighttime birth, however, those positioned in this place will make authors of forged writings, the wicked, the malicious, the malevolent, sorcerers, and those who are always entangled in the greatest evils and necessities.

But in this place, if **Mercury** (☿) is positioned with **Saturn** (♄) <note>Mercury represents communication and intellect; Saturn represents discipline, restriction, and time.</note>, whether by day or by night, if it looks upon them with any "aspect" <note>an "aspect" is a geometric relationship between planets</note>, either through a square or a diameter <note>a "square" is 90 degrees and a "diameter" or "opposition" is 180 degrees; both were considered difficult or stressful alignments</note>, it will cause men to be entangled in inevitable evil and punished by the judgment of a public death.

<margin>VII</margin> In the **seventh house** <note>The house of marriage, partnerships, and open enemies.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an astrological term meaning at the same degree, intensifying the effect</term> with **Saturn** (♄), will make men heirs to women and those who burn with desire for great resources, as well as the lovers of these women. If, however, they are found in this place in a nighttime birth, they will make men miserable in every interaction of life, and those who are bound by the greatest debts; they also become prone to vice, weak, malicious, and spiteful, and those who are eventually accused and kept in public custody.

<margin>VIII</margin> In the **eighth house** <note>The house of death, inheritance, and shared resources.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Saturn** (♄), decrees an increase in patrimony and honor over the passage of time; others, however, obtain estates because of the death of someone else. Yet, their health will suffer from either a bladder stone or an ailment of the stomach. In a nighttime birth, those positioned exactly by degree in this place are made poor, outcasts, weary, and full of hardship, and those to whom "humors" <note>referring to the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which ancient medicine believed caused disease when unbalanced</note> cause damage; they are rendered weakened, especially if the **Moon** (☽) is waning in light and moving toward Saturn, or if she is full and moving toward **Mars** (♂).

<margin>IX</margin> In the **9th house** <note>The house of religion, philosophy, and long journeys.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Saturn** (♄), will make prophets, or those who dress the statues of the gods, or the porters of divine ceremonies.

<margin>X</margin> In the **10th house** <note>The Midheaven (MC), representing career and public status.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Saturn** (♄), that is, in the Midheaven, will make heirs to others' estates, or inventors of very great things; sometimes, however, it makes scribes, or managers, or the agents of great men. But if any other star looks upon them so positioned, it will make orators of divine genius, or masters of the oratorical art, grammarians, or those placed in charge of any of these arts by the authority of someone else, masters of studies, or tax-assessors who are searchers of celestial matters. For some will practice accounting, while others become either the inventors or masters of the most difficult literature.

<margin>XI</margin> In the **11th house** <note>The house of friends and social gains.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Saturn** (♄), decrees those things which we said he decrees in the fifth house.

<margin>XII</margin> In the **12th house** <note>The house of secrets and hidden enemies.</note> from the horoscope, what **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Saturn** (♄) decrees, the sixth house of the birth chart has more clearly explained.

### MERCURY WITH JUPITER THROUGH THE TWELVE HOUSES. Chapter XII.

**Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree in the horoscope <note>The 1st house, representing the self and vitality.</note> with **Jupiter** (♃) in a daytime birth, will make men famous and glorious, placed in charge of cities, or the ten leading judges of the greatest cities, and those who restore the laws to provinces or cities, and those who always rejoice in just causes. If, however, they are found exactly by degree in this place in a nighttime birth, they will make agents or managers of business; but sometimes they will make scribes for great and powerful men, and those placed in charge of accounts, banks, warehouses, and trades—men who are truly sharp and ingenious, and upon whom the greatest happiness is conferred from the goodness of their talent.

<margin>II</margin> In the **second house** <note>The house of personal wealth and possessions.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Jupiter** (♃) in a daytime birth, will make heirs to another's patrimony, those adopted by strangers, and masters of many estates and stored goods, and those upon whom the greatest increases of happiness are conferred over time. If, however, they are found in this place in a nighttime birth, they will make men rather foolish, those whose happiness is not permanent, and those whom the course of life very often deceives by means of logic.

<margin>III</margin> <note>The OCR shows "II" again, but this section refers to the third house.</note> In the **third house** <note>The house of siblings and communication.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree with **Jupiter** (♃), will make mages <note>original: "magos"</note>, but those always excelling in distinguished goodness, singers of hymns, or porters of the gods, or guardians of temples, or those who initiate and consecrate men into religions, and those who foreknow the future by the warning of the gods; it will also make those placed in charge of sacred games. **Jupiter** and **Mercury** positioned together in the 9th house from the horoscope decree similarly.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the **fourth house** <note>The house of home, family, and hidden things.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) and **Jupiter** (♃) positioned exactly by degree, will make masters of song and the organ through their own invention. Also curators or tutors of minors, and those who take up the care and accounting of women. Some, indeed, find things by chance, while others know the paths to hidden treasures, from which the greatest happiness is prepared for them.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the **sixth house** <note>Traditionally associated with health, service, and daily toil.</note> from the horoscope, **Mercury** (☿) positioned exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an astrological term meaning at the same degree, intensifying the effect</term> with **Jupiter** (♃), decrees the same outcomes by both night and day. But if they are found in their morning rising, they will make the person easy-going and rational in all business: they become overseers of legal cases, disputes, audits, accounts, trade, or certain religious matters, so much so that they acquire very great wealth from these revenues—especially if, with the planets so placed, some star is also positioned in the **tenth house** <note>The "Midheaven," representing career and public standing.</note> from the horoscope. But if the **Moon** (☽) is carried in such a way that it joins them with its radiation while positioned in the tenth house from the horoscope, it will make them rich, affluent, masters of much money or gold, and those who obtain the greatest fruits from their possessions; they will be happy, blessed, and those who arrange the affairs of kings through their intercession, such as collectors of royal grain-supplies or fiscal taxes, or those placed in charge of provinces and cities. If, however, in a daytime birth, with **Mercury** (☿) and **Jupiter** (♃) so positioned in the sixth house, no star is found in the tenth house from the horoscope, it will make for a mediocre life, inheritance, and career. But if they are found thus by night, they turn out to be interpreters of business, fishermen, augurs, sculptors, or those always hindered by laborious activities, or those performing servile duties, or placed in such crafts as are fouled by heavy pleading or filth—such as fullers <note>Workers who cleaned and thickened cloth, often using fermented urine.</note>, or tanners, or shoemakers, or bakers, or wool-workers, or fishermen, and those who are similar to them.

However, these benefits are greatly diminished in nighttime births if **Saturn** (♄) looks upon **Mercury** (☿) and **Jupiter** (♃) so positioned from a diameter or a square <note>Difficult geometric alignments of 180 or 90 degrees</note>, or if he is found with them.

For some, it brings ill repute to their youth, but with the passage of time, it decrees increases of moderate substance. If, however, they are found in this place by night, they either find something from which they have the greatest support for life, or a significant inheritance is conferred upon them, and with the passage of time, they are lifted up by the greatest strokes of luck; nevertheless, they will make them defective in body and sickly.

In a daytime birth, they persist in these actions and duties for however long, and do not frequently cause offense.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS: MERCURY WITH MARS THROUGH THE TWELVE STATIONS OF HEAVEN. CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>Mercury with Mars in the horoscope <note>The first house, representing the self and the physical body.</note></margin>
Mercury with Mars, if positioned in the degree of the horoscope in a daytime birth, will make people short of breath <note>original: "anaphoricos", likely referring to respiratory distress</note>, prone to heart ailments <note>original: "cardiacos"</note>, short-lived <note>original: "oligochronios"</note>, and unhappy. For he will cause them to be falsely condemned either because of women, or the allurements of love, or because of secret writings, or through sorcery, or to perish by a violent death <term>biothanatos: a Greek term for one who dies an unnatural or premature death, often by execution or suicide</term>. But if they are found exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an astrological term meaning the planets occupy the same degree of a sign, intensifying the effect</term> in the horoscope by night, they will make great men: leaders of great religions, commanders, protectors, heralds, or bodyguards, high administrators of emperors, and those upon whom the greatest happiness is conferred from the outcome of battles. If, however, when they are so positioned by night, Saturn (♄) should look upon them from a square <note>an aspect of 90 degrees, considered tense</note> or diameter <note>an opposition of 180 degrees</note>, he will make them dangerous people who are very often deceived and hindered in all their actions. For Saturn so positioned will make men lazy and weighed down by every burden of unhappiness.

**II** In the **second house** <note>The house of wealth and personal values.</note> from the horoscope, with Mercury and Mars positioned exactly by degree, in a daytime birth, he will cause the newborns to be abandoned; and if they are raised, he will for some reason make them fugitives, frequently exiles, and sometimes captives, and he will make many be stripped of everything through proscription <note>State-sanctioned seizure of property</note>. He entangles some in serious illnesses and powerful defects; others he will cause to die a violent death, if one or both of them are radiated by the light of a full Moon (☽). But if they are found thus by night, they make men of evil mind—malicious, obscure, fearful, and those who are deceived in all their actions. Yet they will make their activities manifold: for they will be either tax collectors, or customs officers, or imperial agents <term>curiosi: official inspectors or secret service agents of the late Roman Empire</term>; they even render some insane or frenzied.

**III** In the **third house** <note>The house of siblings, short journeys, and communication.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury with Mars positioned exactly by degree will cause one to have the substance of life from sacrifices or from activities related to holidays. Such people will be those who predict the future and who always dwell in temples; but they will be terrifying to everyone with whom they do business, even if they know nothing or do nothing. These people, however, in the process of time, will achieve many increases in happiness.

**IIII** In the **fourth house** <note>The house of home, roots, and the father.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury with Mars will make people lazy and humble in all actions and in every fortune, and those who engage in constant enmities with parents or relatives, so that the greatest losses and traps are always brought upon them by these very people. They will also be legal guarantors <term>fideiussores: individuals who take on the legal debt or obligation of another</term>, and those who are shattered by the greatest dangers from this matter and descend to humility and poverty. When this happens to them, they will be the authors of certain illicit arts; from which, either as intermediaries or as accomplices caught in some evils, they are entangled in the greatest snares of danger, so that they are punished by the stroke of condemnation. Others, placed in these calamities, are overwhelmed by the onslaughts of great and long sickness, especially if Saturn (♄) sees them so positioned from a diameter or square. Nevertheless, if Mercury, Mars, and the Moon are found thus in the fourth house of the nativity by night, they also make governors, tribunes, generals, powerful men, and administrators, but for the most part perishing shamefully by a violent death.

**V** In the **fifth house** <note>The house of children, pleasure, and creativity.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury with Mars positioned exactly by degree renders them strong, manly, athletes, and undefeated in all contests; but those who are moved to various places for the sake of a home. To these, the greatest favor of livelihood and grain-supply <note>original: "annona", the state-regulated food supply of Rome</note> is granted from the public or the community; yet in every contest he will make them superior and utterly terrifying to their adversaries.

**VI** In the **sixth house** <note>The house of health and servitude.</note> from the horoscope, Mercury and Mars positioned exactly by degree, if they are in these places by day, decree illness and the greatest defects. They also make those placed in custody and those having knowledge of prison, being condemned from whatever accusation. For they are either attacked, or betrayed, or bound by the false deceptions of crimes; for they are attacked or betrayed either by slaves, or through slaves, or by slave-like men, or by those who are placed in custody because of some crime, so that they perish with the greatest torments of violence and atrocity—especially if, positioned in these places, they are looked upon by a full Moon from any part. If, however, they are positioned in this house by night, they make people entangled in many debts and much interest on loans, causing anxieties of the soul and obstructions. In all actions, moreover, they render them lazy.

This placement causes them to kill themselves or others either because of a woman, a wife, or the perverted desires of some love; or, because of some such admitted crime, they are placed in public custody or prison and are condemned based on that accusation. Generally, whoever has Mercury (☿) and Mars (♂) thus will fulfill homicides and deaths within themselves according to the nature of the zodiac signs involved. For they will be muggers <note>original: "grassatores"</note>, or thieves, or assassins, or pirates, or those like them; and those who, having been caught in these crimes, are punished by the sentence of a persistent judgment. In a nighttime birth, however, this placement makes them be cheated by women through unjust acts, or be joined to viragos <note>meaning strong-willed or aggressive women</note>, and have children from them, and finally and always be involved in great and very bad vices.

<margin>VIII</margin>

### OF JULIUS FIRMICUS

[...they] produce <note>original: "cient"</note> lovers of the gymnasium, athletes, or those destined for public contests. But if they are positioned in the signs or degrees of the **Sun** (☉) <note>Leo</note>, they will produce fighters, lovers of armor, soldiers, hunters, those who take pleasure in raising wild beasts or are overseers of beasts, and royal messengers or couriers <term>veredarios: the express couriers of the Roman imperial postal service</term>. If they are positioned in the houses or degrees of **Venus** (♀) <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, they will make linen-workers, weavers of tunics, embroiderers, dyers, or those who in some way deal with spices, gems, or pearls. In the houses or degrees of **Jupiter** (♃) <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, they will produce overseers, tribunes, or those governing certain regions and cities. In the houses or degrees of **Saturn** (♄) <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, they will produce those who handle wicked and criminal duties: such as torturers, executioners, killers, informants, and traitors. In the house of the **Moon** (☽) <note>Cancer</note>, they produce coppersmiths, blacksmiths, sculptors, furriers, and tanners, who seek the necessities of life through fire or iron. ->MERCURY WITH VENUS THROUGH THE TWELVE<-
->stations of heaven. Chapter XIV.<-

When Mercury (☿) is positioned exactly by degree with Venus (♀) in the horoscope <note>the 1st house or Ascendant</note> in a daytime birth, it will produce shield-makers, or protectors of emperors, or those who through their own watchfulness preserve the safety of princes, or those who govern the royal monies and treasures entrusted to their management, and those to whom duties of such administrations are credited. It will also produce musicians, chorus-leaders, and those who compose musical melodies, or certainly public teachers, orators, grammarians, or inventors of laws, and those who preside over the divine power. 

But if they are found together in the horoscope during a nighttime birth, they will produce people who are sharp, ingenious, and who easily achieve whatever they wish to do. They will be either crowned with honors, or placed in charge of priests, or bearers of sacred images <note>original: "sacrorum baiuli simulacrorum"</note>, and those who receive increases in dignity over the course of time. They will also produce those skilled in a certain harmony, or those in charge of royal correspondence, but whose speech is full of charm and grace.

<margin>II</margin> In the **second house** from the horoscope, Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) positioned exactly by degree in a daytime birth will produce those who handle much business and are occupied with noble acts: yet while they persist in wealth itself through the works of life, and are pleasant and agreeable in character, they are nevertheless prone to vice and lust. But if they are found in this place as "morning stars" <note>rising before the sun</note>, they will make those who seek inheritance for themselves, who are happy, literate, practiced in some discipline or music, joyful, honest, and shining with the splendor of grace. If, however, in a nighttime birth, Mercury (☿) is found in this place as an "evening star" with Venus (♀), it decrees great resources and grants increases of the greatest happiness over the course of time. For they will be leaders of cities, placed in charge of laws, and those to whom the care of the greatest provinces is mandated. For some find something from which they receive the beginnings of happiness, while for others, the greatest inheritances are very often conferred.

<margin>III</margin> In the **third house** from the horoscope, Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) positioned exactly by degree will produce victors in sacred contests, and also priests or prophets, "dressers of the gods" <note>those who maintain and clothe the statues of the gods in temples</note>, or those handling the greatest duties in temples, those placed over priests, or leaders of sacred contests, good ambassadors, and those endowed with good character and institutions, to whom a secure city may entrust its desires.

<margin>IIII</margin> In the **fourth house** from the horoscope, Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) positioned exactly by degree will produce those skilled in hidden literature <note>occult or secret writings</note>, magi, philosophers, and those who often handle celestial matters, or those who care for suffering men and are accustomed to be of benefit to them in any kind of way. Mercury (☿) as a morning star with Venus (♀) placed in this house will cause one to come from slavery to liberty, and will lead one from low birth to splendor and nobility: but they will undertake the protection and defense of wretched women, or slaves, or old women, or virgins, and they will seek out actions of various kinds because of these people. They will be occupied with established acts and businesses according to the substance and quality of the signs.

# BOOK THREE

<margin>V</margin>
In the **fifth house** from the Ascendant <note>the fifth house is traditionally associated with children, pleasure, and creativity</note>, Mercury (☿) positioned exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an aspect occurring on the same numerical degree, signifying a powerful connection</term> with Venus (♀) decrees the greatest resources as time goes on, and in a similar way bestows the marks of wealth. It makes such people those who receive the greatest gifts or rewards from women or wives, and who are always connected by some acquaintance to powerful men.

<margin>VI</margin>
In the **sixth house** from the Ascendant, Mercury (☿) positioned exactly with Venus (♀) in a daytime birth chart <note>original: "diurna genitura"</note> decrees wealth from accounts, business dealings, calculations, teaching, or the revenues of the gods <note>likely referring to temple management or religious administration</note>, especially if some other planet is found in the tenth house of the birth chart. However, these individuals will find it difficult to obtain a wife; for they will be full of lust and, as a result of that fact, somewhat infamous. But in a nighttime birth, if Mercury is found as a morning star <note>rising before the sun</note> in this place with Venus, they will join themselves in marriage to female servants, widows, or prostitutes. They will have laborious careers and servile duties involving water, if no other planet is found in the tenth house from the Ascendant. But if a planet is there, it will make them seek many things through their own hard work. For they will be travelers, merchants, pilots, captains of ships, and goldsmiths. If Mercury is an evening star in this house and is found with Venus, it will make them wise, clever, musicians, or makers of water-organs; or perhaps dyers of colors, or merchants of spices, gems, or pearls. It will make some into perfumers or inventors of medicinal pigments, and frequently overseers of mines, so that from these occupations the greatest support of resources or riches is granted to them.

<margin>VII</margin>
In the **seventh house** from the Ascendant, Mercury (☿) positioned exactly with Venus (♀) decrees the defects of hidden illnesses. For it will make them suffer from liver ailments, or be frenzied, or melancholic, and things similar to these. They will always be estranged from their wife’s affection and will be infamous until the final moments of their life. But if Mercury is found with Venus in this house by night, the greatest substance of wealth will be granted to them by women or wives, and gradually with the passing of age they will obtain grand honors and the marks of the greatest happiness—especially if neither Mars (♂) nor Saturn (♄) (and specifically Saturn) regards them from any direction. For if Mars and Saturn are joined to them by any ray of light <note>referring to an astrological aspect</note> while they are so positioned, all these things we have mentioned will be turned into the opposite.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the **eighth house** from the Ascendant, if both Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) are evening stars in a daytime birth, they will make the individuals ineffective, "cut off" <term>apocopos: literally "docked" or "cut short," often implying impotence or a lack of social power</term>, and unable to achieve anything. They will also make them always entangled in lustful business, flawed in mind and body, and people who obtain marriage with difficulty. For they will be sterile and unable to produce offspring; they will die of either spasms, intestinal blockages, apoplexy, or frenzy. But found together in this house by night, they will make heirs to the estates of others or those who manage the resources of others; yet they will be good, kind, heads of families, and those to whom many things are granted by women or wives. Others will find something that suffices for their support throughout their entire life. But they will have a sudden death, without pain or torment. However, Mercury positioned as a morning star with Venus in this house will make them great students and knowers of all things, even inventors, who obtain whatever they wish very easily and perceive the increase of their inheritance over time.

<margin>IX</margin>
In the **ninth house** from the Ascendant, Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) positioned exactly together will give wives who are enchanting <note>original: "fascinantes," which can mean charming but also implies casting spells</note>, who even make the men's own limbs become bewitched or ghostly. They will seek the protections of life from the duties of temples. For it will make them either priests, or those who, stationed in temples, predict the future, or soothsayers, astrologers, augurs, or magi <note>wise men/magicians</note>, or those who are accustomed to explaining all things.

<margin>X</margin>
In the **tenth house** from the Ascendant, Mercury (☿) positioned with Venus (♀) will create public duties and public men who are honored by the people or by cities, but who contract infamy from the actions of their wife. Mercury as a morning star in this place with Venus will make inventors of musical modes, but also stage-players and those destined for public spectacles, and they will be unhappy in their marriages. For they will have wives who are either prostitutes, or common women, or actresses, or otherwise infamous. Some will also be lovers of perverse things and entangled in the pleasures of many lusts.

From this activity, the greatest support for their inheritance is granted, but later they will be found deeply embroiled in conflicts or massive financial losses.

XII. In the **twelfth house** from the Ascendant <note>the house of hidden enemies and undoing</note>, if Mercury (☿) and Venus (♀) are found in a daytime birth, it makes lovers and those suffering from the vice of obscene passions—people who are nonetheless conspicuous and known to all. But this position forces them to be deeply drawn into those vices, to be condemned because of that behavior, and to perish as a <term>biothanatos: one who dies a violent or unnatural death</term>. If, however, they are found in this place in a nighttime birth, they will suffer many persecutions from unworthy women, or they may acquire prostitutes through the instinct of love with a man acting as a middleman, and they will be occupied with multiple legal judgments arising from these acts. They are the sort who frequently fall away from their purpose, and who are often deceived in their accounts or cheated by schemes regarding their actions, business, or resources. Now that the specific decrees for Mercury in conjunction with all the planets have been explained, let us return to where we left off: the decrees of the Moon through the individual houses.

# THE DECREES OF THE MOON THROUGH THE INDIVIDUAL STATIONS OF THE HEAVENS. Chapter XV.

<margin>To be read in this, or certainly the first, or this place.</margin>
I. If the Moon (☾) is positioned exactly by degree <term>partiliter: an aspect occurring on the same numerical degree</term> in the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopo"</note> in a nighttime birth—if she is found full and in signs where she rejoices—she decrees great increases in fortune and makes the person always superior to their brothers in age and merit. If, however, she is found in a daytime birth exactly by degree in the **fifth house**, she will make captains of great ships. If the Moon is positioned this way in a daytime birth while Mars (♂) and Saturn (♄) occupy another angle of the chart—that is, if they regard her from a square or opposite position <note>90 or 180 degrees away</note>, or are found with her—they will make pirates famous for their cruel and savage ferocity, or judges set over remote places. If no benevolent star regards the Moon when she is positioned thus with malevolent planets, it causes those born then to be exposed <note>abandoned as infants</note>, or it decrees no lifespan for them; rather, it causes them to perish immediately, or threatens a bad end to life and a violent death.

II. In the **second house** from the Ascendant <note>the house of wealth and resources</note>, the Moon (☾) positioned in a nighttime birth makes people famous and conspicuous in their actions, but also luxurious and devoted to the pleasant delights of pleasure; a greater inheritance of property is granted to them as time passes. If, however, she is found in this place in a daytime birth, she either kills the parents immediately, or divides the newborn from the parents, or causes the parents to separate in a dissolved marriage, and the substance of the inheritance is diminished by various types of losses. Such people with the Moon in this position are also occupied with constant travels and divide their activities across many places, but their life is always subject to someone else. If, however, she is waning in light in this place and Saturn (♄) is positioned in this part or in the sign of the Ascendant, it brings about blindness through sudden injuries to the eyes. If the Moon is positioned thus and Mars (♂) is found in the degree or sign of the Ascendant, it causes pain in the joints, dislocations, or fractures; it weakens others with the persistence of hemorrhoidal illness.

III. In the **third house** from the Ascendant <note>the house of siblings and travel</note>, the Moon (☾) makes the mother low-born or polluted by some stain of infamy. If she is found in this place with Jupiter (♃), she provides sustenance for those born then from the treasury or from public grain supplies. If Jupiter (♃) is positioned with the Moon (☾) in this place and Venus (♀) joins them with some ray of light, it makes the person a high priest of a great goddess, or a priest of a most powerful religion, or an administrator or reformer of public religions. If, however, Venus (♀) is found with the Moon (☾) in this place, they will have business involving pigments, spices, wine, or flowers. But if in a nighttime birth the Moon is found in this place with Saturn (♄) alone, it makes people slow, who achieve none of the things they desire, and who utter sacrilegious words regarding religions, and upon whom the wrath of the gods brings the greatest misfortunes. If, however, the Moon (☾) is found in this place in a daytime birth with Mercury (☿), the North Node (☊), and Mars (♂), it will produce sacrilegious people, temple-robbers, the unjust, the impious, the irreligious, murderers, and thoroughly evil men.

But if Saturn (♄) is found in another angle of the birth chart and Venus (♀) is in the west <note>setting</note>, the mother passes from free birth to slavery...

<margin>V</margin>

<margin>VII</margin>
In the **seventh house** from the Ascendant, that is, in the setting <note>the Descendant, representing marriage and partnerships</note>, if the Moon (☽) is found exactly in this place in a nocturnal birth—specifically in those signs where Jupiter (♃) or Venus (♀) is exalted or rejoices—and if they aspect her with favorable rays as her light increases, she will grant a happy old age, profit even from women, and decree suitable betrothals. But if she is oppressed in this place by the radiation of malevolents, especially in a daytime birth and diminished in light, she will give a wife late in life; and when she does give one, she will be low-born, a widow, sterile, or deformed by grave ugliness, or in no way pleasing.

<margin>VIII</margin>
In the **eighth house** from the Ascendant <note>the house of death and inheritance</note>, with the Moon (☽) found exactly there, she will give a person an inheritance from the dead, but decrees death to him quickly and without great pain or torment. But if Mars (♂) or Saturn (♄) aspects her from a square or diameter <note>an opposition</note>, it will bring destruction and a removal from one’s usual status; and she will often make those so constituted "lunatics" <note>original: *lunaticos*; in this era, the term referred to epilepsy or mental illness thought to be triggered by the phases of the moon</note>.

<margin>IX</margin>
In the **ninth house** from the Ascendant <note>the house of travel and religion</note>, with the Moon (☽) positioned exactly there in a daytime birth, she makes the native dwell meanly in temples; and she makes them those who, wanting something, announce it to men as if spoken by the gods. But if she is found in this place in a nocturnal birth, she makes divine worshippers of the gods who study sacred rites and religions, and to some she grants offices or gifts from temples. But she will also give many thoughts and travels through various regions. And if this is the house of Mercury (☿), she will give a knowledge of astronomy; if of Venus (♀), songs and joy; if of Mars (♂), the work of arms and tools; if of Jupiter (♃), divine worship and knowledge of the law; if of Saturn (♄), the science of alchemy; if of the Sun (☉), care for four-footed animals; but if it is Cancer (♋), her own house indeed, she will give knowledge of all things that come from the water.

<margin>X</margin>
In the **tenth house** from the Ascendant, that is, in the Midheaven <note>MC; the house of career and public standing</note>, if the Moon (☽) is found exactly in a nocturnal birth in those signs in which she is exalted or rejoices with increasing light, and Jupiter (♃) protects her with favorable rays, she will make the greatest emperors or powerful administrators to whom the power of life and death is easily entrusted; so positioned, she also gives ordinary consulships. But if she precedes or follows the degree of the Midheaven, yet is positioned in a nearby place, she will produce leaders, tribunes, and administrators. If she is positioned <term>platice: broadly within the sign</term> in the same sign as the Midheaven, she renders them great in all their actions and adorned with various kinds of happiness. But if, with the Moon so placed, Saturn (♄) should possess another angle <note>one of the four cardinal points of the chart</note>, she frequently decrees envies and unhappiness. By day, however, with the Moon positioned in the Midheaven, she will make them mediocre in life and in all actions, and people who are usually deceived by frequent reckonings. But if by day the Moon is so placed and the Sun (☉) is found exactly in the Ascendant in his own house or exaltation, or in the house of Jupiter, she will make great and powerful administrators, and proconsuls of the largest provinces or cities, but they will be terrible in the administration of their duties. Furthermore, with the Moon and Sun so positioned—the Sun in the Ascendant in those signs we mentioned and the Moon in the Midheaven—if Jupiter (♃) protects both together, or even one of the two, with a prosperous ray, he will make emperors very power-

# JULIUS FIRMICUS

...and those whom all receive with the greatest trembling of terror. <note>This sentence fragment concludes the description of the Moon in the tenth house, or Midheaven, from the previous page.</note>

<margin>XI</margin>
**In the eleventh house from the Ascendant** <note>original: *horoscopus*; the 11th house is traditionally the "House of the Good Spirit"</note>, when the Moon is positioned here, she decrees the same effects that we showed in the previous sections regarding the fifth house from the Ascendant. <note>The 11th and 5th houses were often linked as they both deal with favor, children, and support.</note>

<margin>XII</margin>
**In the twelfth house from the Ascendant** <note>the "House of the Bad Spirit"</note>, if positioned in a nocturnal birth, she decrees a short span and duration of life. However, if Jupiter (♃) or Venus (♀), or either of them, is found <term>partonically: exactly by degree</term> in the Ascendant, she grants the freedom of some power along with happiness. But if Mars (♂) and Saturn (♄) are positioned exactly in the Ascendant, or if one of these two occupies the twelfth house, she decrees many evils, misfortunes, serious accidents, and illnesses. In a nocturnal birth, she will cause defects for the native as well as for the mother. If, however, no planet is in the Ascendant and the Moon is found alone by day in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, she decrees the loss of inheritance, miserable actions, and wandering. But if she is found in this place by night, she causes those born to be miserable, humble, or from a humble or servile class; they will be hardworking, always occupied in heavy labors, and their bodies or mouths will be defiled by a foul odor <note>original: *foeditate*; likely referring to chronic bad breath or skin conditions</note>. They are people who are accustomed to being frequently deceived and endangered, or who contract some defect from the hardships of travel.

<margin>XIII</margin>
But you must also diligently investigate the <term>duodecatemorion: the twelfth-part of a zodiac sign</term> <note>original: *δυοδεκατημόριον*</note> and its "bounds" <note>specific sub-sections of a sign ruled by different planets</note>. For whatever is hidden in a birth chart, or generally concealed by the composition of the stars, the twelfth-part and its bounds make public and demonstrate. For if you note the efficacy of the twelfth-parts—especially from the bounds in which they are found—and choose to explain the substance of all <term>apotelesmatics: astrological predictions</term> <note>original: *apoteleſmatum*</note> from them, you will truly never be deceived. For the Babylonians attribute the sum of all decrees to the twelfth-parts, although Ptolemy attributes them to the <term>Antiscia: "shadow-points" or reflections of the signs</term>, while we attribute them to both.

### THE DECREES OF THE MOON, IF FOUND IN THE PLACE OF FORTUNE. Chapter XVI.

<margin>XIIII</margin>
But because our work has progressed this far—so that after the decrees of all the planets through the individual stations of the sky, we come at last to the Moon—before the end of this book is closed, let us discuss something of her application with the **Place of Fortune** <note>also known as the "Lot of Fortune," a mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity</note>, since she is the principal mistress of the life of mortals.

<margin>XV</margin>
If, therefore, she is found in the Place of Fortune and is positioned so that she is moving toward Jupiter (♃), or is with him, she decrees the administration of leadership, glory, and happiness.

<margin>XVI</margin>
But if she is positioned with Venus (♀) in this place, or if she is moving toward Venus, she bestows the honors we mentioned, along with the charm of grace.

<margin>XVII</margin>
If, positioned in this place and increasing in light <note>waxing</note>, she moves toward Jupiter or is with him, she makes people blessed, powerful, and exceedingly wise; they are those who, by the happiness of their talent or the grace of their learning, attain honors, glory, dignity, and the substance of an inheritance.

<margin>XVIII</margin>
But if, decreasing in light <note>waning</note> and positioned in this place, she moves toward Mars (♂) or is with him, she decrees illnesses, defects, malice, and malignancy.

<margin>XIX</margin>
If, positioned in this place in a daytime birth, she moves toward Mars or is with him, she makes people hardworking and miserable, seeking their food from fire, or iron, or from some heavy weight of daily life.

<margin>XX</margin>
But if, positioned in this place in a nocturnal birth, she moves toward Mars or is with him, she decrees military service, glory, power, and leadership in these activities. She also makes athletes—depending on the quality of the signs—but those who are preferred over others by merit of their courage.

<margin>XXI</margin>
But if, positioned in this place in a nocturnal birth and increasing in light, she moves toward Saturn (♄) or is with him, she diminishes the paternal and maternal inheritance; she makes the mother either a widow or one who perishes by a bad death with illness and defect. She makes the natives themselves miserable and hardworking in their first age, but happy as their age proceeds. But if by day, while increasing in light, she moves toward Saturn or is with him, she causes the one so born to be quickly orphaned by the death of parents and compels the inheritance to be dissipated by miserable tearing-apart; nevertheless, happiness and increases in inheritance are granted to them as their age proceeds. Similarly, if she is waning in light at night, she decrees these same things by a similar logic.

<margin>XXII</margin>
If, however, positioned in this place by day and diminished in light, she moves toward Saturn or is with him, she decrees the inconveniences of defects, illness, a bad death, and proscription <note>legal seizure of property or being declared an outlaw</note>.

<margin>XXIII</margin>
If the Place of Fortune is found in the tenth house from the Ascendant—that is, in the Midheaven (MC)—or in the eleventh house (where the Midheaven is found by many frequent calculations), and if the Moon is found there increasing in light, and if she moves thus toward Saturn or is with him, and if Jupiter is positioned exactly in the Ascendant, she makes them happy, blessed,

# BOOK FOUR

...makes them glorious and noble, and decrees the insignias of the greatest power; but it also renders these same individuals entangled in vices and occupied by various illnesses. But if the Sun (☉) is not positioned in the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*</note>, and the Moon (☽) is carried toward Saturn (♄), or is with him, we have demonstrated what that decrees in the previous explanation. 

If, however, positioned in this place and increasing in light, the Moon (☽) is carried toward the Sun (☉) in a daytime birth, or is with him, she will produce powerful people, partisans, administrators, and judges; and if Jupiter (♃) joins them in some association, she grants imperial commands. 

But if Fortune <note>referring here to the Moon as a Bringer of Fortune</note> is waning in light in this place and is carried toward the Sun (☉), or is with him, she will make those born humble and always cast down in their early life, but with the passage of time, she decrees inheritances, glory, honors, and the greatest leadership roles. 

Always, however, if the Moon (☽) is found with the Sun (☉)—whether in this place or in other places of the birth chart and in other signs in the same degree—and has not yet freed herself from the Sun's (☉) association <note>this refers to "combustion," where a planet is so close to the sun its power is obscured</note>, she will involve those who are born in dangerous and humble affairs in their early life, but with the passage of age and after heavy losses, she grants an abundance of substance. 

In all birth charts, it is proper for you to observe the course of the Moon (☽), not only on the day when the human being first enters the tracks of light <note>a poetic phrase for birth</note>, but by diligent reasoning, we must also investigate on the third day <note>The "Third Day" was a traditional Greek astrological technique used to predict the child's viability and early upbringing</note> which star the Moon (☽) joins herself to, or with what radiation; or from whom she is departing and toward whom she is carried. For on that day, the nourishing sustenance is first granted to the newborn. One must therefore inquire on the third day whether she is diminished or full of light, and to what extent beneficial or malevolent stars look upon her. For on the third day, just as on the first, she decrees all things by a similar logic. If these things are collected by diligent inquiry, we can never be disturbed by erratic confusion in explaining the fates of men. Lest anything seem to have been omitted by us, let us explain this treatment briefly at the beginning of the following book.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'P' featuring a foliage pattern and a small animal or figure entwined in the vines.</image-desc> While handling legal defenses <note>original: *patrocinia*; Firmicus refers to his former career as a trial lawyer</note>, I was held by the conflicts of court cases and the quarrelsome battles of—if I may say so—dog-like contention. From this pursuit, nothing else was brought to me day by day except a heap of dangers and a heavy burden of envy. For I always trusted in my upright constancy to resist partisan men, those whom powerless wickedness delighted, those who clung to the wealth of others by the instinct of greedy desire, or those who seemed terrifying to miserable men out of fear of the courts. From this, the spiteful malice of envy and the hatred of wicked men prepared a danger of storms for my virtuous desires. 

Therefore, I abandoned this pursuit, lest by the growing consensus of ignorant and indebted men, I should involve myself in the greatest ambushes and the hazards of the greatest dangers while keeping watch for the benefit of others. While these men were raging against me always and without intermission, and contending with a bitter continuation of hatreds, I exhibited a pure and faithful defense for suffering people and those anxious from various diversities of circumstances by no other means of restitution than a liberal mind, having despised the profits of the forum. 

Now established in leisure and freed from the fights of the battles of the forum, and having also in a way stripped off the snares of envy—with the thick power of spite and plundering (or rather, brigandage) having been left to wicked and treacherous men—I have written these little books to you, Lollianus, released from every care of anxiety. In this way, set apart from earthly conversation, I might apply myself to celestial and divine discussions to cleanse, from whatever part, the vices of the soul which I had contracted from the company of depraved men.

In this book, therefore, that which was in the latter parts of the third book will be explained in the first place...

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...as we promised in the [previous] parts of this book, that is: all the types and forms of the Moon (☽), her conjunctions, her separations <note>original: *defluxiones*; the way the Moon moves away from one planet toward another</note>, and whatever pertains to the power of that deity. We shall also treat with diligent reasoning the Place of Fortune and the Lord of the Birth, whom the Greeks call the *oikodespotes* <note>original: οἰκοδεσπότην; the planetary ruler of the entire horoscope</note>. I shall also explain the efficacy of the planet that decrees one’s actions <note>referring to the *Lord of Profession*</note>. Furthermore, I will show the "full" and "empty" degrees and their decrees, as well as the masculine and feminine degrees. Following this, the Moon (☽) will again receive the final sections. 

For all the things that Mercury (☿) and Aesculapius <note>The god of medicine, often associated with Hermetic wisdom</note> handed down to Enichnus <note>Likely a reference to Enoch/Hanokh</note>, which Petosiris and Nechepso <note>Legendary Egyptian pharaoh and priest-astrologer credited with the foundations of Hellenistic astrology</note> explained, which Abraham, Orpheus, and Critodemus published, and which all the other masters of this art have produced—we have read, collected, and compared these across their various conflicting opinions and written them down in these books. We are making this divine science known to all Romans so that I might explain what seemed most difficult to some—due to the narrowness of the Latin language—by demonstrating the freedom of the Roman tongue through true and clear interpretations. 

Therefore, we promised to explain all the courses of the Moon (☽) at the beginning of this book, and what she decrees and by what logic. For the entire substance of the human body pertains to the power of this deity. For after the vital aura has received the perfected human being and the spirit of the divine mind has infused itself into the body, the Moon (☽) sustains the form of the composed body according to the quality of her course. Thus, we must gather her movements with prudent inquiry so that we can explain the entire substance of the human body. For the nature of man cannot otherwise stand firm unless his body has been fabricated with a strong defense to support life. 

However, those people err who think that only the life and the logic of the spirit should be treated in all birth charts—that is, the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*</note> and the Midheaven (MC). For while the substance of life and the spirit are found from these places, we must also find the course of the Moon (☽) by degree through wise and skillful inquiry, alongside the Ascendant and Midheaven. 

For God, the Fabricator of man, when he composed this living being with divine and singular artistic reason, bound the divinity of the immortal soul with the chains of a mortal and earthly body. He did this so that the soul, diffused within and bound by the command of a great necessity, might govern the falling fragility of the body that serves it through the license of divine power. Therefore, the soul will not have a sound receptacle, nor can it connect itself to its surroundings, nor explain the substance of its own divinity, unless the body has been strengthened with an intact and uncorrupted framework for the reception of the soul. Thus, the soul and body are joined by an equal logic of necessity, sustaining each other with the powers and strengths of their own nature, so that they might manifest the human being—composed of a society of divine and earthly union—as a perfected work in complete appearance and form.

<margin>The power of the Moon.</margin> Wherefore we ought to know what the Moon (☽) has undertaken regarding the human body, and what has been assigned to her powers. For we feel both the increases of the waxing Moon (☽) in our bodies and the losses of her failing light. For the marrows of the human body grow when the Moon (☽) waxes; but when she begins to be empty and deprived of light, they languish with the fatigue of a thinned body. The human body even declines as the Moon (☽) declines, and is again cleansed by the solemn completions of the waxing Moon (☽). 

Thus, every substance of the earthly body is governed by the providence of that deity. Located in the lower regions of the heavens and having obtained dominion over the Earth by her proximity, she sustains all bodies that are animated by the inspiration of the divine mind through the manifold variety of her course. She runs through all the signs with hurried speed and joins herself to all the stars in constant conjunctions. Because of this, the substance of the composed work is changed—integrated from contrary mixtures and from disparate nourishments—so that she both procreates all bodies of living things at conception and dissolves them once they are born. 

Therefore, we must work hard, and in every birth chart, we must greatly seek out that substance in which the Moon (☽) is established. For as much as she transfers herself with swifter motions and joins herself to all the stars with a faster speed than any other, so much more must we gather her course with more diligent contemplation. For the first day and the third day decree by that same similar logic; the seventh and the eleventh days also demonstrate the substance of the entire life through the Moon (☽). Furthermore, the Lord of the Birth and the Giver of Life are found from the conjunctions of the Moon (☽); even the final day of life is learned from the calculations of the Moon (☽). 

Moreover, the Lord of Time, whom the Greeks call the *chronokrator* <note>original: χρονοκράτορα; the planet ruling a specific period of a person's life</note>, is demonstrated to us by the Sun (☉) and Moon (☽). For in nocturnal birth charts, she herself takes up the beginning and the lordship of the times...

### BOOK FOUR

...in day charts, however, we look to the Sun (☉). We will explain its nature and where it is beneficial in later books; although we have spoken of many types and forms in the book of its instruction, we shall now briefly set these same things forth again. For everything that is more difficult, we ought to mention more frequently, so that through repeated handling we may more easily master these difficulties. The Moon (☽) is therefore either synodic <note>original: *synodica*; in conjunction with the Sun, i.e., a New Moon</note>, or full, or halved <note>original: *dichotomos*; the first or last quarter</note>, or crescent-shaped <note>original: *monoides*</note>, or gibbous <note>original: *amphicyrtos*; convex on both sides</note>, and through these changing forms she completes the monthly course of her light. Therefore, these increases or losses of her light, and the changing appearances of her various forms, must be diligently inspected—first when treating the birth on the day of birth, and again on the third day—noting which planets she joins and from which she flows away <note>original: *defluat*; the "separation" of the Moon from a planet it has just passed</note> or recedes, and to what extent she associates herself with secondary conjunctions after the first, and even which ones she joins by moving ahead of them. We must observe when she is carried through the heights, which stars she regards with a trine <note>original: *trigonica*; 120 degrees apart</note>, a square <note>original: *quadrata*; 90 degrees apart</note>, or an opposition <note>original: *diametra*; 180 degrees apart</note> radiation; when and to which stars she is carried while full or while diminished in her lights; and how she is joined to the stars of her own condition. We must see when, placed in the same part, she joins in a synodic union, and when the Sun (☉) in his orbit seizes and hides her while she is located in those same parts. Thus, with all things explored and treated, we may achieve a full science of pronouncement in the births of men.

->THE APPLICATION OF THE MOON (☽) TO THE REMAINING PLANETS, BUT FIRST<-
->HER MOVEMENT FROM SATURN (♄) TO THE OTHER WANDERING STARS. Chapter 1.<-

<margin>Saturn (♄): The Moon joined with Saturn.</margin>
If the Moon (☽) applies herself to the star of Saturn (♄), and if she joins him in that association while increasing in light, or is carried toward Saturn, she decrees widowhood for the mother and constant pains of the eyes for the woman. She makes the subjects themselves spend their time in the conversations of temples <note>Likely referring to religious devotion or working in temple administration</note>, but she causes the ancestral inheritance to be scattered by various tearings-away; yet again, with the passing course of time, she makes them seek another substance of inheritance for themselves through their own labor. If, however, she is joined to Saturn while failing and diminished in light, she will make the parents either low-born or slaves, or submerged in the squalor of wretched unhappiness. Furthermore, debility will oppress the mothers of some, or she will certainly cause them to perish by a violent death <note>original: *biothanatas*</note> while the subjects themselves are still in their younger years. She also makes the subjects themselves either sickly and weak, or short-lived <note>original: *oligochronios*</note>, perishing by some evil end—especially if she is found in this conjunction in the necessary places of the birth <note>The "angular" houses like the Ascendant or Midheaven</note>, or if they are joined to each other in the Ascendant <note>original: *horos.*</note> by an exact radiation.

<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) applies herself to the star of Jupiter (♃), and joins him in that association while increasing in light, or is carried toward him, she will make men happy, glorious, wealthy, and masters of many great estates and very wide possessions. Those having the Moon in this way even predict the future, either by the internal divinity of their own mind, or by the warning of the gods, or from oracles, or from the venerable discipline of some art. If, however, the star of Mars (♂) regards the Moon placed in this conjunction from a square or opposition, all these things are diminished, with the greatest risk to life. If, truly, she is diminished in her lights in this conjunction, she will make those who are adopted, or those previously exposed <note>Abandoned as infants</note> who are later returned to their parents, and those seeking inheritances for themselves through their own efforts. She produces those who grow in wealth gradually and through the passage of time, and who have the power of some glory. But these things are fulfilled only if Mars (♂) does not see the Moon so placed—whether increasing or diminished—from an opposition or square. But if Mars regards the Moon so placed by the radiation we mentioned, he will produce those who are exposed and pressed by the burden of perpetual slavery, or he will cause them to be procreated by a slave mother or a weak one; or they themselves will certainly be weak in some part of the body and will be burdened by the wretched weights of unhappiness—especially if Mars regards this conjunction in a day birth, or Saturn (♄) in a night birth; but Saturn only when the Moon is diminished and failing.

<margin>Mars (♂)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) applies herself to the star of Mars (♂), and joins his association while increasing in light, or is carried toward him, and it is a night birth, she will make men clever, dangerous, and violent, but who are accustomed to being deceived by frequent calculations, and whose life is enslaved to the greatest dangers. They are, however, effective and accomplish all things, being either dedicated to arms or assigned to athletic contests—especially if they are established in the primary places of the birth. Some, however, will be suffering from some defect. Their mothers will either be taken by debility beforehand, or she will cause them to perish by a violent death. If, however, it is a day birth and the Moon is so joined to Mars, she will make them weak or amputated in every part of the body; for she harms the eyes of some, and the stomach of others with hidden...
