->### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATHERNUS<-

...it weakens them with a continuation of [trials]: some it makes short-lived <note>original: *oligochronios*</note>, or causes them to die a violent death <note>original: *biothanatos*</note>. But all these things it decides according to the specific nature of the signs, and it produces diverse outcomes according to the pivots <note>original: *cardines*; the four most powerful points in an astrological chart</note>, and according to the houses following the pivots <note>original: *anaphoras*</note>; and according to those signs which we have said are alien to the fellowship of the Ascendant <note>original: *horoscopus*</note>, a diverse variety of decrees is found. For in those signs which we have said are alien to the fellowship of the Ascendant—that is, in the sixth or the twelfth place from the Ascendant—if the Moon (☽), increasing in light, joins herself to Mars (♂), it will diminish the marriage and prepare the death of the parents: and with the parents lost, it will cause the person to be exhausted by the miseries of orphanage. For some, the body is cut by the scarring of iron. For others, such wounds arise that no cures can free them except for fiery cauteries <note>branding with hot irons for medical purposes</note>. It grants, however, skills that involve always handling either fire or iron, but it makes others soldiers, who are weighed down by the perpetual burden of military service. 

But in the fifth or eleventh place from the Ascendant, or in the second, or in the eighth, or in the Ascendant itself, if the Moon (☽) is carried toward Mars (♂) in a day birth, it decrees ailments of the sides, a short span of life, and causes violent deaths <note>original: *biothanatos*</note>. If, however, it is in a night birth, and the Moon is carried toward Mars (♂) with her light diminished—in those same places we have mentioned—it will make people great, powerful, terrifying, and effective, who may subjugate the greatest cities by the license of some power, especially if it is found thus in the primary pivots of the birth. If, however, they are found in this way in the principal places of the birth during the day, it dissipates the paternal inheritance and destroys the parents themselves by a weakened or violent death. Nevertheless, it will make them public craftsmen or soldiers, but entangled in illnesses or physical defects, and it frequently decrees the greatest dangers and an end by violent death.

<margin>☽ ☉</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is carried toward the Sun (☉) and joins him in a degree-based aspect <note>original: *partili radiatione*; an exact alignment</note>, in whatever chart it may be, it will make people dangerous, miserable, and cast down from meager resources, prostrated throughout their whole life by the dejection of a humble social standing. Sometimes it makes them convulsive <note>original: *spathicos*; likely referring to spasms or paralysis</note> and those who are contracted by constant ailments and defects: it makes others prone to falling <note>possibly epilepsy</note>, for others it decrees the hardships of alienation, and for many others it decrees insanity.

<margin>♀</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is carried toward Venus (♀), and Venus herself receives the rays of the approaching Moon (☽) by degree, and the increasing Moon (☽) applies herself to a conjunction with Venus (♀), it will make the parents noble and raised up by the power of the greatest authority: but those who are born are separated from the affections of their parents, and it quickly imposes the burden of wretched orphanage. They will certainly always be well-known and noble, those who always succeed in every act and easily obtain all that they desire: and who shine with the greatest honors of power, full of charm and grace. But all these increases will follow in the course of time. 

If, however, the waning Moon (☽) is thus carried toward Venus (♀), it decrees great deeds, the highest honors, and the insignia of great power, and those to whom a great increase of happiness is granted by powerful people from their earliest age: but it causes these people to be defamed by constant rumors. For the Moon (☽) in every configuration of her rising, if she is carried toward Venus (♀), will always make people entangled in the perverse vices of love, and those who because of this are struck by constant infamy—impure, lustful, and always burning with immoderate desire regarding the love of women, and whom incestuous desire always inflames toward wicked unions. For they either debauch their own sisters, or their sisters' daughters, or the wives of their sons, or their step-sons, or they lie with their step-mothers, or they corrupt the concubines of their fathers with hidden desire, or a similar injury is imposed on their paternal uncles through them, especially if Mars (♂) regards this conjunction from an opposition <note>original: *de diametro*</note>. 

For if it is a day birth, and the Moon (☽) is placed in the pivots of the birth and is thus carried toward Venus (♀), and Mars (♂) is found in the setting <note>the 7th house</note> or in the Midheaven <note>original: *MC*; the 10th house</note>, it will cause them to perish by the sword because of these crimes we have mentioned. If, however, in a woman's birth the Moon (☽) is thus carried toward Venus (♀), she will always be impatient with envious braying, one who is roused to promiscuous lusts by depraved desires, and who conceives the vows of incestuous and illicit cravings, always seething with the impure desires of lusts. For she will lie either with brothers or with sons, or with the sons of brothers, or she leads her own paternal cousins, captured by her allurements, or her step-sons to the injury of the marriage bed with a perverse heat of desire, or she joins her own kinsmen to herself, known through debauchery. At other times it makes them masculine women <note>original: *viragines*</note>, especially if Venus (♀) is positioned in cardinal <note>original: *tropicis*</note>, movable <note>original: *erraticis*</note>, mutable <note>original: *duplicibus*</note>, or scaly signs <note>original: *squamosis*; such as Pisces</note> and the Moon (☽) proceeds to her (as we have said) while she herself is also positioned in similar signs. But these people are stirred by a stronger heat, if [they follow] this...

### FOURTH BOOK ###

...course, if Mars (♂) or Saturn (♄) should look upon her with a square or opposite aspect <note>original: *quadrata seu diametra radiatione*; these are geometric angles between planets considered tense or difficult</note>, or if Venus (♀) begins to look upon them with the same aspects. These evils are even stronger if Venus (♀) or the Moon (☽) are situated in the house <note>the zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet</note> of Saturn (♄) or Mars (♂), as we have said, without the helpful testimony of Jupiter (♃), and if they are aspected by Mars (♂) or Saturn (♄) especially by a square or opposite ray.

<margin>Mercury ☿ Moon ☽</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is carried toward Mercury (☿) and joins him by the ray of her course, and if she is full of light, she will make people sensible, ingenious, and orators shining with the highest nobility of eloquence—especially if Mercury (☿) is positioned in favorable places in the birth chart <note>original: *geniturae*</note>, found in his own signs or degrees, and if Jupiter (♃) looks upon him with a trine aspect <note>original: *trigonica radiatione*; a harmonious 120-degree angle</note>. For then, by the merit of their learning and the brilliance of their eloquence, the greatest honors are conferred upon them. Such people, by the power of their eloquence, can restrain the fickle and turbulent minds of a public incited to sedition; they can soothe furious minds and those irritated by the indignations of a lost madness through the freedom of their speech. They will know mathematics <note>original: *computos*; likely referring to astronomical or fiscal calculations</note>, they will know music, they will always practice gymnastics, and they will understand the secrets of celestial and divine debates. From these opportunities, a wealth of glory and the greatest leadership is decreed for them. But if the Moon (☽) is carried toward Mercury (☿) so positioned, with such testimony from Jupiter (♃), she will cause the person to always be placed in charge of the accounts of the treasury or of the people; or she will certainly make them the kind of people to whom property is entrusted for foreign accounting. She will also cause financial dealings to be entrusted to them through constant interactions. However, if the Moon (☽) is carried toward Mercury (☿) [under poor conditions], she will make people malicious, spiteful, wicked, unstable in their desires, wavering in error, and those who multiply all their plans and keep them suspended in wandering doubt; people who change their actions with constant shifts, who deny things entrusted to them, or who desire to make public what is hidden, and who publish secrets entrusted to them, leaving these betrayals to posterity, always deceiving with malicious greed; or those who join in a conspiracy with burglars or thieves, or who are certainly thieves or burglars themselves. But they will surely be weak in body, sluggish, full of vices, and made feeble by sickness brought on by malicious humors <note>referring to the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which ancient medicine believed governed health</note>.

<margin>Moon ☽</margin>
But if the Moon (☽) is so placed that she is carried toward no planet, nor joins herself to any star by her own ray, and no benevolent star occupies the pivots <note>the four most powerful points: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</note>, she will make people poor and failed, those who are destitute of all necessities and to whom the daily supports of life are denied, or who always require the protection of others to sustain life, supporting the narrowness of their poverty through miserable begging. They will be infinitely inferior to their parents. Their body will be weak, sluggish, and consumed by constant thinness. They will also be attacked by malicious humors and fatigued by the constant swelling of wounds; a malicious humor will always slip inside the skin, binding their joints, especially if the Moon (☽) is running through a void—which the Greeks call <term>void of course <note>Greek: *κενόδρομον* (kenodromon); a Moon that makes no major aspects to other planets before leaving its current sign</note></term>—and is struck by Saturn (♄) or Mars (♂) by a square or opposite aspect. 
<margin>void of course</margin>
Or if, running through a void on the third day of the birth, she is struck by the Moon (☽) or Saturn (♄) by the same aspect we mentioned, or if malevolent stars are positioned in the pivots. Truly, if while running through a void she is joined by the aspect of benevolent stars, she will always make the person empty and naked in their early life, fatigued by constant labors. She will also cause them to be shaken by constant accounts of miseries, seeking protection through the greatest sweat and toil; and though she makes them neighbors to happiness, she will cause them to fall again from the highest step in a ruinous dejection. Sometimes, even when they are led to the very top, she does not allow them to grasp full happiness. For by directing her course through various signs, she causes the first part of life to be entangled in miserable and varied cases of misfortune. But when she has shaken the mind and body with a heavy continuation of misfortunes, and broken their youth with many dangers, and dragged them here and there in miserable wandering, then she decrees increases of many goods and the greatest happiness—so that as much as was taken away by misfortunes in the first age, that much happiness is conferred in the later age. But if, while running through a void, she afterwards joins herself to Saturn (♄) or Mars (♂), she will make them unhappy, moon-struck <note>original: *lunaticos*</note>, and prone to falling <note>original: *caducos*; often referring to epilepsy</note>, and those who are depressed by various kinds of unhappiness from the first age to the last. She will also make them poor, miserable, destitute, and those whose bodies are bare because of ill-hanging fates, or guardians of tombs, or those who are shut up in the perpetual punishment of prison.

<meta>This page continues from the previous discussion regarding the Moon's (☽) conjunctions. Having concluded the analysis of how the Moon joins with other planets, the author now transitions into the "defluxion" (separation) of the Moon—how the influence changes as she moves away from one planet and toward another.</meta>

JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

Having explained the conjunctions of the Moon (☽) and shown their significance with diligent care, let our discourse be transferred to another interpretation, lest anything should seem to be overlooked by us in such subtle disputations—especially since the entire substance of our life is gathered from the courses of this very deity <note>The "deity" refers to the Moon, which ancient astrologers believed governed the physical body and daily life</note>.

## THE DEFLUXION OF THE MOON FROM THE PLANETS, TO THE PLANETS, and first the defluxion of the Moon (☽) from Saturn to the other wandering stars. Chapter II.

<margin>The Moon (☽) is carried from Saturn (♄) to Jupiter (♃).</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating <note>original: *defluens*; a term for the Moon moving away from a planetary aspect</note> from Saturn (♄) and joins herself to the star of Jupiter (♃), or is carried toward Jupiter (♃), and if she is waxing <note>original: *crescens*; increasing in light</note> when joined in this society, she will make people wealthy, rich, affluent, famous, noble, and set in charge of great peoples or cities. For to some she grants the greatest inheritances, to others treasures, and to others truly the greatest gifts. If, however, she is waning in light <note>original: *minuta luminibus*; decreasing in light toward a new moon</note>, she decrees no such thing, but makes agents, curators, or those to whom the protection of private property is handed over, and those who dwell in foreign businesses. She also makes pilots, ship-owners, or collectors of taxes, and those whose actions involve the right of leasing around water—yet in such a way that only a small substance <note>meaning wealth or property</note> is conferred to them from these arts.

♂ If the Moon (☽) is separating from Saturn (♄) and joins herself to Mars (♂) while full of light, she decrees ill-health and defects, and will cause one to perish in early youth. If, however, she is waning in light, she decrees torments of long and very great sickness for the mother, and makes her subject to certain defects; but she also strikes the mother with the danger of a "bad death" <note>an "evil death" usually implied a violent or shameful end</note>, such as perishing while constantly vomiting blood. As for the children themselves who are born, she makes them fatigued by the languors of misery and bereavement, or causes their parents to be separated by perpetual dissension. Furthermore, she squanders both the paternal and maternal estate through various tearings-apart, and constantly inflicts wounds of the sword upon them; she decrees such sicknesses that, for the sake of curing them, the remedy of cauteries <note>medical branding or burning of the flesh</note> is applied. She will also cause constant labors in hidden arts, or cause them to fulfill the duty of life while submerged in the pains of long sickness; or she makes them <term>biothanatos</term> <note>original Greek: *biothanatos*; one who dies a violent or unnatural death</note>, perishing by various types of death. For they either perish submerged by floods, or are consumed by fire, or they hang themselves with a noose, or cruelly extinguish themselves by their own hand with a sword.

☉ If the Moon (☽) is separating from Saturn (♄) and is carried toward the Sun (☉), she decrees the greatest misfortunes and the greatest calamities. She also makes people insane, "moon-struck" <note>original: *lunaticos*; believed to be influenced by the phases of the moon</note>, subjects of the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note>, dropsical <note>edema/swelling</note>, or leprous <note>original: *elephantiacos*; likely referring to Elephantiasis Graecorum, a form of leprosy</note>. Indeed, she perpetuates these misfortunes with stubborn persistence, and anyone born under such a constellation is entangled in these snares of calamity until the final day of life.

♀ If the Moon (☽) is separating from Saturn (♄) and joins the star of Venus (♀), and is herself waxing in light, she will make people great, noble, powerful, happy, wealthy, and rich—though indeed cruel in their great power, and lustful, and those who are struck by heavy infamy because of these things. If, however, she is waning in light, she decrees the depraved allurements of loves, or causes one to be entangled in impure and immodest lusts, or decrees shameful acts in constant succession; but nevertheless, she makes these same people seekers and havers of the greatest resources of substance, and those for whom the greatest happiness and power is prepared by the protection of money.

☿ If the Moon (☽) is separating from Saturn (♄) and joins herself to the star of Mercury (☿), and if she is waxing in light, she makes people obscure, hidden, silent, and privy to secret and illicit writings <note>original: *illicitarum literarum*; often referring to magic or forbidden knowledge</note>, or occupied with celestial religions, or interpreting the courses of the stars through skilled calculations. She also makes those set in charge of businesses, public masters of the liberal arts, orators shining with the splendor of eloquence, or physicians adorned with the testimonies of all. If, however, she is waning in light, she either impedes the sound of the voice or dulls the ears; furthermore, the body of those who have this placement wastes away with miserable fatigue. For she makes them melancholic, jaundiced, splenetic <note>suffering from the spleen</note>, consumptive <note>original: *pthificos*; tuberculosis</note>, dropsical, suffering from pleurisy, and constricted by a tumor of the bladder in a narrow passage with bitter discomfort of pain.

## THE DEFLUXION OF THE MOON FROM JUPITER (♃) TO THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter III.

<margin>The Moon (☽) from Jupiter (♃) to Mars (♂).</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from Jupiter (♃) and is carried toward Mars (♂), and if it is a nocturnal birth and a waxing Moon (☽) is thus joined to the society of Jupiter (♃), she makes people great, powerful, and [masters of] cities or very large regions...

But if Mars is positioned in cast-down <note>original: *deiectis locis*; places in the chart where a planet’s influence is weakened</note> places, and the Moon (☽) moves toward him in this way, she decrees the fiery arts <note>Trades involving fire, such as blacksmithing or glassworking</note>; but she makes the individuals themselves humble and abject, and by a frequent reckoning, she decrees illnesses, defects, and the perils of a bad death.

If, however, the waxing Moon (☽) separates from Jupiter (♃) and associates herself with the star of Mars (♂), she will make them outcasts, slaves, weighed down by the wretched burden of beggary, entangled in defects and illnesses, and those whose servitude is similar to captivity, and who lose their life by a violent death.

And if Jupiter (♃) is found in the principal places of the birth chart, and the Moon (☽), diminished in light in a nocturnal birth, separates from Jupiter (♃) and moves toward Mars (♂), she will make judges, generals, and those to whom the highest command of power is entrusted. 

But if Mars (♂) is found in the cast-down places of the birth chart, and if the Moon (☽) is carried toward him as we have described, she will make soldiers, athletes, and those who seek the support of life from fire and iron; or she will make surgeons <note>original: *medicos chirurgicos*</note>. 

If, however, the Moon (☽) is waning by day and, separating from Jupiter (♃), is carried toward Mars (♂), she dissipates the paternal and maternal inheritance, destroys the parents in their early years, and imposes the burden of extreme beggary. Upon others, she inflicts the defect of sharp pain, and makes them sometimes slaves, sometimes captives, and frequently those who die a violent death <note>original: *biothanatos*; from the Greek, referring to one who dies by execution, suicide, or accident</note>; especially if, while the Moon (☽) is running thus, Mars (♂) is found in the cardines <note>term: *cardines*; the four pivotal points or "hinges" of the sky: East, West, Zenith, and Nadir</note> of the birth chart, or in its anaphoras or cataphoras <note>term: *anaphoris* and *cataphoris*; houses that "follow" the angles or "fall away" from them</note>. For then all the things we have mentioned will come to pass if, with Mars (♂) positioned with these, the Moon (☽) joins herself in that association.

<margin>The Sun (☉)</margin>
If the Moon (☽), separating from Jupiter (♃), is carried toward the Sun (☉), she dilapidates the paternal and maternal inheritance through various tearings-away, alienates the children from their parents, and establishes them in long-distance travel. She makes some exiles and others fugitives; upon some she imposes slavery, and upon others the burden of captivity, especially if the Sun (☉) or Moon (☽) is found in the house of Saturn (♄), or with Saturn (♄) himself.

<margin>Venus (♀)</margin>
If the Moon (☽), separating from Jupiter (♃), is carried toward Venus (♀) while waxing or full of light, she will make the parents shine with the noble authority of power, and they will be those who have achieved the greatest influence. However, she forces the child to be alienated from his own people and quickly makes him an orphan; but nonetheless, she also decrees power, glory, and nobility for the person himself. Yet she grants all these things as age progresses, and decrees an increase of the greatest happiness from wives. She also makes them charming, pleasing, and elegant, and those for whom the greatest power is acquired through favor or grace. 

But if the Moon (☽), separating from Jupiter (♃), is carried toward Venus (♀) while diminished in light, and is in the principal or necessary places of the birth chart, she decrees infinite increases of happiness; and the one in whose birth chart she is found thus will be exceedingly fortunate. For she decrees honors, powers, the rods of office <note>original: *fasces*; the bundles of rods symbolizing Roman magisterial authority</note>, the bordered robes <note>original: *praetextas*; the *toga praetexta* worn by high-ranking Roman officials</note>, and the insignia of magnificent power, and those to whom this merit of dignity is conferred by their parents. In the first stage of life, she also decrees dignities and the ornaments of the greatest power, and causes increases of riches and happiness to be conferred upon the wife and women.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
If the Moon (☽), full of light, separates from Jupiter (♃) and is carried toward Mercury (☿), she makes critics <note>original: *criticos*; here meaning those capable of sound judgment or discernment</note>, that is, good, kind, and glorious judges. For they will be either collectors of fiscal payments, or those placed over religious matters, or interpreters of the law. From these opportunities, the greatest happiness and the greatest riches shall be conferred upon them, so that this happiness perseveres through the entire span of life. 

But if, diminished in light, the Moon (☽) separates from Jupiter (♃) and is carried toward Mercury (☿), she will provide the substance of life from litigation, or from some discipline, or from granaries, or from business dealings; or, seeking support from these, they will obtain certain inheritances. Others indeed find things, while others will deny things entrusted to them, so that from that treachery they may acquire for themselves the protections of a patrimony.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
If the Moon (☽), separating from Jupiter (♃), is carried toward Saturn (♄) and is waxing or full of light, she will cause them to be adopted by strangers, or will make them the fathers of others' offspring, or will make them guardians or managers for minors. Others are forced to find children who were exposed or taken away after a long space of time. They will also be always entangled in watery and moist activities, or wandering in constant travels, or sailing for the sake of merchandise, so that the protections of life are prepared for them from that way of living.

### THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM MARS TO THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter IV.

<margin>The Moon (☽) from Mars (♂) to the Sun (☉).</margin>
The Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), if it moves toward the Sun (☉), decrees the greatest vices and illnesses; it grants a short span of time and causes them to die a violent death, and generally decrees the greatest disadvantages of unhappiness. For this position makes some die in foreign and strange lands, while others are weighed down by another kind of death.

The Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), if it moves toward Venus (♀) and is waxing or full of light, will make adulterers, lustful people, lovers, and those always devoted to the desires of Venus (♀); because of this, they are entangled in frequent cases of danger. Furthermore, they will practice the arts of pigments and spices, or of stones and pearls, and they will frequently become dyers from this association with the Moon. They will also deal in the commerce of the same metal <note>Likely copper, associated with Venus, or iron, associated with Mars</note>, and will become innkeepers according to the quality of the signs, or they may prepare those things which are necessary for food or drink in famous and public trades.

If the Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), diminished in light, is thus carried toward Venus (♀), it will make them effective, blessed, and happy; but women will certainly solicit and take away the riches of these men. It will also make them wealthy, but through the wives of others, from whom the greatest marks of happiness will be prepared for them. For through these women, they will be honored with the greatest distinction of dignity, especially if this occurs in a nocturnal birth; but it will make them hardworking and occupied with various tasks, and people who are struck by frequent infamy on account of sexual matters, and whom the dishonest vows of promiscuous lust always solicit.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
The Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), if in a nocturnal birth it is full of light and moves toward Mercury (☿), it will make soldiers and athletes, sometimes glorious ones; it will cause others to be placed in charge of public and glorious offices. But they will be great and malicious men, whose greed grows every single day toward every crime. For they will be either executioners or scouts <note>original: *spiculatores*; soldiers acting as bodyguards or executioners</note>, and those to whom public authority commits the license of bringing charges. 

But if the Moon joins this association by day and is full of light, it decrees the disadvantages of a wretched condemnation, so that they are forced to undergo the sentence of a judge, and they become victims of a violent death from that condemnation. 

If indeed the Moon is waning in light in a diurnal birth, separating from Mars (♂) and moving toward Mercury (☿), it decrees one immersed in infinite greeds. For it makes muggers and robbers, but those who, caught in that crime, are punished by the severe animadversion of a judge. Others are crushed by the ruin of falling roofs; others pass from the course of a right life to infamy. 

If, however, the Moon is waning in light in a nocturnal birth, it will make prison governors, guards of the watch, and those who acquire the substance of an inheritance for themselves from this office. They will certainly be lovers of ships and athletes, and those who attend to four-footed animals with constant duties; nevertheless, they will have defects and be overwhelmed by the constant disadvantages of dangers.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
The Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), if full or waxing, moves toward Saturn (♄), it makes people slow, lazy, and those who can profit in no actions; they achieve nothing of what they desire. It renders the mother either a widow or entangled in vices and illnesses; but it also kills her by the end of a bad death. It dissipates their own inheritance with constant tearings-away; it causes them to be entangled in "watery" defects <note>original: *aquarijs... uitijs*; likely referring to dropsy or edema</note>. 

If, however, the Moon is failing in light and separating from Mars (♂) and moving toward Saturn (♄), it decrees famous sicknesses and illnesses. For it makes those who are "moon-struck" <note>original: *lunaticos*; often referring to epilepsy in this period</note>, those suffering from hemorrhages, the lame, the paralyzed, the hunchbacked, and the short-lived <note>original: *oligochronios*</note>; or if it is none of these, it causes a violent death. It kills the mothers or fathers of some beforehand, oppressed by the quality of woods <note>Possibly a reference to building materials or specific types of accidents</note> or by defects, or it causes them to die a violent death.

<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
The Moon (☽) separating from Mars (♂), full or waxing in light, if it moves toward Jupiter (♃) in favorable places of the birth chart, makes men rich, leaders of an army, powerful, imperial, and those who are terrifying for every reason, or those who possess provinces and cities by the power of their authority. They will certainly be rich, wealthy, moneyed, and those who achieve everything they wish by the easiest means, and who are victors in the conflict of every struggle,

## THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM THE SUN TO THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter V.

<margin>The Moon (☽) is carried from the Sun (☉) to Venus (♀).</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Venus (♀), and it is a daytime birth <term>diurna genitura: an astrological chart for a birth occurring between sunrise and sunset</term>, it will make the individuals sterile and unable to produce offspring, and they will find it difficult to be joined in marital affection. For they marry either sterile women, or old women, or handmaidens, and take these same sterile women as wives; or they seek out shameful and miserable intercourse with boys, which results in the lineage of children being denied to them forever. They will surely be bound by perverse vices of love, or devoted to impure and shameful desires, and always occupied in servile studies and acts. Nevertheless, they acquire excessive wealth, seeking the greatest support for life through their own efforts, and they are those who follow increases in happiness as time passes. 

But if at night the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Venus (♀), it decrees many wives and makes the children common <note>Perhaps meaning popular or relatable</note>, grateful, accepted, and involving themselves in great deeds; it also decrees great wealth. For they will be noble, shining with the greatest splendor of glory. It will also make them imperious, powerful, rich, and those upon whom the greatest happiness is conferred: especially if none of them is struck by Saturn (♄) through a square or diameter radiation <term>aspects: geometric angles between planets; squares (90°) and diameters/oppositions (180°) were usually considered challenging or harmful</term>. However, these happinesses and honors are only decreed if this conjunction occurs in the necessary places of the birth chart <note>referring to the "active" or "pivotal" houses like the Ascendant or Midheaven</note>.

<margin>Mercury (☿)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Mercury (☿), and it is a daytime birth, it makes individuals dangerous in their life and actions, possessing bad morals, always perverse through sacrilegious error, and denying divinity—men who would even deny things entrusted to them. But if at night the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Mercury (☿), it makes them public scribes <note>original: *tabelliones publicos*; legal scriveners or notaries</note> and those who seek their life's support from letters. They will, however, be honored in their cities because of this study, and will be preferred by the judgment of all over all other men of the same business. Frequently, however, if Jupiter (♃) regards them with a trine radiation <note>a harmonious 120° angle</note>, they undertake the care and protection of the city. They will be inventors of difficult literature or of some wisdom, or devoted to celestial religions, and those to whom the secrets of divinity are entrusted; or they will cling to the activities of hidden writings or illicit things. Others find hidden things, and to others a secret inheritance is conferred, provided that Jupiter (♃) and Saturn (♄) are both absent from this association.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Saturn (♄), and it is a daytime birth, it dissipates the patrimony, divides the parents, and imposes the hardships of wretched bereavement <note>original: *orbitatis*; the state of being an orphan or childless</note> upon them. But in the process of time, it decrees for them the greatest abundance of substance, grants increases of great happiness, and bestows the lordship of many estates. But if at night the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Saturn (♄), it decrees bereavements, diminishes patrimonies, and decrees the hardships of unfortunate travels. It also creates grave vices and serious illnesses, or causes them to be entangled in cases of grave and violent dangers, from which they are scarcely preserved.

<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Jupiter (♃), and it is a daytime birth, it bestows insignias of fortune and happiness from the parents. For some will obtain regions, some the greatest cities, and some will be adorned with happiness beyond the measure of benefits. But if at night the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Jupiter (♃), it will make them those who acquire the substance of wealth through themselves, but who are devoted to constant travels. It deceives these people in their first youth, but when they have advanced in age, they attain glories, good and suitable recommendations, and the supports of wealth.

<margin>Mars (♂)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Mars (♂) in a daytime birth, it strikes down the parents with a swift death, so that the one born is weighed down by the burden of bereavement. Indeed, the parents frequently perish by a violent death <note>original: *biothanati*; an astrological term for those who die by execution, suicide, or accident</note> due to this conjunction. For those born, it decrees a defective blindness of the eyes, or makes them weak with an amputated part of the body, or kills them in their first age; or if it does none of these, it still makes them die a violent death. But if at night the Moon (☽) is separating from the Sun (☉) and moving toward Mars (♂), it makes them violent, cruel, and those who always commit dangerous crimes; or it makes them entangled in vices or illnesses. Nevertheless, it decrees public acts and military service, or makes glorious athletes: especially if Mars (♂) and the Moon (☽) are in necessary...

->THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM VENUS TO THE OTHER<-
->planets. Chapter VI.<-

<margin>The Moon (☽) from Venus (♀) to Mercury (☿).</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) and, while waxing or full of light, is carried toward Mercury (☿), it creates defenders or agents of noble women, and those who, through the protection of women, receive some rank of promotion. They will, however, be either dyers, or pearl-merchants, or inventors of weapons, and frequently renowned musicians, or doctors, or leaders and masters of athletes; but they will be lustful and subject to constant desires for love affairs—yet they will be pleasing and lovable regarding sexual unions. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) with its light diminished and is carried toward Mercury (☿), it decrees vices, impurities, and illnesses; it will also create various and manifold occupations. For it will make either orators, or torturers, modelers <note>original: *plastas*; those who work with wax or clay</note>, and sculptors, or pigment-makers and discoverers of colors, or pharmacists, or tavern-keepers, and those who undertake the care and anxiety of other people's pleasures.

<margin>Saturn (♄)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) and, while waxing and full of light, is carried toward Saturn (♄) in a nocturnal birth chart, it will give a wife of advanced age, or it will bring a public woman to the companionship of the marriage bed, or someone from among the relatives; it happens in such a way, however, that through the protection of the spouse, the individual attains a leading place of honor, increases in dignity, and the marks of promotion. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) while full of light in a daytime birth and is carried toward Saturn (♄), it makes those devoted to the worst cravings of lust and to vicious pleasures, and those who are struck by frequent infamy because of their lustful acts. They will surely be base, wandering, and miserable in their servile lowliness, becoming lessors of prostitutes or certainly their pimps. If this is the birth chart of a woman, she will be a public prostitute and one who seeks the means of life in a public place through the loss of her bodily modesty. 

If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) in a nocturnal birth with its light diminished and is carried toward Saturn (♄), it will create either sterile men, or eunuchs, or high priests of Cybele <term>archigallos: the chief eunuch-priests of the goddess Cybele</term>, or hermaphrodites; or certainly those who are forced by the heat of wretched lust to endure womanly roles. They will therefore be short-lived <term>oligochronij: a Greek term for those with a brief lifespan</term> or die by violence. 

If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) with diminished light and is carried toward Saturn (♄) during the day, it will make them vicious and weak, and those whom a malignant humor always plagues. It will give occupations involving water, but it will cause them to be exhausted by miserable continuations of labor. For they will either be forced to lift water from deep wells by daily work, or they will be ordered to constantly clean pits and sewers, or they will be gardeners—but miserable and poor—or sailors, or water-carriers, or fishermen, or hunters. But the changing quality of wood will frequently provide these occupations <note>This likely refers to working with timber or in forests</note>. It will make ox-drivers, herdsmen, water-carriers, and shepherds, and those who are ordered to purge or clean the stables of beasts of burden. It also frequently makes guardians of tombs, or even undertakers <term>pollinctores: those who prepared a corpse for burial by washing and anointing it</term>, who undertake the care of those to be buried by the judgment and consent of everyone. But the stars decree these things according to the variety of the places or signs, about which we have also spoken most fully in other astrological interpretations <note>original: *apotelesmatis*; the effects or outcomes of the stars</note>.

<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) and is carried toward Jupiter (♃) while waxing in light, it will make men who are great, powerful, noble, and placed in charge of cities; it makes some of them be raised up by the protection of women. They will surely be pleasing, charming, lovers of women, and those who, by the grace of their charm, attain everything they desire. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) with diminished light and is carried toward Jupiter (♃), it will give support for their resources from women, and it will render them as people whose parents are granted the grace of happiness and glory from their earliest age. For to some it will give inheritances, others it will compel to find the greatest profits, or it decrees honored offices of sacred rites in temples.

<margin>Mars (♂)</margin>
If the Moon (☽) is separating from Venus (♀) in a daytime birth and is carried toward Mars (♂), and the Moon (☽) is full of light or waxing, it decrees the destruction of a miserable calamity by the impulse of a lover; because of this, it indicates a heavy crisis of dangers, such that it leads both to the custody of prison and to the crime of condemnation, and those who perish on account of this by a violent death. It will cause others to be plundered,

->THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM MERCURY TO THE<-
->other planets. Chapter VII.<-

<margin>The Moon (☽) from Mercury (☿) to Saturn (♄).</margin>
If the Moon (☽), separating from Mercury (☿) while full of light, is carried toward Saturn (♄), and it is a diurnal birth, it makes them either always stammerers, or deaf, or it will hinder their words with a slow sound of the voice. They will, however, have occupations either from accounting, or teaching, or from business, or travels, or from the interpretation of words; some always suggest heavenly secrets, others take up the care and protection of prison guards, so that from these occupations the supports of life may be sought for them. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Mercury (☿) by night, full of light, and is carried toward Saturn (♄), it will cause one to be always fatigued by constant labors around water, and will render workers devoted to everlasting labors, and those who are accustomed to hire out their body for some work, seeking the supports of life with laborious shoulders and backs. It places others in custody, thrusts others into prison, opposes others to public trials, condemns others, and will cause others to perish—oppressed, defiled, and deformed by the filth of prison and the squalor of public guards—especially if this conjunction occurs in the signs of malevolent stars. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Mercury (☿) by day with diminished light and is carried toward Saturn (♄), it will make doctors, poor people covered in rags, and those submerged in the wretched calamity of want. It makes some serve in temples, and compels others to wander. It frequently makes people "moon-struck" <note>original: *lunaticos*; likely referring to epilepsy or mental illness thought to be influenced by the moon</note>, or those oppressed by the vices of sacred illnesses <note>original: *sacrarum ualetudinum*; a common historical term for epilepsy</note>, also those who are falling and insane with wretched commotion. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Mercury (☿) by night with diminished light and is carried toward Saturn (♄), it either causes one to be exposed <note>abandoned as an infant</note>, or imposes the squalor of wretched slavery, or indicates the burden of bitter captivity; it also decrees the greatest illnesses and vices, or kills in the first age of time, or will cause one to be condemned for some reason; but if none of these occur, it nevertheless causes them to die a violent death.

<margin>Jupiter (♃)</margin>
The Moon (☽) separating from Mercury (☿), if it is carried toward Jupiter (♃) while full of light, will make people great, powerful, and those to whom the letters and secrets of emperors are entrusted, or those who guard royal wealth and treasures with the protection of good faith, or those who have the power of commanding or arranging in a royal house; it also makes many masters and messengers of kings, temple-wardens <term>neocoros: a Greek title for an official in charge of a temple</term> also, or prophets, or leaders of priests. From these honors or opportunities, the greatest marks of happiness are conferred upon them, and from these acts they acquire increases of powerful riches. If, however, the Moon (☽) is separating from Mercury (☿) with diminished light and is carried toward Jupiter (♃), it either puts them in charge of accounts, or causes them to be managers of money-lending businesses <note>original: *fœnorum negociationibus*; the business of high-interest loans</note>, or it makes agents and such people to whom public or fiscal documents are entrusted, or it puts them in charge of public or fiscal weights, or it makes judges of private disputes; or from these acts it decrees the greatest increases of means and grants great marks of happiness,

When the Moon (☽) is separating from Mercury (☿), if in a **diurnal** <note>original: "diurna genitura," a birth occurring during the day</note> birth it is carried toward Mars (♂), and the Moon is waxing or full of light, it makes people who are irreligious, perjurers, and deceivers, whose malice grows toward every crime day by day. For they will be housebreakers, thieves, and those who always plunder the temples of the gods with sacrilegious fury. They will be bandits, murderers, and always armed for the slaughter of men. But when caught in these crimes, they are handed over to the bonds of custody and prison, and are punished with the sword by the severe sentence of a judge, or they perish by some other kind of violent death <term>biothanata: a Greek-derived term for a death caused by violence, execution, or suicide rather than natural causes</term> on account of these deeds. 

But if it is a **nocturnal** <note>a birth occurring at night</note> birth, and the Moon is full or waxing while separating from Mercury and carried toward Mars, it will produce leaders, tribunes, and soldiers—but terrifying ones, elevated by tyrannical powers—or governors of cities, or defenders, or those who never persist within the license of just powers, but who always cause offense in various ways. Of these, some are turned

into flight, others are sent into exile, and others indeed perish by a violent death, especially if Mars and the Moon are found in the principal places of the birth chart. 

If indeed the Moon is separating from Mercury in a nocturnal birth while full of light and is carried toward Mars in the **dejected places** <term>deiectis locis: houses in an astrological chart considered weak or unfavorable, such as the 6th, 8th, or 12th</term> of the birth chart, it decrees the commission of parricidal crimes <note>In Roman law, "parricidium" referred to the murder of any close relative, not just a father</note>. For either they kill their own children in a parricidal madness of fury, or the fury of perverted greed drives them to the murder of brothers, or a parricidal end is brought upon parents through them; or they slaughter their own kinsmen, or, turned against marital affection, they pollute the marriage bed with the blood of a mangled spouse, so that in every way they range about in parricidal insanity by various instincts of fury. But these things are decreed according to the variety of the places and signs. Their death indeed will always be violent and afflicted. For either on account of slaves, or on account of persons reduced to custody, or on account of condemned men, a grave crisis of danger is brought upon them; and because of this, having been more often condemned, they perish by a public execution. 

If, however, the Moon is diminished in light in a diurnal birth, separating from Mercury and carried toward Mars, it will make forgers, sorcerers, housebreakers, thieves, or accomplices and receivers of bandits; for which crimes they are either placed in custody or condemned by a severe sentence. Others also become public executioners, to whom the duties of public punishment are entrusted, or scribes for personal legal cases, so that they handle such duties, or they become assistants to such condemned men, or they become guards of the public prison from this conjunction. 

If the Moon is diminished in light, separating from Mercury and carried toward Mars in a nocturnal birth, it will designate either soldiers, guards of arms, athletes, or those destined for certain contests. It will also make them effective, terrifying, and famous, and those whose duty reaches the knowledge and shores of all the most celebrated people. But if Mars or the Moon is positioned in the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> or in the fifth place from the Ascendant, it will cause them to be extinguished by some violent kind of death. In the other places of the birth chart, however, it decrees vices of health, dangers, laborious acts, constant vigils, or certain violent businesses. 

But all these things (as we have frequently said) vary according to the diversity of the signs. For in **tropical signs** <term>signs marking the solstices and equinoxes: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</term>, with Mars so positioned, if the Moon separating from the Sun or Mercury is positioned in the signs of malefic stars <note>Saturn and Mars</note> and is carried toward him by opposition <note>180 degrees apart</note> or quartile <note>90 degrees apart</note> aspect, or if it joins him in a nearby or exact degree, it will make tanners, leather-workers, boot-makers, cooks, smiths, and those completing their arts and duties by fire or iron. 

If indeed this conjunction is in the signs of Venus (♀), it will make linen-weavers, dyers, molders, or tavern-keepers. If, however, this conjunction is in the house of Mercury or Mars, it will make lovers of arms or the wrestling-ground, and those handling the duties of public business. If indeed this conjunction is in the house of Jupiter (♃), it will make tribunes, leaders, or commanders of great legions, or governors of cities. If indeed this conjunction is in the house of Saturn (♄), it decrees heavy and wretched or wicked duties: for it will make either torturers or executioners; or informers, or hunters of wild beasts, or such **Marsi** <note>The Marsi were an ancient Italian people famous for their skills as snake-charmers and healers</note> who are accustomed to hunt asps or wild cattle, or masters of beasts. It will also make others fishermen or bird-catchers; others from very deep wells...

When the **Moon (☽)** is separating from **Saturn (♄)**, if it be carried toward the **Sun (☉)**, it makes them either mentally captive <note>insane or cognitively impaired</note>, or impeded in tongue <note>a speech impediment or stutter</note>, or deaf, or poor, and always weighed down by the miserable filth of poverty; also always wanderers and foreigners, and those who never establish a seat or home for themselves. When the **Moon (☽)** is separating from **Saturn (♄)**, if in a **nocturnal birth** <note>a birth occurring at night</note>, and the Moon is full of light, and it be carried toward **Venus (♀)**, it causes them to have foresight in public affairs, in which they always find the leadership of glory; it also decrees increases of great happiness. For it makes some orators, adorned with an abundance of speech; others poets, whom it ennobles with the authority of divine songs: others it establishes in the service of the gods or emperors with a constant continuation of honors: others truly it leads to happiness and power with the grace of charm, through the influence of important persons and the recommendations of women, or from certain feminine activities. 

If indeed the **Moon (☽)**, separating from **Saturn (♄)** and being full of light, be carried toward **Venus (♀)** during a **diurnal birth** <note>a birth occurring during the day</note>, it will make either sellers of spiced pigments <note>perfumers</note>, or discoverers of colors or medicines, or of precious stones, or those making precious tunics by their art, or makers of musical instruments, or pantomimes, or those who adapt themselves to every kind of dance, or those who delight others with a sweet voice: but nevertheless they are mediocre in life, being those who neither abound in resources nor are weighed down by the narrowness of necessities. If indeed the **Moon (☽)**, diminished in light <note>waning</note> in a **nocturnal birth**, separating from **Saturn (♄)**, be carried toward **Venus (♀)**, it makes them rich, powerful, imperial, and great, and those to whom the protection of regions or greatest cities is entrusted, especially if the Moon is found in the sign of the **horoscope** <term>horoscopus: here referring to the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and is freed from the rays of the **Sun (☉)**, and if **Venus (♀)** in a similar way, freed from the rays of the **Sun (☉)**, has received the course of the incoming Moon in the places we have mentioned. 

If indeed this conjunction <note>planetary configuration</note> should be in other places of the birth-chart, it will make them honorable and those conducting much business, and who seek for themselves the substance of an inheritance by their own strength. 

If indeed the Moon is carried toward **Venus (♀)** by day, diminished in light, and this conjunction is in the **bottom of the sky** <term>imum coeli: the lowest point of the chart, the 4th house</term> or **middle of the sky** <term>medium coeli: the highest point of the chart, the 10th house</term> or in the tenth place from the horoscope, it bestows the palms and crowns of sacred contests, or makes them overseers of sacred contests, or builders of temples, or consecrators of statues, or certainly temple-wardens <term>neocoros: a Greek term for an official in charge of a temple</term>, or chiefs of priests, or those handling great duties in temples.

It also makes turners <note>lathe workers</note>, or sculptors or makers of statues, or those chanting sacred songs in temples, or temple flute-players, and those who have a notion of heavenly things, or who know heavenly secrets, or who learn hidden and secret things by easy reason, so that from these occasions the supports and helps of life are thoroughly sought for them.

### THE SEPARATION OF THE MOON FROM ALL PLANETS,
### toward none. Chapter VIII.

When the **Moon (☽)** is separating from **Saturn (♄)**, if it be carried toward no other planet, but directs its course through the void <note>This refers to the Moon being "void of course," having no upcoming aspects</note>, and the Moon is waxing or full of light, it squanders the inheritance <term>patrimonium: the family estate or inheritance</term> with miserable tearing apart, and causes one to be alienated from parents, or does this in the first age <note>childhood</note> once the parents are slain. It also often renders them lazy, or keeps them occupied in long-distance travels. 

If indeed the Moon be diminished in light, it will cause a constant coldness around the belly, which the Greeks call *phrikokoilian* <term>phrikokoilia: a medical condition involving a chilling or shivering sensation in the abdomen</term>. It also renders them suffering from infinite vices of phlegm, making them thin, splenetic, dysenteric, dropsical, pleuritic, or suffering from difficulty in urination, and those who are tortured by hidden pains. But it decrees these things according to the quality of the signs.

<margin>♃</margin>
When the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is separating from <term>Jupiter (♃)</term>, if it is carried toward no other planet but directs its course through the void <note>This refers to the Moon being "void of course," meaning it makes no further major aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign.</note>, and if it is full of light, it makes people wanderers through constant travel, poor, and those who lose all the ornaments of happiness over the course of time. But if it is waning in light, it makes them abandoned children and captives, whose lives are weighed down by the burden of slavery. Some will be entangled in many vices and illnesses; others become "short-lived" <note>original: "oligochronij," from the Greek for "few-timed"</note> and destined to die in a short time.

<margin>♂</margin>
When the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is separating from <term>Mars (♂)</term>, if it is carried toward no other planet but directs its course through the void, and if it is full of light, it dissipates the family inheritance and kills the parents in the first stage of life; or it strikes them with some defect or the danger of a "bad death" <note>An unlucky, sudden, or violent death.</note>. As for the individuals themselves, it causes them to fall from high places, or decrees great dangers from four-legged animals, as well as defects and illnesses; it makes some die a violent death <note>original: "biothanatos," a term for those who died by execution, suicide, or accident.</note> by public execution. If it is waning in light while separating from <term>Mars (♂)</term> and moving toward nothing, it causes them to be alienated and separated from their kin and scatters their inheritances through various losses, or gives them laborious crafts such as those involving fire and iron, or makes them wretched soldiers.

<margin>☉</margin>
When the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is separating from the <term>Sun (☉)</term>, if it is carried toward no other planet but directs its course through the void, it will make people poor and unhappy, wanderers, vagrants, and those who are always stuck in servile tasks. Others, though aspiring to various deeds, it causes to abandon what they have begun out of various kinds of despair. But over time, the weight of this misfortune is mitigated, and the wretched outcome of the prevailing calamities is partially changed; the burden of poverty being set aside, a small support for life is obtained for them, and they are even compelled to aspire to certain deeds.

<margin>♀</margin>
When the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is separating from <term>Venus (♀)</term>, if it is increasing in light and moving toward no other planet but directing its course through the void, it makes people passive in sexual intercourse and never persisting in the love of their wives, but rather those who always delight in unholy embraces. It also makes these same people destitute, poor, and those who, putting their shoulders to labor, seek daily sustenance. But if it is waning in light, it makes them full of vice, shameful, poor, and burdened by a constant weight of miseries, always involved in dishonest and wretched crafts and deeds.

<margin>☿</margin>
When the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is separating from <term>Mercury (☿)</term>, if it is carried toward no other planet but directs its course through the void, and is full of light, it makes grammarians, orators, doctors, musicians, and those who, by clever calculation, know the courses of the stars as witnesses. It also makes those who handle duties of lending and business, from which they achieve glory and substance, but only over time. If it is waning in light, it decrees defects arising from the "humors" <note>The four bodily fluids thought to control health: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> or indicates a grave danger from waters. It harms the minds of some, binds the tongues of others, and affects the ears of others—making all of them estranged from literature. However, it makes others prophesy, but in temples; it leads others to the eternal guardianship of temples, and makes others their slaves and ministers.

### GENERAL DECREES OF THE MOON, AND THEORIES TO BE NOTED. Chapter IX.

Now all the types of influence must be explained which the <term>Moon (☽)</term> completes with its swift course, so that we may appear to have explained everything both specifically and generally. If <term>Saturn (♄)</term> applies itself to the Moon, it makes the parents miserable. If <term>Mars (♂)</term> joins it, it makes both parents humble but indicates various miseries for the father. If it is carried from the <term>Sun (☉)</term> to <term>Saturn (♄)</term>—that is, if both its sides are occupied by the Sun and Saturn—it acts severely; but if it is carried from <term>Saturn (♄)</term> to the <term>Sun (☉)</term>, it does these same things moderately. It decrees defects for women when <term>Saturn (♄)</term> attacks the Moon with its rays. It makes people "lunatics" <note>Moon-struck or experiencing mental illness.</note> if the figure or shape of the Moon is compared to the likeness of <term>Saturn (♄)</term>, while the <term>Sun (☉)</term>, <term>Jupiter (♃)</term>, and <term>Venus (♀)</term> are in foreign signs. But if <term>Jupiter (♃)</term> and <term>Venus (♀)</term> look upon all these conjunctions or separations (through which miserable ends are decreed for men) with a favorable aspect <note>original: "radiatione," the "rays" or light cast by the planets.</note>, the outcomes of the decreed evils and miserable calamities are mitigated. A person will be happy, even exceedingly happy, and adorned with the brilliance of wisdom along with every happiness, if the Moon joins with the rays of <term>Jupiter (♃)</term> or <term>Venus (♀)</term> (or one of the two) in those places where it "rejoices," without the hostile radiation of <term>Saturn (♄)</term> or the <term>Sun (☉)</term>. For then happiness, then substance, then honors, then all the ornaments of life are decreed. The Moon rejoices in the Horoscope <note>The Ascendant or first house.</note>, or in the fifth, or in the eleventh place from the Horoscope, in conjunction with <term>Jupiter (♃)</term> or <term>Venus (♀)</term>.

...adorned with good actions. But if the <term>Moon (☽)</term> is in the eighth house <note>The eighth house is traditionally associated with death and inheritance.</note> of the birth chart in a nocturnal birth, and in signs in which it rejoices <note>Signs where the planet has "dignity," such as its home or exaltation.</note>, if it is supported by the testimony of **Jupiter (♃)** or **Venus (♀)**, it decrees the greatest happiness. Therefore, whatever topic you wish to treat in the birth chart—whether nature, upbringing, lineage, parents, siblings, marriage, offspring, or the final day of life—you must diligently inspect the Moon’s course, its conjunctions <note>When two planets are in the same degree of the zodiac.</note>, its separations, its latitudes and longitudes, and which planets "receive" her conjunctions.

For in every birth chart we must hope that the **Sun (☉)** does not receive the conjunction of the Moon as she approaches him. For after she departs from the opposition <note>The Full Moon phase.</note> to the Sun and begins to suffer the loss of her light, hurrying toward the conjunction <note>original: "synodum," the New Moon.</note>, she decrees destruction in any configuration of that light, according to the measure of each. If her radiation is strong, she decrees strong evils and the destruction of great misfortunes; if the radiation is middling, the destruction of evils is tempered. But if, failing, she approaches the Sun's rays and is somehow "glued" to his orb and snatched from human sight so that she no longer appears <note>This refers to the Moon being "combust," or hidden by the Sun's glare.</note>, then she decrees more powerful evils and the destruction of all calamities, according to these results <note>original: "apotelesmata," meaning astrological outcomes or decrees.</note> which we noted in the preceding part of this book.

If, however, she is freed from the Sun's conjunctions, and joins herself to **Saturn (♄)** during the day while he is "adding to the numbers of his course" <note>Moving direct and at a normal or fast speed, rather than retrograde.</note>, she decrees increases of great goods and great happiness. But if **Jupiter (♃)** joins her with a similar radiation, the marks of all goods and happiness beyond measure are bestowed. For anyone in whose birth chart the Moon is found with Jupiter in this way will be happy—exceedingly happy.

If, however, she is with **Mars (♂)**, as we said, she decrees the destruction of great evils: for they will be "violently slain" <note>original: "biothanati," referring to those who die by execution, suicide, or accident.</note> according to the nature of the signs. But these evils are moderately mitigated if Mars is found in a feminine sign. 

If she is joined by this radiation to **Venus (♀)** in the <term>Midheaven (MC)</term> <note>The highest point in the chart, representing career and public life.</note>, she decrees a good marriage, especially if she is alienated from Mars in her conjunctions. But if this conjunction occurs in other places of the birth chart, she indeed decrees a good life, but makes them people who mate with their own relatives. If Mars should "see" <note>Aspect or look upon.</note> this conjunction, it decrees illicit sexual acts with wretched desire. 

If, however, this conjunction is with **Mercury (☿)**, it decrees infinite and unheard-of evils with constant affliction. Whence we ought to pray and ask with the highest prayers that the Moon never joins Mercury with such a radiation. 

If during the night, with her light diminished, the Moon joins herself to **Saturn (♄)** while he is retrograde or stationary, she decrees great misfortunes: for some, according to the nature or power of the houses, die a violent death <note>original: "biothanati."</note>. But these misfortunes are mitigated in some part if Saturn is found in a feminine sign. 

If **Venus (♀)** joins her by this radiation at night, she makes them abundant in all goods. If **Mars (♂)** is joined by a similar radiation, it decrees the marks of great happiness; but these effects are made greater if Mars is adding to his number <note>Moving direct.</note>. 

If **Jupiter (♃)** joins her by this radiation, either in the Midheaven, or in the fifth or eleventh house from the <term>Horoscope (Rising Sign)</term>, or in the Horoscope itself, there will be good things concerning marriage, provided Saturn does not strike them with any radiation. They will be even happier if <note>The text here suggests "if retrograde Venus has harmed the principal places," though this may be a scribal error for "has NOT harmed."</note> retrograde Venus has harmed the principal places. 

If **Mercury (☿)** is joined by a similar radiation, it often produces "physicists" <note>original: "physicos," meaning natural philosophers or scientists.</note>; but it decrees stronger goods when this conjunction occurs at night. For the good things are diminished and all evils grow from these stars if it is a diurnal <note>daytime</note> birth.

## CHAPTER X: APPROXIMATE AND EXACT ASPECTS, AND THE INVESTIGATION OF THE LOT OF FORTUNE.

Now that the Moon's course has been explained and shown by diligent reasoning, let the intention of our discourse be transferred to the definition of the promised work—that is, to a brief explanation of **Fortune**. For we cannot explain the whole substance of fate unless this "place" <note>In astrology, a "place" or "lot" is a calculated mathematical point.</note> is collected by the most diligent reasoning. Just as we ask in the Horoscope who is in that place, who is setting, who is in the Midheaven, who is in the bottom <note>The "Imum Coeli" or bottom of the sky.</note>, or who is in the other places, and where the lord of the sign in which the Horoscope is established is positioned—so we must also calculate the "Place of Fortune" by similar reasoning. 

I will show by an easy method in what place it is: when you have found it, you will inspect the associations and radiations of all the planets; then you will be able to explain that whole place with a true and faithful judgment. In every nocturnal birth, therefore, count from the Moon to the Sun...

### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...for a daytime birth, however, from the **Sun (☉)** again to the **Moon (☽)**: and whatever the number of signs shall be, counting that many signs starting from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horoscopo," the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>: and whatever sign holds the final number, that indicates the **Lot of Fortune**. But this is the "sign-based" <note>original: "platica," meaning a general calculation by whole signs rather than exact degrees</note> calculation, which we have set down so that nothing may seem to have been omitted by us. But the Lot of Fortune is gathered by "exact degree" <note>original: "partiliter," referring to precise mathematical calculation</note> by this method, which you ought to follow in every discussion: for then the definition of the outcome will be brought forth from the <term>astrological predictions</term> <note>original: "apotelesmatis," the traditional term for the results or effects of planetary configurations</note> whenever each individual place has been gathered by the method of exact degrees. Thus you will explain life, thus hope, thus brothers, thus parents, thus children, thus health, thus spouse, thus death, thus journeys, or religion, thus actions, thus friends, thus enemies, and thus all other things which are required in the substance of the human race, with true definitions. We shall, however, explain all these things when we come to the interpretation of the <term>Barbaric Sphere</term> <note>A term used for non-Greek (often Egyptian or Babylonian) astrological traditions</note>, which that divine **Abraham** and the most prudent **Achilles** attempted to find by the truest methods and hand down to us. The Lot of Fortune, therefore, of which we have begun to speak, is gathered by degree according to this method.

<margin>How the Lot of Fortune is to be found.</margin>
If you begin to seek the Lot of Fortune while treating a daytime birth chart <note>original: "genituram"</note>, investigate it primarily by this method: Starting from the degree of the **Sun (☉)**, collect the degrees of all the signs up to that sign in which the **Moon (☽)** is, including the degrees of the Moon herself; whatever total the degrees make, adding also the degrees of the **Ascendant** if necessary, collect them. Once these are collected, beginning from the Ascendant, divide this calculation through the remaining signs to the right of the Ascendant, specifically returning ten <note>The Latin says "denas" (tens), though standard practice usually involves increments of 30 degrees; the author may be referring to specific subdivisions or this may be a scribal variant.</note> degrees for each sign: and into whatever sign the final part of the total number falls, that sign will show you the Lot of Fortune and its substance. But in a nocturnal birth, starting from the degree of the **Moon (☽)** and proceeding in a similar way through the following signs up to the degree of the **Sun (☉)**, collect the total degrees of the signs, adding also the degrees of the **Ascendant** if necessary; make one sum of the number, which, starting from the degree of the Ascendant, you will divide through all the signs which follow the Ascendant, assigning thirty <note>original: "triginta"</note> degrees to each sign, as we said: and into whatever sign the final part of the total number falls, that sign itself will thoroughly show you the Lot of Fortune. From this place, moreover, the quality of life, the substance of inheritance, and the course of happiness and unhappiness are shown. Love also, and what the affection of men toward women may be, is learned from this place: the condition of one's upbringing and of one's desires is also sought from the substance of this place. This place also demonstrates the fatherland, or the square sides of that place, by an easy calculation. It is called, however (as Abraham says), the place "of the Sign of the Moon." You should see, therefore, who is the lord of that sign, or who is the lord of this degree—that is, in which planet's <term>bounds</term> <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note> that degree is—and in what place each lord is, both of the sign and of the degree in which the Lot of Fortune was found, and in which places of the birth chart they are established—whether in the principals (that is, in the **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful points in a chart</note>), or in the second places, or in the fallen places, or in their own heights <note>Exaltations</note>, or in their houses, or their depressions <note>Falls</note>: and whether the lord of the sign itself, from that place in which its sign is (that is, the Lot of Fortune), looks upon it by favorable <term>aspects</term> <note>original: "rationibus," referring here to the geometric relationships or "rays" between points</note>, and if both are together in an angular relationship. And then, when you have collected all these things with diligent reasoning, and it is a nocturnal birth, attend again to the degrees of the **Moon (☽)**; if daytime, the **Sun (☉)**: and see who is the lord of the degrees—namely, the Sun in a daytime birth, the Moon in a nocturnal one. See if the lord of the Sun also looks upon the Lot of Fortune itself by an angular radiation. If, however, the lord of all these Sun-degrees is found and is well-placed in the birth chart, both in those signs in which it rejoices, or in those in which it is exalted, or in whose house it resides, it decrees a happy birth. But if the **Sun (☉)** is placed here with the **Moon (☽)** and looks upon the Lot of Fortune, a greater happiness is decreed by the multiplied radiation. If, however, the **Moon (☽)** and **Jupiter (♃)** are returned here, along with the sign-based Lot, and it is established in the angles, even so, happiness is decreed by the multiplied radiation. If the lord of the sign itself in which the Lot of Fortune is located and the lord of the degrees are not one and the same, nor does the lord of the Sun or Moon's degrees hold the primary position, look for the one who has the greatest power in deciding; and if he is benevolent and found in benevolent signs, or in his height, or in his own house, and placed in the principal angles of the birth chart, and sees the Lot of Fortune from an angle, he decrees a great and noble birth. But he does this only if he is placed in the angles by exact degree. For if he is found generally in those places which we mentioned, he decrees a middling birth: so that one is neither happy beyond measure, nor depressed by the narrow straits of poverty. If, however, both...
