...have turned out well, and the lord of the sign itself in which the lord of fortune is located, and the lord of that degree in which the final degree was found, are established in good signs—that is, in places where they rejoice or are exalted, or in their own houses—and are specifically located in the <term>cardinal points</term> <note>original: "cardinibus," the four most powerful angles of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>, they decree such great wealth that the one born under these conditions is equaled entirely to Emperors. If, however, they are found in the signs of the cardinal points not exactly by degree, but generally by whole sign, they decree increases of moderate prosperity. But if the lord of the sign itself <margin><unclear>Place of Fortune</unclear></margin> in which the Place of Fortune is found, and also the lord of that degree—that is, the lord of the <term>terms</term> <note>original: "finium," the specific sub-sections of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</note>—and the lord of those degrees in which the Moon (☽) was found in the same <term>birth chart</term> <note>original: "genitura"</note>, were well-situated, either in their places of exaltation or their own houses, and occupied the principal places of the birth chart, or were placed in those locations where they rejoice, they will create Emperors whose empire is directed across the spaces of the whole world, and whose power is so great that they approach the divinity of the gods. 

If, however, none of those stars mentioned should fall well, the one born thus will be weighed down by the burden of unhappiness until his final day of life. When this is the case, look specifically at the Midheaven (MC) and the sign in the <term>ascension of the horoscopos</term> <note>original: "anaphora horosc.," the house or sign immediately following the rising sign, known as the 2nd House</note>. For if none of the stars mentioned was well placed, and a benevolent star is found in the Midheaven or the ascension of the horoscopos, having followed the power of its own condition, it corrects the misfortunes as time goes on, despite the preceding evil. But if those three mentioned before are badly placed, and no protection of benevolent stars is left in the Midheaven or the ascension of the horoscopos, that birth chart will be unhappy, wretched, and weighed down by a continuation of all evils. But also inquire diligently into the <gloss>spirit</gloss> <note>original: "ὃν δαίμονά," referring to the Lot of Spirit</note> of fortune, lest the sought-after intent of the <term>astrological outcomes</term> <note>original: "apotelefmatum"</note> deceive you.

### THE LOT OF THE DAEMON, DISCOVERED BY EXACT CALCULATION. Chapter XI.

We determine the place of the <term>daemon</term> <note>Often called the "Lot of Spirit," it represents the soul, intellect, and divine will, contrasting with the more material Lot of Fortune</note> by this method, which we have added to this book for this reason: because **Abraham** showed by similar reasoning that the **Sun (☉)** is its source. It was unfair for the place of the Sun to be separated from the place of the Moon (☽). It is gathered in this way: in a daytime birth, collect the degrees of all signs from the Sun's degree to the Moon's degree, and starting from the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>original: "horoscopo"</note>, distribute this entire sum through the following signs; and into whatever sign the final degree falls, it will demonstrate the daemon to you. In a nighttime birth, collect the degrees of all signs from the Moon to the Sun, and distribute all that sum from the Ascendant through the following signs; and whichever sign the final degree falls into will show the daemon. This place is called the "Sector of Action" and the "Substance of the Soul," for from it we find all action and seek the increases of all substance. It also reveals the nature of a wife's affection toward her husband. Furthermore, this place and its <term>square sides</term> <note>original: "quadrata latera," referring to the signs at 90-degree angles to the Lot, which create tension or action</note> demonstrate the fatherland to us by a clear method. See, therefore, if malevolent or benevolent stars look upon this place, and you will know the outcomes explained by the testimonies of the individual stars.

### THE LORD OF THE BIRTH CHART, AND HIS FATAL DECREES. Chapter XII.

<margin>Lord of the birth chart</margin>
Investigate in this way how you ought to determine the <term>Lord of the Birth Chart</term> <note>original: "oikodespotes," the planet that acts as the primary governor of the native's life and longevity</note>: for he himself possesses the sum of the whole birth, and the individual stars receive their decreed diligence from him. If he is well placed—either in the signs where he rejoices, or in those where he is exalted, or in his own houses—and the birth chart is of his condition, and he is neither struck by the harmful radiation of malevolent stars nor destitute of the protection of benevolent stars, he decrees all good things according to the quality of his nature, and likewise a full number of years for the life. If, however, he is hindered by malevolents and deserted by benevolents, all his effectiveness becomes weak and languishes. Therefore, I will explain how you may find him, having first shared all the opinions of the ancients. For some wished to determine the Lord of the Birth Chart by this method, saying that the lord is the one who, placed in the principal places of the chart, is found in his own signs or <term>terms</term> <note>original: "finibus"</note>. Others sought the Lord of the Birth Chart from the Sun and Moon, saying that the lord is the one in whose terms the Sun and Moon were found—that is, so that the Sun has the rationale in a daytime birth and the Moon in a nighttime birth. Still others said that the lord was the one who was found to be the lord of the Moon's latitude. Others indeed said this was the

...the lord of whatever sign the Moon (☽) entered after the person was born, having left that sign in which she was located at the moment of birth. We also follow this reasoning, for it is the truest and approved by all. But it is pleasing to discuss all these things we have mentioned with diligent reasoning, so that you may find what the lord of the <term>birth chart</term> <note>original: "genituræ," the individual's astrological map at the moment of birth</note>, thus positioned, can decree. Because your intent follows this reasoning, we ought also to instruct you with examples. 

For if someone had the Moon (☽) in Aries (♈) at the first hour of birth, because after Aries she makes a transition in the second place to Taurus (♉), Venus (♀) will possess the lordship of the birth chart, because Venus rules the sign following Aries, and so on in the other signs. 

However, we must know this: that neither the Sun (☉) nor the Moon (☽) are made the lords in any birth chart. 
<margin>
The Sun and Moon do not become lords of the birth chart.
</margin>
For they disdain to be allotted a lordship of the total lordship <note>Being the "luminaries" or lights of the sky, the Sun and Moon are considered too high in the celestial hierarchy to serve as the specific planetary "lord" of a chart; they are the sovereigns who delegate power to the five other planets.</note>. Therefore, if the Moon is found in Gemini (♊) on the day a man is born, she will show the lordship of the birth neither in Cancer (♋)—which is her own house—nor in Leo (♌)—which is the house of the Sun (☉). But when she has passed these signs and come to another sign, then she will show the lordship of the birth. Thus, because Virgo (♍) is the house of Mercury (☿), he shall be made the lord of the birth chart. Nevertheless, the Sun and Moon will have a share in the lordship if the Sun holds the <term>bounds</term> <note>original: "fines," specific degrees within a sign traditionally assigned to a planet</note> of a daytime birth, or the Moon holds those of a nighttime birth.

<margin>
Saturn as lord of the birth chart.
</margin>
If Saturn (♄) is found to be the lord of the birth chart and is opportunely placed in the chart, and the waxing Moon (☽) has decreed the lordship to him, he will make men puffed up in spirit, elevated by honors, rarely laughing, and keeping anger for a long time. They will be good men, of good counsel, whose faith is always proven by right judgment, and who complete all business with the reasoning of right judgment; but toward wives and children, they will always be of an estranged affection. They will also be solitary, spending time by themselves, taking little food, but rejoicing in much drinking. 

In body they will be thin, small, pale, weak, of a cold nature, and those who are accustomed to handling food constantly, and whom a <term>malignant humor</term> <note>In ancient medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) that determined health and temperament. A malignant humor implies an imbalance causing illness.</note> attacks. An internal pain collected within will torment them with constant belching. Their life indeed will be malicious, laborious, anxious, and entangled in constant sorrows of the mind; they will find the supports of their life near water or in a watery place. 

But if he, having been made lord of the birth, is either in his own house, or in his own bounds, or in the house of Jupiter (♃) or his bounds, or in the house of the Sun (☉), and it is a place of a daytime birth, he makes them famous and noble in life, and decrees every happiness according to the power of those places.

These evils will be stronger if it is a nighttime birth and if the Moon (☽), diminished in her light, has decreed the lordship to him. For then the head is bared by a thinning of hair, or he makes them bald with hair falling out shamefully, and those whose eyes are hindered by sudden blindness or lose their sharpness by constant <term>suffusion</term> <note>original: "suffusione," likely referring to cataracts or glaucoma</note>. 

He also makes them pleuritic <note>afflicted with lung or chest pain</note>, gouty, <term>falling</term> <note>original: "caducos," meaning epileptic</note>, or spastic—especially if, having been made lord of the birth and placed in that rejection of signs or parts, he has received the rays of a waning Moon. But if benevolent stars reach him while he holds lordship and is positioned as we said, with a good radiation, then either the protection of some god or skillful medicine will cure these ailments. 

But if a malignant star radiates upon Saturn (♄) positioned as we said, these evils we have mentioned are increased with a maximum growth of calamity. He will cause deaths from long and grave sickness, which will be brought about by a faulty flooding of the humors. They will die, moreover, in damp or watery places, or hidden and unknown places. If, however, he is in the house or parts of Mercury (☿), he will make them sorcerers, poisoners, perjurers, and enemies of their own brothers and parents.

Their life will be glorious, notable, and full of happiness; and they will achieve everything whatsoever they desire. Moreover, these people are always adorned with good conversation, and...

## DECREES OF THE SUN AND MOON, WHEN THEY HAVE BEEN
## joined with the lord of the nativity.
### Chapter XIIII.

But we ought to know, as we understood above, that the Sun ($☉$) and Moon ($☽$) never receive the lordship of the nativity <note>In this astrological system, the two "Luminaries" are considered too superior to be ranked among the five planetary "lords"</note>. But when the lords of the nativity have been placed in their <term>bounds</term> <note>original: "finibus"; specific degrees within a zodiac sign governed by a planet</note>, or joined with them by a favorable radiation, or placed in their houses, and they themselves [the Sun and Moon] are established in the bounds of the lord of the nativity, or placed in its houses, and have looked upon its place, beholding it with certain radiations, they also decree that much of their own nature is communicated. And although another may be the lord of the nativity, nevertheless much is conferred by the fellowship of radiation from the Sun and Moon. What therefore the Sun decrees with the lord of the nativity, with an equal power of fellowship, I will briefly explain: what likewise the Moon, placed with the lord of the nativity, constitutes, I will then reach in a brief axiom of speech. For however much each decrees in a determined space of time, we have touched upon sufficiently and specifically enough in the previously tasted book of institutions.

<margin>The Sun with the lord of the nativity.</margin>
The Sun ($☉$), therefore, if it shall be joined by this radiation of which we have spoken with the lord of the nativity, along with the other things which the lord of the nativity has given, also confers these things according to the powers of its nature by its own kindness. For it makes men full of faith, but inflated with a spirit of a certain pride in no small measure: yet wise, and composed with every spirit of moderation of equity, humane, religious, and those who always cherish their fathers with an intact love. It also makes them corpulent, and those whose head shines with yellow hair. It also makes farmers, and those seeking their own patrimonies by their own virtue, effective, prudent, and who always rejoice in the watery delight of regions. It also makes such as those who complete all acts with the greatest honesty. But these will be separated from their wife and from the affections of their children. But it causes vices and illnesses around the eyes and other parts of the body to be frequently burned by fire. But it decrees the outcomes of death in foreign places as violent and public. Yet it increases the time of life if, well-placed, it holds the bounds of the nativity, and if the rays of malevolent stars do not hinder it.

<margin>The Moon</margin>
The Moon ($☽$), if she shall be joined with the lord of the nativity by this radiation of which we have spoken, along with the other things which the lord of the nativity has given, also most bountifully confers these things by her own kindness to the one born, according to the powers of her nature. She also makes men stable, honored, orderly, honest, great in body, but yet a sufficiently proportioned beauty graces the body, taking much food, but rejoicing in little drink. However, their life will be unequal, and will change according to the reason of the times, so that their patrimony is both continually increased and again diminished by continual loss. She also makes them dwell continually in watery places. But toward the wife, and children, and mothers, she always makes their affections prone, and makes them overcome by paternal affections.

### GENERAL APHORISMS FOR THE LORDS 
### OF THE BIRTH CHART. Chapter 14.

When, therefore, the Lord <note>The "Lord" or "Ruler" is the planet that holds the most power in a specific birth chart</note> of the birth chart has been found through a skillful investigation based on the course of the moon, we ought not to look at it alone in a single way, but form a picture from all the temperaments of the stars. For when one star is with another, or when it provides its testimony, it either increases or diminishes everything according to its own nature. For the Lord of the birth chart, instructed by the radiations of others, makes its decree based on each individual star—whichever provides testimony to it—and from the power of the place and the sign: having borrowed this diligence, it composes its own efficacy from the radiation of another. If, therefore, the ruler is malevolent, it is softened by the prosperous radiations of benevolent stars, and the entire malice of its wickedness and evil is changed. Thus, although it may be prepared to do harm out of its own malevolence, nevertheless, through the testimony of good stars, a certain benevolent grace is, in a way, instilled in it, especially if it has been met by the prosperous radiation of all the benevolent stars. For a benevolent star always softens both the sign and the place, even if it is evil. If, therefore, there are many stars in which there is a healing protection, the ruler itself receives the image of a healing will. For it takes up a better desire for deciding if, through the society of good stars, it changes its will to do harm. Then, indeed, misfortunes and heavy accidents are corrected again by prosperous acts: then those accused and placed in heavy dangers are freed either by the sentences of judges or by the indulgences of princes: then, finally, God heals sicknesses, and all evils are suppressed even in the very attempts of misfortune. But if a malevolent star alone receives the license to rule, it rages against the person with bitter continuity, and exercises the strength of its license with the command of great necessity. So, in turn, benevolent stars, if they have not been hindered by the threatening rays of malevolent stars, decree all the ornaments of happiness and dignity. But if the ray of malevolent stars attacks them, they can decree nothing of the promised happiness. Thus, we must always diligently inspect the mixtures and radiations of all; for otherwise the substance of the entire fate cannot be explained, unless all these things have been collected by diligent inquiry. Whether that star, having obtained dominion, is placed in favorable places in the birth chart, or in "lazy" <note>original: "pigris"; referring to cadent houses where planets have less power to act</note> or dejected ones, or whether it is established in its own house or in its exaltation: for from all these things, when they have been composed by diligent comparison, and when you have collected everything from the nature of the stars and signs, and from the powers of the places or <term>pivots</term> <note>original: "cardinum"; the four most important points of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</note>, you will be able to explain this entire topic with the truest and most certain sentences—a topic which contains the whole sum of the birth chart, and shows the end of life and the entire substance of the decree. Therefore, when you begin to treat a birth chart, and have perceived the entire course of the stars with diligent reason, and have seen the power of the places and pivots, and collected everything by specific degree, being placed at the very beginnings of the <term>prognostications</term> <note>original: "apotelesmatum"; the predicted outcomes or results of a chart</note>, you ought to collect nothing else in the first place but the length of life by diligent reason, and frequently inspect the power of the Lord of the birth chart. For even with certain stars being well-ordered, if the Lord of the birth chart decrees a narrow space of living, whatever the well-placed stars had decreed is changed by the premature arrival of death.

# BOOK FOUR

<margin>Septenary years <note>original: "Hebdomatici anni" - cycles of seven years</note></margin>
<margin>The Climacteric <note>original: "Androdas" - a Greek/Egyptian term for the 63rd year</note></margin>
Therefore, one must discuss the span of life with careful reasoning, looking at the Sun (☉), the Moon (☽), the part of the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopi"</note>, and what is most important, the Lord of the Birth Chart <note>original: "domino genituræ"</note>. Although all these matters are discussed scattered throughout this work, they have been specifically included and explained in the individual book which I wrote to our friend Murinus concerning the Lord of the Birth and the Time-Lord <note>original: "chronocratore" - the planet governing a specific period of life</note>. One must therefore labor and seek the Lord of the Birth with all the skill of one’s focus: so that through this, once the life span is found and the division of time among individual stars is assigned by the Time-Lord, we can explain all the decrees of fate. Among other measures, this must be especially observed: that the seven-year and nine-year cycles, running throughout the entire time of life in a multiplied ratio, always affect a person with various crises of danger through a certain natural and hidden reason. For this reason, the 63rd year is called the **climacteric** <note>original: "androdas"</note>, because it receives the sum of both numbers equally: for nine times seven years make 63, and again, seven times nine similarly make 63 years. Therefore, because the course of both numbers meets in an equal ratio in this year, it always imposes a great crisis of danger. For if the seven-year and nine-year cycles—which are called *Septenary* <note>original: "hebdomatici"</note> and *Enneatic* <note>original: "enneatici"</note> by the Greeks—always indicate grave dangers to men, what will the 63rd year do, which completes a sum multiplied by both numbers and bound to one another? For this reason, it was called **androdas** by the Egyptians, because it breaks and weakens the entire substance of life. Therefore, among the other dangers which the malevolent stars decree according to the ascensions of the signs and threatening radiation <note>the "aspects" or rays sent from one planet to another</note>, we must also gather these by careful reasoning: in those dangers, and in these which we gather from the seven-fold or nine-fold ratio of years, we must also inspect the time itself to see what crisis of danger is imminent, and whether the Moon, the times, and the Lord of the Birth are regarded by benevolent stars with an equal radiation. For if Jupiter (♃) and Venus (♀) are found in favorable places in the birth chart, and if they regard the Ascendant and the Moon with an exact radiation <note>original: "partili radiatione" - a precise degree-based aspect</note>, and see the Lord of the times and the birth, they relieve the threatening attacks of dangers with the healing protection of their benevolent stars, and deliver men from imminent perils. Now, the nature of dangers is not of one kind: for the crisis of dangers is brought about either from accusations and delays, or from ambushes and voyages, or from travels and losses, the loss of inheritance, or from sicknesses and "venereal matters" <note>likely referring to sexual scandals or sexually transmitted diseases</note>, and the weakness of the body, or from wild beasts and ruins, or from mud and precipices. Therefore, when you see what kind of crisis is in a place, look (as we said before) at how the Ascendant or the Moon are regarded, or from what place the benevolent stars regard them, and similarly the Lord of the Birth and the times: so that when you are certain about the substance of life, you may then see by what methods the crises of imminent or pressing danger can be avoided. You ought also to look at that star which will stir up the danger—that is, the star in which the Lord of the times is located, in what place or sign and in what parts of the birth chart it is established—and especially then, when it decrees the danger, and similarly to what extent the benevolent stars regard it. For if the star which causes the danger is found in good places, or in those signs and bounds <note>astrological subdivisions of a sign</note> in which it rejoices, and is regarded by benevolent stars and well-placed in the birth chart, it mitigates the crisis of the imminent danger. But if it should be otherwise, and it has received the power permitted to it with the license to do harm, it causes the person to be entangled in the inexplicable snares of miseries, so that the imminent death or danger cannot be avoided by any reason or foresight.

## THE PLANET SIGNIFYING THE ACTS OF OUR LIFE
### Chapter 15.

Now, however, we must investigate which planet decrees whichever acts for individual men, the place of which must be gathered by careful reasoning. There are those stars which decree the acts of men: the Sun (☉), Venus (♀), and Mercury (☿) <note>While the text lists these three, the following paragraph begins with Mars (♂), which was often grouped with them in determining profession</note>. But from these three, that one decrees the acts: which is either in the Midheaven (MC) <note>the highest point of the chart</note>, or in the right trine of the Midheaven, or in the left, or which is found in those angles <note>the "cardinal" points: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, or Lower Midheaven</note> in a person's birth chart.

<margin>Mars decrees the acts.</margin>
If, therefore, Mars (♂) has decreed the acts and is well-positioned and joined by favorable radiation to benevolent stars in a nighttime birth, he gives arms and leadership, decrees glory, the "license of the sword" <note>the legal power to execute or command troops</note>, and the insignia of the greatest powers, insofar as the power of the decree allows: or certainly he makes one famous through bright and noble arts involving fire and iron

<note>The text continues describing the influence of Mars (♂) on a person's career.</note>
...Mars illuminates the individual and, with the clear judgment of nobility, places them ahead in every field of knowledge. However, if he is positioned in sluggish or low-lying places <note>original: "pigris & deiectis locis" - areas of the birth chart where a planet's power is weakened</note>, and in those zodiac signs where he does not rejoice <note>technical term for a planet being in a favorable sign</note>, he decrees certain honest skills, but accompanied by a lack of noble status. But if, with Mars so positioned, the benefic stars <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> lend him their rays, they decree both a certain glory and material resources from whatever career or work was assigned. If, however, Mars is abandoned by the benefic stars, yet still holds the power of decreeing the person's actions, and the malefic stars <note>Saturn</note> regard him, he will make the subjects hard-working and industrious, but they will be the type who spend more on the necessities of life than they actually earn from their labors.

<margin>♀ <note>Venus</note></margin> If **Venus** (♀) should decree the person's actions, and it is a daytime birth, and she is in her own house or her own <term>bounds <note>original: "finibus" - specific degrees of a sign ruled by a particular planet</note></term>, or positioned exactly on the <term>Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopo"</note></term>, or in the <term>Midheaven <note>original: "MC" or Medium Coeli</note></term>, or in the 11th or 5th house from the Ascendant, or in those places where she rejoices, she decrees great actions and the symbols of great glory. This is especially true if **Jupiter** (♃) regards her from a <term>trine aspect <note>original: "trigonica radiatione" - a favorable 120-degree angle</note></term>, or if the **Moon** (☽), while waning in light, is carried toward her. For then she will establish such a freedom of power that the person who has Venus so placed may be compared to kings or Emperors. In such a case, she decrees golden crowns, the <term>praetexta <note>a purple-bordered toga worn by high-ranking Roman magistrates</note></term>, and the golden <term>palm-embroidered robes <note>original: "palmatas" - garments worn by conquering generals and consuls</note></term> of the consular or proconsular rank. Depending on the region and the scale of the birth chart, she will also create through noble power the directors of gymnasia <note>original: "gymnasiarchas"</note> and provincial priests—men who are always famous and noble, and whose symbols of honor are carried across the spans of the entire world. She also renders them pleasing, lovable, charming, and just—the kind of people whom everyone desires to help in any way possible; these individuals are also granted great signs of happiness by women or wives. 

If, however, she is not in these specific places, signs, or bounds, but in those belonging to others, she will give honest and clean crafts: for she creates goldsmiths, gilders, gold-beaters, silversmiths, musicians, organ-makers, and painters. But if she is found in low-lying places, she will create hosts, cook-shop owners, tavern keepers, and perfume sellers <note>original: "myropolas"</note>, as well as those who are accustomed to selling crowns woven from a variety of flowers on festive and sacred days, and whatever else is necessary for joy or delight. 

But generally, if a benefic star is with the planet that decrees the action, or regards it with a trine aspect, it decrees glory, fame, and nobility for that career, and grants the greatest increases in resources. The more benefic stars that contribute their rays and associations to the planet decreeing the action, the greater the increase in happiness they provide, and they add a greater name of glory from that career—especially if the benefic stars providing testimony are found in their "morning rising" <note>visible in the east before the sun</note> while moving in direct motion. 

But if, without the testimony of benefic stars, only the malefic stars regard the planet decreeing the action, they decree a humble life and careers that are subordinate and full of toil; they make such people as are struck by constant scandals arising from those very actions. If both malefic and benefic stars agree in equal aspect to the planet decreeing the action, they all produce effects according to their own nature of decreeing; however, those that join themselves with a stronger aspect will be more powerful.

<margin>☿ <note>Mercury - Note: The original Latin text and OCR here repeat the symbol for Venus (♀), but the professions described (orators, mathematicians) are traditionally ruled by Mercury.</note></margin> If **Mercury** (☿) should decree the action and be positioned in the principal places (as we said before regarding Venus and the Sun), and be in his <term>exaltation <note>original: "altitudine"</note></term>, his bounds, or his own house, he makes kings, or those placed in charge of judges, or those to whom royal accounts are entrusted. He also decrees the teachers of Emperors, or similar careers, by every reckoning—following, however, the nature and power of the signs that lend him their testimony. He also creates orators, architects, mathematicians, astrologers, and soothsayers <note>original: "aruspices"</note>, which he decrees according to the quality of the signs. 

For if he is positioned in **fixed signs** <note>original: "solidis" - Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, he decrees the greatest judgments and accounts. In **tropical signs** <note>original: "tropicis" - Cancer, Capricorn</note>, however, he decrees offices involving changes or interpretations. In **equinoctial signs** <note>original: "æquinoctialibus" - Aries, Libra</note>, he places one in charge of public weights. In **double-bodied signs** <note>original: "duplicibus" - Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, he makes prudent men, astrologers, and ingenious inventors; he decrees everything that seems similar to these arts and disciplines by this same reasoning. 

Generally, therefore, we ought to know this: that whenever Mercury decrees the action, if he is adorned by the testimony of benefic stars, he decrees glory, the advancement of honors, and the signs of the greatest authority. On the contrary, malefic stars decree demotions, humility, miseries, and infamy. But in these very decrees, there is no small difference based on the nature of the stars. **Jupiter** (♃) providing testimony will make people who are influential <note>original: "autores"</note>, bold, dangerous, quickly mobile, and who may be deceived in every way, but who are never brought under the yoke by the permission of any power. **Saturn** (♄) will make them mild-mannered, high-minded, silent, and proud, and those who do everything with dissimula... <note>The text cuts off mid-word "dissimulatione" (secrecy/dissimulation)</note>

### THE THIRTY-SIX DECANS OF THE SIGNS, AND
### their decrees. Chapter XVI.

**A**s I am now about to explain the secrets of this venerable teaching—which the divine ancients spoke of with the greatest trepidation, and which they left shrouded in the ambiguities of obscurity, lest this divine knowledge, once published, should reach the awareness of profane men—let whatever they said be made known in this treatise with the simplest explanations, to a focused and quiet mind, not occupied by other matters. In the previous book of instructions, we said that each sign has three <term>decans <note>original: "decanos" - from the Greek word for "ten," these are 10-degree divisions of the zodiac signs, each ruled by a specific spirit or deity</note></term>. Moreover, the decans are of great divinity and power; through them, all prosperity and misfortunes are decreed. Thus even Necepso <note>A legendary Egyptian Pharaoh-priest considered a founding father of Hellenistic astrology</note>, the most just Emperor of Egypt and also the best astronomer, compiled all vices and illnesses through these decans, showing which illness each decan produced: because one nature is conquered by another, and one god by another. Therefore, from contrary natures and contrary powers, he discovered the cures for all ailments by the instructions of divine reason. 

Thus, thirty-six decans possess the entire circle of the zodiac: and this multitude of gods, or decans, is divided through the number of the 12 signs. But since there are three decans in each sign, their divinity is not established in all thirty degrees of them; rather, through each sign, the three decans possess certain degrees and leave others. Thus, the degrees in which the decans are found are "full"; but those to which the number of decans never approaches are "empty." Whoever, therefore, has the Sun (☉), Moon (☽), and the five planets in full degrees in their <term>birth chart <note>original: "genitura"</note></term>, will be like a god, uplifted by the protection of the greatest majesty. But it can never happen that in a person's birth chart the Sun, Moon, and five planets are all positioned in full degrees. 

Those who have one star besides the Sun and Moon in full degrees will be of moderate status; those with two will approach every kind of happiness; those with three will receive the ornaments of happiness multiplied beyond measure; while those with four will reach the power of royal happiness. Beyond this number, stars possess full degrees in no birth charts. But those who have neither the <term>Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopus" - the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note></term>, nor the Sun and Moon, nor any star in full degrees will be miserable, always destitute and poor, and attached to a continuation of miseries at every crisis of happiness. 

Truly, in all places and stars, you must carefully inspect this logic: for if the Ascendant is in full degrees, they will be powerful by the virtue of their mind, the balance of their body, and the power of their authority. But those who have the Ascendant in empty degrees will be miserable in body, dejected in mind, with weak strength, and always serving those more powerful, and subject to their equals; and they lose the freedom of authority in all business. By similar logic, even the <term>Midheaven <note>original: "MC pars" or Medium Coeli - the highest point in the chart, representing career and public life</note></term> point, if found in empty degrees, offers an empty efficacy to its decree; but if in full degrees, it decrees everything whole and incorrupt that this place is accustomed to provide. In the same way, the <term>Lot of Fortune <note>original: "fortunae locus" - a mathematical point in the chart signifying prosperity and fate</note></term>, the Lord of the Birth Chart, and even that planet which we noted above provides the person's "action" <note>the planet governing career</note>. For all these, even if they are positioned in favorable places of the birth chart, lose their power of liberty if they are not established in full degrees; but if they possess full degrees, they decree with incorrupt power everything we promised they would decree. 

I will therefore explain the full and empty degrees, so that no stain of envy may defile the secrets of this discipline. I will also provide the names of the decans in the Egyptian language, so that we may make known to you everything we promised, beginning from **Aries** (♈), the most powerful. For those degrees are full in which you find the names of the decans; but those are empty which the decans have left entirely bare and uncultivated.

The writers of old left this system shrouded in various obscurities, so that this most true and unchanging system would not become common knowledge among men. But the great Petosiris <note>A semi-legendary Egyptian priest-astrologer believed to have lived in the 2nd century BCE, often cited alongside King Nechepso as a founder of Hellenistic astrology</note> touched upon this part briefly; not because he was ignorant of it—for he had already accessed all the secrets of divinity—but because he did not wish to teach it too fully, lest he leave the immortal discipline of his work [unprotected] to future generations. ->BOOK FOUR.<-

### MASCULINE AND FEMININE PARTS OF THE SIGNS <note>In ancient astrology, "parts" refer to the 30 individual degrees that make up each zodiac sign. Each degree carries its own specific quality.</note>
### Chapter XVII.

Now I shall relate the masculine and feminine parts of the signs. For within both masculine and feminine signs <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Aquarius are traditionally masculine signs; Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, and Pisces are traditionally feminine.</note>, there are likewise masculine and feminine parts. From these parts, one discovers whether a birth chart <note>original: "genitura"</note> is masculine or feminine. There are, in total, 197 masculine parts and 163 feminine parts. I will explain in detail through the following list how they may be most easily distinguished.

♈ <note>Aries</note> From the first part until the seventh, they are masculine; from the eighth until the twelfth, feminine; again from the thirteenth until the sixteenth, masculine; from the seventeenth until the twenty-second, feminine; and from the twenty-third until the thirtieth, masculine.

♉ <note>Taurus</note> From the first until the seventh, they are masculine; from the eighth until the nineteenth, feminine; and from the twentieth until the thirtieth, masculine.

 Gemini <note>original symbol: ♊</note> From the first until the seventeenth, they are masculine; from the eighteenth until the twenty-third, feminine; and from the twenty-fourth until the thirtieth, masculine.

♋ <note>Cancer</note> From the first until the second, they are masculine; from the third until the seventh, feminine; from the eighth until the tenth, masculine; from the eleventh until the twelfth, feminine; from the thirteenth until the eighteenth, masculine; from the nineteenth until the twentieth, feminine; from the twenty-first until the twenty-seventh, masculine; and from the twenty-eighth until the thirtieth, all the parts are feminine.

♌ <note>Leo</note> From the first until the fifth, they are masculine; from the sixth until the seventh, feminine; from the eighth until the fifteenth, masculine; from the sixteenth until the twenty-sixth, feminine; and from the twenty-seventh until the thirtieth, masculine.

♍ <note>Virgo</note> From the first until the seventh, they are masculine; from the eighth until the twenty-second, feminine; from the twenty-third until the twenty-fourth, masculine; and from the twenty-fifth until the thirtieth, feminine.

♎ <note>Libra</note> From the first until the fifth, they are masculine; from the sixth until the tenth, feminine; from the eleventh until the twenty-first, masculine; from the twenty-second until the twenty-eighth, feminine; and from the twenty-ninth until the thirtieth, masculine.

♏ <note>Scorpio</note> From the first until the fourth, they are masculine; from the fifth until the tenth, feminine; again from the eleventh until the twelfth, masculine; from the thirteenth until the nineteenth, feminine; from the twentieth until the twenty-seventh, masculine; and again from the twenty-eighth until the thirtieth, feminine.

♐ <note>Sagittarius</note> From the first until the second, they are masculine; from the third until the fifth, feminine; from the sixth until the twelfth, masculine; from the thirteenth until the twenty-third, feminine; and from the twenty-fourth until the thirtieth, masculine.

 Capricorn <note>original symbol: ♑</note> From the first until the eighth, they are masculine; again from the ninth until the twelfth, feminine; from the tenth <note>The text here says "tenth" (decima), but following the sequence 9-12, this is likely a scribal error for "thirteenth" (decimatertia).</note> until the nineteenth, masculine; and from the twentieth until the thirtieth, feminine.

♒ <note>Aquarius</note> From the first until the ninth, they are masculine; again from the tenth to the twelfth, feminine; from the thirteenth until the nineteenth, masculine; and from the twentieth until the thirtieth, feminine.

 Pisces <note>original symbol: ♓</note> From the first until the tenth, they are masculine; again from the eleventh to the twentieth, feminine; from the twenty-first until the twenty-third, masculine; and from the twenty-fourth until the thirtieth, they are feminine.

BOOK FIVE.

### THE DECREES OF THE MOON, WITH THE INDIVIDUAL PLANETS 
### in the angles. Chapter XVIII.

Having explained all these things and demonstrated them with careful reasoning, I shall hasten toward the end of this book. But because we spoke much regarding the course of the Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note> at its beginning, we shall also close its final parts with a similar conclusion, so that the most powerful divinity of the Moon may be seen to have given both the beginning and the end to this book. Therefore, I shall explain in general, through the truest and most manifest maxims, what the Moon decrees when positioned in the angles <term>cardines; the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</term> with the other stars, so that in the following fifth book we may subsequently reveal the remaining secrets of divine astronomy <note>original: "mathesis"</note> without ill-will.

<margin>The Moon with the Sun in the Ascendant.</margin>
If the Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is found exactly <note>original: "partiliter," meaning by the same degree</note> with the Sun <note>original symbol: ☉</note> in the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopus"</note>, in those signs in which she rejoices or is exalted, or in her own home, and already freed from the Sun's rays, she makes the parents famous and adorned with the splendor of wealth. She signifies this same thing even when positioned with the Sun in the Midheaven <note>original: "MC"</note>. But in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven <note>original: "IMC"</note>, if she is placed exactly with the Sun, she makes the parents either slaves, or wretched, low-born, outcasts, or beggars; however, she decrees these things according to the quality of the signs or the degrees. But if Mars <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, positioned thus, regards the Moon with a threatening aspect <note>original: "radiatione," referring to the light cast between planets</note>, and is opposed to both by an exact aspect, he weakens the body with a heavy defect and frequently indicates blindness of the eyes. If indeed the Sun and Moon are in those same degrees together with Mars, he strikes down both the parents and the children themselves with the wretched humility of dejection, decrees a violent death, and indicates a most wicked end.

<margin>Saturn</margin>
If the Moon is found exactly with Saturn <note>original symbol: ♄</note> in the Ascendant, she will cause the children to be the first-born or the first to be raised, but she will impose the wretched burden of widowhood upon the mothers. For she causes them either to be detained in the company of temples, or she indicates a grave danger to health from the private and female parts. She decrees the same in the Midheaven if she is found exactly with Saturn in that place. But in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, she makes the mother oppressed by the misery of slavery; as for those who are born, she will render them either captives or separated from their parents. Yet she decrees all these things according to the quality of the signs and the degrees.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If the Moon is positioned exactly with Jupiter <note>original symbol: ♃</note> in the Ascendant, she makes the mother adorned with the splendid lineage of nobility; she renders the children religious and able to foresee the future. They will indeed be famous, noble, and powerful. She decrees this same thing when positioned with Jupiter in the Midheaven. But in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, when positioned exactly with Jupiter, she squanders the paternal wealth; but afterward, either through the protection of friends or from the inheritances of relatives, these individuals attain the greatest resources of substance. In all things, however, you must frequently inspect the power of the degrees and places, as we have said.

<margin>Mars</margin>
If the Moon is found exactly with Mars <note>original symbol: ♂</note> in the Ascendant, she indicates a foreign mother or one who is weak, and she weakens the stomach or the eyes of those born. But if the birth chart <note>original: "genitura"</note> is by day, she renders them weak in the whole body or cuts off a part of the body. She promises this same thing in the Midheaven. But in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—or in the Lower Midheaven, if she is found with Mars, she makes them leave their fatherland and dwell in foreign regions. 
<margin>Mercury</margin>
If indeed Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿</note> is found with them, he will make thieves, pirates, murderers, temple-robbers, sacrilegious people, and those who always incur the crime of falsehood; and because of these things, they are often punished by public execution. All things, however, as we have frequently said, are discerned according to the quality of the signs. But if Saturn regards them with any aspect, he will make them bound in public custody, or prisons, or the bonds of chains, so that an offensive gluttony for crimes always defiles them; and he places them in such necessity that they even beg for food from their enemies. Some, however, persisting in custody and chains, even complete the term of their life there. If Jupiter regards all these from any part, he will cause them to be assigned to servile and humble duties in temples.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If the Moon is found exactly with Venus <note>original symbol: ♀</note> in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven, she will make them well-known, noble, and those upon whom the greatest insignia of power are conferred. But in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—and in the Lower Midheaven, they show a humble maternal lineage, but they are those who never lack the support of life; who, however, in their early age, are always struck by various infamies. In all signs and places, if she is found with Venus, of two...

<margin>Mercury with Mercury <note>original symbol: ☿ with ☿</note></margin>
If Mercury is found exactly <note>original: "partiliter," meaning occurring at the same degree</note> with Mercury in the Ascendant <note>original: "horoscopus"</note> or in the Midheaven <note>original: "MC"</note>, he will make people famous and noble through their literary distinction, and fit for every duty of business. But if he is found in the setting—that is, in the seventh place from the Ascendant—or in the Lower Midheaven <note>original: "IMC"</note>, he decrees the handling of credit, of interest, and the duties of accounting. Let it suffice for us to have said these things in the final parts of this book; for this final discourse has worked to recall the effect of the entire preceding discussion to your memory.

## THE THEORY OF THE MOON'S CONJUNCTION 
## and Separation. Chapter XIX.

Now we must indicate by what reasoning the Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note> separates exactly and by what she is joined, which the Greeks call **conjunctions and separations** <note>original Greek: συναφὰς καὶ ἀποῤῥοίας (synaphas kai aporrhoias)</note>. For in all signs, she both separates from many and is joined to many by her radiation. First, therefore, observe in whatever sign she is found, within whose star's bounds <term>bounds: also known as "terms," these are specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term> she resides. For separating from that one, she is carried toward that star whose bounds she has entered in the second place within the same sign. Then observe to what extent the lord of those bounds—and in what place he is positioned—regards her: and once the reasoning of the preceding astrological outcomes <note>original: "apotelesmatum"</note> is understood, you will be able to explain the whole fate of a person with true judgments. Observe also in the third order whose star’s degrees she enters: for from these she also conceives the power of decreeing. And so proceed until she reaches the very last degrees of the sign itself, so that you may find specifically all things that pertain to the Moon’s efficacy. It must also be known that in all signs, whenever the Moon possesses the final degrees, she is carried toward no one; for she is hindered by the obstacles of the approaching sign. But again, positioned in the first degrees of a sign, she separates from no one, and then only the efficacy of conjunction is sought. For all power of the preceding degrees, having been passed over, is left behind at that boundary which exists between both signs, and from the first degree of the sign it rises into those that follow: and this is the exact <note>original: "partilis"</note> conjunction and separation of the Moon. For we determine broad <note>original: "platice," referring to an aspect within the same sign regardless of degree</note> aspects from the whole signs; but in every treatise, we ought to treat all things by exact reasoning. Wherefore again and again we meet you with these same reminders: that whenever you treat a birth chart <note>original: "genituram"</note>, you should inspect the whole body of the decree together, and compose all things from the reasoning of the individual stars, and diligently inspect the power of the places and degrees. Compare also the birth chart of the signs with the qualities of the places, look at the conditions, and likewise the courses and forms of the stars: and consider the separations and conjunctions of the Moon with diligent reasoning. For in this way, whatever place you treat, you will be able to explain with the truest judgments, if you collect all these things with skillful investigation. Now, however, let the remaining treatise be transferred to the principles of the fifth book: so that once all necessary things are explained, the whole reasoning of our discussion may be transcribed for the exact astrological outcomes and the "Barbarian Sphere" <note>original: "sphaeram barbaricam," likely referring to extra-zodiacal constellations or non-Greek astrological traditions</note>. But because the first part of our work is now settled, we approach the second principal part, which is also divided into four members just like the first: so that you may more easily understand what is to be treated in each of them, we shall summarily enumerate the parts of each in a brief proposition.

<margin>The subject of the fifth book.</margin>
The fifth book, therefore, will introduce what the pivots of the world <term>cardines: the four "angles" of the chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven)</term> decree—that is, what the Ascendant and the other three pivots promise when positioned in whichever signs; and how the Ascendant, found in individual minutes, is said to show the whole substance of life. Also, in which star's bounds the Ascendant is found, and by which lords of the bounds either the lord or the Ascendant itself is regarded, and what it threatens. It will also explain what the stars decree when placed in whichever signs, bounds, decans <term>decans: 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign</term>, or houses, and regarding the powers of the twelve signs.

VI. The sixth book will discuss the bright and royal stars of the four signs, the trine, square, opposite, or sextile radiation of the stars, stars positioned together that attack or elevate the rays of others, and simultaneously the diversity of the rays of the Moon and Sun. What stars decree when positioned in different places or bounds and occupied by the rays of others; regarding "approaches" <note>original: "ephodis"</note>, and the division of times, and what they establish.

VII. The seventh book will dispute the state of life, the quality of death, and the vices of men,

<margin>VIII.</margin>

# THE FIFTH BOOK OF THE MATHESIS BY JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS THE 
# YOUNGER, OF SICILY, OF ILLUSTRIOUS RANK, TO MAVORTIUS
## Lollianus, Proconsul.

### PREFACE.

We have laid the greatest foundations of our promise, Mavortius, and as it grows through each individual step, our mature discourse has progressed. For everything that seemed difficult for some to explain, and was wrapped in many winding obscurities, we have demonstrated through a clear explanation in plain language. Therefore, if a capable mind, moved by the desire of a burning soul, drinks in these preceding books—provided it was conceived under a favorable radiation of the stars—it may reach the divine secrets of this science. Once initiated into all the disciplines of this same science, the mind will receive the entire order of divine interpretation, so that it may be able to both discover and explain the fates of men. But the listener expects something more from us: for the beginnings of the preceding books were so formed that from those things we have written, the substance of an even greater work is required. Therefore, lest I deceive the longing of the mind with a false promise, I shall set aside all bitterness of envy and cast away all the lethargy of idleness to bring forward the accumulated secrets of Astrology <note>original: "Matheseos"</note>. I do this so that the intent, which was safe in its beginnings, is not abandoned through the vice of envy or malicious silence. Thus, we return this work in its fullness as we promised, intimately sharing all things specifically with your wisdom. But let not this discourse be left naked of divine protection, lest the envy of some malevolent man attack these efforts.

<margin>Invocation.</margin>
You, whoever you are, O God—who continues the course of heaven with swift haste through each passing day, who makes the waves of the sea perpetual with ever-shifting motion, who has steadied the earth's solidity upon an unmoved foundation and throne, who has refreshed the labor of earthly bodies with the riches of the night; who, once our strengths are restored, returns again the grace of the sweetest light; who sustains the fragility of the body by the inspiration of a divine mind, who quickens the whole substance of your work with the health-giving breaths of the winds, who pours out the waves of springs and rivers with tireless necessity, who returns the variety of the seasons through the fixed courses of the days: you alone are the governor and prince of all things, the sole commander and lord, whom the entire power of the divine beings serves. By your will, the perfection and substance of this work stands; your incorruptible nature adorns the whole substance of eternity. You are the father and mother of all alike; you are to yourself both father and son, bound by a single link of necessity. To you we stretch out suppliant hands, you we venerate with trembling prayer: grant pardon that we attempt to explain the courses of your stars and their effects. Let it be yours, that some divine power or other has impelled us toward this interpretation. With a pure mind, set apart from all earthly dealings and purged of the stain of all crimes, we have written these books for your Romans; lest, once all the arts of the disciplines were translated, this work alone should appear to be something that Roman genius had not aspired to. And you, the courses of the eternal stars, and you, O Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, mother of even human bodies, and you, the prince of all stars, who both takes away and returns light in the monthly courses of the Moon—O Sun <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, greatest and best, who composes all things through each day by the moderation of your majesty, through whom the immortal soul is divided among all living beings by divine arrangement, who alone opens and closes the gates of heaven, by whose judgment the order of the fates is arranged: grant pardon, that our slender discourse reaches toward the secrets of your divinity. For it was not sacrilegious greed or the heat of a profane mind that led us to...

### THE SIMPLE DECREES OF THE CARDINES, WITHOUT THE 
### TESTIMONY OF ANY PLANET. Chapter I.

<margin>
The Horoscope in 
Aries.
</margin>
Even the bare substance of the signs has great power of decreeing, Mavortius, our glory <note>The author is addressing his patron, Lollianus Mavortius</note>, without the presence of any star, according to its own nature, and it works in many birth charts <term>genitura: a birth chart or horoscope</term>. But this effectiveness is found only in the *cardines* <term>cardines: the "hinges" or the four most powerful points in a chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</term>: for the cardines, even if they are left by the gods without the testimonies of stars, nonetheless receive the power of decreeing from their own nature. To help you understand this more clearly, I will briefly demonstrate by the authority of reason itself. 

If the horoscope <term>horoscopus: here meaning the Ascendant, the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> is found in <term>♈︎: Aries</term>, then <term>♑︎: Capricorn</term> will be the **M.C.** <note>Medium Coeli, the Midheaven or highest point</note>, the setting <note>the Descendant or western horizon</note> will be in <term>♎︎: Libra</term>, and the **I.M.C.** <note>Imum Coeli, the Lower Midheaven or lowest point</note> will be in <term>♋︎: Cancer</term>. I will therefore explain in a general way what the remaining three cardines decree for one who has the horoscope in Aries. 

When the horoscope is in **Aries**, it decrees a very long youth for the native, but denies brothers, or preserves only one out of many: but even that one it weakens with the bitterness of some defect, and his name is always pursued with hatred. His paternal substance <note>family inheritance or wealth</note> does not remain in the same state, but is now squandered and scattered, and then again collected after being dissipated. To some, he will certainly seem safer because of his excessive liberality, but to others, the inconsistency of his generosity will be displeasing; he will grant his benefits to the ungrateful, so that thanks equal to his gifts are never repaid to him. He will certainly be changeable, and his head will always be troubled by various pains. 

If indeed the **M.C.** is specifically in **Capricorn**, it decrees the ornaments of a lasting glory, and makes many flatter him with a certain humility. He will be placed in charge of certain businesses and letters <note>administrative or secretarial work</note>, as one who supplies the nourishment of daily life to many, and sustains the resources of others through his management. He will be ingenious in many necessary matters, and one to whom the secrets of hidden religions are entrusted, and who easily penetrates celestial mysteries—especially if the star <term>♃: Jupiter</term> looks upon this place from any part, or if it is found within it. 

The third cardo, which is the **setting** [Descendant], also claims for itself the license of decreeing. If it is found in **Libra**, it decrees a life of constant conversation in a royal house, or places the native in public affairs: yet the native’s life will be changeable in some unequal part, so that unhappiness always follows every happiness, and misfortune follows prosperity; and sometimes he may be called back from the highest rank of dignity to the lowest with a falling humility. For the malice of envy will attack all his fame, especially if **Jupiter** does not see the horoscope with a trine radiation <note>an astrological aspect of 120 degrees, considered very favorable</note>, or if he is not positioned within it: for then these evils grow stronger. 

The fourth cardo will be in the **I.M.C.**; when Aries is the horoscope, this is always in **Cancer**. It will make the native famous and adorned with the ribbons of crowns, for whom statues and images alike are decreed. If indeed **Jupiter**, positioned in the horoscope, looks upon this place, or if he is found in the place itself, some of his relatives will be his adversaries for his own sake or for the sake of someone close to him: and he himself will be unshaven and squalid with dirty hair <note>this could imply a state of mourning, asceticism, or neglect</note>: but he will always be wealthy with an abundance of necessities, especially if **Jupiter** is found in any cardo.

<margin><term>♉︎: Taurus</term></margin>
If the horoscope is found in **Taurus**, the one who has it will be worn out by many continuous labors: and whatever he acquires in his early age, he will always lose: afterwards, however, he will regain what he lost with a cumulative increase of joy, and will possess the ornament of good fortune, and will see his enemies prostrated by a continuation of wretched humility. 

If the **M.C.** is in **Aquarius**, the native will always move in circles of friendship with the powerful, and will have his life in public acts; he will always be involved in watery business <note>original: "aquosis negocijs"; likely maritime trade or management of water resources</note>, and will be one who is never struck by the envy of an accusation: yet he will have increases in wealth as well as losses. 

If indeed the **setting** is found in the sign of **Scorpio**, it makes the native wise in all life's conversation, with the duty of management nourishing others; he will be one who loses his first wife by the intervention of death: if the native is a woman, she will likewise lose her husband and her son. 

If the **I.M.C.** is found in **Leo**, it makes those who seek the support of their patrimony through their own labor, and who, through constant arts, [attain] the greatest...

<margin>Gemini ♊</margin>
If the Horoscope <note>original: "horoscopus"; the Ascendant or the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is found in Gemini, the person born will labor during the first stages of life; however, solace will always be provided to them by their parents. They will also be constantly imbued with celestial talents and bound by the faithful friendships of great men. If, however, the Midheaven <term>M C: Medium Coeli, the highest point of the chart representing career and public life</term> is in Pisces, the one who has it so will establish their life in a watery place <note>This could refer to a coastal city, a port, or a profession involving water</note>, and will possess patrimonies from every kind of substance; their livelihood will be provided from the resources of others, but their power or inheritance will be divided between two cities. If the Descendant <term>occasus: the western angle of the chart, relating to death and relationships</term> is found in Sagittarius, the person will bring some form of destruction either to their brothers or their relatives; their mind will be tortured by great anxieties through the various changes of time. They will also have enemies and, having abandoned their fatherland, will linger in many foreign travels; but having later returned to the ancestral hearth, they will consider themselves restored by the protection of the gods. If, however, the Lower Midheaven <term>I M C: Imum Coeli, the lowest point of the chart representing roots and the end of life</term> is in Virgo, they will be shaken from an early age by a variety of continuous labors; but with the passage of time, they will attain increments of the greatest happiness. Each of these things, however, results from the "measure" of the birth chart, which, as we have said, you must frequently observe in all cases.

<margin>Cancer ♋</margin>
If the Horoscope is found in Cancer, it always creates those with sharp intellects, but who accomplish everything with the moderation of slowness. It also makes them pleasant, learned, and prone to serious anger—men who pursue all wicked people with severe indignation. They are also brave and moderate, yet their indignation is very easily soothed. These people will have resources from royal or public places, from which the substance of their life will be provided. They will also be constantly occupied with public business, but many people will flatter them, driven by various necessities. If, however, while the Horoscope is in Cancer, Jupiter is found in Capricorn <note>Capricorn is the sign opposite Cancer</note> or aspects it, the person will suffer a violent death, or fall into a great defect of health, or their closer brothers will die in their stead. But if the Midheaven is in Aries, the person born will be engaged in constant conversation with more powerful men, or daily nourishment will be provided to them from the resources of others. They will always be seeking good things, but their patrimony will change with constant variety: for as often as it is lost, so often will it be acquired again. If, however, the Descendant is in Libra, they will always be struck by hidden envy; but this will later be settled by quiet reason, though only after many hardships of instability. They will also be ingenious, sharp, and adorned with mental investigations, yet sustaining the torments of some hidden pain and fatigued by infinite sorrows of the soul. If the Lower Midheaven is in Libra, they will be fatigued by many labors; but being applied to civil duties or handed over to popular gatherings, they will dissipate the substance of their previous patrimony. They will certainly be fertile in all parts and necessary to others, but will gain the means of substance from "letters" <note>This suggests a career in writing, law, or administration</note>. They will be the kind of person to whom hidden secrets are entrusted by others; they will reach the final stages of old age and be graced with the honor of a good burial. If, however, Mercury is found in the following sign, they will be the most prominent among all the male children. If Venus is found in the second place <note>The second house, often associated with wealth and family</note>, the lifespan of daughters is preferred, provided that the lord of the birth chart is well-placed and adorned by the rays of benevolent stars.

<margin>Leo ♌</margin>
If the Horoscope is found in Leo, the person will be involved in many labors and dangers, but throughout their entire life, they will be known to everyone and have the free power of possession. They will always be ingenious, and—as one who does not exercise the forces of malice in all things—they will conceive desires for living and commanding, though acquiring the means of substance through their own labors. But if Mars is found in that same Horoscope exactly, or if the Sun regards it with a square or diameter aspect <note>A "diameter radiatione" refers to an opposition (180 degrees)</note>, it will deny children in every way. If, however, Jupiter is found in a similar way, it will give only one daughter. If the Midheaven is found in Aquarius, they will have their life in a public place or in a temple; they will contract marriage with a widow, or a woman defiled by another, or one of a subordinate and servile condition, or an old woman, or one who is struck by public infamy. Nevertheless, the greatest honor will be conferred upon them by a very powerful man. They will be ignorant of all matters, yet one who rejoices in the increases of prosperous fortune. If, however, the Descendant is in Aquarius, both the life of the person born and the increases of that life will always suffer losses; yet they will be grateful and proven in certain matters. <margin>Virgo ♍</margin>

They should also continue their prayers to the divinity with constant repetition. However, they will fall into the snares of love with passive desires of the eyes, and as one who desires the bedding of all women with reckless lust: but they will suffer from these vices until the rising <term>anaphora: the time it takes for a sign to fully rise over the horizon</term> of that sign is completed. They will certainly be joyful, kind, and one with whom a pure bond of friendship remains, and to whom the concern of some loss pertains. They will be knowledgeable in many things, seeking out the secrets of all disciplines, keeping everything within the enclosure of their heart, and adorned with the fame of simplicity. Great happiness and substantial means will be granted to them through the grace of learned speech, or the duty of business, or from inheritance, or sacred matters, or from some virtue. 

If found in Gemini <note>original: ♊</note> at the Midheaven [M C], it will grant substance from public or sacred matters: but only when the threshold of old age has been entered. They will be a just worshiper of religions and the gods, whom the greatest part of the citizens will strive to obey, seeking out hidden things with diligent investigation, though ignorant of many arts and disciplines: yet in the final time of life, the duty of an upright and correct life will be shown to many through them. 

If however the Descendant <term>occasus: the western angle of the chart, relating to death and relationships</term> is in Pisces <note>original: ♓</note>, they will travel through many foreign places, be known to many people, and many will flatter them with diligent service. If found in Gemini <note>original: ♊</note> at the Lower Midheaven <term>I M C: Imum Coeli, the lowest point of the chart representing roots and the end of life</term>, they will be happy, and substance will be granted to them by their own people; many will flatter them, they will be known to all, and will give thanks to the gods for their happiness: public sacred rites will also be entrusted to them. They will rejoice in the happiness of children: and will mitigate the pain of lost children by receiving happy offspring again. They will also be fit for everything, learned, and clear and famous with the highest peak of agile happiness.

<margin>Libra ♎</margin>
If found in the Horoscope [Ascendant] in Libra, they will have illness and be entangled in many snares of danger; a crowd of adversaries will constantly strike at them, and they will have contentious struggles over true and defined matters. They will certainly be religious and a worshiper of the gods, but their life will always change with the variety of instability. In all things, however, they will be unconquered, and such that they seem second to none, and will be glorious: but the place of their children will be changeable: for the full number of their offspring will never remain stable. They will be the type who wants to have correct judgment in all things, coming from divine and celestial religions. 

If found in Cancer <note>original: ♋</note> at the Midheaven [M C], they will be glorious, occupied with certain actions, and will be raised in a religious or public place: and in old age, the greatest marks of glory will be conferred upon them: so that the final time of life is adorned with the splendors of nobility: for in old age they will be rich, wealthy, and one to whom all the substance of happiness comes gradually over time: but they will obtain children late, or have only one. If Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> looks upon this place with any aspect, they will rejoice in many and happy offspring. 

If however the Descendant is found in Aries <note>original: ♈</note>, they will have profit from watery things, or will be anxious with some fear from watery places, and will run into some life-threatening danger in deserted places, and many dangers will shake them in succession, and they will be divided by many and frequent travels. They will certainly have a hidden physical defect: but the greatest happiness will be granted to them in old age, though their wife will suffer from the dangers of madness. 

If the Lower Midheaven [I M C] is in Capricorn <note>original: ♑; the OCR incorrectly identified the symbol as Saturn ♄</note>, the inheritance of the person born will change for various reasons: for whatever is acquired by them, they will lose again: and again, what was lost, they will find: yet all their substance will be sought through the strength of their own virtues, and placed in the final stage of life, they will be adorned with the greatest increase of happiness. They will, however, be forced to adopt the child of another, or obtain one from a woman of the lowest class.

<margin>Jupiter ♃</margin>

But if the Midheaven is in Pisces <note>original: ♓</note>, he will have his means of life in watery places; he will be such a person that all things are entrusted to his loyalty. If Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> looks upon this place with any aspect, he will easily take a wife and his marital affections will be pleasing; however, he will obtain a wife known through debauchery or adultery.

<margin>Saturn ♄</margin>

He will be lovable, small-minded, and always annoying to the gods with long and wordy prayers. He will be the type of person who always has an abundance of wealth; but yet he is bound by the love of women, and one who strives to disparage them once his lusts are satisfied. He will be a student of the secrets of some oath, or sacred rites, or the life of another, or hidden religions. 

But if the Midheaven is in Libra <note>original: ♎</note>, he will be pious, adorned with the grace of honest speech, learned, and one who fulfills his vows to the gods. Freed from certain necessities or dangers, he will also have prosperous actions; but after he has been oppressed by bad actions, happiness will be conferred on him from the misfortunes of others. He will have profit from the deaths of others, or he will find the comforts of happiness from some antiquity or hidden thing. 

But if the Descendant is in Cancer <note>original: ♋</note>, he will have the greatest troubles from his relatives and will be involved in the greatest dangers. 

But if the Midheaven is in Capricorn <note>original: ♑</note>, he will be in great errors; but after the inconveniences of life, he will obtain rest, and his life will be changed by a refined variety: for he will be now in a high degree of dignity, now recalled to the lowest. But this instability will be born from the friendships of the powerful. This person also will bury his wife and his first son; or certainly, whoever is born will be weakened by a serious defect of health.
