### THE DECREES OF THE SUN IN THE BORDERS OF OTHER PLANETS. Chapter XIII.

<margin>Sun in its own places</margin>
If the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> is found in its own house or decan <note>the sign of Leo</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it will create kings—wealthy, great, and strong—who acquire vast riches and glory from foreigners. This is especially true if, so positioned, they are placed in the "pivots" <term>cardinibus: the four most powerful points in a chart—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term> of the birth chart or in their "ascensions" <term>anaphoris: the houses following a pivot, also known as succedent houses</term>. But if it is a nighttime birth chart, it decrees sorrow for the father and a sudden death. It often makes people travelers, though they will find advantage and profit in their journeys.

<margin>Saturn ♄</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it will make people of high heart and deep thought, who always seek out great and hidden things with wise investigation. They will be stable and constant in all their works, and will never cease from what they have begun until they reach their desired goal. If, however, it is a nighttime birth chart, all these things are decreed by a lighter fate, and the people are rendered inconsistent in their works.

<margin>Jupiter ♃</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>, in either type of birth chart it will make people gentle, faithful, and greater and more worthy within their own family, but they will not be very watchful for wealth and profits. This is especially true if the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is also joined in that same place in equal partnership. These people will also be extremely lustful, desiring the wives of their kinsmen; they may even consider it no shame to have intercourse with their own mother or stepmother. The same lust is decreed in a woman’s birth chart.

<margin>Mars ♂</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it decrees liver pain and such sicknesses from which death itself may be feared. It also causes the father to die a violent death <term>biothanatum: a violent or unnatural death</term>, especially if there is a meeting of planetary rays <note>an aspect</note> in such a place. Yet it makes people quite rich and opulent, as well as industrious and accomplished in their business. If it is a nighttime birth chart, all the aforementioned evils will be lessened, and they will not rage with such a cruel decree.

<margin>Venus ♀</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>, in both daytime and nighttime birth charts, it will make people divine-like, casters of lots, astronomers, interpreters of dreams, and those who predict the future by some heavenly mystery. They will be seekers of hidden things, speakers of truth, good, faithful, and those who take delight in various travels and journeys. They will, however, be somewhat irritable and prone to anger <term>cholerici: having a 'choleric' temperament, associated with a fiery nature</term>, and suffering so much from "moist" qualities <note>an imbalance of the phlegmatic or watery humors</note> that they often suffer ailments from them.

<margin>Mercury ☿</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, in a daytime birth chart, it will make people of great knowledge and good works—clever, secretive, faithful, and greatly loved by the nobility. However, they will mostly be sickly and suffer from moist ailments. If it is a nighttime birth chart, it renders them poor and wicked in their youth, performing evil deeds; but later it makes them rich and involved in magical illusions, though they are often exhausted by ailments of the eyes and stomach.

<margin>Moon ☽</margin>
If the **Sun** is found in the house or decan of the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, it will make people worthy, honored, and lovable, achieving many marks of office and honors. They will be joined to kings and princes in the intimacy of close friendship. Yet, often weighed down by moist qualities, they fall into various and troublesome sicknesses. If it is a nighttime birth chart, all these things are nonetheless granted, but they are decreed with a more restricted influence.

# THE DECREES OF VENUS IN THE BORDERS OF OTHER PLANETS. Chapter XIV.

<margin>Venus in her own places.</margin>
If **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> is found in her own house or decan <term>decan: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign; there are three in each sign</term>, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart <term>genitura: the planetary configuration at the moment of birth</term>, she decrees a multitude of joys, an increase in happiness, and the rewards of good fortune. However, she will make these men pursue foolish and reckless women with the greatest intensity of affection, which may cause them to acquire disgrace and infamy among the people. Yet, they will be fortunate in their other endeavors and always beloved by everyone.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>, in either type of birth chart, she will make men sterile and following after no children at all. They will be wicked: adulterers, seducers, and those who especially pursue the wives of others or of their own relatives, even striving to corrupt their own mothers with dishonorable lustful desires. These men will also be of evil thought and mind, and their wives will often be taken away by a most grievous death.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>, in either type of birth chart likewise, she decrees honors, riches, magistracies, and useful income arising from women. These men will certainly be counselors or administrators for noblewomen, whereby they achieve fame, honor among others, and very many resources. However, because of this, they will be hateful to their parents; but they will pursue their own wives with a great affection of love, and from this, they will prepare for themselves happiness and joy.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart, she will make men quarrelsome with women. They will associate and become accustomed to women—especially wicked ones—through every kind of foul lust, from which many losses and damages will come to them. They will also be pursuers of other men’s wives, or of public prostitutes or slaves; for this reason, they will either cast off their own wives or kill them cruelly.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>, in either type of birth chart likewise, she will make men who pursue youthful women, whom they abuse with a wicked kind of lust. Yet they will especially be lovers of noble girls, through whom they frequently fall into many losses, damages, and even the greatest infamy—and perhaps into dangers of death that can be avoided only with the greatest difficulty.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, in either birth chart, she will make men who are exceedingly lustful, and especially pursuers of boys or young girls. But in other matters, they will be religious, and particularly skilled in crafting women’s ornaments: merchants of perfumed goods, goldsmiths, or makers of seals and necklaces, and those who strive to serve women with all their art and ingenuity, from which perhaps many inconveniences may arise for them.

If **Venus** is found in the house or decan of the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart, she will make men who are lustful, incontinent <note>lacking self-control</note> beyond measure, dissolute, and always driven by the impulsive sting of desires. For such men will be held back by no consideration of kinship or blood relation, led wherever their appetite drives their affection. They will also be intent on many things, never persisting in one undertaking with a stable purpose.

# THE DECREES OF MERCURY IN THE BORDERS OF OTHER PLANETS. Chapter XV.

<margin>Mercury in his own places.</margin>
If **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> is found in his own house or decan, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart, he will make men ingenious, cautious, shrewd, and industrious in every art and science: but especially mathematicians <term>arithmeticos: those who calculate or work with numbers</term>, and good bookkeepers; also doctors, philosophers, geometers, and those distinguished in the divine speculation of astrology <term>matheseos: specifically refers to the "mathematical" art of astrology here</term>. These men will be strong with such a facility of talent that they dare to accomplish through the industry of their hands whatever they have seen.

If **Mercury** is found in the house or decan of **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>, in either birth chart, he will make men mute, or those who stammer and are impeded in their tongue; they will be slow, secretive, pretenders, of much thought, and hiders of human affairs. They will, however, be religious, perceiving the secrets of laws and sacred rites: sometimes augurs <note>priests who interpret the will of gods through signs</note> or astronomers, and those who delight in the company of wise and religious men. They will, nonetheless, be melancholy...

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If **Mercury** <note>The context from the previous page indicates these descriptions pertain to Mercury (☿).</note> is found in the house or decan of **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart <term>genitura: the planetary configuration at the moment of birth</term>, he will make men sensible, wise, and legal experts <note>original: iurisperitos</note>, such as those who are called to the councils of kings or princes. They will surely be judges of peoples and nations, who decree laws and rights through their wisdom, and who rule certain cities or states in the name of their princes. These men also frequently handle the business of noblemen, demand taxes, and perform the calculations for those taxes. Often, they also instruct others through public readings of the institutions of laws or decrees.

<margin>Mars</margin>
If **Mercury** is found in the house or decan of **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, in either a daytime or nighttime birth chart, he will make men false, liars, treacherous, and those who always strive to betray a trust even when it is religiously committed to them. If you join in a partnership with such people, never commit the secrets of your faith to them, and never entrust anything to them on simple terms. For they will deny it and will fortify their impudence with an irreligious defense of perjury. They will also be armed for every deed of treachery, especially if, when Mercury is so positioned, Mars is found again in the borders <term>borders: also known as 'terms,' specific degrees within a zodiac sign assigned to a planet</term> of Mercury, or if Mercury is placed in the "fallen" positions of the birth chart and a superior Mars strikes it with a square aspect <term>quadrata radiatione: an astrological aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart, usually considered stressful</term>. Then, because of these criminal deeds, they are condemned either to long-term imprisonment <note>original: carceris custodia</note>, or to perpetual exile, or being possessed by a share of crimes and fearing the severity of an imminent sentence, they are led into wandering flight to remote and distant places, having abandoned their native labors. But if Mercury and Mars are so positioned, and a full **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is carried toward Mars through a square or diameter <term>diameter: an opposition aspect of 180 degrees</term>, and the benevolent stars do not fortify her with a prosperous aspect, nor is the malice of Mars mitigated by the testimony of Jupiter or Venus, they are punished with a savage sentence because of these deeds.

<margin>Sun</margin>
If **Mercury** is found in the house or decan of the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>, and it is a daytime birth chart, he will make men of mediocre status, bold in both spirit and mind, and observant. He will cause them to handle difficult and malicious letters <note>This likely refers to complex legal or deceptive correspondence</note>, and he will cause the duties of laborious literature to be entrusted to them and for them to be assigned to public offices. He will also make them prudent, though with a certain curiosity, and involved in secret and illicit acts and ineffective studies. If, however, it is a nighttime birth chart, he will make them either mentally impaired <note>original: mente captos</note>, or weakened in hearing or speech. He also decrees errors and vices in their life; he makes such men the target of bad reputations, whom the judgment of good speech never rightly introduces.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **Mercury** is found in the borders or decan of **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>, he decrees all things in a similar manner in both daytime and nighttime birth charts. For then he will cause the speech of men to be adorned with the pleasing splendor of grace; he joins them to the powerful and to kings with the faithful love of necessity. He makes such men who are accustomed to finding everything through the right reasoning of counsel, and whose every act is followed by a prosperous outcome. They are imbued with "double letters" <note>original: duplicibus literis; likely referring to being bilingual in Latin and Greek</note>, and they attain all calculations and all disciplines through their skill. They will either be appointed to the honor of some powerful person over athletes, or they will compose musical measures with sweet modulation, or they will follow the discipline of poetry, or they will be dyers of colors, or the sweet scent of spices <note>original: aromatum</note> will be brought forth by them, or they will handle the trade of precious gems or the duties of foreign commerce, so that in every way from these acts both an inheritance and dignity are conferred upon them. They will certainly be libidinous in sexual intercourse, and they will corrupt the marriages <note>original: matrimonia</note> of others with the depraved desire of the mind; they will also be prone to vice and will always be struck by frequent infamy arising from these vices.

### THE INSTRUCTIONS OF THIS FIFTH BOOK
### Summary. Chapter XVII.

All these things, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work</note>, our glory, have been specifically revealed to you, nor has anything been omitted by us which the prophets of the divine race and the interpreters of this discipline have brought forth with the study of prudent skill and learned speech. But this which we have frequently said, we suggest to the reminders of your own prudence: that you should compare the whole power of the stars, the mixtures of all the signs, and the efficacy of the parts <note>original: "partium," referring to specific degrees or subdivisions</note> according to the powers of their locations in turn. Do not wish to explain the entire substance of a birth chart <term>genitura: the configuration of the heavens at the moment of birth</term> from the course of a single star, but first join the Ascendant <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> with the powers of the twelve places; compare stars with stars individually, and seek which star is joined with the Ascendant and by what radiation <note>original: "radiatione," referring to astrological aspects or angles between planets</note>, and to what extent the strengths of the constellations either attack or elevate their own stars. You must also see what forms the natural appearance of the signs or parts attributes to individual stars, and what the authority of each of the places and cardines <term>cardines: the "hinges" or four primary angles of a chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and IC)</term> decrees. 

When all these things have been gathered by wise inquiry, then, having inspected the substance of the birth chart, bring forth your judgments on individual matters. But first, with a moderated comparison, you should diligently inspect these same forms, lots <note>mathematically derived points in a chart, like the Lot of Fortune</note>, and even the risings <note>original: "anaphoras," the order in which signs rise over the horizon</note> of the signs. For Jupiter entering the places of Saturn does not always decree wives, nor does entering the place of children grant children; rather, he returns these things to those for whom the substance of the prior birth chart has decreed wives or children. Nor does Mars, when moving around the setting <note>the West or 7th House</note>, always look back with threatening radiations. Nor does Saturn, coming from the part of the Ascendant, always decree grave dangers with a general cruelty of malice. But for whomever dangers have been decreed from the substance of the whole birth chart, then those who have been promoted by the risings of the signs and made the "lords of times" <note>the planets currently ruling a specific period of life</note> shall execute the orders of all those dangers. 

Wherefore, blended by very frequent mixing through the powers of individual parts, these things ought to instruct your mind—formed by divine instruction—with skillful conjecture. For frequently the hospitality <note>original: "hospitium," how a planet is received in a sign or house</note> of an evil sign changes the goodness of Saturn, and the salutary hospitality of a good part weakens the malice of Jupiter <note>Firmicus emphasizes that the location can override the natural character of the planet</note>. Nor should you expect danger from an "evil" place when a healthy star has aspected it; just as the threatening rays of even malevolent stars are broken by the opportunity of the location. For in the birth charts of men, the mixture of places, parts, signs, and stars composes everything. If you collect all these with balanced moderation, you will be able to explain the whole fate of a human being with the truest judgments. But with this book completed, let our discourse be transferred to the principles of the sixth book. There I shall reveal to you all the mixtures of the stars with the truest interpretations, so that once that book is explained, our intention may be transferred, under good omens, to the specific interpretation of the prognostications <term>apotelesmatum: the completed results or effects of astrological configurations</term>.

# Preface.

Frequently, Mavortius our glory, our discourse has warned about the mixtures of the stars, that nothing else is to be sought by you in all judgments, nothing in the substance of the decrees, if you suggest the efficacy of a mixed temperament <note>the blending of planetary influences</note>; especially since in the birth charts of men, the primary cardines do one thing, and the secondary cardines do another. For the primary cardines possess the Ascendant and the Midheaven <note>the 1st and 10th Houses</note>; the secondary ones receive the Bottom of the Sky <term>IMC: Imum Coeli, the lowest point of the chart or 4th House</term> and the Setting <note>the 7th House</note>. From the varied and always contrary power of these four cardines, the whole substance of the birth chart is known. All stars, according to the powers of their nature, decree one thing when constituted in the primary cardines, and another in the secondary. But also the fifth and eleventh places from the Ascendant—that is, the place of Good Fortune and [Good Spirit]—the signs of sluggish places, [decree...]

<summary>This page concludes Book V with a methodological warning that no single planet determines a fate, but rather the "mixture" of all factors; it then begins Book VI, introducing the importance of the four "cardines" or angles of the chart.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the transition from Book V into Book VI of the Mathesis. Firmicus Maternus is concluding his technical explanation of how the twelve houses (places) of a birth chart relate to the Ascendant before introducing the "Royal Stars" and the complex "mixtures" of planetary influences.</meta>

...dissenting in their strength, when they are joined to sluggish and dejected places by no association of reason. But the ninth and third places from the Ascendant <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> obtain the true efficacy of decreeing; for these places also join the greatest partnership of association to the Ascendant. 

However, the second and eighth places from the Ascendant are separated from the partnership of association, having been dissolved from every bond with the Ascendant. Furthermore, the sixth and twelfth places from the Ascendant are excluded by every reason of association and are attacked by the falling lowliness of their dejection. Therefore, from this variety of places, the power of the stars is either raised up or falls away, just as we showed in the preceding explanation. For in the third book we specifically included what each individual star decrees when situated in each place. 

But you, with whatever prayers possible, implore that the course of either the beneficent or malevolent stars never occupies the sixth or twelfth place from the Ascendant, nor even the second and eighth, in the decrees of men. For these places are always occupied by the hostile radiations of all the stars. For whatever star settles into these places, it either loses the saving protection of its goodness, or, if it is a malignant star, it exasperates the power of its malice more strongly to do harm. Even malevolent stars are strengthened in these places when positioned with the Moon, and generally decree the destruction of misfortunes in all things without any remedy. Truly beneficent stars, closed off in a way in the hidden lowliness of these places, lose the saving protection of their power. 

But the changeable condition of the stars also works differently in daytime births than in nighttime births <term>genitura: a birth chart or the configuration of the stars at birth</term>. They have various powers of decreeing when the individual stars are joined to one another by a radiation that is trine, square, or diametrical <note>original: "trigonica, uel quadrata, uel diametra," referring to the 120, 90, and 180-degree angles between planets</note>. From this, the entire society of mixtures is tempered; from this, the entire power of the decrees is inspected. For the stars, always opposed to one another in turn according to their nature or condition, compose the fates of men with an equal moderation of variety. 

Therefore, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom this work is dedicated</note>, our glory, I will now explain to you this substance of the mixtures, so that I may instill in you the full discipline of this divine wisdom. But before our discourse proceeds to the explanation of the mixtures, I shall speak a few things to you concerning the royal powers of the brilliant stars, so that the beginnings of this book, adorned with the explanations of the majestic stars, may proceed under a more fortunate omen.

## THE ROYAL STARS OF THE SIGNS, AND 
### Their Decrees. Chapter I.

We find bright stars, shining with the radiation of majestic greatness, in all the signs; but we find the royal ones in four: namely, in Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. In which parts <note>original: "partibus," meaning specific degrees</note> of these signs you may find this majestic light, I shall show in a brief discourse. 

The fifth degree of Leo has a star shining with clear splendor <note>likely referring to Regulus, the "Heart of the Lion"</note>. If the Moon, increasing in light, is found in this star while the Ascendant is in Scorpio, presiding exactly over the angle <term>cardinis: one of the four pivotal points of the chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, or Lower Midheaven)</term>, it decrees kingdoms and the greatest commands of power. 

But also the twentieth degree of Aquarius is decorated with a similar splendor of majesty. For if the Moon is in this star at the time of rising, full of light, and possesses the primary angles of the birth chart, it decrees in a similar way the insignia of royal power and imperial dignity. 

Furthermore, the fifteenth degree, the twenty-seventh, and the thirtieth of Scorpio <note>original: "♏"</note> are likewise adorned with the light of majesty. For if the Moon is found in the fifteenth degree of Taurus <note>original: "♉" - Firmicus often notes stars by their opposition; here he describes the Moon in the opposite sign to the Scorpio degrees mentioned</note>, it decrees an increase of most powerful and affluent substance, provided it possesses the primary angles of the birth chart. 

But if the Moon is found in the twenty-seventh degree of Taurus, it decrees great insignia of dignity and makes such men who sustain the life of great populations by their own power, giving to the people whatever is demanded by popular zeal, and consecrating magnificent and famous gifts to the temples, so that they may be honored by these perpetual splendors of glory. 

Also the thirtieth degree, as we have said, of Taurus flashes with the divine light of majesty. For if the Moon is found in this part, it decrees the insignia of great power and license. For if, situated in this degree, she is found in the primary angles, she decrees leadership, empires, and kingship, especially if the favorable radiation of Jupiter looks upon her while she is increasing in light. For then, raised up by the license of their power and possessing the domains of both sea and land, they will lead an army fortunately wherever they go. 

The seventh degree of Scorpio will also produce these same effects; for a similar splendor of majesty adorns that very part. But the Moon situated in this part in the primary angles, along with the preceding marks of dignity, decrees an honor of dire cruelty and of immoderate terrors. For he who has the Moon thus, situated in the greatest license of power, roams with the fury of unbridled greed against all men...

rendered. Now, let us make known all the mixtures of the stars, as we promised, so that once the tempering of all of them has been composed, we may briefly explain everything we have promised. Regarding the bright stars of all the signs, I will tell you everything specifically in the eighth and final book, and regarding their decrees.

### THE RADIATIONS OF THE PLANETS AND THEIR DECREES: and first, the trine radiation of the planets. Chapter II.

All stars, if they regard each other with a trine <term>trigonus: an aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, forming a triangle</term> radiation, whether they are beneficent or malevolent, are compared to always prosperous mixtures of temperaments. Indeed, the wickedness of malevolent stars is mitigated by this radiation, while the most saving benefits of the beneficent stars are strengthened.

### THE TRINE ASPECT WITH THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter III.

<margin>Saturn with Jupiter in trine.</margin>
Therefore, if Saturn is joined with Jupiter by a trine radiation, even if this conjunction has vitiated sluggish and dejected places, provided they are both in the signs in which they rejoice, or one of them is situated in its own house and regards the other with a trine radiation, and they are joined to the Ascendant <term>horoscopus: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> by a degree-based radiation, they decree resources of infinite wealth with great happiness. This is especially true if one of them receives the light of the waxing Moon. For then Saturn grants ownership of infinite and great possessions; then he decrees sacred sowings, then pastures, and wooded glades. He will also make them public builders of certain sacred temples, yet in such a way that the greatest merit of dignity comes from that construction. He also makes them collectors of fiscal payments or overseers of the sacred grain supply <note>original: "sacræ annonæ"; the state-controlled grain dole and supply of ancient Rome</note>. But in these activities, he confers the greatest dignity of power; he will even advance them infinitely beyond their paternal dignity. But according to the measure and substance of the birth chart <term>genitura: a person's individual horoscope at birth</term>, he confers duties of administration on some, benefits from the greatest inheritances on others, and profits on others, even if sought through the labor of another. However, he commends all these powerful and great men with an incorruptible introduction of faith. But if Mercury joins the trine radiation of Saturn and Jupiter with an equal ray, he entrusts the secrets of sacred and inaccessible religions, such that he makes them manage the duties of great cities or kingdoms. He makes such men those to whom kings entrust all the duties of their actions, and frequently even impose the duty of a distinguished embassy. Yet these men are worn out by excessive misfortunes from the deaths of their sons, and losing their sons, they are forced to nourish another’s offspring, or certainly they receive their own sons back after a long span of time, having been raised by others. But they bring these things about if the birth is by day, without the testimony of Mars. For if either Mars strikes this mixture with a threatening radiation, or it is a nocturnal birth, all these things we have mentioned are diminished. Furthermore, he decrees the reproach of envy, oppositions, and the hatred of malicious insinuation, so that whatever good has been decreed, the hostile and hateful testimony of Mars attacks it.

<margin>Saturn and Mars</margin>
If Saturn is joined with Mars by a trine radiation, and this association is in favorable places of the birth chart, and both are in those signs or degrees in which they rejoice or in which they are exalted, and the testimony of Jupiter or Mercury is not lacking to them, they decree the greatest profits and daily gains and increases. They will also make such men whom a prosperous outcome follows in all actions, and who are raised up in every action by the license of power, acquiring the greatest marks of dignity for themselves by their own labors—notable, noble, authoritative, and governing the offices of the greatest cities. But these people constantly witness the painful deaths of their brothers.

<margin>Saturn and the Sun</margin>
If Saturn is joined with the Sun by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places of the birth chart and separated from all lowliness, and it is a daytime birth, they accumulate marks of life with constant promotions of dignity and decree the power of the greatest glory. They also confer fame and nobility. They also make their parents honored with a similar increase in dignity, especially if, situated in masculine signs, they are joined by this radiation. But if it is a nocturnal birth, the paternal wealth having been dissipated, they will cause an inheritance to be conferred on them by their own virtue.

♄ **Saturn**, if joined to ♀ **Venus** by a trine <term>trigonus: a harmonious aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, forming a triangle</term> radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart <note>original: "genituræ"</note> and removed from all the lowly states of their dejections <term>deiectio: also known as a "fall," the sign where a planet's influence is weakest</term>, will make the lives of men distinguished by a gentle moderation. They adorn their character with the ornament of modest conduct and keep them entirely removed from all impurity; however, because of this very distinction, a great deal of envy is stirred up against them by their inferiors. Yet, these same stars cause such individuals to be joined in marriage only late in life.

<margin>The star of Mercury rejoices when alone in the 12th place from the horoscope.</margin>
☿ **Saturn**, if joined to ☿ **Mercury** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, will make men sensible, talented, and always devoted to all the duties of the sciences <note>original: "disciplinarum"</note>. Their character will be adorned with the weight of mature gravity, and they will be the kind of people whose counsel is always strengthened by lively reasoning. They will either give actions based on logic, or they will certainly be placed in charge of public and fiscal accounts, or become royal scribes, such that great financial resources are granted to them from these activities. But it is proper for us to remember that the star of Mercury rejoices when it is situated alone in the twelfth place from the horoscope <note>The "horoscope" here refers to the Ascendant or first house; the 12th house was traditionally a difficult place, but Firmicus notes Mercury finds "joy" there</note>.

☽ **Saturn**, if joined to the ☽ **Moon** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, and the Moon is full of light, always introduces those who have this chart to kings, emperors, or powerful men with prosperous and happy recommendations. For the greatest marks of glory are decreed from this conjunction. If, however, the Moon is small in light <note>i.e., a waning or new moon</note>, the increases of the aforementioned happiness are diminished. But in this, we must also remember that the Moon alone is found to be fortunate in the eighth place from the horoscope in a nocturnal birth, especially if she is found in this place in the signs or "bounds" <term>fines: specific sub-divisions of a zodiac sign</term> where she rejoices and is full of light. For then she decrees marks of happiness and dignity, the greatest support of resources, high offices, and leadership from the power of that place—especially if ♃ Jupiter is found in the eleventh place from the horoscope.

### JUPITER WITH THE OTHER PLANETS in trine. Chapter IV.

<margin>Jupiter in trine with Mars.</margin>
♃ **Jupiter**, if joined to ♂ **Mars** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, decrees the greatest commands of dignity and great power of license. They render such individuals as complete all their actions with the most successful reasoning, and they decree duties of the greatest administration. They make those to whom frequent honors are conferred by the judgment of kings.

☉ **Jupiter**, if joined to the ☉ **Sun** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, decrees the greatest increases of nobility and abundant resources of flowing wealth. They also bestow marks of great glory, create the greatest joys from the successes of children, and always adorn and render a life honored with the clear distinction of dignity.

♀ **Jupiter**, if joined to ♀ **Venus** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, decrees the greatest grace of truth. They always associate the person with all good people through a likable conversation and always bring about the faithful love of wives toward them. However, the increases of inheritance and the marks of dignity are conferred upon them entirely through the protection of either friends or wives.

☿ **Jupiter**, if joined to ☿ **Mercury** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, makes men talented, sensible, and formed by the sharpest power of intellect, who execute all business with always prosperous outcomes. They also cause them to be placed above all men by merit of magnificent and most powerful dignity, and they make them such that in all acts they are always both praised and pleasing. They will also make scribes in charge of public and fiscal accounts, handling public duties without any blame, and arranging royal necessities by their own dispositions; they will also make others properly understand the secrets of the celestial stars <note>This refers to the study of astrology and astronomy</note>.

☽ **Jupiter**, if joined to the ☽ **Moon** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, and the Moon is also full of light...

### MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS

#### Trine Aspect. Chapter V.

<margin>Mars with the Sun in a trine aspect.</margin>
If ♂ **Mars** is joined to ☉ **the Sun** by a trine <term>trigonus: a harmonious aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart</term> radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection <term>deiectio: also known as a "fall," the sign where a planet's influence is weakest</term>, they decree the symbols of the greatest power and the highest dignity. This is especially true if, in a nocturnal birth <note>a chart for someone born at night</note>, the Sun is situated on the right side of Mars; for then the powers of glorious authority and the commands of high honors are decreed. If, however, while these are so arranged, ♃ **Jupiter** looks upon these same planets with a favorable radiation from another side of the trine, being positioned in the primary angles <term>cardines: the four most powerful points in a horoscope—the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term> of the birth chart and in a good place, and the rays of ☽ **the Moon** are added to all this, then they entrust the greatest military administrations and decree infinite symbols of dignity with the power of the greatest license. But these effects will be stronger if Mars, the Sun, and Jupiter are positioned in masculine signs.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If ♂ **Mars** is joined to ♀ **Venus** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, they decree daily profits from a steady continuation of gains; and they bring about the union of a prosperous marriage from this partnership. Such individuals will be those who always conduct themselves with grace and honor, though uplifted by a proud spirit of power; yet, while they may seek out many marriages, they will obtain these very things by the easiest means.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If ♂ **Mars** is joined to ☿ **Mercury** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, they make men wise and successful in all their actions through the logic of their plans. They are people whom a prosperous outcome always follows in every business dealing, and who are able to mitigate the hardships of all necessities through the authority of their counsel. They are sharp, effective, and handle the duties of accounting and calculations or literary offices.

<margin>Moon</margin>
If ♂ **Mars** is joined to ☽ **the Moon** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, and if the Moon is waning in light <note>original: "minuta luminibus"</note> and it is a nocturnal birth, they decree all the ornaments of happiness and grant successful outcomes in all actions with constant good fortune. They also ensure that individuals obtain everything they desire by the easiest means. But if ♄ **Saturn** looks upon this mixture of Mars and the Moon with its own radiation, men will surely promise the greatest things from such a configuration, and they will likewise decree the commands of dignity, glory, and grant the license of great power. By such a favorable radiation, they produce men who may rightly be compared to the first magistrates of the republic, and who hold dominion over many peoples, and by whose counsel even the deeds of princes are managed, and who possess the highest power and veneration among nations. If, however, the Moon is full of light, amidst these prosperities they nevertheless weaken the body with the constant affliction of various illnesses and sometimes consume it with many troubles and the hindrances of disturbances through their fatal radiation.

They grant them the rewards of many goods; they make them noble and distinguished, to whom many symbols of happiness are decreed. This is especially so if they are further adorned by the favorable testimony of other planets' partnership, such that the Sun itself fully receives the light of the Moon not while it is waning, but while it is waxing. ### VENUS WITH THE MOON ALONE, TRINE. Chapter VII.

If ♀ **Venus** is joined to ☽ **the Moon** by a trine <term>trigonus: an aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, usually considered harmonious</term> radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection <term>deiectio: the "fall," or the sign where a planet's power is most weakened</term>, and if the Moon is decreasing in light <note>original: "minuta luminibus"</note> and it is a nocturnal birth, the highest marks of happiness are decreed through them. For then successful actions and glory proceed from this partnership of conjunction. Then maternal affection for children grows; then marriages are preserved with the faith of incorruptible modesty; then grace is always introduced through the lovable affection of children; then brothers are loved with faithful affection; then the graces of beauty, the joy of happiness, and the glorious discipline of power are handed down to mortals.

### MERCURY WITH THE MOON ALONE, TRINE. Chapter VIII.

If ☿ **Mercury** is joined to ☽ **the Moon** by a trine radiation, and both are positioned in favorable places in the birth chart and removed from all the lowly states of dejection, they decree all things according to the variety of the signs. For to some they assign eloquence of speech; for others they decree distinguished marks of the arts; to others they hand down the sweet sound of music; others they make painters—but the kind whose noble excellence always introduces their arts. To others they decree the power of arms; to others they hand down the discipline of joy and gladness. Others, singing with sweet modulation, they assign to popular pleasures; but all these people they always introduce to the judgment of the public through faithful recommendation. Others they make into those who handle the duties of business. But they explain all these things according to the testimonies of the other stars, and according to the strengths of the places and signs. Which trines are "right-handed" and which are "square" was explained in the second book.

### THE SQUARE RADIATION OF ALL PLANETS. Chapter IX.

Now I shall tell you the decrees of the square <term>quadrata: an aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart, usually indicating tension or conflict</term> radiation, which is a partnership always composed of a strong and threatening star. For from this conjunction, the power of malevolent stars is increased, and the protections of benevolent stars are sometimes overcome. For a threatening radiation, along with a diametrical <note>opposition, or 180 degrees</note> conjunction, always rages with equal power in the perpetration of evils.

### ♄ SATURN WITH THE OTHER PLANETS, SQUARE. Chapter X.

<margin>Saturn joined to Jupiter in a square.</margin>
If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ♃ **Jupiter** by a square radiation, and Saturn is superior <note>meaning it has a more dominant position in the chart's order</note> and possesses the higher part of the right square, while Jupiter, placed in the left square, appears inferior, they decree crises of life, diminish the substance of the inheritance, turn the counsels of all men toward the perverse, impede actions, and disturb their minds with various dissensions of the soul. They also attack fathers with various kinds of calamity and dissipate paternal substance through various tearings-away. If, however, Jupiter is made superior and possesses the right side, while Saturn, positioned in the left square, looks upon him, the misfortunes of the preceding calamities are mitigated; the parents are ennobled by some splendor of praise or glory, and according to the measure of the birth chart, daily benefits of profit and increases in happiness are conferred upon them.

<margin>♂ Mars</margin>
If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ♂ **Mars** by a square radiation, and Saturn is made superior and, possessing the right square, looks upon Mars positioned in the left with a threatening radiation, they always impede all actions through this conjunction with ineffective zeal, and they make people strangers to every duty of business because of a cold numbness of the mind. They also always indicate illnesses of various kinds, so that a cold mixed with heat shakes their body in a dreadful continuation. This conjunction also squanders the resources of the paternal substance and always shows the deaths of brothers through a heavy case of misfortunes. If, however, Mars is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon Saturn established in an inferior place with a square radiation, he prepares a swift end of death for the mother from this conjunction; but these people [he leads] toward all prosperous [actions and...] <note>The text cuts off mid-sentence; the catchword "conatus" suggests the next page begins with "efforts" or "attempts."</note>

->### BOOK SIX.<-

If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ☉ **the Sun** by a square radiation <term>quadrata radiatio: an aspect where planets are 90 degrees apart, typically associated with obstacles and tension</term>, and Saturn itself holds the higher part of the right square <note>In ancient astrology, the planet in the "right" or "dexter" position—the 10th house relative to the other planet—is said to "overcome" or dominate the aspect</note>, looking upon the Sun positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction weakens the marks of the preceding lineage. It decrees a loss of dignity with a bitter diminishment of honor, and deforms their bodies with a constant contraction of the nerves; it even binds their parents with this same stain of misfortune. It also causes these same fathers to perish before the mothers, but it decrees that the individuals themselves always wander in various kinds of sins, and determines their ruin through the company of harmful people. It always indicates grave illnesses arising from the bitter coldness of the humors <term>humores: the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which ancient doctors believed governed health and temperament</term>; it also equally cuts off and shatters the patrimony and all actions. But if ☉ **the Sun** is made superior and holds the right side, looking upon ♄ **Saturn** established in the lower place with a square radiation, this conjunction disperses the paternal substance and always indicates grave enmities from those within the household; it always attacks every impulse of the mind and all actions with various kinds of indignation. Furthermore, it never allows plans to have successful results, and in early age, it indicates bitter and frequent inconveniences of illnesses, weakening the body, which is exhausted by a manifold continuation of sickness and a frequency of evils.

If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ♀ **Venus** by a square radiation, and Saturn itself holds the higher part of the right square, looking upon ♀ **Venus** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction indicates a grave burden of beggary once the patrimony has been squandered; it always threatens ruinous ends from the bitter calamities of women. It grants no grace of beauty, nor does it ever allow their desires to have successful results. But if ♀ **Venus** is made superior and holds the right side, looking upon ♄ **Saturn** established in the lower place with a square radiation, this conjunction grants wives of honorable and modest character; but they are wives who claim all power of ruling in the home. Nevertheless, they love their husbands with a faithful and incorruptible affection, so that a conjugal grace associates them both in turn, though they may try to hide their love with a certain dissimulation.

If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ☿ **Mercury** by a square radiation, and Saturn itself holds the higher part of the right square, looking upon ☿ **Mercury** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction decrees ruin from the first day of birth. It equally attacks all thoughts of the mind and all orders of counsel, and always pursues all actions with a cold lethargy. It also makes them always subject to the powers of others, though in their actions they may handle the secondary duties of business; yet it indicates to them the greatest storms of envy. For some, a bound tongue will create a stuttering sound of the voice; others it makes deaf with dull ears. These defects persist unless they are mitigated by ☿ **Mercury** being removed from the bad testimony of ☉ **the Sun**. But if ☿ **Mercury** is made superior and holds the right side, looking upon ♄ **Saturn** established in the lower place with a square radiation, nothing good indeed is decreed from this partnership of conjunction, but the wickedness of the preceding misfortunes is somewhat mitigated.

If ♄ **Saturn** is joined to ☽ **the Moon** by a square radiation, and Saturn itself holds the higher part of the right square, looking upon ☽ **the Moon** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction will cause the body to be fatigued by malicious humors, and will make them separated from all actions by the sluggish lethargy of the mind; it renders them such that they can never dare to attempt any actions. Moreover, this conjunction always dissipates the maternal substance with wretched tearing apart, so that it makes sons undergo parricidal <note>original: "parricidalia," here likely meaning deadly or unnaturally bitter family strife rather than actual murder</note> struggles of enmity against their mothers. But if ☽ **the Moon** is made superior and holds the right side, looking upon ♄ **Saturn** established in the lower place with a square radiation, this conjunction casts them down in a wretched death and surrounds the native with a bitter continuation of dangers; it indicates ruin from grave illness due to malignant humors, and causes them to be fatigued by various misfortunes of errors. It also always indicates losses and forfeitures of marriage and honor; and unless this conjunction is supported by the protection of other stars, it exasperates bitter dissensions of hatred in the wife's mind and leaves the individual destitute of all protection from friends and children.

## JUPITER WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### In Square Aspect. Chapter XI.

<margin>Jupiter joined to Mars by a square radiation.</margin>
If **♃ Jupiter** is joined to **♂ Mars** by a square radiation <term>quadrata radiatio: an aspect of 90 degrees, considered an "aspect of enmity" or tension in ancient astrology</term>, and Jupiter himself occupies the superior part of the right square <note>original: "dextri quadrati superiorem... partem." In ancient astrology, a planet in the 10th house relative to another planet is said to "overcome" or dominate it from the "right"</note>, looking upon Mars positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction determines the highest marks of glory. It always commends these individuals with a good reputation; it will cause some to be involved in military duties and will assign others to royal houses, decreeing for them the duties of noble and public actions. It will cause them to be elevated by the duties of business, so that they attain these businesses with the greatest increase in dignity; but these people will never be able to preserve their father's estate <note>original: "paternae substantiae facultatem"</note> well. Furthermore, this conjunction always indicates constant grief from the misfortunes of children, or certainly will cause children to be born late in life. 

But if **♂ Mars** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **♃ Jupiter** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation: this conjunction sharpens every fiery impulse of the mind. It will cause one to stumble through various errors throughout their whole life, and compels men to undergo the hardships of great labor without cause; but this labor is obtained either from public or royal actions. Moreover, it decrees the dangers of malicious insinuations and bitter accusations with a hostile heat.

**☉ Jupiter and the Sun:** If **♃ Jupiter** is joined to **☉ the Sun** by a square radiation, and Jupiter himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Sun positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction decrees marks of dignity through both one's own and one's father's merit. It also grants increases of goods and great honors, as well as promotions, and always commends them with a good testimony, so that many people are subject to them by right of their dignity. 

But if **☉ the Sun** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **♃ Jupiter** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation: this conjunction will make a man adorned with the bright splendor of nobility, but it will cause his patrimony <note>The inherited estate</note> to be recorded in a wretched public confiscation <note>original: "publicatione conscribi," referring to the state seizure of property</note>, and it will stir up threatening crowds of misfortunes and evil enemies.

**♀ Jupiter and Venus:** If **♃ Jupiter** is joined to **♀ Venus** by a square radiation, and Jupiter himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Venus positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction always associates the person with the friendships of many. It will cause both actions and gains to be conferred through the protection of women by that same reasoning, and it always adorns the entire substance of life with honorable dignity; it will also cause these same people to observe the religions of the gods with devoted veneration. 

But if **♀ Venus** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **♃ Jupiter** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation: from this conjunction, he decrees the allurements of loves. Regarding the care of the body, he always indicates ornate clothing and decrees the luxurious desires of the will. But as often as they have attained the prosperous joys of happiness, so often will the decrees of these fates be changed into the opposite, and their happiness will slip into a worse state.

**☿ Jupiter and Mercury:** If **♃ Jupiter** is joined to **☿ Mercury** by a square radiation, and Jupiter himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon Mercury positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: from this conjunction are decreed the duties of writing or the liberal arts <term>liberales artes: the traditional curriculum of a free citizen, including grammar, rhetoric, and logic</term>. They are put in charge of accounts and computations; patrimony and career are also conferred upon them from some kind of public defense. 

But if **☿ Mercury** is made superior and occupies the right side, looking upon **♃ Jupiter** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation: this conjunction will provide a sufficient support of resources. However, these people always hinder themselves in every action, avoiding all good things as if they were evil due to an unknown fear of the mind. They will be such that whatever they desire to obtain even with great prayers, they will despise the whole of it with an obstinate judgment of the mind even if it happens to them by chance; they are people who neither desire any benefits to be conferred upon them by others, nor do they themselves attempt to acquire any good for themselves.

**☾ Jupiter and the Moon:** If **♃ Jupiter** is joined to **☾ the Moon** by a square radiation, and Jupiter himself occupies the superior part of the right square, looking upon the Moon positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation: this conjunction decrees infinite riches for both the mother and the individual himself. It indicates the greatest duties of business, and places him above all his kinsmen by the merit of great dignity, so that in the highest... <meta>The text cuts off here as the catchword "gradu" (step/degree) indicates the beginning of the next page.</meta>

## MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### In Square Aspect. Chapter XII.

<margin>Mars square the Sun.</margin>
If **♂ Mars** is joined to the **☉ Sun** by a square radiation, and he himself, possessing the superior part of the right square, looks upon the **☉ Sun** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction omits no case of misfortune; rather, it always attacks all opportunities for advancement and the ranks of promotions with a malignant arrangement. But if the **☉ Sun** is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon **♂ Mars** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation, a miserable death is prepared for both the father and the one who is born from this conjunction, and a heap of misfortunes is added, and various inconveniences of calamities are decreed: for it stirs up seditions, proclaims battles, and rouses fearsome dangers of public punishment <term>popularis animaduersio: literally "notice of the people," referring here to legal prosecution or public execution</term>; it also destroys the foundations of an intact mind and plans, and always imposes the miserable weight of blindness upon the eyes. Furthermore, these dangerous crises are more strongly roused in a diurnal birth chart <term>diurna genitura: a chart where the Sun is above the horizon</term>, especially if the conjunction itself is joined to the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc." or Horoscopus</note> with a threatening logic; or if **♂ Mars**, positioned in the setting <note>the West or 7th house</note> or possessing the **Midheaven** <note>original: "MC" or Medium Coeli</note>, looks upon the part of the **☉ Sun**, which, being positioned in another cardine <term>cardine: one of the four "pivotal" houses (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th)</term>, receives the light of the waxing **☽ Moon**. For then, they cast down the natives by public punishment and scatter them with miserable tearings of the flesh; then also, with limbs torn by popular fury, the honor of a due burial is denied; so that both in life and after death, as the danger of punishment persists, the greater outcome of calamity is increased. But in a nocturnal birth chart, these same things are perpetrated by a similar order of logic from this conjunction.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **♂ Mars** is joined to **♀ Venus** by a square radiation, and he himself, possessing the superior part of the right square, looks upon **♀ Venus** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction decrees all evils; for then it proclaims quarrels and accusations and fearsome dangers; then losses shake the man on account of a woman. But if this conjunction occurs in tropical signs <term>tropical signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn, which mark the turning points of the seasons</term>, then all the impurity of unchastity gathers in the effeminate bodies of men, and then men will suffer the fires of womanly lusts; then, with the shipwreck of shame and reputation, they are polluted by the stains of unchaste impurity. Furthermore, they will compel their own wives to commit adultery, and they surrender the patience of their prostituted shame to the embraces of others; and they force a marriage joined under evil omens to serve the lusts of others with the miserable necessity of calamity; or with the mind of a pimp, they willingly acknowledge the hidden adultery of a wife, even if the women sustain this necessity of a prostituted body through the husband with bitter grief of soul. But if **♀ Venus** is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon **♂ Mars** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation, she decrees these same things by a similar logic; but those who have **♀ Venus** so placed exercise their crime secretly, so that the wicked trade of prostituted shame may be protected by the hidden impurities of lusts, and a bad conscience may conceal whatever has been perpetrated by the vicious desires of the soul, especially if **♃ Jupiter**, either positioned with one of them or looking upon them with a trine radiation <note>an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note>, should intervene.

Ancient astrologers distinguished between charts of people born during the day versus at night, as different planets held more power in each</note>; in a night birth, however, they are mitigated to some extent. Furthermore, it causes the natives themselves to be entangled in the bitter incursions of demons, so that the soul, possessed by the power of a malignant spirit, grants the demon the power of dominating the body—especially if **♂ Mars** is found in the bounds of **♄ Saturn**, and the **☽ Moon** is in the bounds of either **♄ Saturn** or **♂ Mars** <note>The "bounds" or *fines* are specific degrees within a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note>. But those who are possessed by such a calamity of misfortunes, avoiding these dangers of incursions, flee to the saving protection of some deity, so that they may thus be liberated from the crisis of that peril.

If, however, the **☽ Moon** is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon **♂ Mars** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation, this conjunction makes the mother of an ignoble and dejected birth; it also always indicates narrow circumstances of life resulting from miserable necessity. It prostrates the fate and the substance of life with the dejection of miserable humility. Among these misfortunes, and even with the greatest increase of unhappiness, it also decrees bad wives: those who not only try to attack their husbands with a certain proud kind of arrogance, but also strive to dissipate the entire substance of the family estate. Even if perhaps any happiness was promised by the favorable radiation of other stars, these wives always study to turn it away by their own wickedness, and they daily think to disturb their spouses and almost the whole household with various insults.

If this conjunction is also struck by the adverse radiation of malefic stars, they will be shaken by a detriment that is worse in proportion to the power of those who have provoked this "sinister consolation" of the stars with a threatening ray. But if **♂ Mars** and the **☽ Moon** are unhappily positioned, and joined in an adverse confederation in dejected places of the birth chart, even if the testimony of benevolent stars is present, though their radiation may be of little help, some of the aforementioned evils are occasionally diminished—especially if such benevolent stars are in a good state or rejoicing in some of their own power.

# THE SUN WITH THE MOON ALONE IN SQUARE
## Chapter XIII.

If the **☉ Sun** is joined to the **☽ Moon** by a square radiation, whether they preside over the right or the left side cardinally <note>meaning they are in "angles" or "pivot points" of the chart, such as the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, if the influence of prosperous happiness is added to the decrees for the man from the rays of other stars, the greatest deeds, a sufficient substance of life, and the insignia of glorious dignity are conferred from always favorable commendations. Often, with the laudable applause of good men, the business of magistracies and royal offices are granted, not without great profit.

But if malefic stars, without the protection of benevolent ones, meet this society of the **☉ Sun** and the **☽ Moon** with a malignant radiation, the greatest crises of life and the inconveniences of misfortunes are decreed. Unless one overcomes these by the skillful prudence of the mind, they lead the man at some point to the highest calamity. ### **♀ VENUS** SQUARE WITH THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter XIV.

<margin>
How a square aspect between **♀ Venus** and **☿ Mercury** can occur from one to the other, I cannot know. For the greatest distance by which they can be separated from each other is 75 degrees <note>In modern astronomy, the maximum elongation of Venus is about 47° and Mercury 28°. Firmicus correctly notes they can never be 90° apart, making a "square" impossible by degree</note>, unless you wish to understand it "platically" <note>original: "platicè." From the Greek *platys* (broad). In astrology, this means counting the aspect by whole signs rather than by the exact degree</note>.
</margin>

If **☿ Mercury** is joined to **♀ Venus** by a square radiation, with whichever of them possessing the right or left square, they decree all things in an equal manner. For this conjunction promises the duties of famous, lovely, and worthy arts, or a discipline of great learning is handed down from this conjunction, so that from this duty of instruction, the joy of a famous life may follow. But, because of love affairs, the malicious talk of envious people spreads a mark of infamy upon them.

If the **☽ Moon** is joined by a square radiation, and the **☽ Moon**, possessing the superior part of the right square, looks upon **♀ Venus** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, this conjunction decrees the greatest gains of wealth. But it always affects men with various losses on account of women, or always imposes the weight of infamy. If, however, **♀ Venus** is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon the **☽ Moon** established in a lower place with a square radiation, she always increases the greatest happiness with prosperous growth and decrees better things than the preceding goods. This conjunction also adorns one's actions, life, and social standing; it preserves the incorrupt love of a wife and decrees pure and good affections of spouses. It also decrees benefits full of joy, the insignias of famous arts, an honorable order of life, and the grace of sweet speech with the greatest happiness. Nevertheless, it indicates sexual unions with others through impatient desire; yet it grants an honorable glory of chastity to their mothers. These men, however, obtain obedient wives from the manumissions <note>The formal act of freeing a slave</note> of others.

### **☿ MERCURY** SQUARE WITH THE **☽ MOON**. Chapter XV.

If **☿ Mercury** is joined to the **☽ Moon** by a square radiation, and he himself, possessing the superior part of the right square, looks upon the **☽ Moon** positioned in the left square with a threatening radiation, he indicates those who are wisely adorned from this conjunction, endowed with the eloquence of learned speech and honorable talk. But a crisis is frequently brought upon these people from popular sedition. If **☿ Mercury** is so positioned and a malevolent star is made superior and looks upon it with a square radiation—such that the **☽ Moon** looks from an opposition and **♃ Jupiter** from a square—it strikes them with the fear of a false accusation. In that crime, if they are detected, it causes them either to be placed in custody or thrust into prison, or to undergo chains, exile, or the punishment of a public sentence. If, however, the **☽ Moon** is made superior and, possessing the right side, looks upon **☿ Mercury** positioned in a lower place with a square radiation, this conjunction will make them unstable with a lightness of mind, and will shift their plans here and there with varied thought, so that their mind never uses the logic of a single counsel. The authority of the fates brings forth these decrees from square radiations in the births of men, and these sentences from the square sides, day by day—which you ought to inspect diligently in every treatise, especially since this same square change of stars causes the decrees of statutes to be changed. But having explained these, I will also specifically make known the efficiencies of the oppositions <note>original: "diametrorum." Literally "diameters," referring to planets 180 degrees apart</note>. Which squares are right and which are left, we have stated most clearly in the book of instruction.

### THE OPPOSITION RADIATION OF ALL PLANETS. Chapter XVI.

Now I will explain to you the decrees of the opposition radiation, which partnership is always composed by a threatening star and, most of all, destroys the condition and nature of the stars and forces them for the most part to tend toward unhappiness. For an opposition radiation always fights against itself with contrary power and rises up with a hostile kind of partnership against itself; and just like the square, it is always a threatening radiation.

### THE WORKS OF JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

<margin>Saturn in diametrical radiation with Jupiter.</margin>
If they strike each other from opposite places <note>The OCR reads "tuti locis" (in safe places), but context and parallel passages in the *Mathesis* suggest "contrariis locis" (in opposite places).</note> with the long-lasting power of their strengths, this conjunction decrees many destructive misfortunes in all actions: and it always imposes the bitter torments of grief from the death of children. But if **♄ Saturn** is positioned as a cardinal point <note>A planet on one of the four "hinges" of the chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses. These are the most powerful positions.</note> in the degree of the **Ascendant** <note>term: horoscopus. The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> or in the Ascendant itself, and looks upon **♃ Jupiter** positioned in the **Setting** <note>term: occasus. The 7th house or Descendant, where the sun sets</note> by a diametrical radiation, then after the heavy misfortunes of youth, the slow benefits of happiness will be granted in the final period of old age.

**♂ Mars**
</margin>
If **♄ Saturn** looks upon **♂ Mars** by diametrical radiation, so that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long power of their strengths, this radiation decrees the inconveniences of heavy dangers and many anxieties: for it will cause most people to be entangled in many evil oppositions, and it will cause them to be struck by the bitter stain of envy, and it imposes the wretched straits of necessity. It will also cause the body to be fatigued by constant illnesses and a continuation of labors: it always imposes heavy life-dangers and frequently shows the image of a fearsome death: it decrees the incursions of domestic enmities and stirs up frequent storms of terrible seditions. It also denies the birth of children, causes the father to be struck down by a swift death, and perpetuates labors after labors in a constant succession. 

But if **♄ Saturn** and **♂ Mars**, being positioned in **watery signs** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>, look upon each other by diametrical radiation as we have described, then it exposes the person to raging waves, submerged and shipwrecked by gales and heavy storms: or it will cause them to be entangled in many dangerous crises, overwhelmed by the heavier waves of rushing torrents: or a plague thickened by malignant moisture imposes strong and perpetual calamities of sickness. But if one of them is positioned in a **bestial sign** <note>Signs representing wild animals, such as Leo or the latter part of Sagittarius</note> and looks upon the other by diametrical radiation, it brings a wretched crisis of danger from the strike of a four-footed or wild beast: for others, the venom of poison inflamed in their marrow decrees the bitter end of death by a mournful calamity. 

But if they are positioned in **quadruped signs** <note>Signs representing four-footed animals like Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, and Capricorn</note>, or if only one of them is so placed and looks upon the other by diametrical radiation, then along with those evils we mentioned previously, they either die or are forced to undergo dangers near to death, crushed and scattered by the heavy weight of ruins and worn out by the tearing of the body. But all these misfortunes grow strong with a heavy heap of calamity when **♃ Jupiter** mitigates them with no radiations. 

For if, while they possess the **cardines** <note>term: geniturae cardines. The four angles or pillars of the birth chart: East, West, North, and South</note> of the birth, the **☽ Moon**—positioned in any cardinal point—should look upon them with this same radiation, or in a square aspect, then this conjunction decrees heavier dangers, then fugitive wanderings, then exiles and public deaths: then, with the honor of liberty snatched away, it imposes the yoke of wretched slavery. 

But if they are positioned in the fifth, tenth, or ninth house from the Ascendant and look upon each other by diametrical radiation, they always extinguish every outcome of prosperous happiness and decree the ruin of a wretched failing with a falling humility. But these misfortunes grow stronger in the middle period of life. However, if they are positioned in failing or **idle places** <note>term: pigris locis. These are "cadent" houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th) which were thought to be less active or effective</note> and look upon each other by diametrical radiation, they will indeed do less harm: but nevertheless, they decree pains and the inconveniences of wretched poverty from that radiation. But all these fearsome dangers of evil things are mitigated by the favorable testimonies of **♀ Venus** and **♃ Jupiter**: and the malice of the malevolent stars is blunted by the prosperous testimony of a saving god <note>note: original "dei salutaris." In this astrological context, Firmicus is likely referring to the planet Jupiter, often called the "Greater Benefic" or "Salvific Star"</note>, and the threatening outcomes of the preceding dangers are mostly resolved.

<margin>**☉ Sun**</margin>
If **♄ Saturn** looks upon the **☉ Sun** by diametrical radiation, so that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long power of their strengths, and the saving star **♃ Jupiter** does not look upon them from any part, they will either cause the father to be entangled in laborious necessities, or they will certainly impose the weight of a laborious life upon the individuals themselves, or they decree the straits of poverty with a certain tenacity, while for others they mark a bitter danger to health. And even if they have any resources of wealth, these perish while they are still surviving, or are scattered by wretched tearings after their death. They also decree the end of an evil death from this radiation, and the substance of the whole life is shaken by various and evil continuations of labors. Moreover, the wickedness of these evils grows more strongly if, being positioned in **feminine signs** <note>The signs of the Earth and Water elements</note>, they look upon each other by this radiation at the same time.
