But if a marriage was decreed by the rest of the birth chart's makeup <note>original: "geniturae substantia"</note>, they will obtain a wife who brings detriment to their own honor: or certainly a wife is decreed for others whom a deadly vice always defiles with a wretched contagion: or she is always significantly older: and even to these people, every grace of Venusian beauty is denied.

<margin>☿ Mercury</margin> If Saturn looks upon **Mercury** with a diametrical radiation <note>An aspect where planets are directly opposite each other in the zodiac.</note>, so that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their strengths, they impede the tongue with a slow-sounding voice: so that in the very throat, words fail, hindered by slow efforts, or are confused by a binding of the tongue. But these evils grow stronger if Mercury is positioned in a **mute sign** <note>Signs such as Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, which were traditionally thought to hinder speech.</note> and Saturn looks upon it with a diametrical radiation: or if Mercury, hidden **under the rays** <note>term: combust. When a planet is so close to the Sun that its light and power are overwhelmed or "burnt up."</note> of the **Sun**, is struck by a diametrical radiation from Saturn. Furthermore, if Saturn looks upon the **Moon** when she is joined in the same partnership with Mercury by a diametrical radiation, these evils we mentioned grow stronger—unless the testimony of **Mars**, provided in some way, eases the disadvantage of the preceding malice: for with the others we mentioned, without the testimony of Mars, even a fatal weight of labor is imposed. Yet with these mental evils, a wisdom of discipline is decreed, and skilled mastery of studies is granted: but they always watch over the study of their art with ineffective zeal, and the sadness of their haste always worsens their inner turmoil. They themselves are also lifted up by a haughty spirit of pride, and they generate various hatreds and anxieties for themselves every day; they are even preferred over their brothers in order of age. For whoever were the older brothers, they will be separated either by death or by long travels abroad: they also see their mothers perish for the most part in their youth.

<margin>☽ Moon</margin> If Saturn looks upon the **Moon** with a diametrical radiation, so that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long power of their rays, they first cause the substance of the mother’s resources to be undermined: they also weaken the mother herself with a continuation of various pains and hidden sicknesses, or they always involve her in the sadness of perverse circumstances. If the radiation of benevolent stars <note>Jupiter or Venus.</note> has moved away from them, and they are destitute of all testimony from the health-giving stars, then a dishonest filthiness of the body disgraces the mother, and losses shake her with constant attacks: but various dangers and crises always rise for the individuals themselves as well. These things Saturn and the Moon decree according to the variety of the signs: for if one is positioned in **quadruped signs** <note>Signs representing four-legged animals, such as Aries, Taurus, Leo, or the latter half of Sagittarius.</note> and looks upon the other with a diametrical radiation, the danger is brought by such animals. If, however, they are positioned in **feminine signs** and look upon each other with this radiation, a deadly end is prepared from wild beasts, or monsters, or from the poisonous bites of serpents. If this diameter occurs in **human signs** <note>Signs representing human figures, like Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>, a variety of calamities arises from the plots of men. If they are positioned in **watery signs** and strike their rays with diametrical obstinacy, a wretched crisis of pestilence is brought by floods of water or by malignant humors <note>In ancient medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids; an imbalance caused disease.</note>. And if no protection from benevolent stars breaks the power of the threatening radiation, the entire form of the body is changed by the calamity of a foul sickness: or the clear light of the eyes is shadowed by the darkness of wretched blindness. For others, stars so positioned compel them to desert their fatherland by the necessity of various dangers and crises.

It also decrees all the ornaments of power, and makes such a person who can never be subject to foreign powers, and who always, by the grace of virtue and constancy of mind, confidently resists foreign powers. But if the Moon is diminished in light, they decree nothing of the preceding goods, but rather the greatest destructions of misfortunes. These evils grow stronger if it is a nighttime birth decreed with a similar conjunction.

## MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### The Diameter [Opposition]. Chapter XIX.

<margin>Mars with the Sun in diameter.</margin> If **Mars** looks upon the **Sun** with a diametrical radiation, so that being positioned in opposite places, they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their rays, and if it is a daytime birth, this radiation strikes down the father with a wretched atrocity of death, or always blinds the light of the eyes with illness. It casts the persons themselves down from high places, hurling them down with wretched tearing, or a heavy danger is always brought to the unsuspecting, and it causes all actions to be hindered by heavy oppositions. # BOOK SIX

...provided that **Jupiter** (♃) has offered no prosperous or happy testimony in this configuration.

If **Mars** (♂) looks at **Mercury** (☿) with a diametrical radiation <note>An "opposition," the astrological aspect where two planets are 180 degrees apart, often considered a source of tension or conflict.</note>, such that they are positioned in opposite places and strike one another with the long-lasting power of their rays, this conjunction decrees the most extreme forms of misfortune and calamity. For those who have Mars and Mercury in this position either incur the crime of forgery by altering the integrity of records and writings, or they are joined in a fellowship of every wicked deed born of a guilty conscience, or they enter into a life of criminal partnership with sorcerers and poisoners. Alternatively, they are forever oppressed by the heavy interest of debts and are dragged into public trials with the loss of their reputation. These individuals are also possessed by a perverse fire of greed; polluting the dealings of religious faith, they attempt to deny property that was deposited or entrusted to them. As a result of this treachery or their previous crimes, they face the danger of public sentencing, and being subjected to the power of judges, they are shaken by the terrifying dread of legal cases. Others, haunted by the terrors of their past deeds and exhausted by the burden of a guilty conscience, are separated from their errors <note>Likely meaning they are cast out or isolated due to their mistakes.</note>—especially if **Mercury** is found in the bounds of **Saturn** (♄), or in Saturn’s house, or in his own house in a daytime birth chart <note>original: "diurna genitura"</note>, and **Jupiter** does not look upon either of them with a trine radiation <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious and protective.</note>.

If **Mars** (♂) looks at the **Moon** (☽) with a diametrical radiation, such that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their rays, they will either make the subjects short-lived <note>original: "oligochronios," a Greek term for those with a brief lifespan</note>, or pursue them with a series of grave dangers. They do not decree marriage; or, if a wife is granted through the protection of other stars, she will perish in wretched and agonizing death. The subjects themselves will also die a bad death, or be laid low by public execution, especially if the Moon was full of her light and rays.

### THE SUN WITH THE MOON ALONE IN OPPOSITION
->Chapter XX.<-

If the **Sun** (☉) looks at the **Moon** (☽) with a diametrical radiation, such that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their rays, they cause the life and status of the person, the order of their substance <note>Their wealth or property.</note>, and all marks of dignity to change for various reasons. For then, after wealth has been gathered, the burden of poverty is brought back again; and the hardships of poverty are again eased by the comforts of other riches. Thus the person’s condition is ambiguous: at one moment they are wealthy, exulting in abundant resources; at another they are destitute, forced to seek the means of a miserable life through unseemly and shameful profit. They also cause blemishes of unseemly ill-health upon the face, which deeply stain the body itself and deform it with a certain foul ugliness. Sometimes, through a strange and pitiable kind of sickness, they even weaken the body itself with wretched contractions, so that the debilitated limbs can scarcely fulfill their desired duty for the necessary uses of life.

### VENUS WITH THE MOON ALONE IN OPPOSITION
->Chapter XXI.<-

If **Venus** (♀) looks at the **Moon** (☽) with a diametrical radiation, such that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their rays, they decree unhappy marriages from this alignment; nor, when positioned thus, do they allow the person to be raised up by any order of happiness. For they will either never have children, or they will see the offspring they have received laid low by a wretched death. Furthermore, the men themselves are forced to endure frequent evils and many injuries from their wives, who, desiring to dominate their husbands, frequently lash out at them with a proud and arrogant spirit.

### MERCURY WITH THE MOON ALONE IN OPPOSITION
->Chapter XXII.<-

If **Mercury** (☿) looks at the **Moon** (☽) with a diametrical radiation, such that being positioned in opposite places they strike each other with the long-lasting power of their rays, they stir up the violence of an unrestrained multitude and popular seditions, as well as bloody crises, so that the spiteful voice of the people always pursues them in public gatherings. They also instill a foul state of dread and trembling through both their mind and words, having cast aside all courage.

JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

# THE SEXTILE RADIATION OF 
### ALL PLANETS. Chapter XXIII.

When stars look upon each other with a **sextile** radiation <note>original: "hexagona radiatione"; the sextile is an aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart, or two signs away from each other.</note>, they determine outcomes in the same way we said they do from a **trine** radiation <note>original: "trigonia radiatione"; an aspect of 120 degrees, generally considered harmonious.</note>. However, the effect of their decrees is diminished in some part, and the radiation, being deprived of its full vigor, composes its influence with less power in all birth charts. But it is important for you to remember that sextiles have an effect on strength if they are divided by **tropical** <note>Signs marking the start of seasons: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn.</note> or **double** <note>Also known as "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note> signs. They truly manifest their effectiveness, however, whenever a **fixed** sign <note>original: "solidum signum"; Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius.</note> intervenes in such a radiation.

# THE EQUAL RADIATION OF 
### ALL PLANETS. Chapter XXIIII.

In order to fully inform you, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work.</note>—our great honor—of the complete effectiveness of planetary mixtures, we have now disentangled the trines and the squares, and specially explained every diametrical radiation <note>Oppositions.</note>. Now, we shall mark the joined associations of the stars with a clear interpretation of speech. Once the tempering of every mixture has been shown, we may come to the specific decrees of the **results** <note>term: "apotelesmatum" — from the Greek *apotelesma*, referring to the predicted effects or outcomes of astrological configurations.</note>.

# SATURN TOGETHER WITH 
### THE OTHER PLANETS. Chapter XXV.

<margin>$\saturn$ Saturn and $\jupiter$ Jupiter positioned together.</margin>
If **Saturn** (♄) and **Jupiter** (♃) have received lodging in the same degree <note>original: "unum partis hospitium"; meaning they are in the exact same degree of the same sign, a "conjunction."</note>, and being positioned together in one place, they are joined by an equal power of association, they decree certain outcomes. If they are joined in favorable places of the birth chart <note>term: "genitura" — the individual's horoscope or birth chart.</note>, and in signs or degrees in which they rejoice, they decree marks of happiness, increases in inheritance, the benefits of glory, incorruptible defenses of virtue, and a happy lineage of children. This is especially true if it is a **daytime birth** <note>original: "diurna genitura"; ancient astrology distinguished between charts for births during the day versus the night.</note>. For then they grant great deeds, offices of administration, and power over the property of others. But if **Mars** (♂) strikes them from a higher position with a threatening radiation, all that I have said is changed by that envious radiation of Mars, and it always tends toward the worse.

If **Saturn** (♄) and **Mars** (♂) have received lodging in the same degree, and being positioned together in the same place, are joined by an equal power of association—if this conjunction occurs in favorable places of the birth chart—it composes the character of the person with a steady moderation of gravity and softens all impulses of the mind with gentle tempering. The ill-advised rashness of death, the wickedness of passion, and the impatient chill of inflamed heat are tempered by the conjunction of Saturn’s coldness. Once the fires which the nature of his own heat had ignited are softened, his gravity is changed by the association of the cold joined to him to shape the character of men; the heat of Mars in establishing character is always blunted by the slow cold of Saturn. For when he has cooled things with Saturn’s chill, and when Saturn’s cold has extinguished those flames, the character of men perceives the perfect ornaments of gravity from this moderation of tempering. 

Nevertheless, action is hindered by the contrary disagreements of these stars; in business, one calls back while the other pushes forward. Those who have Mars and Saturn in this way never prosperously achieve what they wish; for always troubled by sadness of mind and ineffective desire, they leave the vows of their wishes unfulfilled. They are also entangled in various risks of illness, and their body is fatigued by continuous bouts of lingering weakness. Toward the harmful detriment of the body, the destruction of **black bile** <note>A reference to the "humoral" theory of medicine; black bile was associated with melancholy and Saturn.</note> is constantly stirred up against them. Furthermore, a swift death oppresses both the father and the mother, the paternal inheritance is torn apart and scattered by various losses, and an evil end is always prepared for their brothers through them. Even those who are first-born are either laid low by a wretched death or, destitute of any protection of happiness, they receive the power of fraternal glory with the greatest humble veneration <note>Likely meaning they serve their younger siblings or live in their shadow.</note>; but they frequently impose the greatest difficulties and the error of heavy anxieties upon themselves. All these things grow stronger if they possess one of the **pivots** <note>term: "cardinem" — the four most important points in a chart: the Ascendant (East), Midheaven (Top), Descendant (West), and Imum Coeli (Bottom).</note> of the birth chart in that same degree of association. For then their mind sustains virtues through a shifting variety of reasons—unless **Jupiter** (♃), positioned in the primary pivots and in signs in which he is exalted, or in his own house, or in favorable places of the birth chart, softens all these dangers of evils with his propitious star.

-># BOOK SIX.<-

<margin>The Sun</margin>
If Saturn and the **Sun** <note>original: "Saturnus & ☉"</note> have accepted the same degree of a house, and being positioned together in that same place, they are joined in an equal fellowship of power, this conjunction dissipates all paternal inheritance. Furthermore, it decrees a miserable death for both the individual and their father. These evils grow stronger in **nocturnal birth charts** <note>original: "nocturnis genituris"; charts for people born at night. In ancient astrology, planets changed their "sect" or behavior depending on whether the Sun was above or below the horizon.</note>, whether the Sun is found in a morning or evening rising. For then, the individual always encounters heavy heaps of misfortunes for the father, wretched dangers, and the conjunction decrees bitter deaths for brothers. But if, in a nocturnal birth chart, Saturn and the Sun are joined in this fellowship, but while positioned in the same sign they are separated by a distance of degrees—so that the Sun has few degrees and Saturn has more—then a miserable calamity of death is indicated for the father. Indeed, all the things we have mentioned proceed from a powerful continuation of evils. But along with all these misfortunes—the inheritance being torn apart or proscribed, and all the wealth of fortune dissipated—the ultimate burden of poverty is imposed. **Illnesses** <note>original: "Languores"</note> are also brought on by **corrupt humors** <note>original: "uitiosis humoribus"; referring to the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile—which Greek and Roman medicine believed caused disease when unbalanced.</note>, and all the strength of the weary body is weighed down by weakness; in the eyes of others, the miserable destruction of blindness is even inflicted. However, this conjunction will always make these people skilled **farmers**; so much so that after a long span of time, suitable resources and wealth are conferred upon them from the cultivation of fields. They will, of course, always be somber in their sadness. But if Saturn and the Sun are placed together in the **house** <note>The zodiac signs ruled by these planets: Leo for the Sun; Capricorn or Aquarius for Saturn.</note> of either the Sun or Saturn, they make the father glorious, but destitute of all protection of wealth. Conversely, the Sun and Saturn placed together embitter these individuals against their fathers with parricidal hatreds; yet the miserable decrees of those misfortunes we mentioned always attack these same people.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If Saturn and **Venus** <note>original: "♄ & ♀"</note> have accepted the same degree of a house, and being positioned together in that same place, they are joined by an equal power of fellowship, this conjunction decrees marriage to unworthy women and always stirs up wretched misfortunes in marriages. Likewise, it decrees wives who are either sterile or weak, whose appearance is disgraced by some notable defect of the body; for they are either struck by heavy infamy, or from these misfortunes, the birth of children is denied to them. Furthermore, those having Saturn and Venus in this way will never have children, or will have them late; and they will always be **cold toward Venus** <note>original: "frigidi semper ad Venerem"; meaning they lack sexual desire or passion.</note>, and their savage mind will always be distinguished by unstable variety. Saturn and Venus positioned together in the birth charts of women decree these same things through an equal fellowship of radiation. But these effects grow stronger if Saturn and Venus are found together in the signs of **Mars** <note>Aries or Scorpio.</note>; for these signs of Mars always infect them badly, especially if the fellowship of Saturn is added. For then, the malice of that conjunction can be mitigated neither by the presence of **Jupiter** nor by his testimony <note>original: "testimonio"; an "aspect" or look from another planet that might provide help.</note>.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If Saturn and **Mercury** <note>original: "Saturnus & ☿"</note> possess the place of a single degree in equal fellowship, they always induce a sound of the voice with a stuttering confusion of the tongue, or they cause hindered words to be brought forth with slow speech, or they always attack the hearing with heavy illness, and never permit their desires to be fulfilled. They will also be, in all their acts, destitute of the testimony of good faith, hardened by a rigid authority of mind, and composed of an always obstinate and gloomy dissimulation. But they will hide the plans of their mind with a deep silence of malice; yet their natural talents will be thoroughly imbued with many scholarly disciplines by a happy star.

<margin>The Moon</margin>
If Saturn and the **Moon** <note>original: "Saturnus & ☽"</note> have accepted one house together, and being positioned in turn in the same place, they are joined by an equal reasoning of fellowship, they always attack all impulses, thoughts of the mind, and all acts with a weak trembling of death. Furthermore, maternal wealth is dissipated by wretched tearing apart because of this fellowship; their mothers, and these individuals themselves, are weakened by a heavy continuation of sicknesses. But if it is a **diurnal birth chart** <note>Born during the day.</note>, and the Moon is full of light, and the timely radiation of favorable stars is added, the wickedness of all the preceding evils is prohibited. But if it is a nocturnal birth chart, and the Moon is either waning or full, this conjunction decrees all kinds of unhappiness and every destruction of evils. But if **Jupiter** or Venus have likewise added their testimonies, the destruction of calamity grows stronger, the salutary protection having been ignored.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS
$\jupiter$ & $\venus$

### JUPITER WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
->in conjunction. Chapter XXVI.<-

<margin>Jupiter with Mars</margin>
If **Jupiter and Mars** <note>original: "IVpiter & ♂"</note> are positioned together in one place, and established together in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree the greatest marks of rank and confer the greatest power of authority. For they make men who govern the offices of great cities or regions; even among the greatest populations, they grant the power of glorious authority. Such people will also be those who achieve everything they desire with a prosperous outcome—especially if they are positioned in favorable places in the **birth chart** <note>original: "genituræ"; the map of the sky at the moment of birth</note>, either in the primary **angles** <note>original: "cardinibus"; the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven</note>, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horoscopo"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, and are established together in the house of Jupiter or Mars. For then the **fasces** <note>term: "fasces"; bundles of rods and an axe signifying a Roman magistrate's power to punish or execute</note>, then weapons, and then the greatest armies are entrusted to them; then, placed in great honors, they are allotted the license of magnificent power by a fortunate star.

<margin>The Sun</margin>
If **Jupiter and the Sun** <note>original: "♃ & ☉"</note> are established together in the same sign, and Jupiter is **hidden under the Sun's rays** <note>original: "sub radijs ☉ absconfus"; in astrology, a planet is "combust" or weakened when it is too close to the Sun, as the Sun’s brightness overwhelms its influence</note>, he diminishes the entire order of happiness through various setbacks. But if Jupiter is freed from the rays of the Sun, positioned in a **morning rising** <note>original: "matutino ortu"; appearing in the sky just before the Sun</note>, and is joined in the same sign's hospitality with the Sun, he decrees fate, substance, and life, and the fruits of these happinesses with the greatest power of honor. Such people will be seen to be born of a good parent, so that from the day of their birth, all the marks of happiness are conferred upon the parents. Furthermore, those who have Jupiter and the Sun in this way will be happy, and will rejoice and be glad in the offspring of children they receive.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **Jupiter and Venus** <note>original: "♃ & ♀"</note> are established together in the same degree or sign, they decree marks of honor with the greatest grace of beauty, and they always associate the individual with the faithful friendships of good and great men. When they are positioned in this way (as we said before), girls captured by the persuasions of promises surrender their virginity to the desire of a seducer; but from this occasion, both crimes are stirred up and the noise of seditious outcry is brought in. However, the turning points of danger become greater if Mars is found with Jupiter and Venus. But if, in the sign of **Capricorn** <note>original: "♑"</note>, Mars and Venus are positioned together and occupy the same degrees, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is found in the neighboring sign (that is, in the second sign) so that he himself first catches the conjunction of the approaching Venus, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is looking on, joined by whatever aspect, and Saturn also looks upon the Moon, and the Sun is in the **Midheaven** <note>term: "MC" or "Medium Coeli"; the highest point in the sky at the time of birth</note>, while the Moon and Ascendant are established in **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note>—from this, freed from the protection of any power and driven by an unholy fire of madness, they obtain marriage with their own mothers; or, possessed by a perverted fire of the mind and desire, they invite their stepmothers to the partnership of the marriage bed. If this is the birth chart of a woman, for the sake of marriage she will be joined either to her father or her stepfather. Ancient records of readings say that **Oedipus** <note>historical: "Oedipus"; the mythological Greek king who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother</note> had such a birth chart. For the Ascendant was in Cancer, the Sun in Aries, Saturn in Pisces, Jupiter and Venus in Aquarius, Mars in Libra, the Moon in the **nebula of Cancer** <note>original: "nebula ♋"; likely referring to the Praesepe star cluster in the sign of Cancer</note>, and Mercury with the Sun.

BOOK SIX.

<margin>Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury</margin>
If **Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury** <note>original: "♃ ♀ & ☿"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree the greatest marks of religious rank. They render the person skilled in the law, and one who is complete in both sense and understanding in their reasoning. They also signify a victor in legal cases, and one who, following the **Socratic method** <note>The "Socratic institution" refers to the philosophical tradition of seeking the common good and moral utility through dialogue and reason.</note>, looks after the utility and advantage of many people. They also produce very sharp **accountants** <note>original: "supputatores"; those skilled in complex calculations or "reckoning."</note> and, for this reason especially, secretaries to kings and princes.

<margin>Saturn</margin>
If **Jupiter and Saturn** <note>original: "♃ & ♄"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree a very great increase in wealth and fortune. But if Jupiter is **oriental** <note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note>, it renders the person better than their parent—not only in resources but also greater in dignity. If, however, the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is diminished in light and at a lower degree than Jupiter, it greatly diminishes that superior fortune, wealth, and the decreed dignity of the person born.

### MARS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### in conjunction. Chapter XXVII.

<margin>Mars with the Sun</margin>
If **Mars and the Sun** <note>original: "Mars & ☉"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they announce that the parent of the person born will die quickly. They decree no small amount of labor and pain for the individual, destroy their substance and expectations, and decree losses by iron or fire; they also make the person inconstant and wavering in their plans and thoughts. If, however, they are established in the **angles** <note>term: "cardines"; the four most powerful points in a chart (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven).</note> or their **succedent houses** <note>term: "anaphoris"; the houses that "rise up" immediately after the angles.</note>, all these things will be established by a firmer and more certain decree.

<margin>Jupiter</margin>
If **Mars and Jupiter** <note>original: "♂ & ♃"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree lawsuits, losses, and hindrances on account of women. But if they are in a **moveable sign** <note>A sign marking the start of a season: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn.</note>, they suggest a lowly and obscure woman of ill repute. But wherever they are established, they produce shameful and manifest types of **Venusian** <note>Relating to love, sex, or desire.</note> behavior. If it is a woman’s birth chart, they will argue for a manifest and bold prostitute, famous for much lust.

<margin>Venus</margin>
If **Mars and Venus** <note>original: "♂ & ♀"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree the person born to be a liar, but of good reasoning—wise, sharp, eloquent, and for this reason commended by many. If a favorable **aspect** <note>original: "radiatio"; the "beaming" or geometric relationship between planets.</note> from Venus is added, it will achieve the same, but make them especially pious toward their parents. If, however, an aspect of Saturn is added, it diminishes these goods. But if Mercury is joined in this way, under the rays of the Sun and in an angle, looking toward the Moon, it will decree evil thoughts, thefts, and deceits.

<margin>Moon</margin>
If **Mars and the Moon** <note>original: "♂ & ☽"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they decree injury to life, harm by iron, and a **violent death** <note>original: "biothanatam mortem"; an unnatural or premature end.</note>; they threaten the mother with anxiety, worry, and labor. But if they are joined in such fellowship in any angle, they establish various arts and subtlety of work, but not without the highest damage and loss, from which they add no small amount of sorrow not only to themselves but also to relatives and friends.

### THE SUN WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
### in conjunction. Chapter XXVIII.

<margin>Sun and Venus</margin>
If the **Sun and Venus** <note>original: "Sol & ♀"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, and Venus is positioned in the **west** in a nocturnal birth, or in the **east** in a diurnal one, they decree a truly great name, wonderful expectations, and almost divine fame for the person born. Such a person is not only loved by all the people but also follows others with a certain wonderful affection of love. But this is better achieved if both, so joined, are positioned in the angles.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
If the **Sun and Mercury** <note>original: "☉ & ☿"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power—whether they are oriental or occidental—this decrees a wonderful sense of mind and piety. For these make men wise scribes, for the most part, as well as accountants and those handling the business of princes. From such wisdom, they not only attain the greatest marks of honor for themselves, but also acquire the highest resources and support for others, through which they may preside over some magisterial honor.

->JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS<-
<meta>catchword: ♀ if in</meta>

If the **Sun and the Moon** <note>original: "☉ & ☽"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they offer bad testimony in whatever part of the birth chart they are located, and they weaken the significance of that part. But if, being established together in this way, they are placed in the **seventh house** <note>The "seventh place" from the Ascendant, traditionally associated with marriage and partnerships.</note> from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>, they decree wives who are bad, litigious, and swollen with a spirit of puffed-up pride. If, however, they are placed in the **sixth house** <note>The "sixth place" from the Ascendant, traditionally associated with illness and misfortune.</note> from the Ascendant, they threaten the person born with misfortune, sickness, and very often blindness.

# VENUS WITH THE OTHER PLANETS
## in conjunction. Chapter XXIX.

**Venus and Mercury** <note>original: "♀ & ☿"</note>, if they are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they induce a love of jokes and games, and they also grant many wives and female friends. They produce poets, singers, and eloquent orators; but **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> may greatly harm these individuals, not only by diminishing their thoughts and plans, but even their natural talent and industry. But if **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> regards them so positioned with a favorable **aspect** <note>original: "radiatione"; literally "radiation" or "beaming," referring to the geometric angles between planets.</note>, and is especially established in the Ascendant, he decrees the greatest marks of honor derived from women.

If **Venus and the Moon** <note>original: "♀ & ☽"</note> are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, they will make men who are very carefully groomed and adorned, with beautiful and cheerful faces, and possessing great expectations and fortune; yet they will be least constant in their marriages. For, desiring the wives of others, they will suffer under various crimes of adultery. It also often happens to these men, conversely, that their own wives return the favor in the same way through sexual union with others.

# MERCURY JOINED WITH THE MOON
## in conjunction. Chapter XXX.

**Mercury and the Moon** <note>original: "M-ercurius & ☽"</note>, if they are placed together as one, and established equally in the same sign, joined by an equal fellowship of power, and if **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is there, or at least joined by a benevolent aspect, they produce famous and wise men—though they are often liars and inconstant. But if the **malefics** <note>The "unfortunate" planets, usually Saturn and Mars.</note> aspect them, this [instability] will be more firm, and it will produce **pederasts** <note>original: "pedicones"</note> and infamous people. If, however, the Moon is increasing in its number of degrees <note>Waxing or gaining strength.</note>, Jupiter wipes away all the evils and will more firmly add good decrees through the stable disposition of the Fates.

# GENERAL DECREES ON PLANETS PLACED
## indiscriminately. Chapter XXXI.

If the **Moon** is found in the **bounds** <note>original: "finibus"; specific sub-divisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets.</note> and has received a planet of the masculine gender—especially in **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>—and is not joined to **Venus or Jupiter** by a **trine aspect** <note>original: "trigonica radiatione"; an aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note>, those who have this configuration will never be allotted any children.

If the **Moon** is found in the equinoctial signs at the Ascendant—that is, in **Aries** or **Libra** <note>original: "♈, uel ♎"</note>—and is joined with **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> in an exact degree, and they are placed in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C" or "Medium Coeli"; the highest point of the chart.</note> or in the West [the descendant], while **Jupiter and Saturn** <note>original: "♃ autem & ♄"</note> are established together in Aries or Libra and possess the same degree number, and regard the Moon and Mars by any aspect, they will make people who are sterile and effeminate, as well as those who are castrated or **Galli** <note>The Galli were the eunuch priests of the goddess Cybele.</note>, serving in the ceremonies of religions.

If **Saturn and Mars** <note>original: "♄ & ♂"</note>, joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, are established in the **house of Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra.</note>, possessing the West or the Midheaven, and **Venus** is positioned in the **house of Mars** <note>Aries or Scorpio.</note> in opposition to them <note>original: "in diametro"</note>, and the degrees of Mars and Saturn are equal in the opposite reckoning, this arrangement of stars shows us the birth of a **eunuch** by the clearest demonstration.

If **Mars and the Moon** are in opposition <note>original: "diametra"</note> to each other and both receive the same degrees while in opposition, and **Venus** is established in a **right square** <note>A 90-degree angle to the right.</note> to them, and regarding **Saturn** from an opposition, she [Venus] strikes the Moon and Mars through a **left square**, such that she regards Saturn from an opposition and the Moon and Mars from a square, and Venus possesses the Midheaven: from this mixture of stars are born either sterile people, **hermaphrodites**, or certainly eunuchs.

If **Saturn and Venus** <note>original: "♄ & ♀"</note> are established together in the sign or bounds of Venus and possess the Midheaven, and **Mars** is made a stranger to them <note>Mars does not aspect the configuration.</note>, this conjunction decrees either a poor wife or wives of advanced age. But if **Jupiter** regards Saturn and Venus so established with a trine aspect, or if he is found with them, by this testimony of Jupiter, a widow is indeed decreed as a wife, but one with a copious abundance of riches.

# BOOK SIX.

If **Venus** <note>original: "Venus"</note> is found in the degree of **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> together with **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, this association decrees a wife who is known for adultery. If, however, with these planets so positioned, the star of **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> approaches this same partnership of the degree, the woman will leave her husband—whom she had obtained through intervening adultery—and pass again to a marriage with another husband. This she will do either because she is captured by the love of a youth, or because she follows the bed of some poor man, or because she desires the cohabitation of an ignoble person with a humble and prone desire of the mind. In this way, by the allurements of a depraved love, she ignobly obtains the partnership of an inferior man.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna"</note> is found exactly with **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is placed exactly in the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note>, while **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is positioned in the **second house** <note>original: "anaphora horosc."; the house that 'rises after' the Ascendant.</note> and is joined to the **Moon** by a **trine** <note>original: "trigonica radiatione"; an aspect of 120 degrees, considered harmonious.</note> radiation, from that conjunction or association, clear insignias of nobility are decreed.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> regards **Venus** <note>original: "Venerem"</note> by a trine radiation when she is positioned in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C"; Medium Coeli, the highest point of the sky and the 10th house of a chart.</note>, or if he is found together with her, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is separated from the radiations of all malevolent stars <note>Specifically Mars and Saturn.</note>, the greatest insignias of happiness are conferred through the protection of women by this conjunction; or perhaps the beginning of prosperity is granted from some work related to women. This configuration also makes individuals bend the measures of a musical song sweetly, or strike the cithara and lyre, or certainly dance with a graceful enough charm through the soft movement of the body.

**Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> always impels one to the intercourse of sordid women through a miserable zeal for lust when positioned exactly in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C"</note>. If, however, **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is found with him, possessing that same degree, he causes the person's wife to be violently snatched away by another. But if the star of **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> joins them, a woman taken from a brothel <note>original: "de meritorio"; a place of hire.</note> is joined by conjugal grace to illustrious men. If the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> approaches all these in a **square** <note>original: "quadratus"; a 90-degree aspect associated with tension.</note> aspect, they join the wives of their paternal uncles in marriage; but when the nuptials have been completed by depraved desire, the marriage—which had previously been joined under ill-omened auspices—is dissolved by the flight of the woman.

If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is found in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "M C"</note> with the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is placed exactly in the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horosc."</note>, while the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **Setting** <note>original: "occasu"; the 7th house, representing the western horizon and marriage.</note>, with **Jupiter** regarding **Mars** and the **Moon** from the **opposite side** <note>original: "de diametro"</note> and by a square radiation, this conjunction decrees a marriage characterized by a deadly conflict of strife. For then the threatening sword of those contending inflicts grave wounds; then a heavy battle is stirred up by contests of savage heat; then the famous contests of battles are bloodied by the desires of fatal fury, by the groans of the falling, the noise of the fighters, and the bitter shedding of blood. It is suggested that **Paris Alexander** <note>The Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen led to the Trojan War.</note> had such a decree, from whose marriage famous contests of battles and the legendary destruction of his fatherland occurred. The whole birth decree of Paris Alexander was composed by this calculation: the **Ascendant** was in **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>, the **Sun** in **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note>, the **Moon** in **Virgo** <note>original: "♍"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> in **Leo**, **Jupiter** in **Aquarius**, **Mars** in **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>, and both **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> in **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note>.

**Saturn** <note>original: "Saturnus"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, if they are positioned exactly <term>partiliter; meaning "by degree," an exact mathematical alignment</term> in the **Midheaven** <term>M C; the Medium Coeli, the highest point of the sky in an astrological chart</term>, or if they are situated in other cardines <note>the four "pivot points" of a chart: Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Bottom of the Sky</note> and regard this same place through a square <note>an aspect of 90 degrees</note> or opposite <note>an aspect of 180 degrees</note> alignment, and if the beneficial protections of **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> do not mitigate their malice, this conjunction will produce people who are hardworking, poor, crushed by the wretched burden of poverty, and shattered by the continuation of daily labor, so that they seek the miserable nourishment of life through constant physical exhaustion. If, however, **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> regards this same place from an opposite position—whether he is positioned in the **Midheaven**, the **Bottom of the Sky** <term>I M C; the Imum Coeli, the lowest point of the sky</term>, or certainly in the **Ascendant** <term>horosc.; the sign rising on the eastern horizon</term>—and they are all destitute of divine testimony <note>referring to the lack of supportive aspects from beneficial planets</note>, then in addition to the preceding evils, custody in a public prison and the iron bonds of chains are decreed. But if, with these planets so situated, **Jupiter** regards the full **Moon** with a merciful alignment, they are liberated from such great labors and crises after many hardships, and they transition into a better standard of living.

If **Mars** is found exactly in the **Midheaven**, and the **star of Saturn** occupies the second sign from it in close proximity, this conjunction will produce people who are hardworking, poor, and seeking their life by manual labor; moreover, a sad expression always clouds their faces. But if **Venus** regards the **Midheaven** from an equal degree, and **Saturn** is positioned in the second sign (as we said before), greater burdens of unhappiness are decreed, and a heap of greater misfortunes is added; and those who have them thus will never achieve what they desire.

If the **Moon** is found in the "lips" <note>the early degrees or boundaries</note> of **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>, or in **Scorpio** <note>original: "♏"</note>, or occupies **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note> in a similar manner, it will indeed make women into viragos <note>women who display masculine or aggressive traits</note>; but it always impels men toward all the vices of lust, so that, stirred by the wretched goad of **Venus**, they conceive desires for impure and shameless intercourse. If the **Moon** is placed in those parts of the signs which we have mentioned, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> and **Mars** occupy these same parts with the **Moon** in the same way, and the **Moon** wanes toward the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, in whatever part of the sign the **Moon** is found, the vice of lust is found in that area; however, the wickedness of the aforementioned vices is covered and mitigated. If, truly, the **Moon** is found with them without the testimony of **Jupiter**, every vice of shameless impurity is pronounced: then men, by a spontaneous urging of madness, suffer "womanly things" <note>a Roman reference to taking a passive role in same-sex relations</note>, then they strive to pursue the heat of a vicious lust with impure honor. If this is a woman’s birth chart, it will make her a prostitute of prostituted modesty, who surrenders her body to the depraved cravings of lusts, condemning her modesty to the power of a pimp for the sake of a daily wage; and she will be prostituted in public brothels, even if she appears to be descended from a high-born family.

The **Sun**, **Jupiter**, and the **Moon**, if they are so positioned in a birth chart <term>genitura; the configuration of stars at the moment of birth</term> that none of them are joined to each other by any aspect, and the **Sun** does not see the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** likewise looks at neither the **Sun** nor the **Ascendant**, nor are they joined by any partnership of degrees—they weary the person with such a burden of poverty that those who have them thus, weighed down by various burdens of unhappiness, approach the extreme ruin of beggary under unlucky omens <note>original: "sinistris auibus"; literally "with left-hand birds," a reference to Roman augury</note>.

If the **Sun** and **Moon** occupy signs of the feminine gender, and the **Ascendant** is found in a feminine sign, and **Venus** is positioned there exactly, these people are compelled to "prune their own nature" with their own hands <note>a reference to self-castration or religious self-mutilation, common in certain ancient cults like those of Cybele</note>.

If the **Sun** and **Jupiter** are positioned exactly in the **Ascendant**, or if one precedes the **Ascendant** and the other follows it, provided that this happens in the sign of the **Ascendant**, and **Mars** is positioned in the house following the **Ascendant** <term>anaphora; the second house</term>, and **Saturn** is joined to **Mars** by some radiation of testimony, this celestial configuration imposes the wretched burden of blindness upon the eyes.

If the **Moon** is found in the **Midheaven**, and **Venus** is positioned in the **Bottom of the Sky**, and regards the **Moon** with an exact radiation, this conjunction, through the heat of incestuous desire, will join sisters to brothers as wives. If, however, **Venus** is placed in a right-hand square to the **Moon**, it will make men prepared for all duties of business, who seek for themselves the protection of many friendships, and whom wives always love with faithful affection, and it makes them joined to all friends with lovable charity. But all these things will grow stronger if **Jupiter** regards one of the two with a trine <term>trigonica radiatione; an aspect of 120 degrees</term> and a favorable aspect.

If the **Ascendant** is found in the sign of **Virgo** <note>original: "♍"</note>, and **Mars**, **Mercury**, and **Venus** are positioned exactly in the same sign, and **Jupiter**, positioned in the west <note>the descendant</note>, occupies the sign of **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>, and is joined to those who are in the **Ascendant** by an exact radiation, and the **Sun** is positioned in the house following the **Ascendant**—that is, in **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>...

...protected, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is positioned in the fifth house from the **ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> in **Capricorn** <note>original: "♑"</note>, while **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is placed in the ninth house from the ascendant and holds the sign of **Taurus** <note>original: "♉"</note>. Whoever has all these placements will be such an orator that the insights of his speeches are brought forth in the manner of thunderbolts; so much so that, according to his will, the resting minds of the multitude are either stirred up or, if inflamed, are easily soothed. His words will also be of such a kind that posterity will learn them with eager dedication to increase and nourish their own natural talent. For such an orator, named Hermodorus, lived at the court of Philip of Macedon and pursued everyone with the freedom of his speech, to explain the matter more clearly. This **horoscope** <note>original: "genitura"</note> breathed divine genius into Demosthenes.

### THE HOROSCOPE OF DEMOSTHENES AND HERMODORUS

**Astrological Chart Layout:**
*   **Top (Tenth, Ninth, Eighth Houses):** **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note>, **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note>, **Taurus** <note>original: "♉"</note>. **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is in the Upper-Right (Taurus).
*   **Right (Seventh, Sixth Houses):** **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>, **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>. **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is in the Right-Center (Gemini/Aries transition).
*   **Bottom (Fifth, Fourth, Third Houses):** **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>, **Capricorn** <note>original: "♑"</note>, **Sagittarius** <note>original: "♐"</note>. The **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is in the Lower-Right (Sagittarius).
*   **Left (Second, First/Ascendant, Twelfth, Eleventh Houses):** **Scorpio** <note>original: "♏"</note>, **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>, **Virgo** <note>original: "♍"</note>, **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note>. The **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "♁"</note>, **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are in the Left-Center (Libra).

**Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, if they are placed together in the <term>bounds of Venus; specific degrees within a sign governed by Venus</term>, and the **ascendant** occupies a degree within those same bounds, while **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is positioned in **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note> at the setting point <term>occasu; the descendant or western horizon</term> and regards all these others through a diametrical alignment <note>an aspect of 180 degrees</note>, and is joined to them in an equal fellowship of degrees; if the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is in **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is positioned in the fifth house from the ascendant and holds the sign of **Sagittarius** <note>original: "♐"</note>, so that **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note> is at the <term>midheaven; literally "in the head"</term> (for in these parts the chart causes blindness); and if **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the ninth house from the ascendant in **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note>—this horoscope creates a divine poet of a certain heroic song, who records the sounds of Mars <note>the sounds of war</note> and the terrifying struggles of battles with the nobility of a most celebrated poem. Such a horoscope made Homer the divine interpreter of the Cumean song <note>likely referring to the Sibyl or epic tradition</note> and the prince of poets.

-><image-desc>A square astrological chart titled "THE HOROSCOPE OF HOMER". Planetary symbols are placed as follows: Mars (♂), Mercury (☿), and Venus (♀) in the middle-left house; Jupiter (♃) in the middle-right house; Saturn (♄) in the top-right corner house; the Sun (☉) in the bottom-left corner house; and the Moon (☽) in the bottom-right corner house. A central symbol shows two small circles connected by a vertical line.</image-desc><-

If the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is found in **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>, and in that same part **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are positioned exactly together; and if **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is placed in the setting <term>occident; the descendant or seventh house</term> and holds the sign of **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note>; and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is established in the house following the ascendant <term>anaphora; the second house</term> and holds the sign of **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>; while the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is placed in **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note> and established in the fifth house of the horoscope, looking toward the **Ascendant** with a trine aspect <term>trigonica radiatio; a harmonious astrological aspect of 120 degrees</term>; and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, occupying the ninth house from the **Ascendant**, is established in the sign of **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>: this horoscope produces an interpreter of divine and celestial institutions. This person, composed of eloquent speech and the power of divine genius, and formed in a way by celestial instruction, may approach all the secrets of divinity with a true freedom of discussion. For it is suggested by a true historical narrative that this was the horoscope of **Plato**. <note>The text here attributes this specific configuration to Plato, despite the preceding heading for Homer, reflecting a common overlap in ancient astrological tradition regarding "divine" charts.</note>

# BOOK SIX.

If the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term> is found in **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are positioned exactly together in that same place, while **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is placed in the setting <term>occasus; the seventh house or descendant</term>—that is, in the sign of **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>—and regards the **Ascendant**, **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** with an opposing ray; and if the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is placed in **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note> in the house following the ascendant <term>anaphora; the second house</term>; and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is also placed in **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>, occupying the fifth house from the **Ascendant**; and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is established in the ninth house from the **Ascendant** in **Gemini**: this horoscope produces a divine poet of lyric song, who composes the rhythms of religious verse, crowned with ivy for the dances of Liber <note>another name for Bacchus/Dionysus, the god of wine and theater</note>. Such a nativity bestowed the measures of sweetest song upon **Pindar** and **Archilochus** through the divine inspiration of their genius.

If the **Ascendant** is found in **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note> and in the bounds <term>termini; specific degrees of a sign governed by a particular planet</term> of **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are exactly positioned in the same place; and **Jupiter** is placed in **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>—that is, in the setting sign—and regards the **Ascendant** with an opposing ray; and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is placed in the house following the ascendant, occupying the sign of **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note>; and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is placed in the fifth house from the **Ascendant**, holding the sign of **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>; and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is established in the ninth house from the **Ascendant**, holding the sign of **Sagittarius** <note>original: "♐"</note>: this nativity creates a divine inventor of the mechanical arts. This is our fellow, by whose genius the fabricated sphere <note>an orrery or mechanical model of the solar system</note> showed the movement of the heavens and the courses of all the stars, following the example of divine imitation. This is **Archimedes of Syracuse**, who often overthrew the Roman armies with his mechanical arts. Him did the general **Marcellus** weep for with mournful grief, even while established in the triumph of victory, amidst the shouting of the exulting soldiers and the placement of triumphal laurels.

# THE NATIVITY OF ARCHIMEDES.

<image-desc>A square astrological chart (horoscope) depicting the birth chart of Archimedes. The outer border contains zodiac signs: Aquarius (♒) at the top; Pisces (♓), Aries (♈), and Taurus (♉) on the left; Gemini (♊), Cancer (♋), and Leo (♌) at the bottom; and Virgo (♍), Libra (♎), and Scorpio (♏) on the right. Inside the square, planetary symbols are assigned to the houses: Saturn (♄) is in the top house (Midheaven); the Sun (☉) is in the bottom house (Imum Coeli); Venus (♀) and Mercury (☿) are in the left house (Ascendant); and the Moon (☽) is in the right house (Descendant). Mars (♂) and Jupiter (♃) are positioned within the central compartments.</image-desc>

From this nativity <note>original: "genitura"</note>, the disadvantages of laborious poverty and wretched beggary are decreed.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> are positioned in the seventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, that is, in the setting <term>occasus; the western horizon or 7th house</term>, and they are in that sign in which **Mars** finds its trine <note>an aspect of 120 degrees, considered harmonious</note>—that is, in either **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>, **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note>, or **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>—while **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is positioned exactly <note>original: "partiliter"; degree-for-degree</note> in the **Midheaven** <term>MC or Medium Coeli; the highest point of the chart</term>, and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is joined to it by a trine radiation, this nativity will produce an athlete; but one who, as a victor in sacred contests, brings back glorious and worthy insignia of crowns.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is found in the setting of the nativity placed in a feminine sign, and **Mars** is likewise established in a feminine sign, and the **Sun** and **Moon** also occupy feminine signs, this nativity shows you an effeminate man <note>original: "cinaedum"; a term used in antiquity for a man who did not conform to traditional masculine gender roles</note>. If, however, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> and **Mars** are established together in the region of the **Ascendant**, and it is a sign of the feminine gender, and **Venus** and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are placed in the setting, likewise occupying a feminine sign; or if **Mars** and **Saturn** are positioned exactly in the **Midheaven** and occupy a sign of the feminine gender: this nativity will produce public effeminates, or certainly castrated priests <note>original: "abscisos gallos"; referring to the Galli, the eunuch priests of the goddess Cybele</note>. If, however, this should be the nativity of a woman, it will make her a public and famous prostitute, trafficking her modesty <note>original: "nundinato pudore"</note>.

<margin><unclear>bandits</unclear></margin>
If the **Moon** with **Mars** are placed together in the eighth place from the **Ascendant**, and **Jupiter**, positioned in opposition <note>original: "in diametro"; an aspect of 180 degrees</note>, looks upon them with an exact radiation, in the midst of a heat of cruelty, this nativity will produce bandits <note>original: "latrones"</note>; but we find their crimes according to the variety of the stars. For if **Mars** and the **Moon** are placed in earthy signs, such a person, established as a highwayman in deserted places, will stain his raiding hand with the shedding of blood. But if they are positioned in watery signs, they will produce rustlers of livestock, always resisting among crowds of people with a threatening sword. In fixed <note>original: "solidis"</note> signs, however, they will render them famous house-breakers; who, armed with a sword while people are sleeping, inflict both the loss of inheritance and the danger of life. Such men, caught in these crimes, shall be punished with the severity of public execution. But if **Mars** and **Mercury** are positioned together in the **Midheaven**, or in the setting, and the **Moon** is either in opposition to them, or in square <note>original: "quadrato"; an aspect of 90 degrees</note>, or is full of light with them, these same things which we have said are decreed for a similar reason.

If **Saturn** and **Venus** are placed in the setting of the nativity, while in the eighth place from the **Ascendant** **Mars** is established, and **Mercury** is either with **Mars**, or with **Saturn** and **Venus**, and **Jupiter** does not reach any of these with a favorable aspect: this nativity will produce either slaves or castrated priests, but those who endure all the wicked vices of impurity.

<meta>This page continues the technical astrological instructions of Julius Firmicus Maternus in Book Six. ### BOOK SIX.

But if the planet **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> holds that part, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is placed in the **Midheaven** <term>Medium Coeli or MC; the highest point in the sky at birth</term>, this birth chart <note>original: "genitura"</note> will produce an impure man.

If **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is found in the **Midheaven**, in a feminine sign, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> with **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are positioned in the eleventh house from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point rising on the eastern horizon</term>, and the **Ascendant** itself along with **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are positioned in a sign of **Venus**, those who have their stars so placed will corrupt their own mothers, or stepmothers, or their mothers' sisters with an incestuous desire of lust.

**Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> positioned with **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> in the **Ascendant**, in whatever sign or in whatever degrees the birth chart is set, decrees by license of power either public prostitutes or wives of advanced age, especially if no radiation from **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> regards them <note>Jupiter's "aspect" or "regard" was thought to provide a moderating, beneficial influence</note>.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are located together exactly <note>original: "partiliter"; degree-for-degree</note> in the **Midheaven**, they produce men distinguished by a reputation for goodness, upon whom the marks of blessed happiness are always conferred: especially if this conjunction is found in the house of **Jupiter**, or in his terms <term>fines; specific segments of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet</term>.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is in the **Midheaven**, or is positioned in the house of **Jupiter**, and in that place **Jupiter** is located together with **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is carried toward **Jupiter** full of light, they decree the marks of the greatest happiness.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and also the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> consist together in the **Midheaven**, joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, they indicate indigence and the burden of wretched poverty: and they make these same people doorkeepers, compelled to this service by the necessity of beggary; but they also show the death of children through a frequent calamity of misfortunes, by an unlucky star and a sinister omen.

If the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are positioned together in the fifth house from the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is located exactly in the **Ascendant**, they decree the marks of bright nobility and indicate the trust and love of a king: but these men obtain wives who are known by adulterers. To these men are also decreed, for the adornment of honor, the *praetexta* <note>a purple-bordered toga worn by Roman magistrates</note> and golden garments, and the insignia of golden crowns.

If the **Ascendant** is found in the sign of a malefic star <note>malefics are typically Saturn or Mars</note>, and that same malefic star is placed in the twelfth house from the **Ascendant**, it will cause [the native] to be torn apart in the manner of dogs <note>original: "canum moribus dissipari"; this likely refers to a violent death or being literally devoured</note>. And if the twelfth house from the **Ascendant** is positioned in the sign of a malefic star, and that same malefic star (whose home we said the 12th house is) is positioned in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the setting <term>occasus; the western horizon</term>—this indicates the same danger of death: unless the favorable testimony of **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> together with **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> mitigates the mournful end of this death and the fearful dangers of grave misfortunes by the saving protection of their divine powers.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> are positioned together in a trine <note>an aspect of 120 degrees</note>—that is, either in **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note>, or in **Scorpio** <note>original: "♏"</note>, or in **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>—and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> itself is found either in the **Midheaven** or in the setting, the hardships of constant travel are decreed: so that, being situated in foreign regions, they complete the final day of their life.

If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is found with the degree of the **Ascendant** in its trines—that is, in either **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note>, **Scorpio** <note>original: "♏"</note>, or **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>—and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> with **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are positioned in the setting and are joined to **Mars** in an equal fellowship of degrees, those who have their stars so placed become the wicked killers of their own wives.

If the **Ascendant** is found in a sign of **Venus** <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is located exactly in the same sign, while **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are in the setting, positioned together in a sign of **Mars** <note>Aries or Scorpio</note> and in the terms of **Mars**, the mother of that birth will die struck by an impious sword.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is found in the **Midheaven**, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are positioned together in the **Midheaven**, the person who has this will be dragged away from his father's labors and will receive the heavy yoke of captivity.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is found in the **Midheaven**, and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> are positioned with her, joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, they will make either go-betweens or servants of shameful lusts: so that from such gain, the daily protections of life are prepared for them.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is found in the 6th house from the **Ascendant**, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are positioned in the 12th house, and all these are striking each other with a diameter radiation <term>opposition; an aspect of 180 degrees</term> and are joined in an equal fellowship of degrees, these men associate their own daughters with the bed of marriage in an incestuous heat of desire. But if **Venus**, **Mercury**, and **Jupiter** change their houses <note>original: "domicilia sua mutauerint"; an astrological technique of exchange</note>, they decree and indicate this same thing by a similar reasoning.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> are positioned together in the 11th house from the **Ascendant**, and all are joined exactly in an equal fellowship, they decree the female slaves of the most powerful wealthy men as wives.
