### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are positioned in the **Midheaven** <term>Medium Coeli; the highest point in the chart</term> in the exact same degree <note>original: "partiliter"</note>, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> does not regard them with any radiation <note>meaning no aspect like a square or trine</note>, and if this is a woman’s birth chart, she will engage in intercourse with eunuchs or sterile men with a useless desire for lust, and she will be involved in shameful acts.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are found together in the fifth or eleventh house from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point rising on the eastern horizon</term>, and no star regards them from any side, they decree difficult marriages or heavy disputes arising from marriage: so that, always entangled in bitter dissensions, they will carry out the quarrels and lawsuits of malicious rivalry.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is joined to the **Ascendant** in an equal partnership of degrees, and both are positioned in a house of **Jupiter** <note>either Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and the **Ascendant** are also regarded by **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> via a trine radiation <note>an aspect of 120 degrees</note>, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is positioned in the final degrees of the **Ascendant**, those who have these stars will sleep either with their mother or their stepmother. But if this is a woman’s birth chart, she will sleep with her father or stepfather with an incestuous desire of lust; and furthermore, this woman will be unable to control herself regarding every lustful act, having prostituted her modesty. If, however, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is found in the fifth house from the **Ascendant**, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> with **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> in the eleventh, they decree marriages with stepdaughters with wicked desire.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is found in any "pivot" <term>cardine; the four main angles of the chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is placed in opposition <note>original: "in diametro"</note> regarding it with a threatening radiation, the birth of children is denied by that radiation.

When the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant**, if **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> are in the **anaphora** <term>the sign or house following the Ascendant; the 2nd house</term> of the **Ascendant**, some defect is inflicted upon the right eye. But if the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and **Mars** or **Saturn** are found in the **anaphora** of the **Ascendant**, the left eye will receive this same defect; but this applies to a nighttime birth. If, however, the **Moon** is found in the **Midheaven**, and the **Sun** is positioned in the **Ascendant**, while **Saturn** holds the ninth house from the **Ascendant**, they bring about the greatest weakness of vision. But if **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is in the ninth, and **Mars** is in the eleventh, and regards the **Moon** (placed in the sixth) with an opposing radiation <note>original: "diametra radiatione"</note>, while **Saturn** and the **Sun**, joined in an exact partnership, are positioned in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**, they inflict the wretched outcome of blindness. But if the **Moon** is found in the **Midheaven**, and **Saturn**, the **Sun**, and **Mars**—positioned in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**—regard the **Moon** with a trine radiation, they decree blindness and physical weakness along with wretched beggary. But if **Saturn** is found in the eleventh house from the **Ascendant**, and the **Sun**, **Moon**, and **Mars**—placed together—regard **Saturn** with a trine radiation, they also decree blindness from that partnership. But if the **Sun** and **Mars** are positioned in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**, and in opposition to them, the **Moon** and **Saturn** are found placed in a "human" sign <note>signs like Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius which are represented by human figures</note>, this radiation likewise decrees blindness along with bodily infirmity. But if **Saturn** is positioned in the "Setting" <term>the 7th house, where stars set in the West</term>, and **Mars** is in the **Ascendant**, while the **Sun** is placed in the **anaphora** of the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** is positioned in the sixth house from the **Ascendant**, over the passage of time, persistent illnesses will bring about blindness through the defect of a cataract <note>original: "suffusionis uitio"</note>. But if the **Moon** is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and the **Sun** is in the seventh house from the **Ascendant** (that is, placed in the Setting), it brings a very great defect to the eyes.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is found in the **Midheaven**, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the eleventh house from the **Ascendant**, and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is in the **anaphora** of the **Ascendant**, and regards the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> (positioned in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**) with an opposing radiation, the light of one eye is extinguished while the other is preserved.

If **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are positioned together, joined in an equal partnership of degrees, and they have **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> positioned on the left side of a square <note>original: "in sinistro quadrati latere"</note>, they either deform the body with a pointed head, or they disgrace the sharpness of the eyes with a distorted arrangement of the lights <note>the Sun and Moon were known as the "Lights"</note>, or they make the neck turn shamefully to one side.

If the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is found in the **Ascendant**, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the **Midheaven**, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> possesses a trine to the right of the **Ascendant**, even this partnership of conjunction inflicts the danger of blindness. But if **Saturn** and the **Moon** are positioned together in a tropical sign <note>Cancer, Capricorn, Aries, or Libra</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and the **Sun** are placed in opposition to them, danger to the eyes is always brought about by that conjunction. But if **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is found so placed in the **Midheaven**, it eases all the inconveniences of poverty. If, however, **Saturn** and the **Moon** are found in the **Midheaven**, and the **Sun** and **Mars** are positioned in the eighth house from the **Ascendant**, the misery of blindness is likewise decreed. But if the **Sun** is found in the **Ascendant**, and **Saturn** is positioned in the **anaphora** of the **Ascendant**, with the **Moon** also placed in the **Midheaven**, and **Mars** found in the eleventh house from the **Ascendant**, the misery of blindness and loss of light is likewise decreed.

# BOOK SIX.

If the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are joined in a tropical sign <term>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs marking the turning points of the seasons</term> by a synodic radiation <note>original: "synodica radiatione"; an alignment or conjunction</note>, and the **Moon** is deprived of all the splendor of its light, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is with them, they decree the greatest wisdom, an illustrious mind, and knowledge of many things, but accompanied by blindness of the eyes and bodily weakness.

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> are positioned by the exact degree <note>original: "partiliter"</note> in equinoctial signs <term>Aries or Libra; where day and night are of equal length</term>, they stain the whole body with certain marks, or disfigure it with white spots, or certainly a creeping skin disease <note>original: "impetigo"</note> will possess the bodies of men: or the form of the body will be changed, roughened by small falling scales, or a daily itch will shake the person, or leprosy will certainly defile them with a shameful appearance.

If **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> are positioned together in the seventh house from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point rising on the eastern horizon</term>—that is, in the setting <note>the Descendant</note>—and in the sixth house from the **Ascendant**, the **Moon** is joined with the **Sun** in an equal partnership of degrees, they either make people lame, or disabled with amputated hands: or they certainly make them insane, suffering greatly from a failing mind <term>likely referring to epilepsy or severe mental illness</term>.

Now to you, **Mavortius** <note>original: "Mauorti"; referring to Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work</note>, our glory, I will show a mocking decree: instructed by this example, you will also be able to define similar birth charts. That deformed and weak Greek, whose composite body's form **Homer** announced to us in his divine poems—whom the wise man <note>referring to Odysseus in the Iliad</note> chastises with a severe rebuke amidst everyone’s laughter—had his decree composed by this logic. The **Ascendant** was established in **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>: in **Capricorn** <note>original: "♑"</note>, however, which is the twelfth house from the **Ascendant**, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> were joined by an equal power of degrees; **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> was positioned in the *anaphora* <term>the 2nd house, following the Ascendant</term> of the **Ascendant**; **Mars** and **Mars** <note>original: "♂ & ♂"; likely a scribal error for Mars and the Moon, as shown in the accompanying chart</note> in the ninth house from the **Ascendant**, with the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, occupied the sign of **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>: while **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> were established in the **Ascendant**, that is, in **Aquarius**. This decree of birth showed us **Thersites**: for he was feeble, weak, ridiculous, and always impatient with babbling verbosity. All these things, therefore, the birth chart prescribed above demonstrates.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is established in **Capricorn** <note>original: "♑"</note> and strikes with a diameter radiation <term>an opposition; an aspect of 180 degrees</term> from **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, it makes such men that their wives curse them with every kind of insult: and whose bodies exhale a dismal filth of a goat-like odor <note>original: "hircini odoris"</note>, from heavy perspired fluids: and they themselves will be cursed in their intercourse, always infamous from Venereal lusts: and who, with a headlong greed of mind, desire the vicious couplings of promiscuous lust. But **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> mitigates these things in some part, if he regards **Venus** with a trine radiation <term>an aspect of 120 degrees</term>: or at least, while the other things remain, he wipes away the fatal and foul filth of the goat-like odor.

<meta>This page continues Julius Firmicus Maternus’s detailed astrological catalog in Book 6 of the Mathesis. ->### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS<-

If the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are positioned in the seventh house from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point rising on the eastern horizon</term>—that is, in the setting <note>the Descendant</note>—they will create effeminate men <note>original: "cinædos"</note> with soft bodies, who often mimic the tragic ends of ancient myths by dancing on stage. But if **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** <term>Imum Coeli; the lowest point of the chart, the Fourth House</term>, looks upon them with a square aspect <term>quadrata radiatione; an angle of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</term>, he will make them impure and prone to every vice of lustful filth, and those who are always joined with their wives in shameless and impure intercourse. If, however, **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> from the **Lower Midheaven** looks upon all these planets positioned in the setting with a square aspect, in addition to all those vices, he will make them lovers of boys and infamous pederasts <note>original: "pedicones"</note>.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> are positioned in the **Midheaven** <term>Medium Coeli; the highest point of the chart, the Tenth House</term> by the exact degree <note>original: "partiliter"</note>, joined in an equal partnership of degrees, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** looking at all of these with an opposition <term>diametra radiatione; an angle of 180 degrees</term>, they create lovers of boys, but those who restrain this vice of lust at the cost and expense of their own bodies.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note>, **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note>, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> are placed together in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the setting—an inheritance will be granted from the death of a wife; but the men themselves will be shaken by a long continuation of heavy sickness, and the birth of children is decreed for them only with great difficulty.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is positioned in the **Midheaven**, and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are placed with her, they decree foreign wives, but wives who are abundant with a great flow of wealth.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant**, while **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are placed in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**, they deny children. But if this arrangement of the order is changed—that is, if **Jupiter** and **Venus** are in the **Ascendant**, and **Saturn**, positioned in the setting, looks at them with an opposition—they decree the same thing.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are placed together in the **Lower Midheaven**, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, occupying the **Midheaven**, strikes these same planets with an opposition, it decrees a woman of advanced age as a wife; but the man and his wife will also be mixed in impure intercourse.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is placed in the **Midheaven** and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is joined to her in an equal partnership of degrees, while the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** looking at these same planets with an opposition, it decrees wives who are either sterile or certainly of advanced age, so that children are denied from that union forever.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is positioned in the fifth house from the **Ascendant**, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is joined with her in an equal partnership of degrees, it decrees either sisters or the daughters of sisters as wives.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the **Midheaven**, and while he is so placed, a partnership with **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is added in the same place, they cause every kind of sadness to be prepared by everyone, so that they can never experience the joy of marital grace.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is placed in the evening rising in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—that is, in the setting—and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the **Midheaven**, it will make men sluggish toward women; but it will also make women "cold" toward intercourse, with their desire for Venus <note>sexual desire</note> lulled to sleep and all the substance of lust extinguished.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are joined in an equal partnership of degrees in the **Midheaven**, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are likewise positioned and look at them from the **Lower Midheaven** with an opposition, this decree in a man's natal chart <note>original: "genitura"</note> will create public *galli* <term>priests of the goddess Cybele who castrated themselves in religious ecstasy</term>; but it will render women as prostitutes, destitute of all honorable shame.

If **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> are positioned together in the **Lower Midheaven**, or placed in the setting—that is, in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—they indicate a heavy weight of sadness from the misfortunes of children. But if **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is found with them in those same places, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is placed in the same spot joined to them in an equal partnership of degrees, they will make women sterile and separate men from all intercourse, leaving them destitute of masculine desires. If, however, they are positioned in a tropical sign <term>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</term> (as we have said), they cause the natural body of the woman to be "glued together" with an unpierced opening <note>referring to vaginal atresia or an imperforate hymen</note>. If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is also found with all of these, it will create castrated *galli* serving in sacred ceremonies.

If **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are positioned together in the **Ascendant**, and while they are so placed, **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> occupies the **Midheaven**, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> positioned in the setting looks at them with an opposition, while **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> looks with a square aspect, they cause children who are in their tender years and still crying in the arms of their nurses to perish by untimely fates.

If **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is positioned in the **Midheaven**, and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note>, **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> <note>The text repeats Venus here; this may be a scribal error for the Moon or Mercury</note> are joined to her in an equal partnership of degrees, they cause children to perish before the eyes of their fathers by miserable and bitter deaths.

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is found in the **Lower Midheaven**, while **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is positioned in the setting, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant**, with **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> joined by a square aspect and **Saturn** by an opposition, a swift death is prepared for a beloved wife from this fellowship of stars.

<meta>This page continues Firmicus Maternus's exhaustive catalog of planetary combinations. -># BOOK SIX<-

If **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is found in the setting <note>the Descendant, the Seventh House</note>, and in the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term> **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> are joined by the exact same degree, they will deny children. But if **Jupiter** and **Saturn** are positioned in the **angles** <term>cardines; the four most powerful points of the chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> and look upon each other in an **opposition** <term>diametra radiatione; an aspect of 180 degrees</term>, and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is in the **Ascendant** so that one is in the setting, another in the **Midheaven** <term>M C / Medium Coeli; the 10th House</term>, and another in the **Lower Midheaven** <term>I M C / Imum Coeli; the 4th House</term>, they cause male children to perish through wretched and atrocious deaths. However, if **Jupiter** is positioned in any angle and looks upon **Saturn** placed in the opposite angle by opposition, by this configuration the birth of offspring is denied.

If the **Ascendant** is positioned in **tropical** <term>the turning signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</term> or **double-bodied** <term>mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</term> signs, and in its degree **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and **Mercury** are joined in an equal partnership of degrees, and **Saturn** also looks upon the **Ascendant** and those planets by opposition, they make men who are either epileptics or certainly always insane with a distorted mind.

If **Venus** is positioned in the **Ascendant** by exact degree, and **Saturn** is placed in the **Lower Midheaven** and joined to **Venus** by a **square aspect** <term>quadrata radiatione; a 90-degree angle</term>, it will produce men assigned to the service of temples. Driven by a hidden instinct of divinity and a changed state of mind, and possessed by the power of an imminent religion, they predict the future to those who ask; thus, through this way of life, they seek the sustenance for their daily living.

If the **Ascendant** is positioned in **Virgo** <note>original: "♍"</note>, and in that same sign **Jupiter**, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note>, **Mercury**, and **Venus** are all located, while **Saturn** is in **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>—that is, in the setting—looking upon all those we mentioned by opposition, and the **Sun** is positioned in the **house following the Ascendant** <term>anaphora; the 2nd House</term> occupying the sign of **Libra** <note>original: "♎"</note>, while the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is placed in **Aquarius** <note>original: "♒"</note>, and all are positioned in their own **terms** <term>finibus; specific degrees within a sign traditionally assigned to a planet</term>—that is, **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, the **Sun**, **Mercury**, and **Venus**—from this birth chart the decree of a most powerful emperor is revealed.

If the **Moon** is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** is either moving toward the **Sun** or away from it, this partnership of conjunction decrees a humble life, heavy defects of health, bitter crises of danger, and the onset of wretched calamity. But if **Mars** is found in the setting and the **Moon** moves away from him, these same things are brought to pass in a similar manner.

If the **Sun** is positioned in **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note> or **Gemini** <note>original: "♊"</note>, and the **Ascendant** is joined to it in an equal partnership of degrees, while **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, and **Mercury**, placed in favorable places of the birth chart, look upon each other with a **trine aspect** <term>trigonica radiatione; a 120-degree angle</term>, they will produce tyrants who are cruel, terrifying, and powerful, who always rage with cruel ferocity in the slaughter of men and the punishment of the wretched.

If the **Moon** is found in the **Ascendant**, and either **Saturn** or **Jupiter** positioned in the setting—that is, in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—looks upon it by opposition, the conscience of the one who has them thus will be polluted and deeply contaminated by a secret murder.

If the **Sun**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** are in the setting—that is, in the seventh house from the **Ascendant**—and in a **tropical sign** joined in an equal partnership of degrees, this gathering of stars will produce a murderer and a bandit, always soaked in human blood and armed with every kind of cruelty. If, however, **Saturn** is found with them, he shows us the doom of death; for, caught in these crimes, the person is cruelly raised on a cross, fixed to a yoke <note>original: "patibulo suffixus"</note> by the severe sentence of a judge.

If **Jupiter** is found in those degrees in which **Andromeda** <note>the constellation</note> is positioned, and **Saturn** receives the conjunction of the incoming **Moon**, the greatest disadvantages of unhappiness are decreed from this conjunction. But if **Mars** looks upon the **Moon** positioned as we described by opposition, he causes men caught in wicked thoughts to be raised on a cross.

If **Venus** is positioned in **Taurus** <note>original: "♉"</note>, and she occupies those degrees of **Taurus** in which the **Pleiades** are placed, and the **Moon** is full of light, and **Mercury** and **Mars** are either joined with her in an equal partnership of degrees or are in a superior position from a **square aspect** <term>de quadrato latere superiores; a position of astrological dominance</term> and look upon her with a threatening radiation, the one who has them thus will perish captured by bandits, struck by the point of a threatening sword. However, if **Venus** is found in **Taurus** with the **Ascendant**, and strikes the full **Moon** positioned in the **Midheaven** with a square aspect, she will bring about this same result we mentioned through a similar radiation. But if the **Ascendant** is found in **Taurus**, and **Mars** is positioned in **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note> and looks upon the **Ascendant** from the **Lower Midheaven** <note>the 4th House</note> with a threatening radiation, he will cause death by the sword. But if the **Ascendant** is found in **Libra** and **Mars** is in **Aries**—that is, looking at the **Ascendant** from a square in the **Lower Midheaven** with threatening radiation—even so, he will cause them to perish struck by the sword. It should be known, however, that if the **Ascendant** is placed in **Aries** or **Libra**, and **Mars** is found in the setting or in the **Midheaven**, with even slight testimony from the **benefics** <term>benevola; the "good" planets, Jupiter and Venus</term>, he decrees no evil, especially if it is a nocturnal birth; for **Mars** always protects his own house and never destroys it when positioned in the setting.

If **Cancer** <note>original: "♋"</note> or **Leo** <note>original: "♌"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, and the houses of **Saturn** <note>Capricorn and Aquarius</note> are in the setting <note>the Descendant or Seventh House</note>, and **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> himself is placed in the **Midheaven** <term>M C / Medium Coeli; the highest point of the chart or 10th House</term>, he will cause men to perish from **dropsy** <note>an old medical term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</note>. But if these signs we have mentioned hold the Ascendant and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is placed in the Midheaven, she will cause men to perish by poison. If, however, with these signs as the Ascendant, **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is found in the Midheaven, sudden death is decreed amidst cups and tables, and among the joyful noise of banqueters, caused by indigestion or excessive drinking. But if, with those same signs rising, **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> and the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> are positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** <term>I M C / Imum Coeli; the bottom of the chart or 4th House</term>, they are either killed by the sword or consumed by the heat of fire. If, truly, **Venus** is in these rising signs and the **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> is found in the Midheaven, she will cause men to perish shaken by **sacred diseases** <note>a historical term for epilepsy</note>.

**Venus**, if found in **Cancer** or in the Lower Midheaven, will make one fulfill the gift of a wretched life, either oppressed by diseased humors or submerged in rushing waves.

**Mars** and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note>, if placed together in the eighth house from the Ascendant, will produce wicked thieves who desire the property of others with a depraved greed of mind; and who, possessed by an immoderate madness of mind and the vice of avarice, always pursue the estates of others with unjust desires.

If the **Sun** is found in the Ascendant and the **Moon** is positioned in the setting, while **Saturn** and **Mars** are either with the Sun or placed equally with the Moon, and one of the malevolent planets is with the Sun or Moon while the other malevolent planet holds one of the following **angles** <term>cardines; the four pivot points of the chart: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, he who has such a conjunction of planets will be **exposed** <note>infant exposure was the practice of abandoning unwanted newborns in the elements</note>.

If **Saturn** is positioned in the Ascendant and **Mercury** is placed in the Midheaven joined by a **square aspect** <term>quadrata radiatione; a 90-degree angle</term> from **Mars**, it will produce public and malicious accusers. But if **Mercury** is found in the setting and the **Sun** is placed in the Lower Midheaven while **Saturn** looks upon them with a square aspect, he will produce bandits, specifically those who are frequently stained with human blood.

If **Saturn** is found in the Ascendant and **Jupiter** is placed in any **anaphora** <term>a house rising immediately after an angle; a succedent house</term> of an angle, while the **Moon** and **Jupiter** are positioned together in a **fallen place** <note>a cadent house, considered weak in astrology</note>, those who are born live only as long as the **Moon** in her swift course passes **Jupiter**. But if the **Moon** is joined to **Jupiter** by a "faithful" aspect, they live as long as **Saturn** passes the first angle he encounters. If, however, the rays of the **Moon** are unstable, they live for as many days (as we said before) as the **Moon** was found with **Jupiter**. But if (as we said) **Mars** or **Saturn** is positioned and the **Moon** is in a fallen place, or if the **Moon** is found in a primary angle—that is, in the Ascendant—they will, because of **Mars**, be <term>oligochronios</term> <note>original: "oligochronios"; Greek for "short-lived"</note>, dying with a bad turning point of death. If, truly, **Saturn** is found in the Midheaven and the **Moon** is positioned in the Lower Midheaven joined to **Saturn** by an **opposition** <term>diametra radiatione; an aspect of 180 degrees</term>, while the **Sun** is either positioned in the setting or in the Midheaven, looking upon the **Moon** with a threatening aspect while yet possessing degrees equal to the Moon, he immediately bursts the narrows of the womb and delivers the oncoming birth to death. But if the **Sun** is found in the Ascendant and the **Moon** is positioned in the setting, joined to the **Sun** by an opposition, and **Mars** or **Saturn** is positioned with one of them—that is, with either the **Sun** or the **Moon**—or if one is with one and the other holds any other angle, the child who is born will be **exposed**.

If the **Sun** is found in the seventh house from the Ascendant and **Saturn** is placed in the twelfth from the Ascendant looking at the **Sun** by opposition, but **Venus**, the **Moon**, and **Mars** are joined in the twelfth with **Saturn** in an equal partnership of degrees, and they themselves are also diametrically opposed to the **Sun**, they will produce the weak and the <term>paralyticos</term> <note>original: "paralyticos"; those suffering from paralysis or loss of motor function</note>, whose bodies, with the framework of their nerves loosened, are disgraced by broken and dissipated strength.

If **Saturn**, **Mars**, and the **Moon**, positioned together in an equal partnership of degrees, are joined in the twelfth house from the Ascendant, and **Jupiter** looks upon them with a **trine aspect** <term>trigonica radiatione; a 120-degree angle</term> while positioned either in the setting or in the third house from the Ascendant, and the **Sun** likewise holds the Ascendant, that birth reveals to us a cruel tyrant.

If **Mercury**, **Venus**, **Saturn**, and **Mars** are composed in an equal aspect in the eleventh house from the Ascendant, they produce a luxurious man who, with lavish spending, is entangled in lustful desires.

If **Saturn** and **Mercury** are placed together in the 8th house from the Ascendant, and **Saturn** being made superior looks upon them with a square aspect, or if placed with them he is joined in an equal partnership of degrees, he will produce counterfeiters, or those who imitate public money with the adulterated arts of smelting. If, however, with these so placed, the **Moon** agrees in a following position, he will produce bandits and murderers. ...[with an opposing] radiation, it strikes [them]; because of the crime of forgery, the stars decree the end of a public death, so that those cast down by this vice are punished by the severe sentence of a judge. If, however, the **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is positioned in the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, and **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is placed with it, while **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> and **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> are positioned in the setting <note>the West or Seventh House</note> and look upon the **Sun** with a diametrical radiation <term>opposition; an astrological aspect where planets are 180 degrees apart</term>, they will cause those caught in the crime of forgery to be raised on a cross. Nor can the good testimony of **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> mitigate this danger; rather, with his healthy protection disregarded, the threatening rays of the malevolent stars decree a public and violent death in every way.

If **Saturn** and **Mars** are positioned exactly in the **Ascendant**, and the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "☽"</note> are positioned equally in the setting and look upon them with a diametrical radiation, from this fellowship of radiation, either a foot or a hand is amputated. But later, when they have been worn down by this laceration of the body, they also encounter a miserable end of death and a fatal destruction.

If in the same sign of the **Ascendant**, a point is found midway between **Saturn** and **Mars**, it shows a mournful case of sorrowful misfortune. For with the birth hindered within the mother's womb, the mangled offspring is scattered by wretched lacerations, so that once the parts of the womb are opened, all the limbs are brought forth by the aid of a cruel artifice <note>this refers to a historical medical procedure to remove a fetus that died during labor to save the mother</note>.

If the **Moon** is positioned in a double sign <note>such as Gemini, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and occupies the portion of **Jupiter**, and **Saturn** is in the setting and **Mars** is in the **Lower Midheaven** <term>I M C / Imum Coeli; the bottom of the chart</term>, it will make them epileptics <note>original: "caducos"; those suffering from the "falling sickness"</note>. But if the **Moon** is in conjunction with the **Sun**, and **Mars** is positioned equally with her, and all of them hold a part of the **Midheaven** <term>M C / Medium Coeli; the highest point of the chart</term>, and **Mars** is in a morning rising, and **Saturn** is positioned either with them or in the setting, it will make them epileptics by a similar reasoning—those who, changed by an insane madness of the mind, lose the right order of life. If, truly, with the **Moon**, **Mercury**, and **Sun** positioned as we have said, **Saturn** is found in the **Midheaven** and looks upon those positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** with a diametrical radiation, the end of a miserable death will take those oppressed by a vice of the mind and thrown over precipices. But generally, always, if the **Sun** and **Saturn** are positioned equally in double signs and are found equally in the setting, they decree these same things by a similar reasoning, just as was said above.

If the **Ascendant** is found with the **Sun** in **Gemini** <note>original: "Ⅱ"</note>, and the **Moon** is placed in the **Midheaven** (that is, in **Pisces** <note>original: "♓"</note>), and **Mars** is positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** (that is, in **Virgo** <note>original: "♍"</note>), and [one of them] holds the setting of the cardines <term>angles; the four most powerful points of a chart</term>, so that positioned in double signs they possess all the angles of the birth <term>genitura; the natal chart</term>, they will also make them epileptics from that fellowship, and those raging with a heavy disease.

If **Jupiter** is positioned in a double sign and holds the **Midheaven** angle, and **Saturn** positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** looks upon him with a diametrical radiation, and **Jupiter** is joined to **Saturn** in a fellowship of conjunction, those adopted by strangers will seek an inheritance under the title of patrimony, so that they become children by law to those whom nature had denied their own children.

If **Saturn** and **Mercury** are joined in the **Midheaven** by an equal fellowship of degrees, and the **Moon** approaches these as a fourth witness, it will create prostitutes who, through the loss of their traded modesty and for the sake of a prostituted body, seek a miserable profit every single day. If, however, this is a male's birth, he will be entangled in the womanly vices of lust by the heat of an effeminate madness.

If the **Sun** and **Mars** are found together in the **Ascendant**, and **Saturn** is positioned in the **Lower Midheaven** looking upon them with a square radiation <term>an aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful</term>, and the **Moon** is placed in the **Lower Midheaven** looking at **Saturn** diametrically and at the **Sun** and **Mars** through a square, it always stirs up the parricidal hatred of parents toward children and a fatal slaughter.

If the **Moon** is positioned in the **Ascendant**, and **Jupiter** is placed in the sixth house from the **Ascendant**, and the **Moon** together with **Mercury** and **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> possesses a part in the **Midheaven** in an equal fellowship of conjunction, that union decrees the marks of distinguished nobility.

If the **Ascendant** is found in **Aries** <note>original: "♈"</note>, and **Mars**, **Saturn**, and **Venus** are there equally, and the **Sun** is also in the same sign, it decrees a slave girl or an old woman as a wife, or certainly one who is humble and destitute of any protection of dignity. But if **Mercury** joins them, he leads public prostitutes to the marriage bed of the wedding chamber. If, with all these things positioned thus (as we have said), the **Moon** is found in the **Midheaven**, they compel those possessed by an incestuous heat of madness and a wicked desire of the mind to come to the bedding of their own daughters.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...is punished by judicial observation <note>original: "animadversione punitur"</note>.

The **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>, and **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>, if they are positioned together in the eleventh place from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, and if this is the feminine sign of **Cancer** <note>original: ♋</note>, and **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> regards them with a **trine aspect** <term>trigonica radiatione; an aspect of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</term>, they create musicians who strike the lyre, either the "sand-players" <note>likely referring to a type of performance or arena music</note> or those who play on bronze strings with sweet modulation.

**Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>, **Venus**, and the **Moon**, if they are positioned together in the **Ascendant**, or in the **Midheaven** <term>M C; Medium Coeli, the highest point of the chart</term>, will produce dancers and pantomimes adorned with the grace of charm. If, however, **Jupiter** regards these so positioned with a favorable radiation, he bestows glory upon them from the judgment of the people, especially if **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> provides good testimony to them in such a position.

If the **Moon** is found in **conjunction** <note>original: "synodica"</note> with the **Sun** in the eleventh place from the **Ascendant**, and **Jupiter** is positioned together with them, but **Saturn** and **Mars** regard the **Ascendant** with different radiations—such as one from a **square** <term>an aspect of 90 degrees</term> and the other from an **opposition** <term>de diametro; an aspect of 180 degrees</term>—and one of them is positioned in an **equinoctial sign** <note>Aries or Libra</note>, they decree the long and lasting sickness of **elephantiasis** <note>a term used in antiquity for severe, chronic skin and nerve diseases, often equated with leprosy</note> even until the final day of life.

If **Saturn** or the **Moon** is positioned humbly in a part of **Aquarius** <note>original: ♒</note>, or **Mars**, and **Saturn** looks upon this same part from an **opposition**, it will cause children to be separated from their parents.

If the **Moon** is found in the **Pleiades** <note>a star cluster in Taurus</note>, or in the **Nebula of Cancer** <note>Praesepe</note>, or in the **Mane of Leo**, or in the **Brow of Scorpio** (specifically from the eighth degree to the tenth in Scorpio), or in the **Thorns of Sagittarius**, or in the **Hollow of Pisces**, or in the **Head of Aries**, and if she is diminished in her lights—that is, with all the splendor of her light spent—and either **Saturn** or **Mars** regards her with some radiation, it will cause blindness. If indeed she holds any **angle** <term>cardinem; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</term> in these signs and in the places we have mentioned, the very substance of the eyes is destroyed, and the miserable crisis of blindness is brought about. If, however, the **Moon** is full of light and still receiving an increase of splendor, she will not cause blindness, but always inflicts either a defect, a sickness, or a scar or mark on the face, so that it disgraces the countenance with a certain unseemly appearance.

If **Jupiter** and **Saturn** are found in the **Midheaven** by degree, and in the third place from the **Ascendant** **Mercury** and **Venus** are joined in an equal fellowship of degree, and **Saturn** holds the eighth place from the **Ascendant**, while the **Sun** is in **Gemini** <note>original: ♊</note> and the **Moon** is positioned either in her own **house** <note>Cancer</note> or in her **exaltation** <note>Taurus</note>, this decree produces a hero, a brave man, and a slayer, who with his victorious right hand creates heaps of enemies in extraordinary slaughter.

If the **Ascendant** is found in **Taurus** <note>original: ♉</note>, a **double-bodied sign** <note>original: "ditropico"; though Taurus is usually fixed, the author may be using a specific technical classification here</note>, and the **Moon** is positioned in the twelfth place from the **Ascendant**, and **Jupiter** and **Mars** are joined in an equal fellowship of degrees and verge toward the **Lower Midheaven** <term>I M C; Imaum Coeli, the 4th house</term>, while **Venus** and **Mercury** possess the **Midheaven** at equal degrees, this birth demonstrates the mind of a malicious prostitute. She invites many to her bed for the sake of her beauty, but she will be led through foreign places and will be entangled in frequent legal cases and great accusations. She will also be taken into public custody and will endure frequent disturbances and injuries. She will likewise abort twin sons. For the sake of profit and lust, she will even trade her shame to two brothers and will invite both father and son to her intercourse alike. For she will accomplish all these things with an immoderate heat of lust and an unbridled desire for money. But when she enters the time of middle age, she will then return to her fatherland and will associate herself in the union of the marriage bed with a young foreigner, poor and unworthy. Joined in a vehicle of manumission <note>likely referring to a transition out of her former status</note>, she will reach the final day of life in wretched necessity.

But there is still something required for the full substance of this work, and I will now show that to you with a most true exposition. For we cannot come to the secrets of the **Mathesis** <term>the science of astrology</term> which the seventh book will contain, nor to the **Barbaric Sphere** <note>referring to non-Greek/Egyptian constellations and systems</note> which the eighth book shows you, unless all things pertaining to the foundations of the entire science have first been collected with diligent tradition. We shall show, therefore, what you should seek in which place, and to what extent. For the **square place** <note>the 4th house</note> from the **Ascendant** does not show parents or the life of parents, nor the **seventh** the spouse, nor the **tenth** the children, nor the **eleventh** the friends, nor the **sixth** the illnesses. Because we have promised that we would say all things, receive the account full of truth and faith, so that you may be able to gather all these things by diligent consideration...

### BOOK SIX.

...lest you gather poorly, or being preoccupied with pleasing definitions, you lose the full integrity of truth; instead, you shall find it most certainly.

If you wish to determine the **Place of the Father** <term>A "lot" or mathematical point in the chart used to predict the father's life</term> by the degree-based method, and it is a daytime birth, calculate the number of all degrees from the degree of the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> to the degree of **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>; count all the degrees of all the signs that lie between the **Sun** and **Saturn**. When you have the total sum of this number, start counting from the **Ascendant** <term>horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, assigning thirty degrees to each sign. In whichever sign the final degree falls, that sign will show you the **Place of the Father**. In a nighttime birth, however, calculate from the degree of **Saturn** to the degree of the **Sun**, doing the same. <margin>Haly, part 4, chapter 16. <note>This is a later editorial reference to the 11th-century astrologer Haly Abenragel.</note></margin> Once you have found the sign of the father through careful calculation, you will describe the father's substance from the nature of that sign. Observe also to what extent this same sign is adorned by the rays of **benefic** <term>lucky or helpful planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</term> stars. For if there are benefic stars in the sign of the **Ascendant**, or if they look upon it with a prosperous radiation, the father's happiness is found. If, however, **malefic** <term>difficult or harmful planets, usually Saturn and Mars</term> stars do the same, all things contrary are announced to us regarding the father. Look also into this very sign to see whether there are benefic or malefic stars, and how the **lord** <term>the planet that rules that specific zodiac sign</term> of that sign is placed in the birth chart: in which sign, in which **bounds** <term>fines; specific sub-divisions of a sign</term>, and whether it stands in the first or second **angles** <term>cardines; the most powerful houses of a chart</term>; and in which places it "rejoices," or if it is in dark and dejected places. From all these things you will find what kind of father the native had, all of which I shall declare in detail.

<margin>The Place of the Father in Saturn.</margin> If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign ruled by **Saturn**, seek where **Saturn** is positioned in the birth chart. For if it is a daytime birth, and **Saturn** is found in that very place, or in his own degrees, or in the signs in which he is **exalted** <term>a sign where a planet's influence is most powerful</term>, or in those places where he **rejoices**, and if he is in his **morning rising** <term>matutino ortu; appearing in the east before the Sun</term>, adding to his number, and if **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> looks upon him with prosperous radiation, he will make the father grave, modest, mature, and formidable with a calm severity. He will be a tiller of the fields, one to whom the greatest protections of inheritance are brought from these fruits, and who is raised up by great promotions. If, however, it is a nighttime birth, and **Saturn** is in dejected places, or in dejected angles, or in his **debilities** <note>original: humilitatibus</note>, or is **retrograde** <term>appearing to move backward in the sky</term>, or is hidden under the rays of the **Sun**, he makes the father hardworking, sordid, horrible, sad, always hesitating in dark endeavors, and a slave, or polluted by the squalor of the most shameful servitude.

If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign ruled by **Jupiter**, and **Jupiter** is positioned in that very place, or in signs where he is exalted, or in the first angles, or in the **fifth** or **eleventh** house, and is adding to his number and positioned in his morning rising, and looks upon the place by a **trine** <note>original: trigono</note> or **sextile** <note>original: hexagono</note> aspect, it shows the father adorned with happy marks of dignity. If, however, **Jupiter** is either in the second angles, or in dejected and dark places, or retrograde, or hidden under the rays of the **Sun**, it will demonstrate plainly that the father was mediocre.

<margin>Mars</margin> If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign ruled by **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, and it is a daytime birth, and **Mars** is in that very place, or in the angles, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **Ascendant**, or in the eighth or third, and is in his morning rising, proceeding in a direct degree of his parts, he will make the father austere, rash, involved in various labors and dangers, **short-lived** <term>oligochronium; having a short life</term>, and always entangled in perverse desires. If **Mars**, thus positioned, sees the **Place of the Father** by a **square** <note>original: quadrato</note> or **opposition** <note>original: diametro</note> aspect, he will make him a **violent death** <term>biothanatum; one who dies by violence or non-natural causes</term>. If, however, it is a nighttime birth, and **Jupiter** or **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> looks upon the place of the father or the mother with prosperous radiation, these things which we have said are mitigated in some part: he makes the father upright, military, severe, and one whom arms and iron always delight, and according to the measure of the birth, renders him either a prince or a leader.

If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign ruled by the **Sun**, and it is a daytime birth, seek in which sign or in which place of the chart the **Sun** is positioned. For if the **Sun** is in that very sign, or in his **height** <note>exaltation</note>, or in the principal angles, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **Ascendant**, it shows the father rich with flowing wealth, adorned with the greatest marks of dignity, and bringing home the glory of great happiness. If, however, he is in dejected places, or in the second angles, or in his debilities, and being destitute of benefic stars, the rays of **malefic** stars attack him, all these things we have said are for the most part diminished, especially if it is a daytime birth: for then he strikes down the father, among other things, with a swift death.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

...placed. For if he <note>Referring to Jupiter, the planet associated with the father's success</note> is in that very place, or in the primary **angles** <term>cardines; the four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, or in the signs in which he **rejoices**, or in which he is **exalted**, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **ascendant** <note>horoscopus</note>, and is rising in the morning, and increasing in number <note>meaning the planet is moving forward and gaining speed</note>, and established in those places or signs, and regards the **Place of the Father** with a prosperous **radiation** <term>an astrological aspect or beam of light from one planet to another</term>, he decrees for the father the greatest marks of honor and the greatest beauty of grace. If however he is in **dejected places** <note>houses 6, 8, or 12, considered weak or unlucky</note>, and in those signs in which he is humbled, or **retrograde**, or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** ☉ <note>When a planet is too close to the Sun, it becomes invisible and loses its power</note>, he will show us a mediocre father.

☿ If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign of **Mercury** <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, look for where **Mercury** ☿ is placed. For if he is either in that very place, or in his height <note>exaltation</note>, or his own house, or in his own degrees, or in those **angles** and places in which he rejoices, and is rising in the morning and increasing in number, he will make the father dedicated to all duties of business, and one to whom the greatest profits are frequently brought, and who always loves his children with tender affection. If however **Jupiter** ♃—that is, the lord of the paternal place—is helped by the prosperous **radiation** of benefic stars, greater increases than those we have said will follow. If however **Mercury** ☿ is in **dejected places**, or in those in which he does not rejoice in the angles, or in his humilities <note>his "fall," the sign opposite his exaltation</note>, and is retrograde or hidden under the rays of the **Sun** ☉, the decrees of the preceding happiness are changed, and all things we said are granted to the father only slightly and mediocrely.

☽ If the **Place of the Father** is found in a sign of the **Moon** <note>Cancer</note>, look for where in the **nativity** <note>genitura; the birth chart</note> the **Moon** ☽ is positioned. For if she is in that very place, or in those signs in which she is exalted, or in the principal **angles**, or in the fifth or eleventh place from the **ascendant**, and is full of light <note>a Full Moon</note>, and it is a nighttime birth, and **benefic stars** look upon her with a prosperous radiation, and she is separated from all associations with **malefic stars**, it will make the father famous, clear, wealthy, and one to whom inheritance and dignity are always granted. If however the **Moon** ☽ is in dejected places, or in the secondary angles <note>the "succedent" houses</note>, or in her humilities, and she is destitute of the protection of benefic stars, and a ray of a malefic star attacks her, and it is a daytime birth, or she is diminished in light, and **Saturn** ♄ regards her, or a strong **Mars** ♂, all things we said before are for the most part diminished, and the father becomes either an exile or a **violent death** <term>biothanatus; a Greek term for one who dies by execution, suicide, or accident</term>, not knowing the right path of life due to errant character. But in this matter, as we said before, you must always inspect with diligent reason the mixtures, concessions, and radiations of all stars, so that with all things mixed and composed by a wise conjunction of tempering, you may be able to explain the **Place of the Father** with true judgments. Also search for the father himself diligently, and see who is the lord of the father and where he is positioned: for he himself by his nature colors the place. You must also observe this method of **predictions** <note>original: "apotelesmatum"</note> in the following places. For in the **Place of the Mother**, and brothers, and wife, and children, and of health and vices, you must temper everything with very frequent radiations: so that having looked through the radiation of all stars, and having gathered the power of places and signs, and also of the **bounds** <note>original: "finium"; the Egyptian Terms/Bounds are subdivisions of signs</note>, you may be able to explain everything with true judgments. However, although we may gather places for others according to these same predictions, generally in birth charts the **Sun** ☉ is placed for the father's location: but we find it better by the **degree-based method** <note>original: "partiliter"; calculating the exact degree of a Lot rather than just using a general planet</note>.

<margin>The Place of the Mother.</margin>
If you wish to calculate the **Place of the Mother** by the degree-based method, and it is a daytime birth, beginning from the degree of **Venus** ♀ and proceeding through the following signs, count all the degrees up to the **Moon** ☽: and when the sum of all degrees is collected, beginning from the **ascendant**, divide them all by thirty among the following signs: and in whichever sign the final degree comes to, this sign will show you the **Place of the Mother** in a daytime birth. If however it is a nighttime birth, beginning from the degree of the **Moon** ☽, collect up to the degrees of **Venus** ♀, and you shall perform the rest by a similar method. When you have thus gathered this place by the degree-based method, you shall investigate everything just as we said you ought to investigate in the **Place of the Father**, namely the rays of benefics and malefics, the powers of places and signs, and also the mixtures and temperings of the rays: which when you have compared with an equal balance, you will be able to explain the **Place of the Mother** with true judgments.

...determined. If, however, it is a nocturnal **birth chart** <note>genitura</note>, you will calculate the total number of degrees from **Jupiter** ♃ to **Saturn** ♄ in a similar manner; and starting thus from the **ascendant** <note>horoscopus</note>, you will complete the calculation by the same method. When you have gathered this **Place of the Brothers** <term>locus fratrum; a mathematical point (Lot) in the chart representing siblings</term> by precise degree, examine this same place to see how the **malefic** and **benefic** stars <term>benefics are helpful planets (Jupiter, Venus); malefics are challenging ones (Saturn, Mars)</term> regard it. Observe also the power of the sign, and in what place of the birth chart this sign appears to be positioned. For if benefic stars are found either in that sign itself, or are established in favorable places of the birth chart, and are located in those signs in which they **rejoice**, or in which they are **exalted**, or in their own **domiciles** <term>specific signs where a planet is most powerful or "at home"</term>, they decree a companion of many and good brothers. But if malefic stars do the same, destitute of the testimony of benefic stars, they do the opposite. If, however, benefic and malefic stars regard this same place with an equal share of power, they both give brothers and take them away. But you shall treat all things according to the types of the stars: for masculine benefic stars will give males, but feminine benefics will give females. The malefic stars also perform the same role. And thus all things are fulfilled according to the power of the individual stars. But generally, as we said in the *Book of Instruction* <note>Referring to an earlier part of this work or a basic manual</term>, the third place from the **ascendant** shows the brothers; however, let us seek it specifically by degree.

<margin>
Hermes, according to Alcabitius <note>Al-Qabisi, a 10th-century astrologer</note>, took the Lot of Marriage in a woman’s birth chart from **Saturn** ♄ to **Venus** ♀, by day and night. It appears that the Lot of Marriage is taken from **Saturn** ♄ to **Venus** ♀ from the saying of Hermes, which Hali <note>Ali ibn Ridwan</note> approves in Book 5, Chapter 6; otherwise it would be different. So also Alcabitius, in the fifth distinction concerning the Lots.

If you wish to find the **Place of the Spouse** <note>locus coniugis</note> specifically by degree, calculate from the degree of **Saturn** ♄ to the degree of **Venus** ♀; and whatever total that calculation makes, starting from the **ascendant**, divide it through the following signs. In whatever sign you find the final degree, this will show you the **Place of the Spouse** in a diurnal birth chart. In a nocturnal birth chart, however, you will calculate starting from **Venus** ♀ to **Saturn** ♄, and similarly divide the gathered number of degrees starting from the **ascendant**; in whatever sign the final degree falls, this will show you the **Place of the Spouse** in a nocturnal birth chart. Others calculate from the **Sun** ☉ to **Venus** ♀ in both diurnal and nocturnal charts, and count the same distance from the **ascendant**, calculating similarly for both male and female birth charts; and we have also proven this in many nativities. Therefore, when you have gathered the **Place of the Spouse** by the method we have described, first look at the power of the sign—whether it is **fixed**, **double-bodied**, or **cardinal** <note>original: "solidum, duplex, tropicum"</note>. In the second order, you will seek where the lord of that sign is positioned in the birth chart. Third, you will seek this second place, in which the **lord of the terms** <term>fines; specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term> is located, to see how the benefic or malefic stars regard it. For when benefic stars possess the same sign in which the **Place of the Spouse** was found, being positioned in favorable places of the birth chart and dejected by no lowliness, but following the power of their own condition, they will give glorious and wealthy wives who are always joined by the bonds of harmony. But marriages of many wives are not decreed; for whatever wife they have obtained, the marriage lasts until the final day of life with great joy and charm. However, you can find the deaths of wives from the failing nature of the signs, and types of marriages from their differences. But if malefic stars do the same, all things become contrary to these. Then humble and inglorious wives are decreed; then also dissensions in marriages, then bitter types of grudges, then also the wretched turmoil of separations is perpetrated; then the spouses themselves are sterile, then they are adulteresses. But you will be able to explain all these things according to the powers of the stars. If, in a woman's birth chart,

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

<margin>This should be read as "of condition." For not only are the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> called "conditionary," but also the planets. This is what the Arabs call *Haiz*: that is, when a daytime planet is above the earth during the day, or a nighttime planet is below the earth at night.</margin>

If, however, they are found in the same degrees, you shall begin from the one whose minutes precede the other. But if they are in the exact same minutes, then skip this and calculate from **Venus** ♀ to **Mars** ♂ in a daytime birth, or in a nighttime birth from **Venus** ♀ to **Saturn** ♄, using the same logic. When you have gathered the **Place of Children** <term>locus filiorum; a mathematical point (Lot) representing offspring</term> by its exact degree, examine in the same way to what extent the benefic or malefic stars regard this place. You must also consider the **condition of the stars** <gloss>original: "condonationes stellarum"; referring to their placement and state</gloss> with the most diligent reasoning, as well as the nature and power of the sign. For if benefic stars regard this place while positioned in favorable areas of the birth chart and in "fecund" signs <note>Signs associated with fertility, like Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>, they decree children according to the power of those places and signs; but malefic stars do the opposite. Yet sometimes even the malefics themselves, if the birth occurs in their own **condition** <gloss>*</gloss> <note>referring to the Haiz mentioned in the margin</note>, may decree children: that is, **Saturn** ♄ in a daytime birth and **Mars** ♂ in a nighttime birth.

Children are decreed according to the nature of the signs. We ought to know, however, that if the **Place of Children** is found in a **double sign** <term>mutable signs like Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces, which have dual symbols</term>, children will come from two wives. If it is a **solid sign** <term>fixed signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</term>, the man will have children by one wife and the woman by one husband. If malefic and benefic stars regard the **Place of Children** with equal power, they both give offspring and take them away. Or, if the power of the benefic stars is overcome by the hostile rays of malefic stars, a certain weakness will be brought upon the children born, or surely the children will be separated from their parents by a great feud. In this place, as in all others, you should perceive the mixtures and temperaments of the stars with diligent reasoning, as well as the nature of the signs and the specific powers of the "places" <note>houses</note> following from the **ascendant** <note>horoscopus</note>. But generally, the **fifth house** <note>quinta sedes</note> reveals the place of children, along with the lordship and nature of that sign and the testimonies of the benefic or malefic stars.

If you wish to find the **Place of Defects and Health** <term>locus vitiorum ac valetudinis; a Lot indicating physical ailments or chronic conditions</term> by precise degree, in a daytime birth you shall calculate starting from **Saturn** ♄ to **Mars** ♂, and add an equal amount from the **ascendant**; in a nighttime birth, start from **Mars** ♂ to **Saturn** ♄, and add the same from the **ascendant**. In whichever sign the final number of collected degrees falls, this sign will show you the **Place of Defects and Health**. Generally, however, the **sixth sign** from the **ascendant** indicates the point of destruction. You shall define a defect or illness primarily from the nature of the sign. In our *Book of Instruction* <note>a reference to an earlier part of the Mathesis</note>, we described which parts of the body each individual sign governs.

Secondly, you shall observe to what extent the benefic and malefic stars regard this same place. For if they regard this place with a favorable aspect while positioned in their own houses or in their **exaltations** <term>the sign where a planet's influence is most intense</term>, they will free the person from every onset of illness. But if malefic stars regard this place with a threatening aspect, they decree bitter defects of illness with wretched calamity; they perform these things according to the nature of the signs and their own power. For **Mars** ♂ decrees blows, minor bodily wounds, falls, collapses, and deaths from the accidents of these wretched wounds. **Saturn** ♄ decrees the onset of pestilential fluids, spasms, tremors, dimness of sight, and wretched dangers from water, and other things similar to these. But if, while the malefic stars are decreeing these things, the ray of a benefic star intervenes, all these evils are mitigated. If, however, this place is occupied by malefics and left naked of any protection from benefic stars, perpetual defects of health and fatal outcomes of calamities are decreed. Furthermore, **Mars** ♂ will cause harm within fifteen years, **Saturn** ♄ within thirty, and the **Sun** ☉ within nineteen. If there are two planets together that cause harm, once the years of each defined time are calculated, both stars will decree an onset of the expected defect or illness at both times, according to their own nature.

If you wish to find the **Place of Desire** <term>locus cupidinis; often associated with the Lot of Eros</term> by precise degree, in a daytime birth you shall calculate from the **Lot of Spirit** <note>original: "parte dæmonis"</note> to the **Lot of Fortune**, and add an equal amount from the **ascendant**. In a nighttime birth, calculate from Fortune to Spirit, using the same logic, and add the same from the **ascendant**. When you have gathered this place by precise degree, all your longing for desires will be demonstrated by the sign and the testimonies of the stars. In the fourth book, we explained the method by which you may find the **Lot of Fortune** and the **Lot of Spirit**.

If you wish to find the **Place of Necessity** <term>locus necessitatis; a Lot associated with constraints and compulsions</term> by precise degree, in a daytime birth you shall calculate from Fortune to Spirit. In a nighttime birth, calculate from Spirit to Fortune, and add the same amount from the **ascendant**. When you have gathered this same place by this method, you shall define everything regarding that place according to the quality of the signs and stars.

If you wish to calculate the **Place of Honors** by precise degree, you shall always calculate from the tenth [house]...

...you will calculate <note>original: "computabis"</note> to the **Sun** ☉, and the same distance from the **horoscope** <term>horoscopus; the Ascendant or rising sign</term>; and whichever sign receives the final part, this will show you the insignia of honors, both from its own nature and from the accidental testimonies of all the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Place of Military Service** <term>locus militiae</term> by a proportional calculation, you will always calculate from **Mars** ♂ to the **Sun** ☉, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part falls, this shows you the outcome of military service according to its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to find the **Place of Foreign Travel** <term>locus peregrinationis</term> by its parts, you will always calculate from the **Sun** ☉ to **Mars** ♂, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part falls, this will show the outcome of the journey according to its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Reputation of Fame** <term>fama existimationis</term> by a proportional calculation, you will calculate from the **Sun** ☉ to **Mercury** ☿, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part falls, this will show the fame of your reputation according to its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to find the **Virtue of the Body** <term>virtus corporis</term> by its parts, you will calculate from the **Sun** ☉ to **Jupiter** ♃, and the same distance from the horoscope, and handle the rest by a similar method. For all things will show their decrees to you according to the nature of the signs and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Substance of Possessions** <term>substantia possessionum</term> by a proportional calculation, you will always calculate from **Mercury** ☿ to **Jupiter** ♃, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part falls, you will find the order of possessions from the nature of the sign itself and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Place of Accusation** <term>locus accusationis</term> by a proportional calculation, you will always calculate from **Mars** ♂ to **Saturn** ♄, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part falls, this will show you the outcome of the accusation according to its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Place of Adversaries and Enemies** <term>locus adversariorum et inimicorum</term> by a proportional calculation, during the day you will calculate from the **Sun** ☉ to **Mercury** ☿, but by night conversely from **Mercury** ☿ back to the **Sun** ☉, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part comes, this shows the enemies from its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

If you wish to gather the **Place of Friends** <term>locus amicorum</term> by a proportional calculation, during the day you will calculate from **Jupiter** ♃ to **Mars** ♂, but by night from **Mars** ♂ to **Jupiter** ♃, and the same distance from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the final part comes, this will show you the friends you seek by a most true calculation from its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

The **Place of Glory** <term>locus gloriae</term>, by night from **Venus** ♀ to **Saturn** ♄, but by day the opposite. **Nemesis** <note>The Lot of Retribution</note>, by night from **Fortune** <note>The Lot of Fortune</note> to the **Moon** ☽, but by day the opposite. **Power**, by night from **Saturn** ♄ to the **Sun** ☉, but by day the opposite.

**The Basis** <term>basis; the Lot of the Foundation</term>, by night from **Fortune** to **Spirit** <term>genium; the Lot of Spirit or Daemon</term>, but by day the opposite. But if **Venus** ♀ has reached thirty parts <note>degrees</note>, whether by night or by day, you shall calculate proportionally from Spirit to Fortune.

If you wish to gather the **Place of Servants** <term>locus servorum</term> by a proportional calculation, you will always calculate from **Mercury** ☿ to the **Moon** ☽, and finally from the horoscope; and in whichever sign the last part comes, this will demonstrate the service to you according to its nature and the testimonies of the stars.

### THE DIVISION OF TIME 
### owed to the Chronocrator. Chapter XXXIII.

We have begun to disclose to you, **Mavortius** <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom this work is dedicated</note>, all the secrets of astrology <term>mathesis; the sacred mathematical science of the stars</term> with the truest sentences of definitions: but the seventh book will show you a most full treatment of all these things, so that you may find everything without any difficulty through the easiest and truest inquiries. To the completion of this book, however, this shall be added: that I demonstrate to you which star, when it is the **Lord of Times** <term>chronocrator; Greek for "time-ruler"</term>, and has divided the whole substance of ten years and nine months for itself and the other stars, decrees what thing and by what reasoning. How the Lord of Times is found, whom the Greeks call the **Chronocrator** <note>original: "χρονοκράτορα"</note>, we have shown by clear reasoning in the *Book of Instruction* <note>likely referring to an earlier book of this same work or a foundational text used by Firmicus</note>: inquire into this matter diligently, so that you may be able to have the outcomes and orders of all dangers explored.

### THE DECREES OF SATURN, WHEN HE IS THE
### Lord of Times. Chapter XXXIIII.

If **Saturn** ♄ has been made the **Lord of Times**, he claims for you thirty months from the whole time, as we taught in the *Book of Instruction*. Look, therefore, to how he is positioned in the birth chart <term>genitura</term>, and whether it is a daytime birth or a nighttime birth, and whether he holds the **angles** <term>cardines; the four pivotal points of the chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</term>, and what he decrees from the nature of the sign or the power of the place: when you have gathered all these things with diligent reasoning, then you will find what he does when he is the Lord of Times.
