# THE MATHEMATICS OF JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS THE YOUNGER,
# OF SICILY, OF SENATORIAL RANK <note>original: V. C.; Vir Clarissimus, a title for the highest senatorial class</note>, TO MAVORTIUS
# Lollianus, Proconsul, Book VIII.

->PREFACE.<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'N' featuring a detailed landscape with a town in the background and a figure in the foreground.</image-desc>While we exist in this brevity of life, Mavortius our glory, we must strive for nothing else except that—once the stain of the earthly body is purged and all vices (if possible) or at least most of them are cut away—we may return the incorrupt divinity of the soul, unpolluted by any contagion of crimes, to God our creator. We must not lose the soul, unmindful of its divine craftsmanship and entangled in the vicious snares of lusts, as if it were cast down headlong. For this is what the earthly body works toward every single day: namely, that it might always bind its divine spirit—captured by the depraved pleasures of desires and deceived by flattering solicitation—to its own fleeting fragility, so that the soul, submerged and sunk down, can never find the beginnings of its origin; but always cast into darkness and filth, it blushes at the origin of its majesty with certain tremblings of denial. For we ought to think of nothing earthly, especially since we know that God our maker made us with such moderation of divine craftsmanship that the form of an upright body, set apart from all lowly dejection, would see nothing first, once the sight of the eyes was opened, except the **Sun ☉** and **Moon ☾**, the stars, and the most beautiful and immortal domicile of all these: namely, the universe <note>original: mundum; the cosmos</note>.

For nature composed other living creatures in such a way that, sunk toward the earth and cast down by a certain fleeting lowliness of this world, they would always adhere to earthly dealings in both soul and body. But us, it perfected with a great moderation of necessity, so that the fragility of the body might claim one thing for itself in us, and the divinity of the immortal soul another; namely, that the body, which we seem to have in common with beasts, serving the soul, might be subject to the command of its divinity. Considering therefore the beginnings of our origin, and our soul strengthened by the protection of its own majesty, we ought to so establish ourselves that the soul, convened by the authority of its own divinity through itself, may always both think and do something worthy of its author; so that thus established and formed, it may find the straight and incorrupt path of immortality when it is to return to its origin, and not—with wandering steps and slipping, trembling tracks—be dissolved back into the vices of earthly fragility through eternal errors.

Look therefore, Mavortius our glory, upon the heavens with open eyes, and let your soul always gaze upon that most beautiful structure of divine work. For then our mind, formed by the recollection of its own majesty, is liberated from the depraved allurements of bodies; and stripped of the inconveniences of mortality, it hastens with a quickened step toward its creator, seeking nothing else through every moment of the hours but divine matters, through wise and ever-vigilant inquiry. These institutions will therefore give us whatever small notion of divine science we can grasp and will lead us to the secrets of our origin. For by always being occupied with divine disputations, and applying our soul to the celestial powers and initiating it into divine ceremonies, we are separated from the desires of all depraved lusts. This practice greatly ensures that—having despised everything in human affairs that is thought to be either evil or prosperous—we may return our soul, composed by its natural virtue and authority, incorrupt and untainted to its origin. For when we have learned of incoming hardships, the fear of evils is diminished by the very fact that they...

<header>JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS</header>

...the things that are to come, we have learned to look down upon them with an upright and spirited mind. We do not shrink from the announced dangers of misfortunes if our soul has strengthened itself through the remembrance of its own majesty. Nor are we captivated by the comforts of good fortune, or puffed up by the honors of high rank, once we know that all of this has been promised to us by the pronouncement of the decree <note>The "decree" refers to the fixed fate determined by the stars at birth</note>. In this way, we can always remain composed with stable reason, neither crushed by misfortunes nor uplifted by the joy of success. 

Therefore, what I believe remains for these books, I shall take care to explain here. For I have reserved another time for the explanation of the *myriogenesis* <term>original: "myriogonesin"; a Greek term referring to the "thousandfold" or minute subdivisions of the zodiac degrees</term>. But now, in the opening of this book, we will set forth which signs see each other; for all of this will pertain to the interpretation of the **Barbarian Sphere** <note>The "Sphaera Barbarica" refers to an ancient tradition of constellations and degree-meanings attributed to non-Greek sources, such as the Egyptians, Babylonians, or Persians</note>. We shall also state the measurements of all the parts; we will add which parts are found in the bodies of the signs; and also what the ninetieth part effects, which is called <term>ennenēkontameros</term> by the Greeks. Thus, once everything is explained, we may more easily grasp the Barbarian Sphere, and perceive the power of the effective license of the bright stars.

### <term>Ennenēkontameros</term> <note>original Greek: Εννενηκοντάμερος</note>, OR THE NINETIETH PART. Chapter I.

First, therefore, I will discuss the ninetieth part, which is called <term>ennenēkontameros</term> by the Greeks. This matter seems to be unknown to most and treated lightly by only a few. For even **Petosiris** <note>A legendary Egyptian priest-astrologer whose works formed the foundation of much of Hellenistic astrology</note>, as it seems to me, wished to hide this treatise out of envious spite. For in all nativities <note>original: "genituris"; a birth chart or the moment of birth</note>, the ninetieth part must be sought out with wise investigation. From it, the end of life, death, misfortunes, dangers, successes, and the entire substance of the nativity are gathered. 

Starting from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "horoscopo"; the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, look for the ninetieth part through the following signs. When you have found it, observe which sign it is in: that is, whether it is found in the domicile of a benevolent or malevolent star. See also how the ruler of that sign is positioned in the nativity. Observe carefully to what extent the benevolent stars look upon <note>aspect</note> that part. For each star looking at this part brings things to completion according to its own nature. For malevolent stars <note>typically Saturn and Mars</note>, if they are alone, will bring ruin; if benevolent <note>typically Jupiter and Venus</note>, they decree the greatest signs of happiness. But if both benevolent and malevolent stars are present, the result is tempered by what is drawn from each. 

Seek also in whose lordship and power the part itself lies—that is, in whose **bounds** <note>original: "finibus"; specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</note> it is—and similarly where the ruler of that part is positioned; thus you will complete everything based on the nature of the star and the power of its location. For all things, both bad and prosperous, are completed by the nature of the sign. You should seek this same thing similarly from the **Moon ☽** and from the progression from that part where the Moon is found, so that you may have the 90th part. Collect everything in this part by similar reasoning: what sign it is, what part it is, who is the ruler of the sign and the part, where the rulers are located, and in which signs they are placed, and by what radiation <note>astrological aspect</note> both benevolent and malevolent stars look upon the part itself. 

And if the Moon ☽ is waxing, see to what extent **Mars ♂** looks toward this part; and if it is waning, do the same. For all stars bring things to completion according to the power of their own nature, whether malevolent stars look upon the 90th part with a threatening radiation, or benevolent stars support it with a prosperous testimony. For thus you will find the end of death, the order of life, and finally the entire substance of a human nativity.

### BOOK EIGHT. The Theory of Stars that See and Hear Each Other. Chapter II.

Now I will briefly explain which stars see others, and which hear others. **Aries** ♈ does not see **Leo** ♌, but hears him; but **Leo** sees **Aries**, but does not hear him. **Aries** both sees and hears **Cancer** ♋; but **Cancer** does not see **Aries**, but hears him. **Taurus** ♉ and **Leo** ♌ see and hear each other equally, and similarly **Leo** sees and hears **Taurus**. **Gemini** ♊ see **Virgo** ♍ slightly and hear her; **Virgo** sees **Gemini** slightly, but hears them most fully. **Cancer** ♋ both sees and hears **Libra** ♎ equally. **Libra** ♎ neither sees nor hears **Scorpio** ♏; but **Scorpio** both hears and sees **Leo** ♌ equally. **Scorpio** ♏ looks at **Sagittarius** ♐ from an angle <note>original: "ex obliquo"; referring to a non-standard aspect</note>, but does not listen to him willingly; **Sagittarius** ♐ both hears and sees **Virgo** ♍ equally, as well as **Libra** ♎, and he is both heard and seen by **Scorpio** ♏. **Scorpio** ♏ does not see, but hears himself <note>This likely refers to a relationship with another sign or a self-reflective property in the original table</note>; in the same way, **Scorpio** does not see, but hears **Pisces** ♓ and **Aquarius** ♒. **Sagittarius** ♐ neither sees nor hears. **Pisces** ♓, however, both see and hear equally. **Pisces** ♓ do not see **Gemini** ♊, but hear them. **Capricorn** ♑ and **Taurus** ♉ neither hear nor see each other; **Aquarius** ♒ and **Taurus** ♉ look at each other from an angle and hear each other. **Gemini** ♊ and **Libra** ♎ see and hear each other equally. Similarly, **Libra** ♎ both hears and sees **Gemini** ♊ equally. **Sagittarius** ♐ and **Leo** ♌ both see and hear each other equally. **Virgo** ♍ indeed looks at **Capricorn** ♑, but does not hear him. **Libra** ♎ sees **Aquarius** ♒, but she herself is not seen by **Aquarius**; nevertheless, they hear each other mutually and equally. **Scorpio** ♏ indeed sees **Pisces** ♓, but does not hear them; **Pisces** similarly see **Scorpio**, but do not hear him; **Sagittarius** ♐ and **Aries** ♈ are so positioned that they neither see each other, nor are they able to hear; **Capricorn** ♑ and **Taurus** ♉ can neither hear nor see each other. **Aquarius** ♒ and **Gemini** ♊ indeed see each other, but are entirely separated in hearing. **Pisces** ♓ and **Cancer** ♋ do not indeed see each other, but they do hear. So that you might receive the complete forms of the arrangement, and know how the signs are disposed in the zodiac circle, we have for this reason treated the secrets of this matter; for these twelve signs are not placed in a fixed order and degree, nor are they positioned so that those which rise in a later place always look upon the preceding or following signs. For, so that I might show this to you not by arguments but by the reality itself, we have published this treatise, excerpted from the books of **Abraham** <note>This "Abraham" likely refers to a legendary ancient sage or a specific Hermetic source attributed to the biblical patriarch, who was often considered the inventor of astrology in Hellenistic traditions</note>, so that our discourse might make known to you through clear interpretations those things which we have said.

### THE PARTS OF THE SIGNS DIVIDED BY THEIR LIMBS. Chapter III.

Now I will take care to explain to you which parts <note>The "parts" refer to the 30 degrees of each zodiac sign</note> you should seek in which parts of the signs. For all thirty parts are divided through all the bodies of the signs. So that you may know where the first part is, where the second, and where the rest, I will demonstrate all of this to you in a brief order of speech.

<meta>This page continues Julius Firmicus Maternus's "Mathesis," specifically Book VIII. Having previously discussed the relationships between the signs (who "sees" or "hears" whom), he now moves into a highly detailed anatomical breakdown of the zodiac. He assigns each of the 30 degrees (parts) of a sign to a specific part of that constellation's "body." This technique was used in ancient medical astrology to pinpoint where an affliction might manifest based on the degree of a planet.</meta>

<page-num>214</page-num>

->JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS<-

In **Aries** ♈, the first and second degrees are located in the horns; the third, fourth, and fifth are in the head; the sixth and seventh in the face; the eighth, ninth, and tenth in the mouth; the eleventh and twelfth in the chest; the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth in the whole neck; the sixteenth and seventeenth in the heart; the eighteenth and nineteenth in the right shoulder; the twentieth, twenty-first, and twenty-second in the left shoulder; in the belly, however, are the twenty-third, twenty-fourth, and twenty-fifth; the last feet have the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh degrees. In the kidneys are the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and the thirtieth degree is in the tail. And thus, these thirty degrees are divided throughout the whole body of **Aries** in such an order.

In **Taurus** ♉, the first and second degrees are located in the horns; the third, fourth, and fifth in the whole face; the sixth and seventh in the neck; the eighth, ninth, and tenth in the forehead; the eleventh and twelfth in the heart; the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth in the shoulders; the sixteenth and seventeenth in the front feet; the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth in the belly; the twenty-first in the knees; the twenty-second, twenty-third, twenty-fourth, and twenty-fifth in the hind feet; the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh in the genitals <note>original: "natura"; a common euphemism in Latin technical texts for reproductive organs</note>; the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth in the hips; and the thirtieth is found in the tail. Thus the number of degrees is divided through the whole body of **Taurus**, although the <term>Barbarian Sphere</term> <note>The "Barbarian Sphere" refers to non-Greek astrological traditions, likely Egyptian or Babylonian, which Firmicus often cites as an ancient authority.</note> maintains a different order of parts.

In **Gemini** ♊, the first and second degrees are located in that part of the Twin which turns toward the North; the third, fourth, and fifth are in the heart of the same Twin; the sixth and seventh in the shoulders; the eighth, ninth, and tenth in the chest; the eleventh and twelfth in the hands; and the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth in the feet. In that Twin which turns toward the South, we find these parts: but first we ought to know that the space between both Twins contains the sixteenth and seventeenth degrees. The eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth degrees are placed in the head of the Southern Twin; in the face are the twenty-first and twenty-second; in the chest the twenty-third and twenty-fourth; under the belly the twenty-fifth and twenty-sixth; in the knees the twenty-seventh, twenty-eighth, and twenty-ninth. In the feet alone is the thirtieth degree placed.

In **Cancer** ♋, the first and second degrees are placed in the head; the third, fourth, and fifth in the neck; and in the throat are the sixth and seventh. We find the three following degrees in the eyes—here is the <term>Cloud of Cancer</term> <note>original: "nebula Cancer"; referring to the star cluster now known as Praesepe or the "Manger," which appears as a cloudy patch to the naked eye.</note> of which we have frequently spoken; the eleventh and twelfth are in the back; the three following stretch from the stomach to the pubic area; the sixteenth and seventeenth are located in the sides; the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth in the front claws; the twenty-first and twenty-second in the hind claws; the three following are placed in the right feet of **Cancer**, and the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh in the left. In the tips of the feet are the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and in the tail is the thirtieth alone.

In **Leo** ♌, the first and second degrees are placed in the head; the three following are in the whole face as well as in the mane; the next three are in the mouth; just as many are in the heart; two are in the shoulders; four are in the feet; the two following are in the belly; and the twentieth, twenty-first, and twenty-second are in the back. In the pubic area are the twenty-third and twenty-fourth; the next three are in the knees; the twenty-eighth is in the genitals; the twenty-ninth in the kidneys; and the thirtieth alone is found in the tail.

In **Virgo** ♍, the first and second degrees are placed in the head; the three following in the face; the sixth and seventh in the hands; the next seven follow in order through the chest; the fifteenth, sixteenth, and seventeenth are in the right breast; the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth are located in the left; the twenty-first and twenty-second are placed in the belly; the next three are placed in the right foot; the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh in the left. In the kidneys are the twenty-eighth and twenty-ninth, and in the "natural body" <note>Another euphemism for the genitals.</note> the thirtieth alone is placed.

In **Libra** ♎, the first and second degrees are placed in the head; the third, fourth, and fifth in the left part of the balance; the sixth and seventh in the right; the eighth, ninth, and tenth are said to be located in the head <note>Firmicus or the manuscript may be repeating the head here, or referring to a figure holding the scales.</note>; the eleventh and twelfth in the left part of the yoke; the three following in the right; the sixteenth and seventeenth in the heart of **Libra**; and the four following in order in the right hand of **Libra**; the twenty-second and twenty-third in the chest. In the kidneys are the three following; the twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth stretch down to the extremities of the feet. The remaining numbers are placed up to the thirtieth. For in these latter parts, the earth is said to be composed, as the Barbarian system confirms.

In **Scorpio** ♏, the first and second degrees are placed in the head; the three following in the forehead; the sixth and seventh in the face; the next three are placed in order in the neck; the two that follow are placed in the back; and the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth in the belly.

In the right hand, the next three degrees are placed in order, and two in the left; in the right feet, the following two are arranged, and three in the left. In the sting, which extends toward the north, the last five are placed; and thus they are divided among the limbs <note>This paragraph completes the description of Scorpio, begun on the previous page.</note>.

♐ The first and second parts <note>The author uses "parts" and "degrees" interchangeably to refer to the 30 divisions of a zodiac sign.</note> are located in the head; the three following in order are in the face; the two that follow the preceding parts are placed in the mouth of **Sagittarius**; the next three are in the neck, the two succeeding in the left hand, three others in the bow, two in the front feet, three in the back, and two in the horse's belly <note>Sagittarius is depicted as a centaur, half-man and half-horse.</note>. Women also, if they have the Moon ☽ in these parts, will all be possessed by the vice of shameless desire. The 11th is located in the heart of **Capricorn**; the 12th and 13th in the neck; the next two in the shoulder blades; the three succeeding in the right hand; the two that follow in the back; the next three in the belly; the four that succeed on either side; and the last three are located in the tail, as far as the tip of **Capricorn's** fin <note>Capricorn is a "Sea-Goat," possessing the upper body of a goat and the tail of a fish.</note>.

♓ One of which turns toward the South, the other toward the North; the first and second parts are located in the mouth of the Southern **Fish**; the 3rd, 4th, and 5th in the head of the same **Fish**; two in the throat; the next three in order are placed in the neck; the 11th and 12th are found in the tip of the spine; and the three that follow in order will be taken by the back of the same **Fish**. But the three last parts of **Pisces**, which are between **Aries** ♈ and **Pisces** ♓, are always clouded by a dark mist; for this reason, if anyone has either the Sun ☉ or Moon ☽ in these parts without the testimony of benevolent stars, they will be oppressed either by perpetual blindness or by wretched bodily infirmities. Therefore, from this division of parts, when you begin to seek the location of vices and health, you will be able to find all of this most clearly and easily. For that divine Necepso <note>An 2nd-century BCE Egyptian king and priest to whom many foundational astrological texts were attributed.</note>, in order to find the remedies for illnesses, explained this topic with manifest treatises, most diligently indeed, as the divine genius of such a great man was able. I shall take care to impart the interpretation of this book to you at another time, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom Firmicus dedicated this work.</note>, our glory.

### THE DIMENSION AND MAGNITUDE
#### of the signs and their parts. Chapter IV.

Now I shall briefly explain to you the measures of the individual parts, so that from this interpretation you may be able to find the entire measurement of the Zodiac circle. I shall also explain the measurement and magnitude of the signs to you, so that you may know how the intention of the divine mind approached all the secrets of divinity: which even the immortal soul, remembering the principles of its own majesty, did not learn, but recognized. For this is computed through the twelve signs: when you have done this, the entire measurement of the Zodiac circle is shown to you. One part <note>one degree</note> of a sign, therefore, has twenty-one thousand and forty stadia <note>A stadium was roughly 185 meters; this calculation reflects ancient Greek attempts to measure the circumference of the cosmos.</note>.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS, MATHEMATICIAN
## [Book 8]

...[If you] have [this number]. If you compute this number through thirty parts <note>The author refers to the 30 degrees that make up each zodiac sign.</note> together, you will know from this calculation that the space of a single sign occupies six hundred and forty-two thousand stadia <note>A stadium was a Greek unit of length, approximately 600 feet; Firmicus is calculating the physical "size" of the heavens.</note>.

# THE FIRST OUTCOMES OF THE BARBARIAN SPHERE
### Predictions. Chapter 5.

**Y**ou shall now receive, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman aristocrat to whom Firmicus dedicated this work.</note>, our glory, the fullest instruction of this work, unknown to many Greeks and nearly all Romans—a subject toward which our intellect has aspired even to this present day. For even those divine men and high priests of the most holy religion, Petosiris and Necepso—one of whom held the rudders of imperial power <note>referring to the legendary Pharaoh Necepso</note>—though they explained everything pertaining to the instruction of this art with the most diligent and true interpretations, they were unable to discover that which we are about to publish. 

But lest a long-winded discourse extend our arrangement, I shall briefly intimate the decrees of the promised work to you. Twelve signs occupy the zodiacal circle, as we said in the book of the *Institution*. Alongside these signs, other stars are attached, but these are stars which never wander in an erratic course <note>i.e., fixed stars, as opposed to "wandering stars" or planets</note> from the places assigned to them; rather, possessing the spaces granted to them as the world turns, they are revolved in an always unchangeable motion. These, placed in the regions neighboring the signs, rise with the twelve signs and set with them, always preserving the unchangeable order of their course. 

Antiquity applied the names of ancient myths to these stars. Aratus, a most eloquent poet, also set forth the number of these constellations in Greek; in Latin, however, Caesar <note>referring to the translation by Germanicus Caesar</note> and that glory of eloquence, Tullius <note>Marcus Tullius Cicero</note>, did so. But these men published only their names and rising times, not the authority of their *predictions* <term>apotelefmata: the destined outcomes or effects of stars on human lives</term>. Thus, it seems to me they brought forth their studies of learned speech not from any science of astrology, but rather elevated by poetic license. We, however, having examined the logic of all the predictions, have found that these stars also claim a great deal for themselves in the births of men. Therefore, so that we may explain what we promise, we shall designate both the locations and the names of the stars, so that the whole truth of the predictions may be gathered: which stars decide the fate if, being positioned at the morning rising, they hold the ascendant <note>original: "horosc."; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> or the setting.

# BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH ♈ ARIES
### Chapter 6.

**I**n the tenth degree of **Aries**, the Ship <note>the constellation Argo Navis</note> rises. If anyone is born when this part is rising—that is, if it breaks forth at his birth—he will be a pilot, a shipmaster, or a ship-owner, and one who chooses to involve the entire span of his life in marine acts or duties.

On the left side of **Aries**, specifically in the tenth degree, **Orion** rises. Therefore, if **Orion** is exactly on the ascendant, he will make men conspicuous for the swift mobility of their bodies, and whose minds, entangled in various anxieties, always seethe with wide-awake thinking. These men will frequently vary their dwellings and houses, and change their seats, and they will run through the thresholds of everyone <margin>Perhaps, "with dances."</margin> with always-constant morning salutations.

In the fifteenth degree of **Aries**, toward the north, the Charioteer <note>Auriga</note> rises. He who is born at the rising of this constellation will be either a charioteer, a tamer of horses, or one who leaps across four-horse chariots, or who, standing on the back of horses, supports himself with wonderful balance, and especially one who, carried on horseback, practices military maneuvers. At the rising of this star, Salmoneus and Bellerophon <note>Salmoneus was a king who imitated Zeus's lightning; Bellerophon was the hero who rode Pegasus.</note> are said by ancient authors to have been born.

In the twentieth degree of **Aries**, toward the north, the Kid <note>Haedus</note> rises, which the Charioteer carries. Whoever is born under this star promises one thing on the surface but hides another thing secretly in their character. They are of austere face, with a long beard and an unyielding brow, so that they seem to utterly imitate the institution of Cato <note>Cato the Elder, famous for his stern traditional morality</note>; but they feign all of this with a deceptive display. For they are by nature petulant, always entangled in the wanton desires of lust and libidinous pleasures, and who secretly always seethe with the allurements of love. They will also be separated from every duty of virtue, timid, weak, and those who shudder at every danger of battle. These men, moreover, frequently captured by lusts and occupied by the pursuit of perverted love <note>original: "praeposteri amoris"; often used for socially transgressive or obsessive lust</note>, are forced to bring death upon themselves. From this star also are born shepherds of sheep, but those who, playing upon the woodland pipe, give forth the sweetest melodies of rustic song.

# BOOK EIGHT

In the twenty-seventh degree of **Aries**, the **Hyades** <note>A cluster of stars in the constellation Taurus, traditionally associated with rain, but here linked to Aries via the "Barbarian Sphere" system.</note> rise. Whoever is born at the rising of this constellation will be restless, turbulent, and a man of the people—one who always incites the commoners to turbulent seditions, inflaming their minds with loud and furious contentions. He is an enemy of quiet and peace, desiring internal and domestic wars with a furious passion of the mind. Yet, from this constant agitation, various profits are born for him. For this constellation also produces cowherds, shepherds, herdsmen, and keepers of sheep.

In the thirtieth degree of **Aries**—the degree which always shows the whole sign above the earth—the **Goat** <note>The star Capella.</note> rises, which the fabled poets claim provided nourishment for the infant Jupiter. Whoever is born under this constellation will be anxious with excessive trembling of the mind, and their body will always be afflicted by a constant tremor. They will be overwhelmed by slight disturbances, and even by trivial news, they will be shaken by a heavy onset of fear. They will, however, be curious about all things; they are the sort who desire whatever new thing is said with impatient greed, always following every new curiosity with a longing desire and striving to understand them.

And because we have now said enough and more regarding what these stars do at their rising, we must speak in the following section about what they decree when positioned at their setting. For just as darkness is contrary to light, so is death to life. Life, therefore, shall be found in the rising, but death in the setting. Thus, if the rising is in the *horoscopus* <note>original: "horosc."; refers to the Ascendant, the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> (as we have frequently said), the setting will be at the diameter of the *horoscopus*—that is, in the seventh place from the *horoscopus* <note>The Descendant or the Western horizon, traditionally associated with death and endings.</note>.

<margin>The setting of the constellations under Aries.</margin>
Therefore, if the **Ship** <note>The constellation Argo Navis.</note> is exactly at the setting, and malefic stars <note>Specifically Saturn and Mars.</note> regard this place with an opposition <note>original: "diametra radiatione"</note> or a square aspect <note>original: "quadrata radiatione"</note>, the bitter hardships of shipwrecks are decreed. But if **Saturn** is placed in that star itself, they will perish by drowning in the sea or in rivers.

If **Orion** is found in the setting of the nativity <note>original: "geniturae"; the birth chart.</note>, such men will be born whose minds are always agitated by various anxieties. These men, sent on embassies by their fellow citizens and established in that very duty, will die abroad, bringing some small solace to the underworld in that it was given to them by their citizens. To them are also decreed perpetual honors, images, titles, and the insignia of honorable statues.

If the **Charioteer** <note>The constellation Auriga.</note> is found in the setting of the nativity, and the ray of malefic stars attacks it, they are thrown from four-horse chariots and scattered by wretched lacerations, so that with broken bodies, they suffer the bitter hardships of death; or, struck by lightning, they are overwhelmed by a sudden fall into death; or they are raised upon a cross; or their legs are broken by the public vengeance of judges. If the **Kid** of the Charioteer is found in the setting, and **Saturn** regards it with a square or opposing aspect, those born die at the very moment of life; or, placed in the very light of birth, they are strangled as the mother’s strength fails; or, with their throats swelling <note>Likely referring to a disease like croup or diphtheria.</note>, a bitter end of death is brought upon them. But if **Mars** is found with that star in the setting, and is destitute of all testimony from the beneficent stars, he will cause the newborns to be executed <note>original: "plecti"</note>, or to be sacrificed at an altar by the observances of a fearsome religion.

If the **Hyades** are found in the setting, and the ray of malefic stars attacks that place, a sudden and unexpected end of death is decreed. For, oppressed by turbulent seditions and scattered here and there by the hands of the mob, they will utterly perish, so that the authors of their death can neither be found at any time nor named.

If the **Goat** is found in the setting, they will have the means of substance from estates; but these people, on account of violated religious rites, will be struck by heavy envy. They will also have substance either collected from shipwrecks or acquired from rivers.

But if benevolent stars together with malevolent ones aspect this same place with equal radiation, a pleasant death will come to them without any lamentation, occurring during feasts and drinking bouts, either from the pleasures of Venus <note>Meaning sexual activity.</note> or from excessive food.

If the Horoscope <note>The Ascendant.</note> is in the fixing of the hoof of **Taurus**, and the Moon aspects this same place—or if benevolent and malevolent stars aspect it together with equal radiation—it makes a painter, but one whom this study ennobles with celebrated honor. If indeed, without the testimony of benevolents, the malevolent stars alone aspect this place with a threatening radiation, famous gladiators will be born; those who, after many palms and innumerable victories in that study of fighting, die with an intrepid heart by a threatening and drawn sword, even amid the great applause and favor of the spectators.

If the setting is found in the fixing of the hoof of **Taurus**, whether benevolent or malevolent stars aspect it, those born under this constellation will labor under the tension of violent lust, not without danger.

## BRIGHT STARS RISING AND
## SETTING WITH GEMINI. Chapter VIII.

<margin>The Hare.</margin>
In the seventh part of **Gemini**, the **Hare** rises. Those born under this constellation will be of such lightness of body that when they begin to run, agitated by their own velocity, they will seem to surpass the birds. If Mars aspects this place, he makes <term>stadiodromotos</term> <note>Original Greek: "stadiodromoi," meaning stadium runners or sprinters.</note>. If indeed the Moon is with Mars, he makes <term>pictomacharios</term> <note>Original Greek: "pyktomachoi," meaning specialized arena fighters or boxers.</note>. If Mercury, illusionists or ball players; if Venus, pantomimes or mimes. If Venus and Mercury together, they become perfectors of new arts with a study of excessive diligence, especially if the testimony of Jupiter's radiation assists them in all these <term>apoteλesmatis</term> <note>Original Greek: "apotelesmata," meaning the completed results or astrological effects.</note> we have mentioned. But if Saturn sees this place by a square or diameter aspect, he will make fugitives who, moving to distant regions, will separate their homes with a headlong study of animosity, and be divided from their own people.

If the **Hare** is found at the setting, and it has the testimony of benevolent and malevolent stars together, as we said in the preceding results, they will seek the supports of life with great labor. But if only the testimony of malevolent stars is added, they will die entirely consumed and torn apart by wild beasts.

## SETTING WITH CANCER. Chapter IX.

<margin>The Little Asses.</margin>
In the first part of **Cancer**, the **Little Asses** <note>Aselli, two stars in the constellation Cancer (Gamma and Delta Cancri).</note> rise; at whose rising, whoever is born will be indeed irreligious and treacherous, but devoted to every study of hunting. He will catch wild beasts with nets, or deceive them with pits, or pursue them with iron and various accidents; or with dogs, for the sake of catching wild beasts, he will search the secrets of the forests. But even if a woman is born thus, with the spirit of a virago <note>A woman exhibiting masculine strength or spirit.</note>, she will pursue these same things by similar means. But he will do these things if the Moon with benevolent stars aspects this same place by any radiation. If the Sun does the same, they will be devoted to every study of fishing, so that they even catch sea monsters with exquisite fishing methods.

<margin>Argion</margin>
In the twentieth degree of Cancer, **Argion** <note>Likely referring to Procyon in the constellation Canis Minor, or a star in the constellation Argo.</note> rises. When this is rising, those who are born will be entirely removed from the pursuit of hunting; instead, they will either manufacture or prepare weapons for hunters, such as nets, hunting spears, arrows, and whatever pertains to the equipment of that pursuit. They will also breed dogs to track the lairs of wild beasts and hidden coverts with their prophetic nostrils, as well as all animals that serve the purpose of the hunt.

But if this star is found at the setting, and Mars <note>Original: "♂"</note> should aspect this place in a square or diameter radiation <note>A "square" is a 90-degree aspect, "diameter" or "opposition" is 180 degrees; both are considered difficult or "hard" aspects in astrology.</note>, and it is deprived of the favorable testimony of Jupiter <note>Original: "♃"</note>, they will perish torn by the bite of a rabid dog, suffering from a similar madness of fury: specifically, they will avoid the sight of water and shudder at every draft from a cup, so much so that with parched throats they even fear to desire the water itself <note>A vivid historical description of hydrophobia, or rabies.</note>. Or certainly, while laying snares for wild beasts of the forest, they will be torn apart and destroyed by their bites.

## BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH LEO.
## Chapter 10.

<margin>The Dog Star</margin>
**IN** the first degree of Leo, the **Dog Star** <note>Original: "Canicula."</note> rises, which is called *Sirius* <note>Original: "σείριον" (Seirion).</note> by the Greeks. Whoever is born while this star is rising will apply an unbridled mind to every pursuit of perverse wickedness. They will also be removed from every grace of humanity, and will be the type who willingly follow all pursuits of violence—furious, irritable, terrible, threatening, and whom all men equally hate and fear. They will, moreover, be high-spirited, puffed up with a wordy abundance of speech, and driven by reckless talk toward every kind of insult. These people also stir up new quarrels in lawsuits; they have a heart palpitating with frequent agitations, and a voice that, as the throat swells, imitates the barking of dogs, so that often, moved by impulse and fury, they either gnash their teeth or constantly spit. But if Mars <note>Original: "♂"</note> should see this place, these traits we have mentioned grow even stronger. For these people never fear the secrets of the forests; indeed, they despise the bites of all wild beasts due to the boldness of their minds, so that frequently dangers are brought upon them both by beasts and by fires. Furthermore, if malevolent stars should radiate this place while the Moon <note>Original: "☽"</note> is also looking at Saturn <note>Original: "♄"</note>, there will be born hunters, arena-fighters, and those who fight with wild beasts in cages in the sight of the people; also gladiators, and those endowed with such speed of body that they seem able to catch hares in a race.

But if this star is found at the setting, and Mars <note>Original: "♂"</note> is either in that same place or looks upon it with a threatening radiation, they will be eaten by wolves; or, torn apart by dogs or wild beasts, they will end their lives in a miserable shredding.

<margin>The Bowl</margin>
In the thirtieth degree of Leo, the **Bowl** <note>Original: "Crater."</note> rises: whoever is born with this star rising will love well-watered fields; he will divert springs or streams or rivers from their channels to other places. He will also be a lover and cultivator of vineyards, and one who grafts fruitful shoots into fruitful trees; or one who, shearing boxwood trees, shapes them into the forms of beasts, or makes green porticos with vines bent into a circle: but this man will prefer to drink wine without the admixture of water <note>Drinking wine "neat" was often associated with excess in the ancient world.</note>. If the radiation of benevolent stars should favor those activities, he will trade in liquid merchandise.

If this star should be found at the setting without the testimony of a malevolent star, the one who is born will die of drunkenness amid banquets and cups. But if the radiation of malevolent stars should be added, he will die submerged either in a wine vat or in a well; or he will be found dead in a river, lake, swamp, or the sea, or certainly in a pool or a tub.

Whoever is born under this star will be occupied with various pleasures of luxury and devoted to the pursuits of the womanly arts; an inventor of flowers and wreaths, and one who clings to the pleasant delights of gardens, desiring scents, ointments, and spices with studious greed, and adorning his body with the allure of beauty, and who may secretly practice debauchery and adultery,

<margin>Spica</margin> **Spica** <note>The brightest star in the constellation Virgo; its name means "ear of grain."</note> rises in the tenth degree of Virgo. ### BRIGHT STARS RISING AND SETTING WITH LIBRA <note>Original: "♎"</note>. Chapter XII.

<margin>Sagittarius</margin> <note>The text here refers to the constellation **Sagitta** (The Arrow), which Firmicus places as rising with the eighth degree of the sign Sagittarius <note>Original: "♐"</note> or during the transition of Libra.</note> The **Arrow** <note>Original: "🏹"</note> rises in the eighth degree of Sagittarius. He who is born under this sign will be a shooter of arrows, one who strikes flying birds with a certain special skill of control; or one who, undaunted, pierces fish with a trident or spear even within the depths of the waves.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and both benevolent and malevolent stars look upon this same place with equal radiation, they die as soldiers in the army; placed in the line of battle among the bitter heaps of the enemy, and stained with their infinite blood, they are finally slain by a hostile hand. But if Saturn <note>Original: "♄"</note> alone, with Mercury <note>Original: "☿"</note> standing by, should see this place, or be found within it, he will make such men as sell themselves for the spectacle of death, trading the loss of their blood for the sake of another’s favor <note>A reference to gladiators or mercenaries.</note>. If Saturn alone does this, they are led into the arena by the sentence of a judge. For in this part the **Styx** <note>The mythological river of the underworld.</note> is said to be; nor is there any doubt that the Styx is here on earth. For those who do not fear the heavens shudder in their souls at those things which, having fallen from heaven, are applied to the sustenance of earthly bodies.

<margin>The Kid</margin> <note>Original: "Hœdus," a star in the constellation Auriga.</note> **The Kid** rises in the fifteenth degree of Sagittarius. Whoever is born while this sign is rising will always have a restless mind and an anxious purpose; entangled in various thoughts, he may never enjoy rest with the grace of security. He will also be assigned to the service of magistrates, acting as a scribe, a courier, or managing the duties of public taxes. However, he will be bound to wanton habits and perverse desires of love, devoted to wine and feasts; he may be a dancer or one who learns the theatrical arts with a studious passion.

But if this star is found at its setting, and malevolent stars look upon this place with a threatening radiation, they will either be thrown over precipices and thus perish, or, while practicing leaps, these wretches are broken by the fall of their hanging bodies, meeting an ill-fated death. Or, pursuing the beds of girls in the blind of night and demanding them with an excessive heat of impatience, they die when they have traveled through unknown places and climbed upon roofs to ambush the sleep of husbands, deceived by a headstrong slip. But if benevolent stars look upon this place, they die unhappily as restless and miserable men.

### BRIGHT STARS, WITH JUPITER RISING AND SETTING. Chapter 14.

<margin>Arcturus</margin>
In the 5th degree of Sagittarius, **Arcturus** rises. Whoever is born when this sign is rising will be the sort of person who guards the secrets of friends with faithful silence. To him, royal riches will be entrusted, as well as the people’s treasury and public buildings. But if malevolent stars radiate upon this place, they will either be entrusted with the care of the people, or they will become doorkeepers of the royal house, or such an office will be assigned to them that the duties of admitting or greeting guests in the palace are entrusted to them.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and Saturn <note>Original symbol: ♄</note> with Mercury <note>Original symbol: ☿</note> look upon this place with any radiation, it will cause those accused of serious crimes to perish in wretched treatments, driven by envy, handed over to public prison, and bound in chains.

<margin>Cygnus</margin>
In the tenth degree of Sagittarius, **Cygnus** <note>The Swan</note> rises. Whoever is born while this star is rising will either catch birds, or trade them, or with ingenious study will teach birds the sound of the human voice; or he will studiously raise various birds, especially wood-pigeons.

But if this star should be found at its setting, while he prepares his resources from the estates of others, he will be weighed down by the burden of captivity by enemies, or will be punished by public execution on account of spoils or the theft of spoils.

### BRIGHT STARS, WITH SATURN RISING AND SETTING. Chapter 15.

<margin>Ophiuchus of the Marsi</margin>
In the first degrees of Capricorn, **Ophiuchus** <note>The Serpent-Bearer</note> rises. Those who are born while this is rising will be like the Marsi <note>An ancient Italian people famous for their skills as snake-charmers and healers.</note>, who suppress venomous snakes by soothing and mitigating their stings.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and malevolent stars look upon this place with any radiation, they die unhappily from the bite of a poisonous serpent.

<margin>Delphinus</margin>
In the eighth degree of Capricorn, **Delphinus** <note>The Dolphin</note> rises. Whoever is born while this star is rising will be possessed by a passion for swimming. But with the testimony of Saturn <note>Original symbol: ♄</note>, he will be a diver; with Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> and Mercury <note>Original symbol: ☿</note>, however, he will be an acrobat, a leaper, a balancer <note>Original terms: "petaminarius, ephelmator, orciscopalarius, petauristarius" — various types of specialized gymnasts and circus performers.</note>, or certainly distinguished by an innate agility in running.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and Saturn <note>Original symbol: ♄</note> looks upon this place with a threatening radiation, he will be unhappily submerged in the sea or in a river by whirlpools and storms.

<margin>Lyra</margin>
In the tenth degree of Capricorn, **Lyra** <note>The Lyre</note> rises. Whoever is born while this star is rising will be just, upright, desiring, and fit for every duty of equity, and avengers of crimes, to whom public judgments and investigations are entrusted. But if Saturn <note>Original symbol: ♄</note> looks upon this place with any radiation, they will be torturers, executioners, and those who pursue evil men with eager zeal.

But if this star should be found at its setting, they will perish torn by public tortures, or burned by fires, or by legal execution, especially if Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> or Saturn <note>Original symbol: ♄</note> looks upon this place.

<margin>Cepheus</margin>
In the fifteenth degree of Capricorn, **Cepheus** rises. Such were the Catos among the ancients. Such in our times was Lollianus <note>Likely Quintus Flavius Maesius Egnatius Lollianus Mavortius, a contemporary of the author who held high office in the mid-4th century AD.</note>, who by the merit of his severity even attained the insignia of an ordinary consulship. JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

If Venus <note>Original symbol: ♀</note> and Mercury <note>Original symbol: ☿</note> are in this place and provide testimony, they will, through the tragic art, either always read poems eagerly or compose them eloquently.

## BRIGHT STARS, RISING AND SETTING WITH AQUARIUS <note>Original symbol: ♒</note>
## Chapter XVI.

<margin>Aquila</margin>
In the twelfth degree of Aquarius rises **Aquila** <note>The Eagle</note>. Whoever is born at the rising of this star will have the means of life from the slaughter of men and spoils; they will also catch and tame wild beasts. They will, moreover, be brave soldiers who, endowed with the highest courage, follow the enemy even with a bare chest, believing it adds much to their praise if they have contemptuously despised death with a secure boldness. But if benevolent stars <note>Such as Jupiter or Venus</note> look upon this place with a prosperous radiation <note>An astrological aspect</note>, their homeland will be liberated by them, or they will even found other cities; and having conquered and subdued nations, they will triumph wonderfully. But if Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> or Venus <note>Original symbol: ♀</note> looks upon this place, it will make them commanders, tribunes, ministers of emperors, attendants of kings, and those to whom the care of the empire or the guarding of arms is entrusted in their faith.

But if this star should be found at its setting, it will cause those born to be unhappily suffocated in the first light of life.

<margin>Cassiopeia</margin>
In the twentieth degree of Aquarius, **Cassiopeia** rises. Whoever is born under this star will be goldsmiths, makers of gold leaf, gilders, modelers, pearl-dealers, and those who handle all these arts with ingenious skill, and obtain the greatest means of life from them.

But if this star should be found at its setting, those born will either perish from a collapse <note>Likely referring to a building falling</note> or die by being slain.

## BRIGHT STARS, RISING AND SETTING WITH PISCES <note>Original symbol: ♓</note>
## Chapter XVII.

<margin>Andromeda</margin>
In the twelfth degree of Pisces rises **Andromeda**. Whoever is born while this star is rising will always proceed with cruel ferocity against men. For they will be either ministers of public punishments, or guards of prisons, or executioners, and those to whom the duties of killing men are entrusted. But if a benevolent star joined with malevolent ones looks upon this same place, it will make them overseers of workhouses or of the digging of metals <note>In ancient times, mining was often a form of penal labor</note>.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and malevolent stars look upon this place, they will cause them to be thrown to wild beasts or raised upon a cross. But if, with the malevolent stars so arranged, the favor of benevolent stars is added, they will cause them to be given to the training-school <note>A gladiatorial school</note> or to be bound in perpetual chains.

<margin>Heniochus</margin>
In the twentieth degree of Pisces rises **Heniochus** <note>The Charioteer, now known as the constellation Auriga</note>. Whoever is born while this star is rising will be careful charioteers, drivers, or horsemen, carriage-drivers, scouts, and sometimes even doctors; but those who most fittingly compose remedies from herbs for sick men and cattle.

But if this star should be found at its setting with malevolent stars, he will either be cured after being thrown down by the kick of a hoof, or perish overturned or weakened by a vehicle, or shattered by a wretched tearing of the body and limbs.

<margin>Ingeniculus</margin>
In the final degrees of Pisces rises **Ingeniculus** <note>The Kneeler, now known as the constellation Hercules</note>, which is called by the Greeks *en gonasin* <note>original: "ἐν γόνασιν", meaning "on the knees"</note>. Whoever is born while this star is rising will be fugitives, crafty, equipped with various deceits, liars, and those who seek after men with various traps, and always proceed with unbridled animosity. But with the testimony of Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> and the Moon <note>Original symbol: ☾</note>, they will be rope-walkers, mountain-climbers, dancers on strings <note>Tightrope walkers</note>, and those who handle such things.

But if the star is found at its setting, they will be endangered by various traps. But if Mars radiates upon this place, they will even be unhappily burned alive.

<margin>Orphos</margin>
In the last degree of Pisces, toward the left, a beast rises which is called **Orphos** <note>original: "ὀρφὸς", a large sea creature or sea-monster</note> by the Greeks. Whoever is born while this star is rising will be fishermen, but of larger fish. For these will catch seals, sharks <note>Literally "sea dogs"</note>, swordfish, tunas, or crocodiles. Or they will have duties involving salt, salted fish, or fish sauce <note>Original: "liquamine", likely referring to garum, the popular Roman fermented fish sauce</note>, and will trade in these.

But if this star should be found at its setting, and Mars radiates upon this place, those swimming in a river or the sea will be torn apart by crocodiles or beasts of this kind.

However, when the North Wind rises, which is between Pisces <note>Original symbol: ♓</note> and Aries <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, that is, between the beginning and the end of the wor—

BOOK EIGHT.

...of the world, which is fixed in one place and positioned at the very pole of the heavens, twisting the world with its perpetual speed. Whoever is born under this influence will be tamers of wild beasts, who associate with bears, bulls, or lions—once their ferocity has been laid aside—in human companionship. 
But if this star is found at its setting while Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> provides testimony, they will die a most cruel death, killed by wild beasts.

<margin>The Snake</margin>
The **Snake** <note>The constellation Draco</note> is the last, located between the two Bears <note>Ursa Major and Ursa Minor</note> in the manner of a river that glides along with smoky coils. Whoever is born under this star will be Marsians <note>A tribe famous in antiquity for snake-charming and medicinal skill</note>, or those who are accustomed to preparing healthy remedies for humans from poisons made of herbal pigments. 
But if this star is found at its setting, they will perish from the bite of serpents or surely by drinking poison.

<margin>The Swan</margin>
The **Swan** <note>Cygnus</note> also belongs to this part of the sign. Therefore, whoever is born at the rising of this star will be discoverers of metals, who pursue hidden veins of gold and silver, and of other kinds, with skillful investigations. These people will also become minters of coins. 
But if this star is found at its setting, and Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> is in that same place, or in opposition <note>original: "in diametro"</note>, or in a square aspect <note>original: "quadrato"</note>, they will either burn to death in a house fire or be cremated by avenging flames through a public judicial sentence.

<margin>Those born during an earthquake</margin>
At the end of these decrees, we must know this: if at that hour in which the degree is completed there is either an earthquake or thunder in the heavens, whoever is born then will always be shaky and unstable in body. With a wavering gait and trembling steps, such a person will expect and fear the ruins of overhanging rooftops at every moment of the hour. 
His eyes will flicker and tremble before the burning gaze of everyone. Not even his words will keep a certain order; instead, the impeded sound of his voice will hiss out a trembling murmur, so that his words always fail at the very moment of exit through a tight throat. For such people will always think the heavens are thundering, the earth is moving, and everything is always collapsing, so that by thinking of the terrors of a falling world, they lose the order of a proper life. These, Mavortius <note>Lollianus Mavortius, the Roman official to whom this work is dedicated</note>, our glory, are the principles of the Barbarian Sphere; this is the discipline of the Chaldean work which we promised.

## THE SECOND OUTCOMES OF THE BARBARIC SPHERE
## Chapter XVIII.

Now, however, I shall transfer the entire treatise to the following parts of the Barbarian Sphere, which in some part imitates the *Myriogenesis* <note>A Greek term meaning "ten-thousandfold origins," referring to a highly detailed system of astrology that assigns specific fates to every individual degree or minute of a sign</note>. For whatever the *Myriogenesis* pronounces concerning individual minutes, we shall do concerning individual degrees. Therefore, the entire Ascendant <note>original: "horos. gnomo"</note> must be positioned so that the true degree, collected by skillful computation, allows the outcome to be brought forth by a faithful pronouncement. Otherwise, whatever is promised will be thoroughly shadowed by the fault of error and deceptive lies. Now, therefore, we shall embrace the powers of all the signs and their outcomes according to the Barbarian Sphere through a brief discourse on each of their degrees.

## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF ARIES.
## Chapter XIX.

If the **first degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈︎</note> is found in the Ascendant <note>original: "horos."</note> and the ray of benevolent stars reaches it, kings and leaders will be born, and those who always lead their army prosperously.

If the **second degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈︎</note> is found in the Ascendant, they will be stubborn, thieves, and those who always rage with a backward fury, or those who transfer their household to foreign nations. 
But if, when the Ascendant is fixed in this degree, Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> has testimony, and the Moon <note>Original symbol: ☽</note> looks upon it from a square or opposition, they are punished by public execution once the aforementioned crimes are detected.

If the **third degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈︎</note> is found in the Ascendant, they will be deaf, one-eyed, and consumed by a dull stupor of foolishness.

If the **fourth degree of Aries** is found in the Ascendant, they will be thieves; but those who, caught in that crime, will be publicly killed.

If the **fifth degree of Aries** is found in the Ascendant, they will rule over a great people and judge the greatest matters, and the merit of their dignity will be placed before all. For they will be just, upright, sober, and those who protect the religions of their fathers with the greatest veneration, or who die adorned with every proclamation of goodness.

If the **sixth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈︎</note> is found in the Ascendant, he will be a friend of kings, or of powerful judges, adorned with the insignia of illustrious dignities, and one who carries all the ornaments of glory within himself.

The **seventh degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon, also known as the Ascendant</term>, with the testimony of Jupiter <note>Original symbol: ♃</note>, will make an athlete; but with Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note>, it makes one hunchbacked and a victim of a violent death <term>biothanatus: a person who dies an unnatural or violent death, such as by execution, suicide, or accident</term>.

The **eighth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, with the testimony of malevolent stars <note>Specifically Saturn or Mars</note>, will create athletes, but those whom the merits of illustrious virtues make noble. These, however, after many notable achievements, will perish by a violent death. But if the ray of benevolent stars <note>Specifically Jupiter or Venus</note> reaches this degree, they will be prophets, carrying the greatest signs of divinity in their souls.

The **ninth degree of Aries**, if found in the horoscope, slaughters those placed in the first stage of life by a violent death.

The **tenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make people treacherous, irreligious, and impure; those who, oppressed by various ailments of vice, die in the first stage of life.

The **eleventh degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, with Jupiter <note>Original symbol: ♃</note> either positioned in that degree or joined by a trine <term>trigona: an aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart, considered very harmonious</term> and exact radiation, will make a person powerful and magnificently displaying the insignias of dignity. A faithful bond of friendship will join him to kings and powerful men; he will be wealthy, affluent, and possessing vast stretches of land and estates. It will also make him a famous leader, heaped with every honor of dignity, adorned with prosperous testimonies of fame, and one who will die a natural death.

The **twelfth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, with Jupiter <note>Original symbol: ♃</note> and Venus <note>Original symbol: ♀</note> positioned in that very degree, with the testimony of the Moon <note>Original symbol: ☽</note>, or if Jupiter regards this same degree with a trine radiation, it will make those adorned with the distinguished splendor of nobility. These will also be wealthy and long-lived, dying by a praised kind of death.

The **tenth [thirteenth] degree of Aries** <note>original: "Decima pars"; this is likely a printer's error for "Decimatertia," as it follows the twelfth degree and the tenth was already listed</note> <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make people sterile, to whom the always-desired offspring is denied; but these will die, cut off in middle age.

The **fourteenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make a businessman, but one equipped with flowing riches; also a money-lender, collecting great reserves of wealth from public banks, known to all and always conspicuous. This place also makes weavers, or those who handle wool and purple dyes with constant mastery of their art.

The **fifteenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make one polluted by the shameless stain of lust, and always bound to impure vices; also a person of ill-repute <term>cinaedum: a term used in Roman antiquity for a man who defied traditional gender roles or was considered sexually passive/effeminate</term> condemned by public infamy. If it is a woman, a similar lust for impurity will strike her.

The **sixteenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will cause people to be tortured by constant intestinal pains. Such a person will also die in agony. If it be a woman laboring in childbirth, she will fulfill the final duty of life <note>i.e., she will die in labor</note>.

The **seventeenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make a fowler <note>a bird-catcher</note>, a hunter, or a breeder of birds or wild beasts. But if the testimony of Mars <note>Original symbol: ♂</note> reaches the horoscope, he will be torn apart by wild beasts or by dogs, and die.

The **eighteenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make a mule-driver or a herdsman of mules; but this man, struck by a small beast—either a venomous spider <note>original: "phalangio"</note>, a field mouse, or a scorpion—will die a wretched death.

The **nineteenth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will cause those positioned at the very threshold of life to perish.

The **twentieth degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, and if the prosperous testimony of Jupiter <note>Original symbol: ♃</note> reaches it, or if Jupiter is positioned in it, will make a man wealthy, adorned with many and distinguished children, and protected by the support of many brothers. The merits of faithful friendship join this same man to kings or powerful men. He will also be a worshiper of the gods, adorned with every proclamation of goodness—good, benevolent, just, long-lived, happy in old age, and one who dies his own death.

The **twenty-first degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, with the same star that we mentioned, will decree the same fate.

The **twenty-second degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, with the same star that we mentioned, will decree the same fate.

The **twenty-third degree of Aries** <note>Original symbol: ♈</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make one scrofulous <term>strumaticum: afflicted with swelling of the lymph nodes</term>, possessed by the ulcerated stain of spots, or certainly marked by the contagion of leprosy <note>original: "elephantiaca"</note>.

The **eighth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make those who are advanced by new and sudden honors, yet who die suddenly.

The **tenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make people who are evil, spiteful, malicious, and who are shaken by the hardships of every misfortune, and finally die an unnatural death <term>biothanati: those who die violently or by their own hand</term.

The **thirteenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make supervisors of athletes and famous masters of the wrestling school.

The **fourteenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will cause the body to be possessed by foul odors, so that a miserable stench of a male goat <note>original: *hircini foetoris*, a common Roman metaphor for strong body odor</note> is always exuded, and for this reason, the person is shunned by everyone.

The **fifteenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make liars who are far removed from any trust in the truth; it also makes them gluttons, serving the debauched desires of the belly and the throat.

The **sixteenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make people stained by the outrages of every crime.

The **seventeenth degree of Taurus**, if found in the horoscope, will make blacksmiths and those who work with bronze by hand.

### THE DEGREES OF GEMINI ACCORDING TO THE MYRIOGENESIS ###

#### Chapter 21 ####

The **first degree of Gemini** <note>Original symbol: ♊</note>, if found in the horoscope and Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> regards it with any aspect, will make men powerful and great, the first of their province, and to be feared with the greatest honor by their citizens, but perishing by the indignation of the prince.

The **second degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, and if Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> or Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> is positioned with it—and especially if the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is placed in favorable locations of the birth chart, or is carried toward them full of light—it will make leaders who lead armies of cavalry or infantry, to whom the command of ships is entrusted, who also subjugate many people, who see places unknown to them, and to whom clear signs of power are given even in remote and distant regions. They will certainly be just and religious, providing much to many; and after having many sons, they will finally die a natural death.

The **third degree of Gemini** <note>original symbol: ♊</note>, if found in the horoscope <term>horoscopus: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>, will make priests, or leaders of sacred rites, or distinguished minor rulers.

The **fourth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make people remarkably beautiful of body, whose beloved beauty may recommend them to kings, so that the kings' desires always burn with love for them.

The **fifth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make people noble and always uplifted by a high spirit of pride.

The **sixth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make inspired prophets <note>original: *uates entheos*</note> who sing songs by a certain divine power.

The **seventh degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make guards of prisons and watchmen of public custodies.

The **eighth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, and if **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> also has a place there, will make musicians. If, however, **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is there, it will produce trumpeters, but those who die pierced through in war.

The **ninth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present, will make laborers, ceiling-decorators <term>lacunarios: craftsmen who specialized in ornate, paneled ceilings</term>, and those weighed down by a perpetual burden of unhappiness.

The **tenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who die consumed by pain in the lungs.

The **eleventh degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make gladiators <term>hoplomachos: a type of gladiator who fought with a spear and a small round shield</term> and those who take pleasure in practicing gladiatorial games.

The **twelfth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present, will cause men to die from a wound to the testicles, but women will perish in childbirth.

The **thirteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who die with an inflated belly from dropsy <term>hydropici: a condition now known as edema, involving the accumulation of fluid in the body's tissues</term>.

The **fourteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present, will cause people to die a wretched death by falling from a high place.

The **fifteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make men bath-attendants, common servants, and assistants.

The **sixteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make pantomimes <note>performers of solo narrative dances</note>, but those whose visible physical beauty always introduces them to the loves of many, possessing a soft and delicate heart.

The **seventeenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make men distinguished for both the beauty and the size of their bodies, but who are truly modest and, because of this, friends of good men.

The **eighteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will produce the exercises of athletes, assigned always to the services of the wrestling school.

The **nineteenth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present, will make men who will die by the sword. If, however, **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> is in that degree, it will make them water-drawers, fatigued by perpetual labors. But if the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is positioned in "scaly" signs <note>signs like Capricorn (the Sea-Goat) or Pisces (the Fish)</note> and is carried full of light toward **Mars**, or with diminishing light toward **Saturn**, it will make them lepers <term>elephanticos: those suffering from "elephantiasis," a term often used in antiquity for severe skin diseases like leprosy</term>.

The **twentieth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present, will make men who hold the rudders of the people <note>i.e., political leaders</note> and to whom fair judgments are entrusted; but these will die a violent death <term>biothanata: a death by execution, accident, or suicide rather than natural causes</term>.

The **twenty-first degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Saturn** present and **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> well-placed, will make people rich with flowing wealth and noble friends of kings; but they will be fathers of few sons and brothers of few brothers. The **twenty-second degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make lyre-players and musicians, and those who will carry the greatest marks of nobility from this, or whom a bond of friendship joins to kings; this person, however, will die a violent death.

The **twenty-third degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make men vigorous in virtue and noble in war, or those who are commended by everyone with the testimony of a prosperous reputation; but they will die without children.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with **Mars** present—or with Mars regarding this place from an opposite or square aspect <note>astrological positions 180 or 90 degrees away</note>—will cause them to perish by falling from a height, so that they die either with broken feet or perish torn apart by wild beasts.

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS

The **twenty-fifth degree of Gemini** <note>original symbol: ♊</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make priests, soothsayers <term>aruspices: ancient diviners who interpreted the will of the gods by examining the entrails of sacrificed animals</term>, prophets, and those joined in faithful friendship with kings. But if **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> is in that degree, it will produce those who are effeminate and passive <note>original: "cinædos & pathicos," referring to men who took a passive role in same-sex relations, often viewed with social stigma in Roman law</note>; however, these people will eventually perish through the king's indignation.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make temple wardens, guardians of temples, temple-servants <term>hierodulos: individuals dedicated to the service of a deity or temple</term>, and those appointed to sacred duties.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make those who are subject to seizures, the mentally impaired, and the insane; they will ultimately be short-lived <note>original: "oligochronios," a Greek term for those with a brief lifespan</note>.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make people litigious, quarrelsome, and those who are always involved in lawsuits and disputes. If, however, **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is in this degree, or looks upon this place with a square or opposite aspect <term>quadrata seu diametra radiatione: astrological configurations where planets are 90 or 180 degrees apart, usually considered stressful</term>, it will cause them to be torn apart by dogs and to die without leaving an inheritance to any sons.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope with the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> present, will make people noble but illegitimate; they will die in the first stage of life.

The **thirtieth degree of Gemini**, if found in the horoscope, will make hunters, specifically those who are employed for the pleasures of princes <note>likely meaning those who provide game or entertainment for the Roman elite</note>.

In the line of **Gemini**, whoever has their horoscope there, if **Mars** is found in the same place, they will be struck by a wild beast or a viper and will unfortunately lose a thigh or a foot.
