## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF CANCER.
### Chapter XX.

Between the eyes <note>referring to a specific astronomical point or star cluster between the "eyes" of the Crab constellation</note>, whoever has their horoscope there will be one-eyed or deprived of all sight in their eyes.

The **first degree of Cancer** <note>original symbol: ♋</note>, if found in the horoscope with the **Moon** present, will make merchants and nobles. If **Saturn** is present, it will make sailors, fishermen, tavern-keepers, innkeepers, and the like.

The **second degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men conspicuous for their great power and nobility, but also violent men who possess the property of others through ambitious schemes. These men, however, will travel on long journeys where they will succumb to sudden death.

The **third degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make hardworking merchants who never remain in one place.

The **fourth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who always attack their enemies with every kind of controversy, and they shall become superior to them in every contest.

The **fifth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men whose eyes are afflicted with deeply pitted wounds <note>original: "cauloſis uulneribus," likely referring to hollowed-out ulcers or severe cataracts</note>.

The **sixth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men whose eyes are always turned with a distorted gaze <note>likely referring to strabismus or a squint</note>.

The **seventh degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who have tumors on their heads. But if the **Moon** is moving toward the horoscope, it will make them cunning and impious. If, however, **Mars** casts its rays on the Moon and the horoscope, it will make bandits who roam with cruel ferocity. These people will be raised on a cross <note>referring to crucifixion, a common Roman punishment for highwaymen and rebels</note>, or, having been condemned by public trial, will perish by a most cruel death.

The **eighth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people blind. For in this degree and the fourth, there is a nebula <note>original: "nebula," referring to the star cluster Praesepe (the Manger), which ancient astrologers associated with eye problems</note>, which we have mentioned frequently in this book.

The **ninth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make sailors and ship-pilots—those who, by the moderation of their skilled craft, steer ships through every sea.

The **tenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who accomplish everything through effective social interaction.

The **eleventh degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are fishermen and those who are continually occupied in the water.

The **twelfth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make men who are hardworking and seek their living through constant sweat.

The **thirteenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make scholars who are always occupied with books and diligent study late into the night.

The **fourteenth degree of Cancer** <note>original symbol: ♋</note>, if found in the horoscope, will make goldsmiths, and those who profit from working with gold.

The **fifteenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make rustic men who always keep themselves within their own dwellings.

The **sixteenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people proud and haughty, and those who consider themselves distinguished by nobility.

The **seventeenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people lazy, idle, sluggish, and occupied by no labor.

The **eighteenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people joyful, pleasant, and cheerful, mourning in the face of no adversity.

The **nineteenth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make actors, <term>pantomimos: solo performers who acted out mythological stories through rhythmic movement and gesture</term>, and stage jesters.

The **twentieth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people lazy, and those who perform no work through any weariness of affairs.

The **twenty-first degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people vain, liars, and proven by no truth whatsoever.

The **twenty-second degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people sluggish, lazy, and removed from all the fatigue of work.

The **twenty-third degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people unstable and changeable with a varying agitation of the mind.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people who always desire to be raised above others by the dignity of honors.

The **twenty-fifth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, if the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is present or casting its rays toward it, will make people blessed with every happiness, but who defile themselves with debauchery and adultery, such that their youth is praised, but their later age is brought to infamy. This same thing is also decreed in the birth chart of a woman.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people mobile and deceptive with an inconstant change of perception.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people humble and obscure, and always weighed down by constant servitude.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people sluggish and idle, and those who do not know how to involve themselves in any business.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make people ungenerous <note>original: "illiberales," meaning lacking the qualities or manners of a free-born person</note>, thieves, and coveters of other people's property.

The **thirtieth degree of Cancer**, if found in the horoscope, will make sailors or fishermen, and those who work through the constant fatigue of the waters.

## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF LEO <note>original symbol: ♌</note>
### Chapter XXIII.

The **first degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make pimps <note>original: "lenones"</note>, specifically those who burst forth with a hoarse voice. This is also fulfilled in a similar manner in those degrees which are in the mouth of the Lion <note>referring to the stars in the head of the constellation Leo</note>.

The **second degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make kings and powerful men. But whenever the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> or **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> comes to this place, heavy struggles of wars are stirred up for them. In this degree is the bright star of which we spoke above <note>The "bright star" is likely Regulus, the "Heart of the Lion," considered one of the most powerful royal stars in ancient astrology</note>.

The **third degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make a king possessing a double kingdom, and joining many provinces to the powers of his virtue. The same aforementioned star extends its rays into this degree with a happy divine power.

The **fourth degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make hunters, who are held by a passion for wild beasts and birds.

The **fifth degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make masters of athletes, public trainers <term>aliptes: in the Roman world, these were specialists who oiled and massaged athletes in the gymnasiums</term>, or oilers.

The **sixth degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make athletes, who always rejoice in the exercise of the gymnasiums.

The **seventh degree of Leo**, if found in the horoscope, will make hymn-singers, comic actors, tragic actors, and stage performers of any kind.

The **sixteenth degree of Virgo**, if found in the horoscope, will create great men often handling many businesses, but who eventually die a violent death <note>original: biothanata; a Greek-derived term used in astrology for an unnatural, premature, or violent end</note>.

The **seventeenth degree of Virgo** <note>original symbol: ♍</note>, if found in the horoscope, will create gladiators, assigned to public entertainments.

## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF LIBRA <note>Myriogenesis: a Greek-derived term meaning "ten thousand origins," referring to the specific outcomes of each degree</note>
### Chapter XXV.

The **first degree of Libra** <note>original symbol: ♎︎</note>, if found in the horoscope, will create those with a beautiful body, adorned with lovable grace and elegance. If, however, Saturn <note>original symbol: ♄</note> should be in this degree, it will grant them health in the entire body.

The **second degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope—because there are many stars in this degree, some of which are masculine and some feminine—it must be noted that if someone has their horoscope in the masculine stars, he will be a noble singer of hymns, to whom the secrets of the gods are entrusted. But if it is in the feminine stars, he will be an effeminate man <note>original: cinædus; a term for a man who performs expressive dances or is perceived as gender-nonconforming</note>, but one who is always loved for his sophistication and is dear to everyone.

The **third degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create priests who are just, holy, and long-lived in a happy age.

The **fourth degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create lyre-players and musicians, adorned with sweet-sounding voices.

The **fifth degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create the rich and wealthy, and those who are always involved in legal judgments.

The **sixth degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create the wealthy, who handle many duties of business.

The **seventh degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope while Mars is present, will cause the person to perish by a cruel death captured by pirates, or force them to die a wretched death torn by wild beasts.

The **eighth degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create bath-keepers, lower servants <note>original: mediastinos; general laborers or house-slaves</note>, and attendants of the waters.

The **ninth degree of Libra**, if found in the horoscope, will create gamblers, who are well-known <note>original: perspicuos</note> by popular reputation.

In **Bootes** <note>the constellation of the Herdsman</note>, whoever has the horoscope will be a divine astrologer, a prophet, and highly skilled in the Chaldean art <note>astrology</note>.

### THE DEGREES OF SCORPIO FROM THE MYRIOGENESIS BY JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS ###

->Chapter XXVI<-

The **first degree of Scorpio** <note>original symbol: ♏︎</note>, if found in the horoscope, will create enchanters <note>original: incantatores</note> who are able to soothe pains through the power of words.

The **second degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create shameful men, often polluted by the filth of prostitution.

The **third degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create dwarves, hunchbacks, those who are deformed and objects of ridicule.

The **fourth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will similarly create dwarves, but those destined for the delights <note>likely acting as jesters or court favorites</note> of kings or emperors.

The **fifth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope and if the Moon <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is well-placed, will create those who are noble, just, and religious; they will be honored by a distinguished marriage alliance and have many children. If, however, they derive their livelihood from teaching or interpretations, they will be royal scribes managing literary duties, whom the faithful friendship of kings makes noble.

The **sixth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create priests who are wealthy and have many children; but these men frequently die due to the anger of kings or princes.

The **seventh degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create men who perish torn apart by the cruel bite of wild beasts.

The **eighth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create craftsmen laboring in the work of the mechanical arts, but who die from the strike of an asp or a viper.

The **ninth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create gardeners who are always devoted to the cultivation of their plots.

The **tenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create such men who die while still in the first stage of life.

The **eleventh degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create divinely inspired priests <note>original: entheos sacerdotes; priests "filled with the god" or possessed by a divine spirit</note> who give true answers to those who seek them.

The **twelfth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create temple servants or those assigned to the service of sacred rites.

The **thirteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope and with the Moon positioned in any "cardine" <note>the four "hinge" points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, will create judges who carry the greatest insignia of dignity, even judging the sentences of other judges and possessing the ultimate power of human life and death. But this power is decreed for them only until their 30th or 35th year. These men will also have wives and children. However, in the 27th, 42nd, and 58th years of their lives, they will encounter "climacterics" <note>term: climateras; critical turning points or dangerous years in a person's life</note> and dangers. If their life is extended to the 66th year, they will then perish completely. Nevertheless, they will suffer some physical defect during their lives and will finally die either by the sword, by iron, in water, or by some sudden death.

The **fourteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create men of unstable mind and who use no reason at all.

The **fifteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create the idle, the listless, and the lazy, who exhaust themselves with no activity in life.

The **sixteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create bakers. But if the Moon is in any sign with a bright star, they will be judges, prevailing with great liberty and power. If, however, Mars <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is found in "dejected" places <note>astrological positions where the planet's influence is weakened</note>, it will create executioners <note>original: spiculatores; literally "scouts," but in a legal/imperial context, the guards who carried out death sentences</note> who, with a drawn sword, cut off the necks of men.

The **seventeenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create goldsmiths, gilders, gold-leaf beaters, and those who work in gold.

The **eighteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope, will create men who perish cruelly, wickedly torn apart by beasts.

The **nineteenth degree of Scorpio**, if found in the horoscope and if the Moon is well-placed, will create those adorned with a great power of happiness, who possess the greatest power of life and death. But if Jupiter <note>original symbol: ♃</note> regards the horoscope with any "radiation" <note>an aspect or beam of light between planets</note>, their power will be so great that it may be compared to royal command. But they will be excessively negligent in public affairs, and will die if the prince is offended.

### BOOK EIGHT ###

...who, leading an army successfully, shall achieve infinite victories; their virtue and glory shall be compared to royal power. These individuals, uplifted by an excessive increase in good fortune, may even contemplate rebellion and the seizure of power. They will be bold and reckless, yet they will leave behind surviving sons after their deaths, though these sons may perish by fire or by offending a king.

The **twenty-first degree of Pisces** <note>original symbol: ♓︎</note>, if found in the horoscope, which corresponds to the **right foot**, will produce fishermen who gather sea sponges. If, however, the **second foot** <note>referring to a specific anatomical part of the constellation figure</note> is found in the horoscope, it will cause the person to perish by some beast or four-footed animal. If the **third part**, it will produce effeminate men <note>original: cinaedos; a term used for men who did not conform to traditional masculine roles</note>, and women of prostituted modesty who become public harlots.

The **twenty-second degree of Pisces**, which is the **front left foot**, if found in the horoscope, will produce gardeners. If the **second part**, it will cause death by wild beasts; if the **third**, it will produce barbers. If the **fourth**, it will cause the person to be killed by pirates, or to be torn by beasts and perish in humid places.

The **twenty-third degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, and if **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, and **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> are located in that same degree, they will make the subjects powerful, wealthy, and long-lived; their increase in happiness is decreed for their advanced age, and they shall rejoice in a large brood of children.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, will produce those who, driven by greedy desire and a murderous, mad fury, kill their own brothers; yet they themselves, such being the will of the fates, shall die a violent death.

The **twenty-fifth degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope—and if **Mars** is found in that degree, or is joined to it by diameter <note>opposition</note> or square aspect—it will cause men to be consumed by fire.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, will produce orators, lawyers, and physicians, whose character is ennobled by the genius of their profession. With the testimony of favorable stars, they will be granted the office of ambassador for their country; however, having offended their king or prince, they will perish miserably.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, with **Venus** and **Jupiter** present, will make men wealthy, just, amiable, long-lived, and occupied by the love of many women. For these people, the increase of happiness will come as they age; however, in their early life, the greatest increases in glory and dignity shall occur.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, will produce those who squint <note>original: strabones</note>, but whose crossed eyes are adorned with a certain pleasing grace and beauty; nonetheless, these people will be negligent. But if **Mars** is found in that degree, some will suffer a loss of blood, others elephantiasis <note>a term used in antiquity for severe skin diseases or leprosy</note>, and some indeed madness; and this occurs if the true light of the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> is carried toward **Mars**, in whatever place it is found.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Pisces**, if found in the horoscope, will produce lawyers and wise men. If a benevolent star is in that degree, they will be sent as ambassadors to the emperor and will fulfill everything mandated to them in their embassy, for which they shall receive many gifts; but they will certainly have some defect in the necessary parts of the body.

The **thirtieth degree of Scorpio** <note>original symbol: ♏︎</note>, if found in the horoscope, will produce **Marsi** <note>a people of ancient Italy famous for snake-charming and medicine</note> and poisoners, who sell toxins for the death of men, so that through this pursuit they kill many. These people will also be malicious, liars, and wicked. If **Mars** is found in this degree, they will be hunters, but will perish by a violent death <note>original: biothanati</note>. Adjacent to Scorpio on the right side are **Ophiuchus** and **Vulpes** <note>the Serpent-bearer and the Fox</note>, and on the left are **Cynocephalus** and **Ara** <note>the Dog-head and the Altar</note>.

Those born in **Ophiuchus** will be bold and divinely inspired <note>original: enthei</note>, knowing the future through a prophetic instinct of divinity.

Those born in **Vulpes** will be shrewd, fraudulent, and deceivers, yet very prudent, seeking the means of life through a certain eternal cultivation. But if **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> is found in that place, they will be guardians of monuments, but will die through deceit.

Those born in **Cynocephalus** will frequently be sickly, childless, and short-lived.

Those born in **Ara** will be priests, having only the means of life from sacrifices, but perishing by an evil death.

-># JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS ON ASTROLOGY<-

The **first degree of Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>, if found in the **Ascendant** <note>original: horoscopo; the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, will produce noble, religious, and just people, upon whom the greatest signs of glory are bestowed. But if a benevolent star is positioned in this same degree, it will produce kings or those close to kings, who effectively complete all their business.

The **second degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce people who are furious, perjurers, treacherous, and sacrilegious.

The **third degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will cause the person to lose one eye, in whatever way or manner it may happen.

The **fourth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce guardians of monuments, **undertakers** <note>original: vespillones; specifically those who carried the corpses of the poor at night</note>, and **embalmers** <note>original: pollinctores</note>.

The **fifth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce people who are impure, immodest, miserable, and polluted by the stain of shameful infamy.

The **sixth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, produces dwarfs, hunchbacks, those with varicose veins, the defective, and ultimately those who suffer a **violent death** <note>original: biothanatos; a term for an unnatural or premature death</note>.

The **seventh degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce just and religious people, to whom public judgments are entrusted, so that they may pass sentences upon the judgments of others.

The **eighth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant while **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> is present, will produce long-lived and religious people, who are foremost among their kin, having many sons; they will be advisors or teachers to kings, as well as scribes and those who handle the duties of sacred writings, from which signs of happiness are bestowed upon them as they age, and who pass away by a good death.

The **ninth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce astrologers, prophets, diviners, those **inspired by the gods** <note>original: entheos</note>, and worshippers of the gods.

The **tenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce athletes, **shield-fighters** <note>original: hoplomachos; a type of gladiator</note>, and those who always practice the profession of gladiatorship.

The **eleventh degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce men who, struck down in hostile war, perish cruelly.

The **twelfth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce dangerous and reckless men, who willingly approach every wickedness with a perverse heat of desire.

The **thirteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce those possessed by a murderous fury, and they likewise perish by a **violent death**.

The **fourteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce **lyre-players** <note>original: citharoedos</note> assigned to public entertainments, but who have a defect in the eye.

The **fifteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce mechanics who, making instruments necessary for wars, themselves also die wretchedly in war.

The **sixteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant while **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is present, causes a man to die torn by a spear, while a woman will perish in childbirth.

The **seventeenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce athletes. If, however, **Mars** offers testimony <note>aspects the degree</note>, it will produce hunters. If **Jupiter**, it will produce most capable keepers of horses.

The **eighteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce thieves, perjurers, malevolent and malicious people, without children, and victims of a **violent death**.

The **nineteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce **martial artists** <note>original: pancratiastas; competitors in the pancratium, a blend of boxing and wrestling</note> and athletes, but they die without children.

The **twentieth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce people who are dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, and ridiculous.

The **twenty-first degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce people who consume much food and who deny the property of others <note>implying embezzlement or theft</note>.

The **twenty-second degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant while **Jupiter** is present, will produce great and powerful men who possess the lowest spaces of the earth <note>likely referring to vast landholdings or mines</note>. These individuals will be such that armies of infantry or cavalry are committed to them, and they are often entrusted with naval battles. In this role, they will encounter many wars and will even subjugate barbarian cities; some of these they will restore, while others they will utterly destroy. They will also have children and wives, who will nevertheless have defects and scars in necessary places <note>a phrase often used in Latin astrology to denote hidden physical blemishes or health issues</note>. They themselves, fighting in foreign places, will die a **violent death** in battle.

### BOOK EIGHT.

The **twenty-third degree of Sagittarius** <note>original: ♐︎</note>, if found in the **Ascendant** <note>original: horoscopo; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, will cause those born to perish in desert and hidden places, torn apart by wild beasts.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce tamers of horses or charioteers. If **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> is in this same place, he will produce royal charioteers or mule-drivers, but those who achieve the highest marks of glory for this. If, however, **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bears witness there, he will cause them to perish by a **violent death** <note>original: biothanatos; an unnatural or premature death</note>.

The **twenty-fifth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce drunkards and those who are habitually intoxicated, especially if Mars is found in that degree. But if **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> offers testimony, he will produce **licentious men** <note>original: cinedos; often referring to men who defied traditional gender roles or were sexually passive, leading to social stigma</note> who are condemned by public infamy, and the women will be prostitutes.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce those polluted by a vicious contagion; the women will be **viragoes** <note>original: viragines; women who act with the spirit or behavior of men</note>, prostitutes, and devoted to every crime of lust.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will cause men to waste away by a miserable death in desert places. If Mars is found in that same degree, he will make them **short-lived** <note>original: oligochronios</note> and unhappy, dying from a sharp wound.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce donkey-drivers, mule-drivers, and those involved in constant labors.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce men who are dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, captives, and objects of ridicule.

The **thirtieth degree of Sagittarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce **physicians** <note>original: physicos</note> without grace and full of envy, whose death shall be caused by beasts. But if Mars is in this same degree, they will be short-lived and without children.

Those born on the extreme line of Sagittarius and upon the **Tail** <note>the stars at the end of the constellation</note> will be **potters** <note>original: siguli, likely a transcription error for figuli</note>. Those born below the Tail will be one-eyed or cross-eyed, but very fast runners, yet subjugated under the power of others. These people will also be frequently restless in their blood; they will have long faces, but will perish by a miserable death, torn by a four-legged animal. On the right side of Sagittarius rises the ship **Argo**, and on the left, the **Dog** <note>Canis Major</note>.

Those who have their Ascendant in the **Ship** will be ship-owners or pilots of ships, and also merchants, but those who sail to the West. But if Mars looks upon this same place, they will be killed by pirates while returning to the East.

Those who have their Ascendant in the **Dog** will be litigious and loud. But if Venus is found in that same place, they will be excellent advocates, friends of kings, and distinguished orators.

Those who have their Ascendant in the **Mouth of the Dog** <note>referring to the star Sirius</note> will lead a base life with a polluted mouth, yet inflated with an abundance of varied speech.

## THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES OF CAPRICORN <note>original: ♑︎</note>. Chapter XXVII.

The **first degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce a king and a prince, upon whom the greatest marks of power are bestowed.

The **second degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create leaders of waging war, to whom the arrangement of battles is entrusted; but these will die a "happy" **violent death** <note>original: biothanata morte feliciter; likely implying a glorious death in battle</note>.

The **third degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, with Mars present and the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> well-positioned, will produce great and powerful men who hold the greatest power of the sword, but who always exercise their judgments severely and cruelly. For these will be cruel, clever, bold, and killers of many. They will also be leaders of great armies, but will die in battle.

The **fourth degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, with Venus present, will produce musicians or craftsmen, but those who pursue women with perverted lustful desires, and are negligent in all things. But if the Moon is well-placed, it will produce scribes and nobles to whom the duties of great affairs are entrusted; also wealthy, just, and religious men who die at a great age.

The **fifth degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce base and impure men, devoted to every vice of lust.

The **sixth degree of Capricorn**, if found in the Ascendant, will produce men who finally die miserably of **elephantiasis** <note>original: elephantici; a condition causing extreme swelling of the skin and tissues</note>.

->### JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS<-

The **seventh degree of Saturn**, if found in the **Ascendant** <note>original: horoscopo; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, will create diligent craftsmen whose noble skill earns them praise and the friendship of kings. However, with the testimony of **malefic stars** <note>planets like Mars or Saturn that were traditionally thought to have a challenging influence</note>, those born in this part will also become physicians.

The **eighth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant while **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> is present, will create men who achieve the highest marks of dignity. But if the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is well-positioned, it will make them busy individuals who handle all the duties of commerce; it will also make others prefects of the public taxes.

The **ninth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant while **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is present, will cause men to perish in their early years. If, however, **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> bears witness, it will create moneylenders and wealthy men, but those who die because of their own money.

The **tenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant with **Mars** present, will create adulterers, but those with an amiable and charming grace, who nevertheless corrupt the wives of their own friends with a perverse desire for love. Yet, they are never caught and made public for this crime; instead, through some craft, they will be granted the greatest means of support for their lives. Nevertheless, they themselves will also be allotted wives corrupted by adultery; and finally, at the end of their lifespan, they will pass away without a sudden death.

The **eleventh degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create goldsmiths, leaf-gold beaters, gilders, and those who practice similar trades.

The **twelfth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create an athlete of great courage, but one who dies a **violent death** <note>original: biothanatus; an unnatural, premature, or forced death</note>.

The **thirteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant with **Mars** present, will create those who, for the sake of profit, resort to every act of cruelty. For they will be **Marsi** <note>The Marsi were an ancient people of Italy renowned in antiquity as snake-charmers, healers, and masters of herbal poisons</note>, selling poisons and nourishing serpents after dulling their venomous fangs, through which many may even die. They will also be perjurers and corrupters of lust, but they will recite the measures of songs sweetly with a slender voice, and for the most part, they will deceive everyone with a faked simplicity; they will have foul breath, be noisy, and will receive no joy from either their wives or their children. Furthermore, as they age, they will be lame in their feet and will obtain their life’s support from commerce or from the public treasury.

The **fourteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant with **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> or **Venus** present, will create wealthy men and administrators of affairs to whom some guardianship is always entrusted, and who handle the duties of leading men among their people. They will, however, be negligent and fond of many banquets. But if **Mercury** is found in this place, having been promoted through domestic recommendation, they will attain the friendships of kings.

The **fifteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who are dwarfs, hunchbacks, deformed, and ridiculous.

The **sixteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create hunchbacks and those who have six fingers on their hands.

In the **conjunction of the spine and neck of Saturn** <note>original: in coniuctione spinae & colli ♄; likely referring to specific degrees or a fixed star configuration associated with the "anatomy" of the planetary influence</note>, those who are born with **Mars** present and the **Moon** bearing witness—and joined by a good radiation <note>an astrological aspect or beam of light from another planet</note>—will be noble, parents of noble children, friends of kings and princes, and long-lived, but they will die a **violent death**.

The **seventeenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant with **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** present in the same part or sign, will create killers of their own wives, but those who are punished by public execution.

The **eighteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant with **Mercury** present, will create scribes always assigned to royal duties; but these men, consumed by wild beasts, will die in damp places.

The **nineteenth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create notaries <note>original: tabelliones; legal recorders or scriveners</note> always devoted to legal studies.

The **twentieth degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create noble men and friends of kings, to whom much is granted from the bounties of emperors; they will be beloved by the people and, within a moderate span of time, will achieve many marks of dignity. They will, however, be quick to anger and will pursue their indignations with the greatest force of power; but they will experience misfortunes from the downfalls of their brothers, though they will die a natural death.

The **twenty-first degree of Saturn**, if found in the Ascendant, will create those who are weak in both mind and senses, and who frequently suffer from insanity.

### THE MYRIOGENESIS <term>Myriogenesis: "The Ten Thousand Fates," a system of detailed astrological predictions for every single degree of the zodiac.</term> OF THE DEGREES OF AQUARIUS ♒
### Chapter XXIX.

The **first degree of Aquarius** <note>original: ♒</note>, if found in the Ascendant while **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> are present, or looking upon it with a **trine aspect** <note>original: trigonica radiatione; an angle of 120 degrees, considered harmonious</note>, and with the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> well-positioned, will create great and glorious kings, long-lived, possessing the circuit of all lands, to whom the greatest power is decreed in the course of time; yet they shall perish in water.

The **second degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create craftsmen of the arts pertaining to ornament or painting; but these, while their children survive them, will die by their own natural death.

The **third degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant while **Saturn** is present or looking upon it with any aspect, will create great and powerful men who possess many lands, yet who suffer the loss of their paternal inheritance; nevertheless, by their own strength, they will attain the greatest resources of wealth. These men will also subdue their own people in war, and will be inclined toward every act of cruelty, taking joy in the slaughter of many men. They will also have sons by handmaidens, but will lose them at an immature age. They will be separated from all sadness <note>This may imply a stoic or callous temperament</note>, yet they will be displeasing to everyone and will disparage all people, so that for this reason, all their friends avoid them. They will furthermore be gluttons, consuming much food, yet possessing much land and attaining many marks of power in the course of time. But when they have entered the threshold of old age, their bodies already weakened by their former labors, they will cultivate the fields.

The **fourth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create worshippers of the gods who offer judgments on the opinions of others, yet they will perish unhappily by an **unnatural death** <note>original: biothanata; a death by violence, execution, or suicide</note>.

The **fifth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create such men who end their lives ill-fatedly by the noose.

The **sixth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create water-carriers <note>those who draw or transport water</note>, burdened by a wretched weight of labor, or perhaps noble athletes.

The **seventh degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant while **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> is joined to it by any aspect, will create long-lived men, wealthy and just, who prosper most in their old age; but they at last, with their children surviving them, will die by their own natural death.

The **eighth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who, by an adverse decree of fortune, do not possess themselves <note>likely meaning they lack self-control or are enslaved/dependent</note>.

The **ninth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create builders, architects, sculptors, and those practicing other manual works.

The **tenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, and **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is joined to it by any aspect...

...joined together, it will create bath-attendants and common household servants <note>original: mediastinos; often referring to the lowest class of slaves or workers in a Roman household</note>, but they will die while still in their youth.

The **eleventh degree of Aquarius** <note>original: ♒</note>, if found in the **Ascendant** <note>original: horoscopo</note>, will create men who die unfortunately in watery or damp places. Those born when this degree is "in the peak of the Urn" <note>referring to a specific group of stars within the constellation of Aquarius, the Water Bearer</note> will be physicians. If, however, **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> is joined to this degree by any aspect, they will be undertakers, funeral directors, and corpse-bearers <note>original: vespillones; those who carried the bodies of the poor at night</note>, to whom the duties of burying the dead are entrusted.

The **twelfth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create fishermen who obtain the support for their lives solely from the sea.

The **thirteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create gardeners or cleaners of sewers. If, however, **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bears witness to this degree, it will produce bath-attendants. But if **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> does so, it will produce drawers of water and those who live by such a trade.

The **fourteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bearing witness, will create travelers or sailors—but those who, weighed down by the burden of every labor, lead a miserable life.

The **fifteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create effeminate men <note>original: cinaedos; in a Roman context, this referred to men who took a passive role in sexual acts or displayed "unmasculine" behavior</note> who are shameless, but who practice this vice of lust in secret.

The **sixteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who primarily finish works labored over with fire <note>likely referring to blacksmiths or metalworkers</note>.

The **十七th degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, and if **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is joined to it by any aspect, will cause men to die torn apart by a spear.

The **eighteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who suffer from lung pain along with a grave illness.

The **nineteenth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who finally achieve some power over others.

The **twentieth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create those with dropsy <note>original: hydropicos; a historical term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</note> who, seized by a swelling of the belly, die from this cause.

The **twenty-first degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create goldsmiths, gold-beaters, gilders, and those practicing such arts.

The **twenty-second degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men with beautiful faces and pleasing bodies, but who are destined to die in their youth.

The **twenty-third degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create perfumers <note>original: pigmentarios; also makers of dyes or cosmetics</note>, but wealthy ones, to whom profits come from such an art.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, and if **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> is joined to it by any aspect, will create beautiful men, pleasing for their large stature, and lovable. If, however, **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> is joined to it by any aspect, it will create friends of kings, pleasing for their physical beauty, and happy—but those who, while still in their youth, satisfy the laws of nature <note>a classical euphemism for dying</note>.

The **twenty-fifth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create sterile men without children, always wandering and burning with the desires of love, upon which they spend all their thoughts.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create men who obtain the support of their lives from herbs or the cultivation of the earth; but these men, though oppressed by perpetual labors, will be long-lived and unremarkable.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create sacred slaves <note>original: hierodulos; persons dedicated to the service of a temple</note>, temple servants, and those who sing hymns in sacred ceremonies.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, will create the gouty, who, worn out by the swelling of their feet, are always in pain.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> present or joined by any aspect, will create men who become lame after being thrown from a height. If **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> regards this place, they will die most unhappily from this misfortune.

The **thirtieth degree of Aquarius**, if found in the Ascendant, and if **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> is placed there with the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, or joined by any aspect, it will create nobles who are long-lived, upon whom all the marks of happiness are conferred in the course of time. Some will even cross the great sea for the sake of business. However, they will certainly be without children, holding their step-sons in the place of sons. Outside of these degrees of Aquarius, there rise with the sign itself the Scythe, the Wolf, the Hare, the **Lesser Dog** <note>original: <image-desc>small glyph of a dog</image-desc> minor; referring to the constellation Canis Minor</note>, and the Altar.

### BOOK EIGHT.
<meta>catchword: will make,</meta>

Those born in the **Sickle** <note>original: falce; likely referring to an asterism or group of stars shaped like a scythe</note> will be plowmen who, by cultivating the fields, will gather great abundance of grain.

Those born in the **Mouth of the Wolf** <note>original: ore lupi; referring to the constellation Lupus</note> will be dancers; but if **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bears witness, they will be miserably devoured by dogs.

Those born in the **Wolf** itself will be deceitful, thieves, cruel, and murderers, who strike both their own kin and strangers with the cruel atrocity of wild beasts; but they will die as <term>biothanati</term> <note>original: biothanati; a Greek-derived term for those who die a violent or unnatural death</note>, and their unburied bodies will be left to the wild beasts.

Those born in the **left foot of the Wolf**, with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bearing witness, will be struck by bandits and will suffer a severe weakening of their feet.

Those born in the **right foot of the Wolf** will become frenzied and die in the first stage of their life.

Those born in the **head of the Lesser Aquarius** <note>original: minoris ♒</note> will wander much through deserted places and will live within them; and perhaps some will be dedicated to the practice of fowling <note>the hunting or trapping of birds</note>.

Those born in the **right hand of the Lesser Aquarius** will be masters of horses. If, however, benevolent stars bear witness, they will be made charioteers or the King's mule-drivers.

Those born in the **belly of the Lesser Aquarius** will be cultivators of gardens, moneylenders, and hardworking, but they will die as <term>biothanati</term> <note>those who meet a violent end</note>.

Those born in the **right foot of the Lesser Aquarius** will die unfortunately in watery and damp places.

Those born in the **Altar** <note>original: ara; the constellation Ara</note> will obtain the necessities of life from sacrifices; but nevertheless, they will perish consumed by fire.

Those born in the **Pouring of the Water** <note>original: aquæ effusione; the stream of water flowing from Aquarius’s urn</note> will be wealthy from an early age and possessors of many goods, but they will squander their father’s patrimony through various forms of extravagance. They will be generous, but many people will frequently be ungrateful to them. In the course of their life, however, they will obtain the greatest increases in both inheritance and dignity, and they will see their enemies subjugated to them in every way.

Those born in the **Hare** <note>original: lepore; the constellation Lepus</note> will be poor, unhappy, fearful, and wandering, striving for their labors in vain.

### THE MYRIOGENESIS OF THE DEGREES IN PISCES. Chapter 30.

If the **first degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note> is found in the **Ascendant** <note>original: horoscopo; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, it will make people inquisitive, well-composed, and those who obtain the necessities of life from excellent resources, who take up sons from the enrollment <note>or "union"</note> of sisters or female relatives, acquired through incestuous intercourse.

If the **second degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, it will make men of a harsh spirit, suspicious, and jealous.

If the **third degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, it will make those entangled in the impure vices of lust, and polluted by the filth of harlotry, whose public life infamy always plagues.

If the **fourth degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, it will make men of effeminate character <note>original: cinaedos; a term for men who took a submissive or "unmasculine" role in sexual encounters</note>; it will make women prostitute their modesty through the passive trafficking of lust.

If the **fifth degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, and **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> and **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> are joined by any aspect, it will make them wealthy, noble, and long-lived, who obtain the support for their life from some art. These people will also be introduced to kings, and having advanced to a good old age, will die well with surviving children.

If the **sixth degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, it will make men who die being cruelly torn apart by wild beasts.

If the **seventh degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> present, it will cause them to be torn apart either by beasts on land or by fish in the water.

If the **eighth degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, with **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> and **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> present, it will make them religious, just, long-lived, and practitioners of the duties of literature, known to kings and their scribes, who will die at a great age with surviving children.

If the **nine degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, it decrees the same as we said was decreed in the eighth degree above.

If the **tenth degree of Pisces** is found in the Ascendant, with the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> well-positioned and present there, it will make [them] great...

# JULIUS FIRMICUS MATERNUS
<meta>catchword: Thirtieth</meta>

[The tenth degree of Pisces] will make them powerful and known to all, joined to kings, wandering through many lands, and destined to sail the great sea. These people will also be set over Liburnian ships <note>original: Liburnis; fast, light galleys used by the Roman navy</note> and will be granted naval command. They will be victors and superiors in battle. They will also possess the highest merit of love and favor. They will be just and religious, but always restless regarding sexual encounters with women <note>original: muliebres concubitus; often implying a lack of self-control</note>, yet they will achieve great things and obtain all they seek: but they will die a violent death <term>biothanati</term> <note>original: biothanati; a Greek-derived term used in astrology for those who die an unnatural or violent death</note> through the deceit or anger of a king.

The **eleventh degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, will make people who, torn by wild beasts in deserted places, will lose their lives; or they will die a violent death <term>biothanati</term> in marshy lands in their early youth, without children or heirs.

The **twelfth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make fishermen; but they will be prone to madness <note>original: phreneticos</note> and will die in their early youth.

The **thirteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant with **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> and **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> present, will make people wealthy and noble, obtaining their livelihood through some skill. If, however, **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> is joined to it by any aspect <note>original: radiatione; literally "radiation," referring to the planetary rays</note>, it will make merchants or perfume-sellers <note>original: pigmentarios; those who dealt in dyes, drugs, or cosmetics</note>; yet they will be wealthy and happy, and will die leaving surviving children.

The **fourteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people upon whom the highest marks of dignity are conferred; but they will be killed in watery or marshy places, or by pirates.

The **fifteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> present, will make people who wander through the deserts of the world and sail through unknown seas. For these will always be tormented by labors and will spend their entire lives on ships.

The **sixteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people wealthy and long-lived, and foremost among their kinsmen.

The **seventeenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, makes people who sing poems with sweet melody. If, however, **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is found in that same degree, they will hang themselves by a noose.

The **eighteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people bold and great eaters, but prone to illness.

The **nineteenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make orators and lawyers, distinguished by an abundance of learned speech. But if a benevolent star lends its witness <note>aligns with this point</note>, they will be in the royal court, commanding many things, and always adorned with great modesty, gravity of character, and honorable conduct, and beloved by all.

The **twentieth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people wandering through many nations; but if **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> bears witness to it, they will be captives and slaves in their early youth.

The **twenty-first degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make murderers and those easily moved to brawls by anger <note>original: bile; literally 'bile' or 'choler', the humor thought to govern anger</note>.

The **twenty-second degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people unchaste and defiled by every kind of foul lust <note>original: fœdæ ueneris; literally "foul Venus"</note>.

The **twenty-third degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make fowlers <note>original: aucupes; hunters or trappers of birds</note> and those who obtain their livelihood only from birds.

The **twenty-fourth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make people who, while sailing on the sea, end their lives there.

The **twenty-fifth degree of Pisces** <note>original: Piscium</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make goldsmiths, engravers, painters, and those who are supported by these arts.

The **twenty-sixth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> and **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> bearing witness, will make bath-attendants, menial servants <note>original: mediastinos; low-level workers, often in public baths</note>, sailors, and those entrusted with the operation of mechanical engines; but they will be unhappy and die violent deaths <term>biothanati</term>.

The **twenty-seventh degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant, will make fugitives wandering through many lands, but who perish by being pierced by a thorn.

The **twenty-eighth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant with **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> present, will make people of low status who are torn by wild beasts in marshy and watery places.

The **twenty-ninth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note>, if found in the ascendant—if **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> and **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> are placed in that same degree, and the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is well-positioned—will make people noble and wealthy, living happily throughout their entire lives, and finally passing away by a natural death.

# BOOK EIGHT
<meta>catchword: They will have</meta>

If the **thirtieth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓︎</note> is found in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: horoscopus; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, it will create people who spend their lives at sea and who, always entangled in laborious activities, lead a life of the utmost toil.

In the **extreme tail of Pisces**, that is, on the line which divides Pisces <note>original: ♓︎</note> and Aries <note>original: ♈︎</note>, if Mars <note>original: ♂</note> is present, those who are born will be <term>eunuchs</term> <note>original: apocopi; specifically referring to those who have been castrated</note> and cut off. In the northern part of Pisces, the Deer and the Hare rise. In the southern part, however, the Whale <note>original: cetus</note>, a beast of the sea, rises.

Those born in the **horns of the Deer**, if Mars <note>original: ♂</note> is present, will be placed in charge of arms and leaders of the army: fighting abroad, they will eventually die in battle.

Those born in the **mouth of the Deer** will be like the <term>Marsi</term> <note>original: Marsi; an ancient Italian people famed for their skills as snake-charmers and herbalists</note>, who track down and capture serpents, but they will die a violent death <term>biothanati</term> <note>original: biothanati; a term for those who die an unnatural or violent death</note>.

Those born in the **feet of the Deer** will be great wanderers and will eventually perish by a violent death <term>biothanata</term>.

Those born in the **Hare** <note>original: lepore</note> will be skilled pilots to whom the rudders of ships are entrusted.

Those born in the **tail of the Whale**, if Mars <note>original: ♂</note> is present, will lose their lives by a cruel death, torn apart by wild beasts.

Those born in **two parts of the Whale**, if Venus <note>original: ♀</note> and Mercury <note>original: ☿</note> are present, will be subjects of powerful men: and advancing from there, they will achieve increases in their standard of living. Others, however, will be slaves: but they will be led to great dignity by the indulgence of their patrons, through the honorable and noble merit of their service.

Those born in **three parts of the Whale** will sail and circle many lands. But if Mars <note>original: ♂</note> is found in that same part, they will die, killed by pirates.

### THE THIRD PREDICTIONS OF THE BARBARIC SPHERE. Chapter XXXI.
<note>The "Barbaric Sphere" refers to an astrological system that includes constellations and stars from non-Greek traditions, such as Egyptian, Babylonian, or Persian sources.</note>

In the sixth book, we stated that there are bright stars in many signs, shining with royal majesty of light. Therefore, I shall now take care to explain in a similar way what the ascendant <note>original: horoscopus</note> decrees in those parts where bright stars are found, just as we spoke concerning the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> in that same sixth book.

In the **eleventh degree of Aries** <note>original: ♈︎</note>, a bright star is shown; those born in this degree, if Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> is present or joined to it by a <term>trine</term> aspect <note>original: trigonica radiatione; an auspicious astrological angle of 120 degrees</note>, will be great and powerful leaders, and friends of kings, possessing much and grand land, uplifted by the honorable testimony of their reputation, and will be those who die a natural death.

In the **horns of Taurus**, that is, in its thirtieth degree, there is a bright star; those born in this degree will be kings or leaders.

Those born in the **right horn of Taurus** <note>original: ♉︎</note> will be great princes, to whom command over the navy and infantry is committed; they will be fearsome, hardworking, and liberators of many cities from the sieges of wars. These will be only children and childless, to whom public titles, images, and statues are decreed: but later they will die from the offense of kings. Our text has already shown you in which star Mars <note>original: ♂</note> decrees these same things.

In the **second degree of Leo** <note>original: ♌︎</note>, a clear star is found; those born in this degree will be powerful kings, possessing a double kingdom: but whenever Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> and Mars <note>original: ♂</note> come to this same star, battles will be stirred up against them.

In the **thirteenth degree of Scorpio** <note>original: ♏︎</note>, there is a clear star; those born in this degree, if the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is present and bright, will be powerful, having great powers of life and death, and to whom the greatest part of the empire is committed.

In the **nineteenth degree of Scorpio** <note>original: ♏︎</note>, there is likewise a clear star; those born in this degree, if the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is present and well-placed, will be powerful. If Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> is joined to it by a favorable aspect, they will be very close to the king, possessing divine honors, excellent, and good: but they may be negligent for a time, and death will come to them from the king's indignation.

In the **twenty-second degree of Sagittarius** <note>original: ♐︎</note>, there are some clear stars; those born in these, with Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> positioned in that same sign, will be great and powerful, possessing much land, leading armies of infantry and cavalry, and to whom naval battle is entrusted. They will also be victors in all battles, subjugating barbarians: they will indeed rebuild some cities and destroy others.

The author, Julius Firmicus Maternus, provides a summary of his method—the balancing of planetary influences—and ends with a solemn plea to his patron, Mavortius Lollianus, to keep the sacred knowledge of astrology secret from the uninitiated.</meta>

They will have a wife with defects in her private parts; but they themselves, with surviving children, will die fighting bravely in battle. <note>This continues the prediction for those born under the "feet of the Deer" from the previous page.</note>

In the **third degree of Capricorn** <note>original: ♑</note> is a bright star. If Mars <note>original: ♂</note> is placed in this same sign and the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is well positioned, those born will be great and powerful, holding the greatest power of life and death. However, they will be cruel, delighting in much slaughter; yet they will be leaders of armies, clever, high-minded, and bold, though they will ultimately die in war.

In the **first degree of Aquarius** <note>original: ♒</note> is a bright star. If Jupiter <note>original: ♃</note> and Saturn <note>original: ♄</note> are joined by a prosperous <term>aspect</term> <note>original: radiatione; literally "radiation," referring to the geometric angles planets make with one another</note>, and the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is well placed, those born will be great and glorious kings, religious, just, and long-lived. They are also granted the highest command of power with supreme glory even in their youth.

In the **tenth degree of Pisces** <note>original: ♓</note> is a bright star, specifically in the Southern Fish <note>likely the star Fomalhaut</note>. When Venus <note>original: ♀</note> is present there and the Moon <note>original: ☽</note> is well arranged, those born will be great and known to kings; they will travel through many lands and sail across the great sea. To these people shall be entrusted the command of <term>Liburnian</term> <note>original: Liburneum; a type of fast, light galley used by the Roman navy</note> and naval fleets. They will be victors in battles, loved by all, just, and religious—yet prone to sexual relations with women. Though they will achieve many great things and command superior forces, they will ultimately die, condemned by the king’s hatred or anger. This is what the **Barbaric Sphere** <note>original: sphaera barbarica; a tradition of astrology that incorporated Egyptian, Babylonian, and other non-Greek star maps</note> pronounces regarding individual degrees, which we have explained to you as clearly as possible.

### GENERAL SUMMARY OF THE ENTIRE WORK. Chapter XXXII.

You will not be able to explain a <term>birth chart</term> <note>original: genituram</note> completely unless everything has been compared with the balanced mixtures and traditions of the stars—as you remember us having said most frequently. For when the cold of other stars is placed opposite the fiery stars, and the ice of the cold is tempered by the blazing heat of the fire, this mixture is made equal by reason. Therefore, all things must be gathered according to the powers of the locations and the stars. For a star suffers a loss of its power when it is placed in <term>debilitated</term> <note>original: deiectis; "fallen" or weak positions</note> or low places. However, it rejoices (as we have frequently said) when placed in a principal location: first in its <term>exaltation</term> <note>original: altitudine; the sign where a planet's influence is strongest</note>, and second in its <term>bounds</term> <note>original: finibus; specific sections of a sign ruled by different planets</note>. When all things have been gathered thus by precise calculation, we must inspect the whole body of the birth chart, so that by gathering the fates of men from the powers of all the stars, we can explain whatever has been decreed with true judgments.

### THE FINAL CONCLUSION OF THE ENTIRE WORK. Chapter XXXIII.

Accept therefore, **Mavortius**, our pride, these seven books which we promised you (albeit with great trepidation of spirit), composed according to the order and number of the seven planets. For the first book only undertook the defense of our advocacy; in the remaining books, we have handed down the discipline of a new work to the Roman people. You, however, having been reached by our previous warning and reminded by the religious authority of your oath, guard these books with a pure spirit and a pure mind, lest the knowledge of this work be made known to unskilled and sacrilegious ears. 

For the nature of divinity wished to be hidden and concealed by many coverings from the beginning, so that access would not be easy for everyone, nor would the origin of its majesty be spread abroad if revealed to all. It is appropriate for us to do this also in these books: namely, that their reading should be open only to the religious, but always denied to the profane and sacrilegious, lest we pollute the secrets of the ancients that ought to be hidden with wicked publications. Therefore, hand these down only to your sons, whom you have instructed from an early age in every duty of virtue; hand them also to your friends, whom a faithful bond of love has joined to you, and whom you know to follow the examples of your virtue. 

Let it suffice that we have published the art of these books for you alone, which we entrust to you, believe in you, and consecrate to you. You, the true interpreter, the faithful guardian, the religious priest, you alone by the merit of your virtues will be able to adorn that which we have completed with wakeful care and equal labor of mind and body, and with the greatest anxiety and trepidation.

### THE END 
### OF THE BOOKS ON ASTROLOGY 
### BY JULIUS MATERNUS JUNIOR SICULUS, 
### OF SENATORIAL RANK, 
### TO MAVORTIUS LOLLIANVUM,

# THE FOUR BOOKS OF CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY OF PELUSIUM,
## THE ALEXANDRIAN.
### PREFACE.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'R' depicting a figure (possibly a scholar) pointing upwards at celestial bodies.</image-desc>
OF THE MATTERS, Syrus <note>original: "Iesure," a likely typographical error or variant for "Syre," the name of the person to whom Ptolemy dedicated his works</note>, in which the perfection of the science of prediction regarding the stars consists, we find that there are two great and principal types. One of these, which comes first and is more powerful, is the science that demonstrates the configurations of the sun and moon, as well as the five <term>wandering stars</term> <note>original: "stellarum erraticarum," referring to the planets known in antiquity: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>; it is clear that these occur because of their own movements, and by comparing them to one another and to the earth. The other science is that by which the changes and effects that happen are explained—those which are fulfilled because of the natural configurations of their orbits upon the things that they surround. But since the first of these two is a science in its own right, unmixed with the other, it is necessary that the investigator of science seek it out and learn it for its own sake, and gather its fruit here, even if he does not learn the second science. Since, therefore, it is clear that this is the case, the volume concerning the first science has already been completed by us for you, in which we proceeded as rationally as was within our power. In this book, we shall explain the second science—which is by no means explainable by itself—just as <term>physical reason</term> <note>original: "ratio physica," meaning the laws of natural science or physics</note> requires. It is necessary, however, for its investigator to follow this intention so that he may proceed along a straight and truthful path. Yet he should not wish to compare the method of reaching this science to the method by which the other is reached (which is always of one and the same kind); for he will disparage and reject this science if he compares them. For the brief duration of the accidents of matter, in which this science is occupied, is the occasion for the change in this second science. For this matter never persists in the same state: therefore, one attains a perfect knowledge of this science only with great difficulty. For this reason, however, it should not be cast aside by anyone out of laziness; rather, one should strive to know from it what is possible to be known. It is indeed plain that that which surrounds us is the cause of most of the accidents and changes happening in this world. However, since it is the habit of many to despise things that are difficult to investigate, some, in their blindness of mind and lack of skill, accused and cast aside the first part of the science, while others did the same to the second. Perhaps the occasion that distracts them toward these views is this: because they are either like those who, because they cannot know something due to its extreme difficulty, do not believe others can know it at all; or perhaps, like those who, even if they are able to know, reject it because it easily slips from the memory. And so for these reasons, despising this science, they regarded it as nothing. We, however, before we reveal the particulars of this science, will strive to prove briefly what is contained in it, what can be known of the science of prediction, and what fruit follows from it. And from these two points we shall begin to explain how much it is that we can attain from this science.

### THE METHOD OF ARRIVING AT THE SCIENCE 
### of prediction. Chapter II.

<image-desc>A decorative initial 'V' showing a face or mask-like ornament.</image-desc>
We believe that no one doubts that a certain power exists in the matter of the <term>ether</term> <note>original: "alathir," a Latinized form of the Greek "aither," the fifth element or celestial substance</note> which, reaching down as far as earthly things, compels—indeed forces—them to change. Furthermore, these same things naturally undergo change starting from the two primary materials placed beneath the lunar circle, which are fire and air; these the motion of the ether surrounds and changes, and these in turn surround the rest—namely water and earth—and all the plants within them, changing them by their own changes. This is because the sun and the air act upon all earthly things. And alterations come not only from the four seasons of the year—such as in the conception of living creatures, the fruits of trees, the flooding of waters, and the changes of bodies—but also from the daily revolution in which it is daily contained. For because of this revolution, the earth is heated and cooled, dried and moistened in one and the same way, on account of similar figures in appearance, which are formed according to their positions from the <term>zenith</term> <note>original: "zenith nostrorum capitum," the point directly above our heads</note>. Likewise from the moon also, because it is nearer to the earth, a great power is attributed to us, by which many...

changes are bestowed upon animate and inanimate things. For the increases and decreases of rivers happen according to the waning and waxing of the moon. The seas also change during its rising and setting. Likewise, plants and animals, in whole or in part, enter into growth or decline with its increase or decrease. The revolution of the <term>wandering stars</term> <note>planets</note> and the fixed stars also produces heat, winds, and snow in the air surrounding us in many ways. Therefore, according to their <term>complexion</term> <note>original: "complexionem," referring to the specific mixture of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry</note>, alterations happen to the things placed upon the earth. And according to their configurations relative to each other, which they receive from their conjunctions and the mixing of their powers, various changes in things occur. Beyond this, the efficacy of the sun always prevails over the rest in the variations of things that proceed in an orderly manner. 

Others indeed sometimes assist it, and sometimes hinder it, which happens most evidently and frequently with the moon, as in conjunction, the <term>dichotomy</term> <note>original: "dicothomitate," referring to the moon's quarter phases when it appears cut in half</note>, and the full moon. In other stars, this happens in a longer span of time and with a more hidden significance, according to their times of concealment and appearance, and their deviation toward any latitude. Since, therefore, the work of the stars is such, it is necessary that what they perform by their motions should 
<margin>The power of the stars</margin>
appear not only in obvious things, but also in the very beginning of the growth of seeds and fruits, so that their forms and modes are designated by the qualities of the air at that very hour. From this, it follows that experienced farmers and keepers of livestock, at the hour of animal mating and the sowing of seeds, perceive what is to come through the blowing of the winds. We also know generally that universal matters, which are declared through the configurations of the sun, moon, and stars, are plain and open. For those unskilled in this art often recognize their prognostications through experiments with the sun. Those effects of the stars which occur with the greatest force, and which are accustomed to happen naturally, are predicted by the unlearned, and even by some animals. For we see many animals signify the variations of the seasons and changes in the winds—these are called "signs." Because the cause of these signs is most often the sun, we do not doubt that they happen. 

But those things which happen with lesser force are only predicted by those with frequent experience, such as the individual changes of winter air and long-term winds by sailors. It is clear that these occur through the configurations of the moon and fixed stars with the sun. But because they have been ignorant of the locations of the stars, the hours of the aforementioned events, and the motions of the wandering stars—which greatly assist the knowledge of the things mentioned—they have many times been deceived in this science. Since this is so, if someone has knowledge of the motions of all the stars, and of the sun and moon, so that he truly knows the locations and hours in which their configurations are formed, and if he does not forget their natures, which he has learned through the experiments of many ages—even if he does not know their substantial natures, but knows the effects they perform, such as the sun heating and the moon moistening, and similarly for the rest—and if he is capable of knowing this in a natural way, and discovers the mode of significance in their mixing through good estimation: what could then prevent him from always recognizing future changes of the air, so that he may predict that it will be now warmer, now more moist? He will likewise be able, through the qualities of the air, to perceive the qualities of the natures of all men, so that he may discern that the qualities of body and soul will turn out in such and such a way, and perceive their future events that will happen at certain hours. Furthermore, when the surrounding air and the nature of bodies are in such and such a state, he will predict what action is suitable for health and the improvement of bodies; and when it is the opposite, he will judge the opposite. 

From the things aforesaid, therefore, and others like them, it is manifest that we can reach this work. Those who have said this science is to be blamed and set aside have had some reasons, though frivolous ones. The first of these is the great deception of those who do not attend to this science with authority, since to inspect it requires great industry in many ways. Therefore, many have thought that things happen by chance, even when this science was true. This, however, is an unsuitable reason for them, because this deception is not due to the weakness of this art, but to the rashness of those inspecting it...
