### ON THE SIMILARITY OF REGIONS WITH THE TRIPLI-
### cities and stars. Chapter III.

**S**ince, therefore, the figures of the triplicities <note>A "triplicity" is a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water.</note> which are formed in the circle of the signs are four, as was shown in the preceding sections: we have said that the triplicity of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius is between the north and the west, whose primary lord is Jupiter, for he is northern; Mars is associated with him in lordship, since he is western. The triplicity of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn is between the south and the east, whose primary lord is Venus, because she is southern, and Saturn is associated with her in lordship, for he is eastern. The triplicity of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius is between the north and the east, whose primary lord is Saturn, since he is eastern, and Jupiter is associated with him in lordship, for he is northern. Also, the triplicity of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces is between the south and the west, whose primary lord is Mars, for he is western, to whom Venus is associated in lordship, because she is southern. Since these things are so, the place of our habitation is divided into four parts by the line that passes through our sea <note>the Mediterranean</note>, and begins from the place called the passage of Hercules <note>the Strait of Gibraltar</note>, and reaches to the river called the Citicon <note>likely the Oxus or Jaxartes river in Central Asia</note>, and is on the mountain ridge that follows it from the eastern part; and by this line is divided that which is between the north and the south. Its length, however, is divided by the line that passes through the western river, and through the sea which is called Aggiõ Nabartis <note>possibly the Caspian or a related northern sea</note>, and through the marsh called Mantis <note>the Sea of Azov</note>; and this line divides that which is between the east and the west. These four quarters agree in their arrangement with the triplicities. Therefore, the first habitable quarter, which is placed between the north and the west, is in that part of the lands called Felitogalatiæ <note>the lands of the Celts and Gauls</note>, and these are the lands generally called Europe. The second quarter, however, placed in opposition to that one between the south and the east, is in the part of the lands called the eastern Ithosiæ <note>likely Ethiopia or southern India</note>, and is the southern part of the lands called Greater Asia. The third quarter, established between the north and the east, is situated in the part of the lands called Sesume <note>Scythia or Northern Asia</note>, and is in the northern part of Greater Asia. The fourth quarter, which is placed in opposition to this between the blowing of the western and southern winds, is ordered in the part of the lands called
<margin>Otherwise the deserts of Libya.</margin>

<margin>Otherwise Inoquia.</margin>

The same will undoubtedly happen in the other quarters, so that each one of these quarters is likened to two triplicities opposite to one another. Also, its parts which are around the middle of the earth are appropriated to that to which that part is near, which also is appropriated in contrast to that which that quarter generally approaches. All these stars act upon the regions where they are positioned in direct alignment, specifically those which are arranged on one of the circles passing through the two poles of the zodiac. Associated with these in the significance of their "mothers" <note>likely referring to the foundational or "root" charts of cities</note> are those places where the **Sun** and **Moon** were at the beginning of the founding of those mother-cities, as well as the positions of the **angles** <note>the four primary points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli</note>, and especially the angle of the **ascendant**, just as in individual births. But in those cities where the time of founding is unknown, we must observe the position of the **Midheaven** <note>the highest point in a birth chart, representing authority and public life</note> in the birth chart of the king who ruled at the time they were founded.

### HOW THE PROGNOSTIC SCIENCE
### of general future events is reached. Chapter IV.

After this observation of the aforementioned things, it is necessary that we follow through in explaining how we may know how to forecast universal future events in a general way; and we shall begin with those future things which happen generally to lands and regions. The first account of these—and the more powerful cause of these accidents—occurs only from the **eclipses** of the Sun and Moon, their conjunctions <note>when they meet</note> and their preventions <note>full moons</note>, as well as from the places of the motions of the **planets** at those very hours. Some of these universal prognostications concern the **place**, that is, identifying in which of the regions and lands the significations of a particular eclipse will occur. I also speak of the **stations of the wandering stars** <note>the planets</note> at any given time—namely **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**—when they are stationary and their significations are observed. Some indeed concern the **time**, that is, the hour of the signification and the quantity of its duration must be foreknown. Some concern the **genus**, that is, we must know in what class or category the future accidents will happen. Some also concern the **species** of the future event, and this is the final part, through which we perceive the specific manner of how the future event will be.

### ON THE KNOWLEDGE OF REGIONS IN WHICH
### future accidents will occur. Chapter V.

The first thing we proposed to narrate is the first type of prognostic speech, namely concerning the **place**: here we will indicate how we can arrive at its knowledge. In the eclipse conjunctions and preventions of the **Sun** and **Moon**, and especially in that which is most apparent, we must observe the place of the eclipse in the zodiac. Also, we must observe the regions that are likened to that **triplicity** <note>the group of three signs belonging to the same element</note>. We must also observe the lands that are likened to the sign of the eclipse, either through the **ascendant** of the hour of their founding and through the positions of the **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> at that hour, or through the position of the **Midheaven** in the birth chart of the ruler who dominated them at that time. It must also be known that in whatever regions or lands we find this similarity which we have described, the future significations will happen in all of them, especially in that region which is likened to the sign of the eclipse itself and in which the eclipse is seen above the earth.

### CONCERNING THE NATURE OF FUTURE EVENTS. Chapter VII.

<margin>The Lord of the eclipse.</margin>

The third type of prognostic is that through which we grasp in what *kind* or *genus* the future event will happen: this is indicated by the qualities and figures which are proper to the signs in which the location of the eclipse is found, and also the signs in which the **planets** and **fixed stars** <note>original: "erraticae & non erraticae ... stellae"</note> are positioned, which govern the sign of the eclipse and the sign of the preceding "prevention" <note>syzygy</note>. The <term>almudhebir</term> <note>From the Arabic *al-mudabbir*, meaning the "Governor" or "Ruler" of the chart</note> shall be known from the wandering stars of these two locations, as we teach by describing here. Therefore, that star which has many authorities in the two aforementioned locations—that is, in the location of the eclipse and in the other location of the angle of the preceding eclipse according to the <term>alicitital</term> <note>likely a corruption of a term for planetary strength or dignity</note>, and according to this: that it rules those houses, <term>triplicities</term> <note>groups of three signs belonging to the same element</note>, exaltations, and terms—that star alone shall be the **almudhebir**. If we do not find one star that rules both the location of the eclipse and the angle, we must find two stars having more authorities in these two locations, as we said before, and then the **lord of the eclipse** is to be preferred. But if more than two stars have equal authorities in these two locations, we shall choose in the arrangement and prefer the stronger: concerning which, it is judged more fitting if it is in an angle, or which is of stronger effect, or which more fits its <term>haiz</term> <note>an astrological condition where a planet is in a sign/sect compatible with its nature</note>. And with this, we shall again take the arrangement of the fixed stars thus: from the brightest stars, we shall observe that which first opened the eclipse with the location of the eclipse in the angle that preceded. This will be understood from those things we said in our first book, in which we described the nine modes of the fellowship of the figures which appear to the stars. For again, we shall observe the star which, at the hour of the eclipse, was with the angle of the ascendant or with the angle of the mid-heaven <note>original: "medii coeli"</note>, namely with that of those two angles which follows the location of the eclipse. After we have grasped the stars which we observe in such a way to know the causes of the future, we will add the observation of the form of the sign in which the eclipse is, and the sign in which the stars are that hold the arrangement; since the knowledge of the *kind* in which the future event will happen cannot be had, except through the properties of the qualities of these aforementioned locations. # BOOK TWO.

Regarding those stars that are fixed <note>original: "stellas non erraticas" — stars that do not "wander" like planets</note>, when they are arranged in the likeness of a human form, the events that are signified will happen to the human race. If they represent the figure of a wild animal, or are likened to four-legged creatures, the events will be found among animals similar to them. If they are likened to the forms of creeping things <note>reptiles and insects</note>, they will affect serpents and similar creatures. Likewise, if they bear the likeness of savage beasts, the future event will occur among the wild beasts that harm humans; and if they represent the forms of domestic animals, it will be found among the domestic animals that humans use and by which they are helped at all times of their lives—there is no doubt about this—specifically in each species of these animals, such as horses, oxen, sheep, and similar livestock.

Furthermore, whatever is placed among the figures of wild animals toward the northern part of the sky specifically signifies sudden changes in the earth. However, what is figured toward the southern part shows alterations of the air that bring fear to no one. For when the locations of the stars that hold dominion are in winged figures, such as **Virgo**, **Sagittarius**, the **Hen** <note>the constellation Cygnus</note>, the **Flying Vulture** <note>the constellation Aquila</note>, and similar ones, it is manifest that the future event will happen to winged creatures, and especially to those birds that are eaten by humans. 

If it occurs in the figures of swimming animals, it will happen to fish and all aquatic creatures. For if it is in figures representing sea animals, such as **Cancer**, **Capricorn**, and the **Dolphin**, the future will affect sea creatures and the ships of the ocean. But if it is in the figures of river animals, such as **Aquarius** and **Pisces**, it will appear in the animals of rivers and springs. And if it is in the figure of a ship <note>the constellation Argo Navis</note>, it will be seen in both kinds. 

Similarly, if it is in any of the solstitial or equinoctial signs, the significance will generally be in the matters of the air and in the seasons appropriate to each of them. Their significations will appear specifically in those things that grow from the earth. For when it is in the spring equinoctial sign <note>Aries</note>, their significations will be found in the fruits of trees when they begin to sprout, such as in vineyards, fig trees, and their contemporaries. If it is in the summer solstitial sign <note>Cancer</note>, they signify that future events will happen to fruits when they are gathered and stored—except in the regions of Egypt, where the specific significations will be shown in the rising of the Nile. 

If, however, it is in the autumn equinoctial sign <note>Libra</note>, the significations will be in seeds when they are sown, and in herbs, and similar things. But if they are in the winter solstitial sign <note>Capricorn</note>, their significations will occur in vegetables and in what appears from birds and fish. 

Likewise, when they are in any of the equinoctial signs, they signify that future events will happen in churches <note>original: "ecclesijs" — while this means "churches" in the translator's era, in the original Greek context it referred to public assemblies or temples</note> and in houses established for the honor of God. If, indeed, they are in any of the solstitial signs, they will judge the changes regarding the dead remaining in that region. If they are in fixed signs, they will demonstrate that the future affects foundations and buildings. And if they are in common signs <note>original: "signis communibus" — today called "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, they prefigure that the future will happen to men and kings. 

Similarly, when the hour of the eclipse is in places specifically situated toward the East, they will designate that the future happens to fruits, to those in their youth, and to foundations. If it is in the Mid-heaven <note>the highest point of the sky</note>, the significations will appear in churches, among those in power, and those who are middle-aged. If it is in the West, the signified events will happen to customs, variations of behavior, the elderly, and also the dead. 

The knowledge of the magnitude of the portion in which the future events of the subject kind will appear is grasped from the quantity of the eclipse's darkness, and from the proportion of the stars (which are the causes of the future) to the location of the eclipse. For if they are in evening figures during a solar eclipse, or in morning figures during a lunar eclipse, the future will happen to a smaller portion of that kind; and when they are in opposition across the diameter, half of that kind will be embraced by the future event. If, however, they are in morning figures during a solar eclipse, but in evening figures during a lunar eclipse, they signify that the future will happen to the greater part.

They will suffer from fires, the killing of men, robberies, and the cutting off of roads <note>highway robbery or blockades</note>. In the air, there will be extreme heat, as well as hot and destructive winds that weaken bodies, lightning, and a scarcity of rain. At sea, there will be sudden sinkings of ships due to clashing winds, lightning, or similar events. In the rivers, there will be a lowering of water levels, the drying up of springs, and a loss of drinkable water. Regarding things for human use—namely animals and plants—there will be scarcity and damage to crops, either because they are scorched by heat, or by locusts, or due to the destruction brought upon them by winds, or because they are burned even within their storehouses.

<margin>Venus</margin>
When **Venus** alone is the mistress of the disposition, she will generally act in the same way as Jupiter, but in addition, she will exert some influence over sexual matters <note>original: "venereos actus," relating to the goddess Venus and physical desire</note>. Her specific, particular work among humans includes high rank, honors, cheerfulness, improvement of status, a good marriage, many children, the comforts of all marital affairs, the increase of wealth, pure and clean conduct, a law-abiding spirit, a fit physique, and connection to kings and the kinship of the powerful. In the qualities of the air, however, there will be winds with a temperate and humid nature, and much food will be available; the air will be pleasant and clear. As for the waters, there will be many rains that help things to grow. Ships will also be safe while sailing the sea; profits will be made in trade, and rivers will increase and be full. The animals used by humans and the fruits of the earth will grow, improve, and thrive.

<margin>Mercury</margin>
When **Mercury** alone is the master of the disposition, he will generally be mixed like the other stars and will take on their nature. His own specific work is the movement of things more so than the other stars, and his influence on future events involving humans is very sharp. Perhaps people will also be of a subtle wit in what they wish to do. Roadblocks, robberies, and plundering will happen to them. In sea travels, when he is associated with misfortunes, there will be difficulty. He is also the cause of "dry" illnesses, as well as daily fevers, coughs, vomiting, and consumption <note>original: "phthisis," a historical term for tuberculosis or wasting diseases</note>. He influences the office of divine divination and things that are to come in the inheritances of houses of prayer <note>temples or churches</note>, and the changing of customs and laws, depending on his mixture with the other stars. Because his complexion <note>the balance of his physical qualities</note> is dry and his movements are swift due to his closeness to the sun, and because his retrogradations <note>the appearance of a planet moving backward in the sky</note> are frequent in his orbit, he stirs up turbulent, sudden, and quickly-changing winds in the air, as well as thunder, lightning, openings in the earth, earthquakes, and flashes of light. Perhaps because of these things mentioned above, damage will occur to the animals and plants that humans use most. Decreases in the water levels of rivers will occur at the hours of his setting, but they will increase at the hours of his rising. Each of the planets, therefore, will operate when it is in its own natural state. But when they are mixed with one another, their specific work will arise from the different species of mixtures, according to their shared configurations, the differences of the signs, and their appearance with respect to the sun. In this way, his work will be mixed with the natures that are associated with his own. Therefore, since a description of the specific work resulting from every kind of mixture would be unexplainable and impossible—and since a description of all these things can generally be understood in many ways—one must leave these specific details to further study; one ought to inquire into and observe the particulars within them. We must observe these likenesses of the stars, through which future events happen, alongside the regions and lands in which they signify that these things will occur.

CLAUDE PTOLEMY'S QUADRIPARTITUM <note>The "Four-Part Work," also known as the Tetrabiblos, the foundational text of Western astrology.</note>

We ought to proceed in this manner: When the stars are favorable and harmonize with the places where future events will occur, and if those stars are in their proper *hayz* <term>from the Arabic 'hayz,' referring to a planet being in its preferred celestial "sect" or dignity</term>—meaning no contrary *hayz* rises above them—then the specific work of their own natures will have greater strength. Conversely, if they do not harmonize with those places, and stars of a contrary nature rise above them, their strength will be diminished. However, when the temperament of the stars is harmful and they rule over a future event, if they harmonize with the places where those events will occur, and if stars of a contrary *hayz* rise above them, they will alleviate the harm. But if the arrangement of the regions does not match them, and the stars that harmonize with those regions do not rise above them, the work of their harmful temperament will manifest more strongly. General accidents <note>In this context, "accidents" refers to events or occurrences rather than mishaps.</note> happen most frequently to people in whose birth charts the "necessary places"—that is, the places where the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> and the angles <note>The four cardinal points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note> are located—coincide with the locations of general events, such as the places of eclipses or the points opposite them. This will be more severe and most difficult to guard against when those same parts of the eclipse locations are the same parts of the locations of one of the luminaries in the birth chart; and following this, when those parts are directly opposite them.

## ON THE COLORS OF AN ECLIPSE, AND ON TAILED 
### stars, and things similar to them. Chapter IX.

<margin>Comets.</margin>
In regard to future universal events, we should observe the colors appearing at the hour of an eclipse—that is, the colors of the luminaries themselves and of the things seen around them, such as those called *haleši* and *halela* <note>original: "haleši, halela," likely referring to halos, parhelia (sundogs), or other atmospheric optical phenomena</note> and similar things. Thus, when they are black or somewhat greenish, they signify those things we have said imitate the nature of Saturn. When they are white, they are said to signify the nature of Jupiter. If they lean toward redness, they designate things belonging to the nature of Mars. If they appear golden in color, they indicate things following the nature of Venus. But if they are of diverse colors, they signify things belonging to the nature of Mercury. Furthermore, if that color embraces the entire body of the luminary or the phenomena around it, the future event will happen in the greater part of the regions; but if it occupies only one part of the luminary or its surroundings, the event will occur only in that part which is in the direct path of the section where the color appeared. Likewise, we should observe "tailed stars" <note>Comets</note> that appear at the hour of an eclipse or at another time, as well as other future universal signs, such as those called *haleši*, *abboca*, and *thalhaueni* <note>Transliterations of Arabic terms for meteors or atmospheric displays</note>, whose natures are similar to the Martian and Mercurial natures we described before. these bring about battles, fires, and conditions that cause things to be set in motion, as well as the accidents that happen because of them. We will recognize the places where future events will happen from their positions in the circle of the signs <note>The Zodiac</note> and from the places that are in the direct path of the tailed star. We can also grasp the type of the future significance and its underlying nature from the form of that occurrence appearing then. From the duration of time that the occurrence appears, we shall know the span of the future event. From their affinity with the Sun, the hour at which the future event begins will be indicated. For when they appear more in the morning, their future event will happen suddenly; when they appear more in the evening, their future event will arrive slowly.

### BOOK TWO

...to doubt these places, because it is unknown which of these four is more suitable to be put forward first. For according to a flat circular nature, none of them precedes another such that it is more fit for beginning than any other. However, those who have attempted to treat this in their books have placed these four seasons in different ways and established each one of them as the starting point, led to this by a convenient reasoning and the effects of their nature. For each of these seasons has something specific to it
<margin>The four seasons of the year.</margin>
by which we ought to judge it to be the beginning of a new year. Indeed, for this reason they placed the beginning at the **vernal equinox** <note>The spring equinox, occurring around March 21st.</note>, because in it the day begins to exceed the night, and because it is moist; and a moist nature is prevalent in the beginning of every thing when it is first procreated, as we have shown in what came before. However, the **summer solstice** is placed as the starting point because in it the day is completed and reaches its furthest length; and because during it the flooding of the Nile occurs among the Egyptians, and in it rises
<margin>Otherwise, al-Habor</margin>
the **Dog Star** <note>original: "afchere algemenia," a Latinization of the Arabic *Al-Shi'ra al-Yamaniyya*, referring to the star Sirius.</note>. And the **autumnal equinox** was taken as the beginning because in it is the collection of all fruits, and those things which are to come begin to be sown in it. Finally, the **winter solstice** is established as the beginning because, after the shortening of the days, the lengthening of those days begins within it. And what we have found to be more suitable and in accord with natural reason in the observation of the year’s affairs is the observation of these four beginnings, as well as the **conjunctions** and **oppositions** <term>New Moons (conjunctions) and Full Moons (oppositions/preventions) of the Sun and Moon</term> which occurred near and preceding these seasons. This is especially true of those in which there were eclipses, so that through the beginning found by the Sun’s presence in **Aries**, we may know the quality of spring; through the beginning found from its presence in **Cancer**, the quality of summer; through the beginning known from its entry into **Libra**, the quality of autumn; and the beginning taken from its entry into **Capricorn** demonstrates the quality of winter. This is because the general qualities of the seasons and all their modes exist only through the Sun—the knowledge of which qualities is anticipated not only by experts in the sciences <note>original: "doctrinalium expertores," referring to those skilled in the quadrivium or mathematical sciences.</note>, but even by others. It is also suitable for this knowledge to observe the properties of the **signs** <note>The constellations of the zodiac.</note>, through which we may signify the blowing of the winds, and generally observe their entire nature. We shall signify the variations of increase or decrease happening at certain hours from the conjunctions and oppositions that occur after the aforementioned points, and from the fellowship of the **wandering stars** <term>the planets</term> with them in the general figures. We shall designate specific matters from the conjunctions and oppositions of the Sun and Moon that occur in each of the signs and from the locations of the stars. This is what can be called the observation of the months.

## SECOND BOOK.

In what we shall discuss, it is necessary to observe the specific indicators. Therefore, when a conjunction occurs near a solstitial or equinoctial point, we shall observe the conjunctions that preceded it until that same quarter of the year is completed; and when a **prevention** <note>original: *praeventio*, referring to the full moon or opposition occurring before a conjunction.</note> occurs near any of these points, we shall attend to the preventions until that same quarter is finished. Likewise, we must observe the angles and the stars of each of the aforementioned places of the **Almudhebir** <term>Almudhebir: An Arabic-derived term for the 'governor' or planetary ruler that dominates a specific celestial chart.</term>, so that we may investigate the appearance of nearby stars, and the **application** <note>original: *alictifal*</note> and **separation** <note>original: *alinsiref*</note> of the wandering stars <note>The planets.</note>, as well as the properties and qualities of those stars and the specific winds they move, and also the parts of the signs in which they are located. Furthermore, we shall observe toward which wind directions the latitude of the Moon declines when it has moved away from the **Zodiac** <note>original: *Zodiaco*</note> circle, so that in the majority of cases, through all these things, we may foreknow what will prevail in the quality of the months and their wind-blasts.

<margin>Third</margin>
The third method, however, is that we observe the stronger significator, which indicates the weakness or strength of the matter. This is found from the fellowship of the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> in particular figures, not only in the figures of conjunction and prevention, but also in those detected in the **dichotomy** <term>dichotomy: The 'half-moon' phase, or the first and third quarters.</term> of the Moon. The beginning of a change will more frequently occur three days before the Moon is with the Sun; and perhaps this work will last three days, occurring over an equal length of time. Likewise, it is detected from the fellowships of those two luminaries with the wandering stars, in these or other qualities, such as in the **trine** <note>A 120-degree aspect.</note> and **sextile** <note>A 60-degree aspect.</note>, and because these follow a natural order. We shall arrive at the quality of the variation when the natural similarities held by the signs and the stars being observed are imitated by the surrounding air and the winds. Truly, the strength of these particular qualities, which occurs daily, will specifically be when a wandering star of greater clarity and stronger influence appears in the morning or evening, in the east or west, according to its affinity with the Sun; for this, in most cases, changes and alters particular qualities toward their own natures. Likewise, this will be no less the case when the luminaries are in any of the **angles** <note>The cardinal points of the astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Lower Midheaven.</note>. For the weaknesses and strengths of the qualities of each hour will happen when the luminaries have proceeded into these places. Just as the tides <note>original: *accessus & recessus*, literally 'access and retreat'.</note> are proven to occur when the Moon is in these angles, the change in the disposition of the winds specifically does not occur except during the course of the two luminaries toward these cardines <note>The four hinges or corners of the sky.</note>, and their change is toward the wind to which the latitude of the Moon declines. In every place, however, we must know that the first general occasion is stronger. Those that follow are the occasions of particular accidents, because the work is most certainly verified and corroborated when the stars of general natures are associated with the **Almudhebir** <note>The planetary governor.</note> in the figure of particular natures.

### ON INDICATIONS TAKEN FROM OTHER SIGNS. Chapter XIII.

The signs which are around the Sun, Moon, and stars are indeed useful in the prognostication of particular indications. It is appropriate to observe that which occurs from these signs: knowledge of diurnal qualities must be investigated when the Sun rises, while knowledge of nocturnal qualities must be searched out when it sets. To know the qualities of spaces that are prolonged, we shall consider the hours of the fellowships of the luminaries in the figure, because the quality that exists from that hour until the hour in which the Moon is in the figure that follows it indicates the majority of the outcome. 

<margin>Prognostications of the seasons from the Sun.</margin>

<margin>Signs of storms.</margin>
If these occur, they will indicate wintry weather and rains. Likewise, regarding the Moon, we must observe her position on the day three days before her **conjunction** <note>original: *coniunctionem*, the New Moon</note>, as well as three days before her **opposition** <note>original: *praeventionem*, the Full Moon</note>, and three days before her **dichotomy** <note>original: *dicothomitatem*, the half-moon phases</note>, and also three hours after these times. When she appears, if she seems slender, clear, and bright, and there is nothing surrounding her, it will signify clear weather. But if she is slender and reddish, and all that is not illuminated by her appears clear and seems almost to move, it will signify that blasts of wind are coming from the direction toward which she herself leans. However, if she is in a black, green, or thick atmosphere, she will announce wintry air and rains. It is also appropriate that we pay attention to the halo [circle] that forms around her. For if there is only one, and it is clear and gradually narrows, it will designate clear air. But if there are two or three, they will demonstrate wintry air. If these halos lean toward a bright redness and appear as if broken, they will announce wintry weather brought by powerful winds. If they are murky and thick, they will indicate wintry weather brought by the force of wind. And if they lean toward a black-green and are broken, they will signify wintry weather occurring by both causes. When there are several halos, the effects will be more numerous according to these things we have predicted. Likewise, a halo appearing around the **wandering stars** <note>The planets.</note>, or around the bright **fixed stars** <note>original: *non erraticis*</note>, will signify events similar to the colors of those halos and the natures of the stars they surround. It is also fitting for us to observe the fixed stars, such as the **Pleiades** <note>original: *Pliades*, the Seven Sisters star cluster</note>, **Al-Fakka** <term>Alseca: Likely the Arabic *Al-Fakka*, the star Alpha Coronae Borealis, often called the "Broken Bowl."</term>, and similar ones, so that we may inspect the collections in which many stars approach one another, and so that we may perceive their colors without regard to their size. For when they appear and are of greater light and greater size than usual, they will signify blasts of wind from that direction in which they are situated. In a similar way, those stars which are characteristically similar to **nebulae** <term>Aladcha: An Arabic-derived term used here for nebulous star clusters.</term>, such as those called **The Manger** <term>Nathra: From the Arabic *Al-Nathrah*, referring to the Praesepe cluster in the constellation of Cancer.</term> and similar ones—when they appear in clear weather as if not there, or as thick, they will indicate much rain and wintry air. But if they are clear and shining, they will announce powerful winds. The manner of those things that occur at certain times

from other conditions is similar. For **tailed stars** <note>original: *Caudatae stellae*, referring to comets.</note>, which are like **nebulae** <term>Aladcha</term>, always show winds and dryness of the air. The strength of what follows from this will also be according to the multitude of those things and the length of their duration. And the **hurling of stars** <note>original: *stellarum iaculatio*, referring to meteors or shooting stars</note> and their flight—if it is from one of the **angles** <note>Key points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, or Imum Coeli.</note>, it will signify that blasts of wind are coming from that direction; and if they appear from different angles, it will announce disordered winds. In the same way, when the qualities of the clouds resemble fleeces of wool, they will perhaps signify wintry air.

The **rainbow** <note>original: *Iris*</note> that is sometimes seen—when it appears in clear times, it will prefigure wintry air; and when it is formed during times of wintry weather, it will announce clear skies. ### BOOK THREE

The movement of the Moon and the stars is the cause of every individual and general **accident** <term>accident: a term used here to describe an event or occurrence that happens to a person or the world</term>. Indeed, the difference in the natures of those things mentioned before, and of their similar movements, as well as the observation of what the celestial bodies move—and those things which the heavens themselves surround—is the occasion by which the forecasting of these events occurs. Beyond this, general events are greater and do not require the support of anything else, but particular [individual] events are not so. 

Nor is it necessary to think that there is one and the same beginning for the hours of their origin, in which we place the qualities of the heavens and by which we strive to foreknow what is signified by the assembly of figures formed in those hours. Rather, we ought to consider that there are many beginnings for general events, because we cannot find a single beginning for everything in its entirety. These things have been stated before, and many such occasions are found. For we inquire into most events through the greater **eclipses** and through the stars that move with a manifest [visible] motion. In individual humans, however, both a single beginning and many beginnings are found. For one beginning is the start of the "collection" <note>original: *collectionis*, referring to the gathering of biological material at conception</note> which is within us; but there are many beginnings, which, in respect to the first, are the alterations that happen afterward from the surrounding environment. Therefore, it is more fitting in this place to put forward one beginning, because all other things happen only by the occasion of this one. For this reason, since these are the general properties of the "collection," they are grasped from the observation of the primary beginning; from the remaining beginnings, however, we shall learn what happens in each of the hours from increase or decrease, according to what we shall add concerning the divisions of time.

->**ON THE DEPOSITION OF THE SEED, AND THE BIRTH**<-
->**of the infant. Chapter 1.**<-

<margin>The twofold beginning of the infant.</margin>
Since the temporal beginning of humans is established, this beginning occurs naturally when the **seed is deposited** <note>original: *sperma cadit*, referring to the moment of conception</note>; but it occurs in potentiality and by accident when the infant comes forth at the hour of birth. It is appropriate for those who have grasped the hour of the deposition of the seed—either by chance or by careful observation—to take their investigations from the figure of the stars acting specifically at that hour (the hour of conception) when they wish to know the particular qualities of the body and soul. 

For once it happens that the seed receives a quality at the beginning—which comes to it from the surrounding environment—even though that quality of the body may later vary according to the circumstances of the hours, yet it will naturally attract to itself an increase of matter only similar to itself. When that mass of matter grows, it will resemble the primary quality which is proper to the seed. However, when the hour of the deposition of the seed is unknown, as has been found to happen many times, it is necessarily appropriate to observe the beginning which is the infant’s birth. This same event is the greatest beginning, nor does it differ from the first, except in what follows. 

Through the first beginning (conception), it is possible to foreknow what happens before birth. For that is the first beginning, and the other [birth] will be a similar beginning, as is sufficiently declared by the fact that the latter follows the former in time. Perhaps its power is more perfect in strength than the first. It is also fitting that the first beginning be more frequently called the "beginning of the seed of man," while the second should be called the "beginning of the man" <note>original: *esse hominis*, the being of the human</note>, because the infant then acquires those things which it did not have while it was enclosed in the womb; and with this, it also acquires the properties which are only in the nature of man, and the quality which happens to its body. Likewise, although the environment that surrounds us at the hour of birth is not thought to help in *creating* the newborn (to make it be of a certain quality), it nonetheless helps so that its appearance and its exit are according to the specific quality of the surrounding environment. This is because nature, after the infant's perfection [completion in the womb], causes it to move toward its exit when the quality [of the moment] resembles the quality that formed it. Therefore, we ought to think that the quality of the stars at the hour of the infant's birth signifies things similar to these: not because the hour itself performs these actions, but because it necessarily and naturally resembles the strength of the "maker" [the conception]. And since our intention in this discourse is to manifest this part of the science with a skillful path—as we promised at the start of this book, where we proved that this mode of forecasting can be reached—and since the most ancient way of forecasting is according to all the stars, or at least the majority...

# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM

...the blending [of celestial influences] occurs in many ways and is almost infinite when one attempts to investigate it plainly and openly. This is especially true regarding specific future events that observers of nature inquire into, as can be found in the accounts they provide. Because of the gravity of its use and the difficulty of its explanation, we have decided to pass over these details. However, we intend to concisely describe the method of forecasting by which each of these types is understood in its mode of investigation, as well as the specific creative powers of the stars in their perfection, through what can be achieved by the path of natural conjecture. It is not necessary for our intention to be devoted to every quality of the surrounding environment by which every accident that happens to a human is understood. Instead, it is generally appropriate that we join the creative powers of the [celestial] bodies with their similar locations according to the mode of victory and dominion. We do this much like the shooting of an arrow; we leave the observation of the future—which is gathered in this subject species through a collection of many natures—to the person who has deliberated upon it and investigated it as perceptively as an archer who successfully hits the mark. We shall place the beginning of our discourse on universal matters at the start, as is fitting for the proper order, appearing at the emergence of the infant. For through this beginning, we can arrive at the essence of all things having this nature, as we have said. However, the properties that are born at the hour of the falling of the seed <note>original: *casus spermatis*; referring to the moment of conception</note> are understood through this same type of observation by one who wisely scrutinizes and subtly investigates only those properties which were present in that same "collection" <note>the alignment of stars at the moment of conception</note>.

### ON THE KNOWLEDGE OF THE ASCENDING 
### DEGREE. Chapter II.

<margin>Clocks.</margin>
Since doubt often arises concerning the first matter, which is the support—namely, the **ascending degree** <term>ascending degree: also known as the Ascendant or Rising Sign, it is the specific point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term>—at the hour of the infant's emergence, it follows that in most cases one cannot know the hour of birth without error. This is only possible for those who have observed the time using an **astrolabe** <term>astrolabe: a sophisticated historical instrument used to determine the positions of stars and calculate local time</term> among all the instruments for telling time. Other timekeeping instruments, which many who work in these matters rely upon, perhaps fail and deviate from the truth. For those instruments that indicate the hour by the Sun <note>sundials</note> can fail due to the declination in the positioning of the **shadow-markers** <term>shadow-markers: the Latin *scioterorum* refers to the gnomons or indicators on a sundial</term> and from the distortion of those markers. Moreover, with timekeeping instruments that are adjusted by the flow of water <note>water clocks or clepsydrae</note>, errors occur from the retention of water and differences in its flow, which happens due to various circumstances or any other chance occurrence. Therefore, it is necessarily appropriate that we judge a way by which the degree of the circle of signs <note>the zodiac</note>—which according to natural reason ought to be the following—can be found as the ascendant. After we have roughly found the ascending degree through the hour attributed to us, we must find the degree of the **conjunction or prevention** <note>original: *cōiunctionis uel preuētionis*; these are technical terms for the New Moon or Full Moon (syzygy) that occurred immediately prior to the birth</note> which was closest to the birth itself, and we must learn it truly. If that which we find was a conjunction, we shall take the degree of both lights <note>the Sun and Moon</note>; but if it was a "prevention" [Full Moon], we shall observe the degree of the luminary existing above the earth. After this, we inquire as to which of the planets at the hour of birth possesses the "disposition" <note>right of rulership or dignity</note> of that degree. Generally, the way in which a planet is assigned disposition is explained by these five things: **triplicity**, **house**, **exaltation**, **term**, and **appearance** <note>orientality or visibility</note>, or affinity to the Sun in the figure. The disposition of that place will belong to the planet which had more than one of these strengths, or all of them, in that spot. If we find all or many of these in one planet, we shall observe its degree in the sign in which it was truly found at the hour of birth; and we shall say that the degree of the sign (as roughly accepted through the ascending times) which is equal to it in number is the true ascending degree. But if we find two or more planets associated together, we shall look at the number [degree] which each traveled at the hour of birth; and whichever number is closer to the ascending degree that appeared to us through the [rough] rising times, that shall be the ascendant of the hour of birth. If we find the number of degrees of two or more planets equally close to the number of the ascendant, we shall follow the one which has more authorities in the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful points in a horoscope (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli)</term> and whose **Haiz** <term>Haiz: a dignity where a planet is in a sign and house that matches its own gender and the "sect" of the chart (day or night)</term> it was. But if the distance of the degree of the **Almudhebir** <term>Almudhebir: a Latinized Arabic term for the "Governor" or ruler of the chart</term> from the ascending degree (found without subtle observation) is greater than its distance from the degree of the **Midheaven** <note>original: *medij cœli*; the highest point of the chart</note>, we shall use that same number of degrees to balance...

->**ON THE DIVISION OF THE DISCOURSE ON NATIVITIES.**<-
->**Chapter III.**<-

After the positioning of these preliminary matters, we will add that when one wishes to categorize the general observations of <term>nativities</term><note>A "nativity" is a birth chart or the study of a person's life based on their birth moment.</note> with an ordered and appropriate division, they will find that of those things which one arrives at by the natural path, some are occurrences that happen before birth—such as the discussion concerning parents. Some are occurrences that happen both before and after birth, such as discourse concerning siblings. But those things which happen at the very hour of birth are not as simple or as clearly evident as those we mentioned before. Finally, the last of the occurrences that can be known are said to be those that happen after birth. This category, without doubt, consists of many modes and many parts. 

Therefore, from those things that happen at the very hour of birth, the things we wish to know are: discussions concerning males and females, and whether the mother will give birth to twins or more; also discussions concerning monstrous forms, and those who will never grow to maturity. From those things occurring after birth, the things we seek to know are: discourse concerning life <note>original: "de uita"</note>, because those who do not grow do not belong to these narratives; after these, to speak of the form of the body, and of the infirmities and impediments happening to the body. Next, to discuss the qualities of the soul and its accidents; then to speak of the fortune and misfortune of the person born, and of their status, exaltation, and their high rank. Afterward, to narrate what pertains to their deeds and works; then to discuss their marriage and the duration of their time with a spouse, and what will happen to them regarding children, as well as their associations and familiarity with people, and their friends. Next, to show their travels; and finally, to indicate the manner of their death, which in its strength is similar to the discourse concerning life, though its order must be placed after these aforementioned things.

We shall generally describe the method for each of these. We will say these things only when the strengths of our narrative are operating through these [planetary] causes, as we manifested above. We will set aside those things which have been foolishly and redundantly brought forth by many others, in which there is no probable reasoning that fits with the primary natural causes. We will also postpone those things which we can reach not through strengths, nor through numbers, and for which the reasons why they should be so are not held; instead, we will investigate through observations of the <term>configurations of the planets</term> and their similarities with their own places. 

Therefore, so that it is not necessary to repeat this word in every one of the prescribed chapters, it is appropriate for us to state it here generally for all. From the chapters of the observation of nativities, let us consider the place in the circle of signs <note>the Zodiac</note> which is similar to the type of specific chapter sought—just as the place of the <term>Midheaven</term> is similar to one's works, and the place of the **Sun** is similar to matters regarding the father. Afterward, we should observe the planets which, according to the five prescribed types of <term>dignity</term><note>In traditional astrology, a planet's "dignity" or power is measured in five ways: its House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, and Face.</note>, have the governance of that place. If one planet rules that place in all these ways, we shall attribute the governance of the sought matter to it. If two or three rule it, we will give the governance to the one that has the strength of the greater number of dignities. 

Next, we consider the quality of the future event. This investigation will be based on the natures of those stars which hold the governance, and from the natures of the signs in which the planets are located, as well as from similar places. After this, we take the investigation of the quantity of the future from their powers, considering whether they are strong in their qualities in the world and in the nativities, or if the opposite is true. 

In the world, they are said to be stronger when they are in their own or similar places, and when they are <term>oriental</term><note>Rising in the east before the Sun.</note> and increasing in number. In nativities, however, they will be stronger when they are in the <term>angles</term><note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the East, West, Zenith, and Nadir.</note> or in places ascending toward an angle, especially the first two, which are the <term>Ascendant</term> and the **Midheaven**. They will be weaker in the world when they are in foreign or dissimilar places, or when they are <term>occidental</term><note>Setting in the west after the Sun.</note> or diminished in their journey. In nativities, they will be weaker when they have moved away from the angles. We shall also consider the space of future time by investigating whether, with respect to the **Sun** and the **Ascendant**, they are <term>matutinal</term><note>Rising in the morning before the Sun.</note> or <term>vespertinal</term><note>Setting in the evening after the Sun.</note>. For the first two quarters of each of them, and the two opposite them by diameter, are matutinal, while the others are vespertinal. We shall also consider if they were...

### ON PARENTS, CHAPTER IV.

**T**he first path which we must always follow in the investigation of each of these species is of this kind. We shall now begin from the first chapter, which is the discourse concerning parents, as it seems to fit the order we just announced. We say that the Sun and Saturn are naturally likened to fathers, while the Moon and Venus are likened to mothers. Therefore, just as the qualities of these stars are found in relation to each other and to others, we should consider the qualities of the parents to be likewise. Indeed, it is appropriate for us to consider their good fortune or misfortune, and even their sovereignty, from the proximity of the stars to the <term>luminaries</term><note>The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.</note>. For when both are surrounded by the <term>benefics</term><note>Favorable planets, usually Jupiter and Venus.</note> that are in their own <term>haiz</term><note>original: "haiz" — a technical term meaning a planet is in its preferred "sect" (e.g., a daytime planet in a daytime sign above the horizon during the day).</note>, and in their own two signs, or in signs following them, they signify that the parents will be illustrious; especially when the planets surrounding the Sun are matutinal, and those surrounding the Moon are vespertine; for then their position will be favorable. Likewise, if Saturn and Venus are oriental in their own <term>almugea</term><note>original: "almugea" — a complex dignity based on the planet's relationship to the Sun or Moon.</note>, or if they are in the angles, we ought to signify the manifest good fortune of the parents from this, according to the amount appropriate to each of them. But if the contrary of this occurs—namely, if the luminaries are "void of course" and surrounded by no stars—they signify the decline and lowliness of the parents, especially if the position of Venus and Saturn is unfavorable. But if planets not in their own *haiz* surround them—as happens when Mars ascends after the Sun, or Saturn after the Moon—and if the locations of the benefics are not favorable in respect to the luminaries, nor in their own *haiz*, it is not inconsistent for us to signify from this a miserable life and the destruction of the parents. But if the <term>Lot of Fortune</term><note>original: "pars fortuniu," a calculated point in the chart representing material prosperity.</note>, of which we shall make mention, is in a suitable agreement with the stars surrounding the Sun or Moon in the births of the parents, their substance will be preserved and endure. But if the Lot of Fortune does not exist as we have said, or if the opposite occurs, and the benefics do not surround the luminaries, or if those surrounding them are <term>malefics</term><note>Unfavorable planets, usually Mars and Saturn.</note>, the parents' possessions will not prosper, but will suffer harm. We shall consider the length of the parents' life, and its shortness, from the associations of the stars in the figures.

<margin>Life of the father.</margin>
Let us speak, then, of the father's life. Whenever Jupiter and Venus are associated in the figure in any way with the Sun or Saturn, or when Jupiter is associated with Venus, and there is a suitable association of the Sun and Saturn—either if they are <term>conjoined</term><note>Occupying the same degree.</note>, or in <term>trine</term><note>Separated by 120 degrees, a harmonious aspect.</note>, or in <term>sextile</term><note>Separated by 60 degrees, also harmonious.</note> aspect—and both are strong, we shall announce from this a long life for the father. If they are not strong, this will not be so, though they will not truly signify shortness of life. But if this does not happen, but Mars is elevated above the Sun or Saturn, or if he follows them, and Saturn is not favorable to the Sun but is in a <term>square</term><note>Separated by 90 degrees, a difficult aspect.</note> aspect or diametrically opposed, or if both are remote from an angle, it will signify the father's weakness. But if they are in the angles, or in places ascending toward the angles, they will signify a short life for the parents or some injury. For when they stand in the first two angles, which are the <term>Ascendant</term> and the <term>Midheaven</term>, they indicate shortness of life. But when they are in the other two, which are the <term>Descendant</term> and the <term>Angle of the Earth</term><note>The lowest point in the chart, also called the Imum Coeli.</note>, or in places ascending toward them, they are said to be an impediment. When Mars also looks upon the Sun in the aforementioned way, the father will depart by a sudden death, or an impediment will happen in his eyesight. But if he looks upon Saturn, he will signify for the father either death or a fever with trembling, or an impediment arising from a cutting or burning; again, when the configuration of Saturn is unfavorable in respect to the Sun by reason of diseases happening from harmful humors, death will come to the father.

<margin>Of the mother.</margin>
Likewise, let us deal with the life of the mother. When, therefore, in the figure of the Moon or Venus, Jupiter or Venus is again associated with the Moon—either with her, or in a trine or sextile aspect—and both are strong, they will lengthen the mother's life. But if Mars looks upon the Moon, or follows Venus, or remains in a square or diametrically opposite aspect, or if the quality of Saturn in respect to the Moon is of this quality, and if they are of small motion or have receded from an angle, they will signify only that the mothers are entangled in diseases and sicknesses. But if they are increased in motion, or in the angles, they take away the mothers' lives...

Yet it is necessarily required that it resembles them from the beginning; for if it does not hold itself thus, it can do nothing in the future, since they retained no fellowship in the beginning. The first disposition is not the cause of the future time, but the quality of the star, which in respect to the Sun and the angle of the world was the ruling disposition at the time of birth.

### VI. ON MALES AND FEMALES.

After we have explained the account of siblings through the natural path, we ought to add what follows regarding the child itself, and first indicate the consideration of males and females. The observation of this is not of one kind, nor is it taken from a single thing, but from both <term>luminaries</term><note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>, and from the Ascendant, as well as from the planets having authority over these. Since the male and the female are generated in the womb, it is fitting that the judgment of this matter properly belongs to the beginning, which is the hour of the falling of the seed <note>The moment of conception.</note>; and that which we can know of this—the beginning which is the exit of the creature <note>The moment of birth.</note>—is general because of the participation which this beginning has with the first. It is fitting for us also to observe generally: if these three aforementioned places, and the planets ruling all or most of them, are masculine, the child will be male; and if they are feminine, it will be a female; and according to this we shall judge as stated above. It is also necessary to consider the masculine and feminine places and planets, just as we showed at the beginning of this book; we demonstrated, I say, from the natures of the signs in which they are, and from the natures of the planets themselves, as well as from their qualities with respect to the world. For when they are oriental, they are masculinized; but they are feminized when they are occidental. Likewise, from their qualities with respect to the Sun, they are masculinized: for when they are <term>matutinal</term><note>Rising in the morning before the Sun.</note> they masculinize, and being <term>vespertinal</term><note>Appearing in the evening after the Sun has set.</note>, they feminize. Therefore, from all these things, we ought to conjecture which sex occurs in the constitution of the newborn according to the majority of factors.

And if the dominant places are bicorporeal signs, and with this they are associated with many planets in the figure, more than two will be born. Sometimes a planet increases their number, which...

# ON MONSTROUS SIGNS.
## Chapter VIII.

That which by no means departs from our understanding is the description of monstrous forms. We say first that the two luminaries are for the most part found in the birth of such individuals falling away from the <term>angles</term><note>The four primary points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> or not, having some concordance with the Ascendant, and the unfortunate <note>The "malefic" or harmful planets, Saturn and Mars.</note> planets being powerful in the angles. Therefore, when this is so found, it is consistent if this should happen to occur—which is often said to happen in wretched and unfortunate births. 

And if those births were not of monstrous forms, let us observe the past conjunction or prevention <note>The syzygy or the alignment of the Sun and Moon (New or Full Moon) immediately preceding the birth.</note>, so that we may detect the governing planets of that conjunction or prevention, as well as the position of the luminaries at the hour of birth. For if their places in the births, and the place of the Moon or the Ascendant—all things, in fact, or the planet at the place of conjunction or prevention—are not bound together, the newborn will be of a monstrous form. 

If these things are so, and in addition we find the luminaries in quadrupedal or wild-beast signs <note>Signs like Aries (the Ram), Leo (the Lion), or Capricorn (the Goat).</note>, and the malefics are existing in the angles, the newborn will not be of human kind. If indeed none of the <term>benefics</term><note>The "helpful" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> has testimony with the luminaries, but the malefics bear witness to them, the newborn will not be domestic, and its nature will be like that of harmful wild beasts. But if Jupiter or Venus bear witness to the luminaries, the newborn will be like domestic animals, such as dogs, ferrets, and similar creatures. If Mercury bears witness, the newborn will be like animals which men need and use, such as chickens, pigs, oxen, goats, and the like. 

But if the luminaries move in signs whose images are human <note>Signs like Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius.</note>, and all other factors are similar, we do not doubt that the birth will be from humans or from those who live among humans, except that we will say he has a monstrous form. Furthermore, the knowledge of this quality and its property will be found again in this place from the figures of the signs in which the malefics stood, which contained the luminaries or the angles. Likewise, if the signs of the benefics in this place bear witness to none of the aforesaid places, the newborn will be non-speaking, and his form will be truly and perfectly changed. But if Jupiter or Venus bear witness, the property of the newborn where that change occurred will be such that he is honored and exalted, <margin>otherwise, a hermaphrodite.</margin> because from this, that figure <term>hermaphroditus</term><note>original: "armaforodhotis"; a corrupted spelling of the Greek term for an individual with both male and female characteristics.</note> will occur—that is, a form from Venus and Mercury.

### OF THOSE WHO ARE NOT
### REARED. Chapter IX

After the discussion of those who are not reared <note>This refers to infant mortality or children who do not survive to "grow up" (Latin: *crescere*).</note> has preceded this, there remains the discourse concerning those whose condition we seek to know through the hour of birth. It should be known that this explanation—because the investigated chapter is not far removed from both of these modes—sometimes adheres to the discourse on life, and sometimes is contrary to it, because the force of this kind of investigation is altered by certain variations. For the discourse on life applies only to all those who have experienced life. These are they whose life is considered no less than a solar circuit, which is the space of one year; but the life which is in "fortitude" <note>Referring to the immediate vital strength at birth.</note> is that which is said to be less, such as months, days, and hours. 

The discussion of those who are not reared is the speech concerning those who do not reach any of these aforementioned times, but die in a short time due to the excess of evil and harm in the chart. Therefore, the investigation of life consists of many parts, but the investigation of those who do not grow is single and straightforward. 

Generally, therefore, when one of the <term>luminaries</term><note>The Sun or the Moon.</note> is in one of the <term>angles</term><note>The four pivot points of the sky: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>, and one of the <term>malefics</term><note>original: "infortunarum"; typically Saturn or Mars, the "unfortunate" stars.</note> is associated with it in longitude—being at the same degree—or is in an <term>isosceles figure</term><note>original: "figura equicruria"; an astrological aspect where planets are at symmetrical or equal distances.</note>, and no <term>benefic</term><note>original: "fortunarum"; Jupiter or Venus, the "fortunate" stars.</note> is associated with it in the figure, and the ruler of the place of the luminaries is in the places of the malefics, the native shall not live, but will die soon. 

But if it should be in an isosceles figure, yet in the projection of the rays of the malefics rising toward it from the places of the luminaries, and there were two "infortunators" [malefics], with one or both harming the luminaries by rising toward the places of the two or one of them; or if it should be in opposition to him or them; or if one of the malefics should harm one of the luminaries while the other is in opposition, and one rises to the place of the luminary, it is by no means doubted that the native will not have life. This is because the greatest harm in this configuration destroys and hides the health and progress which comes in the span of life from the distance of the place rising to the place of the luminary. 

Specifically, that which hinders the Sun among those things in the place rising toward its position is said to be Mars, while for the Moon it is Saturn. But in their opposition, or when it rises toward her, the contrary happens: for Saturn hinders the Sun, while Mars hinders the Moon—most especially when they happen to be the rulers of the places of the luminaries and the <term>Ascendant</term><note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note>. And if it should have two oppositions, and the luminaries and malefics are in the angles or in an isosceles figure, the infants are born dead or half-dead. 

If this occurs, and the luminaries are separated from one of the benefics, or are associated with it in the figure, and the rays reach the preceding parts, the native shall live according to the significance of the number of degrees which exist between the <term>hyleg</term><note>original: "alhileg"; the planet or point in a chart that acts as the "giver of life."</note> and the rays of the nearest malefic—counted in months, days, or hours, according to the quantity of their misfortune, which is the cause of this. 

But if the rays of the malefics reach the preceding parts of the luminaries, and the benefics reach the following parts, the native shall grow and live. Likewise, when the malefics are <term>elevated</term><note>Positioned in a more powerful or higher place in the chart, such as the 10th house.</note> over the associating benefics in the figure, the native will be of a wretched quality and weak. But if the benefics are elevated, the native will not remain with the parents. And if one of the benefics should rise together with the Moon, or have an <term>application</term><note>original: "ictisal"; an Arabic term for the coming together or "connection" of two planets.</note>, and one of the malefics should set, the native will be nourished by the parents. 

In this way again, the observation of many natives shall be made. When any of the stars, having an association in the figure in two or more ways, is in the west, the infant will be born half-alive, or like a piece of flesh, or of an imperfect creation. And if one of the malefics is elevated over it, the native will not be nourished, or will not have life, according to that which occurs through this configuration.

## ON THE DURATION OF LIFE. CHAPTER X.

<margin>Hyleg <note>original: "Alhileg"; the planetary "giver of life."</note></margin>
<margin>otherwise, God <note>original: "theos"; a reference to the 9th house.</note></margin>
Regarding those events that occur after birth, our first discussion concerns the length of life. This is because it would be a mockery for us to treat those things which occur only rarely—namely, those matters that cannot be fulfilled unless one reaches a certain number of years of life—among those who do not reach such an age. This observation is neither easy nor simple; it is derived from the powers of the "dominant places," and is observed in many ways. The method which, according to our judgment, is most effective and follows the natural path is as follows: this observation is considered based on the position of the Hyleg <note>original: "Alhileg"</note>, those who hold power over the Hyleg, and the locations of the "killing" stars <note>the "anaretic" or destructive planets</note>. The knowledge of each of these things is as follows.

First, you must know that the Hylegiacal places are those in which the star that holds dominion must be the Hyleg. These are: the area around the degree of the Ascendant <note>the eastern horizon</note>, from five degrees above the horizon to twenty-five degrees below it; and those degrees which consist of a sextile <note>original: "hexagona radiatione"</note> aspect to the right of these thirty degrees, which is the house of Good Fortune <note>the 11th house</note>. Also, those in a square aspect <note>original: "aspectu tetragono"</note> to them, which is the Midheaven <note>original: "medium caeli"</note> above the earth; and the degrees in a trine aspect <note>original: "trigona radiatione"</note>, which is the place called God <note>original: "theuz", likely a variant of the Greek "theos"; the 9th house</note>. Finally, there are the degrees in opposition, which is the West <note>the Descendant or 7th house</note>.

Among these, the order of priority—because it possesses the strongest authority—is said to be the Midheaven above the earth, followed by the Ascendant. Next is that which follows the Midheaven <note>the 11th house</note>, then the West <note>the 7th house</note>, and then that which precedes the Midheaven <note>the 9th house</note>. We have determined that everything dwelling below the earth should be omitted from such a noble and excellent matter, except for that part of the Ascendant appearing above the earth. Of the signs above the earth, those which do not "behold" <note>make a geometric aspect to</note> the Ascendant are not to be observed; nor is the sign ascending before the Ascendant <note>the 12th house</note>, which is called the House of Labor. This is because the thick and dark vapor arising from the moisture of the earth disturbs and destroys its strength, as it is removed from the "angle" <note>a primary cardinal point</note>; for this reason, the nature of the colors and qualities of stars existing in this house appears doubtful.

Afterward, it is fitting that we establish the four dominants—which are the Sun, the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune—and the dispositors of those places as the potential Hyleg. We shall know the Part of Fortune by taking the number found from the position of the Sun to the position of the Moon, by day or night, and calculating that same quantity starting from the Ascendant according to the succession of the signs. In this way, we learn the location of the Part. We do this so that the quality of the Sun with respect to the Ascendant is like the quality of the Moon with respect to the Part of Fortune. For the Part of Fortune will be, as it were, a lunar Ascendant. Those who say that in nocturnal births we should count from the Moon to the Sun seem to follow this same logic. Then, starting from the Ascendant, we should calculate that number in the opposite direction to what we said before—that is, according to the order of the preceding signs. When we have done this, the same location of the Part of Fortune that we found will appear according to this method, and the quality of the configuration will be the same.

It is also appropriate that, by day, we first choose the Sun if it is in a Hylegiacal place. If not, then the Moon. If we cannot choose the Moon, we shall choose the star which has the greatest authority in the disposition of the Sun’s place, the place of the preceding conjunction, and the Ascendant. That is, a star which has three or more of the five powers <note>essential dignities: House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, or Face</note> through which a disposition consists in any of the aforesaid places is to be chosen. If this does not happen, we shall take the degree of the Ascendant. By night, however, it is fitting that we first choose the Moon, then the Sun, then the star which has the greatest authority in the disposition of the Moon’s place, the place of the preceding full moon <note>original: "praeventionis"</note>, and the place of the Part of Fortune. If this dominion does not occur, and if a conjunction <note>New Moon</note> preceded the birth, we shall take the Ascendant; but if a prevention <note>Full Moon</note> preceded it, we take the Part of Fortune. If both luminaries and the dispositor <note>original: "alaiz"; likely from the Arabic term for the ruler of the chart or Hyleg</note> are in Hylegiacal places, it is fitting that we take the luminary that is in the place of greater and stronger power. However, to choose the dispositor over the luminaries...

Mercury, again, will be with the stars with which it is associated in the figure. The number of increase or decrease will be understood from the locations of the degrees of each of them. For it will be found according to the number of temporal hours which each of those degrees possesses; for when the time is diurnal <note>daytime</note>, we shall attribute the temporal hours of the day; and when it is nocturnal <note>nighttime</note>, we shall attribute the temporal hours of the night. Similarly, the trine <note>120 degree aspect</note> will act when it is in a fortune <note>benefic</note> and remains in a sign of few ascensions. And when the Moon is the Hyleg, the location of the Sun will sometimes "kill," because when the Sun reaches the Hyleg of this type, it will have the power of killing and saving; for it will go to the place of the Hyleg. For this is prevented when it is within the "term" <note>a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of one of the fortunes, or when one of the fortunes projects rays from a quartile, trine, or opposition to that degree which kills, or to the degree which succeeds it, so long as in the projection of their rays they do not exceed it by more than 2 degrees, nor more than 8 degrees for Venus. Similarly, this will also happen when the Hyleg is joined to a star whose bodily condition it adheres to, and the latitude of those two is not the same. 

When, however, the saving or helping stars, or the killing stars, are two or more, it is appropriate in each of these two cases that we observe which of them is stronger, according to the multitude of things helping them and their strength. Thus, according to the multitude, when one of the two types is more than the other by a manifest increase; and according to strength, when the stars that help or kill are in places suitable to themselves, and no others remain in such places—especially when the stars of one type are oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note> and the stars of the other type are occidental <note>setting after the Sun</note>. Therefore, we generally need not observe anything regarding those who are under the rays <note>invisible due to the Sun's light</note> in setting, helping, and saving, unless the Moon is the Hyleg. For then that same location of the Sun will be the killer; and then also we shall consider if a fortune that was with it hindered it, and no fortunes helped it.
