### BOOK THREE

...the killer <note>original: "abscisorem"; the *Anareta*, or planet/point that signifies the end of life</note>, we find that if it is taken loosely or in any haphazard way, it is least fitting. As many used to do, who always said this was according to the quantity of the times of ascensions of the degrees of that longitude; nor should we consider this at any time unless the place of the Hyleg <note>original: "† Alhileg"</note> itself was the Ascendant, or one of the ascending places <margin>otherwise, Hileg.</margin> relative to the Ascendant. Therefore, those who observe this matter by natural consideration must, in all ways, observe one thing: namely, how many times of the equinoctial circle <note>the celestial equator</note> the place of the following star or figure will be from the place of the preceding star or figure in the nativity. This is because the times of the equinoctial circle travel equally through the circle of the horizon and the meridian line; these are the two circles through which similar local longitudes are measured. Each single "time" <note>one degree of rotation</note> of the equinoctial circle constitutes the space of one solar year.

It is fitting, therefore, that when the place of the Hyleg <note>the "giver of life" point</note> is prominent and situated above the eastern circle of the horizon, the times of the ascensions of the degrees should be taken from that hour until the hour that "kills" <note>reaches the anaretic point</note>. This is because after this quantity of equinoctial time, the killer will be at the horizon in the place of the Hyleg, which is the eastern circle.

And when the Hyleg is on the line of the midday <note>the meridian or Midheaven</note>, the ascensions of the "direct circle" <note>Right Ascension</note> should be taken, according to which the time of the passage of that part of the circle of signs <note>the Zodiac</note> across the midday circle will be measured. 

However, when it is on the western circle of the horizon, we shall take the number of times in which each of those longitudes falls and sets, which is the same as the number of degrees of the ascensions of the parts of the circle of signs that are opposite to it.

But if the place of the Hyleg, when it precedes, is not in any of these three positions <note>Rising, Midheaven, or Setting</note>, but in places situated between them, the aforementioned time of ascensions, time of setting, and time of passage through the midheaven will not be those in which the following places reach the preceding places. Instead, they will be the times in which they reach different places, because the place to which the following point goes is judged to be neither similar nor of the same kind as the place where the preceding point had been, unless its position is made similar to the original position: specifically, its part in respect to the horizon and the midheaven must be the same as the original part was. 

It also happens that, in respect to these two, its position is the same when it is near the places that are above the semicircle formed by the circles passing through the point common to the midday circle and the horizon circle <note>the "proportional" or "temporal" hour circles</note>; and these are those where each one creates one temporal hour, almost equal to each other. 

When, however, this semicircle has rotated around the aforementioned common point, its position will sometimes be like the position of the hemisphere, and sometimes like the position of the midday circle; and the times in which the parts of the circle of signs will traverse these two places will be unequal. Indeed, the times in which parts of the circle of signs cross this semicircle, when it stands in certain other places that are of different longitudes, will be different.

We shall set down the general method by which we operate as follows: namely, when the preceding of the two aforementioned places is in the Ascendant, or in the midday circle, or in the West, or in any other place, the following place alone will go toward the preceding one, according to the times that pass through that same preceding place. For once the degree of the midheaven is known, as well as the degree of the preceding and following points, we will first consider the place of the preceding degree by investigating how many temporal hours it is distant from the midday circle. We do this by counting the ascensions that are under the degrees between this and the midheaven degree, whether it is established above the earth or below the earth in the direct circle <note>Right Ascension</note>; after this, we divide them by the number of times of the hours which the preceding degree had. If it was above the earth, we divide by the times of the diurnal hours; if below the earth, by the times of the nocturnal hours. The result will be the hours of its longitude from the midday circle. 

Therefore, because the parts of the circle of signs whose longitude from the midday circle is one and the same quantity of the number of temporal hours are those falling upon one and the same semicircle of the aforementioned circles: it is necessary that we know, in longitude, how much time from the times of the equinoctial circle the longitude of the following degree from the midday line will yield temporal hours equal in number to the hours of the longitude of the preceding degree from the midheaven circle. # CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITE <note>The *Tetrabiblos*</note>

...the first position of the following degree shall be. This we shall determine from the ascensions of the right circle <note>the celestial equator</note>: after this, therefore, we will observe how great its longitude will be, based again on the number of temporal hours <note>hours that divide day or night into 12 equal parts regardless of season</note> that exist between it and the meridian circle, just as we multiply the hourly degrees of the preceding degree. But if the hours that we find are taken with respect to the Midheaven <note>original: "medium coeli"</note> which is above the earth, the values by which we multiply will be the times <note>degrees of the celestial equator</note> of the diurnal hours. If, however, they are with respect to the Midheaven which is below the earth, we will multiply by the times of the nocturnal hours. Then, we will take the difference between the two longitudes—the amount by which one exceeds the other—because that itself will be the number of years sought. 

And so that what we have said may be more evident, let the beginning of Aries be placed as the preceding location <note>the Hyleg</note>, and let the beginning of Gemini be the following location. Suppose also the climate <note>the latitude</note> in which we are is one where the longest day is fourteen hours; therefore, the hourly times for the beginning of Gemini will be approximately seventeen. Let the beginning of Aries first ascend, so that the beginning of Capricorn is in the Midheaven. For then the longitude of Gemini from the Midheaven which is above the earth will be 148 times, measured in the times of the equinoctial circle <note>right ascension</note>. And because the longitude of the beginning of Aries from the Midheaven (which is above the meridian circle) is six temporal hours, when we multiply those by the 17 times (which is the quantity of the hourly times for the beginning of Gemini), because the longitude of 148 times is only with respect to the Midheaven above the earth, the time of this longitude will be 102 times. Therefore, the following location will change to the preceding location after as many times as there are times of the excess, which is 46. Thus, the times of the ascensions of Aries and Taurus are roughly the same as those times. 

This, however, is so positioned that if the location of the Hyleg <note>original: "Alhileg"; the giver of life</note> is the ascending degree itself, the beginning of Aries is again at the Midheaven: so that if the beginning of Gemini is the first position, the longitude from the Midheaven which is above the earth would be 58 times of the equinoctial circle. For this reason, in this second position, it is fitting for us to observe when Aries and Taurus intersect the meridian circle. And so we calculate the Midheaven in this way, whenever we place the Hyleg there. Likewise, if the beginning of Aries is setting in the same manner, so that the beginning of Cancer is in the Midheaven, the longitude of the beginning of Gemini from the Midheaven above the earth would be, according to the succession of the signs, 32 times of the equinoctial circle. 

Again, because the longitude of the beginning of Aries from the meridian circle toward the west is 6 temporal hours, when we multiply them by 17, we will have 102 times, which is the longitude of the beginning of Gemini from the meridian circle when it has set. Its longitude toward this same part had already been 32 times when it was in its first position. It is proved, therefore, that it goes to the western position in the excess which is between these two times—which is the time of the setting of Aries and Taurus, and the time of the ascensions of the two signs opposite them, which are Libra and Scorpio. 

Furthermore, let the beginning of Aries not be in any of the angles, and let us place its longitude toward the aforementioned part from the meridian circle as three temporal hours, such that the Midheaven is 18 degrees of Taurus. Let the longitude of the beginning of Gemini (when it was in its first position from the Midheaven above the earth according to the preceding signs) be 13 times of the equinoctial circle. But when we multiply 17 times by three hours, the longitude of the beginning of Gemini from the meridian circle, when it reaches the second position according to the succession of signs, will be fifty-one times. Indeed, all these times will be 64. 

The location of the Hyleg had also traveled 46 times when it was in the ascendant, 58 in the Midheaven, and 70 in the descendant. Therefore, the numbers of the times that exist when its location is between the West and the Midheaven differ from each of the numbers that exist then, when its location is otherwise than what we have now said. For it is 64 times, and the difference is according to 3 hours of addition, because there is no doubt that the excess of times that we found (when we calculate by the angles from quadrant to quadrant) would be 12 times of the circle; and since the longitude was three hours, the excess was 6 times. ...as we shall soon describe, we can use appropriately. Therefore, when the approaching degree is the rising point <note>the Ascendant</note>, we will observe the ascensions that exist from that point to the following one. When they are in the **Midheaven**, we will consider the ascensions of the right circle <note>the celestial equator</note>; and when it is in the **West** <note>the Descendant</note>, we will look at the settings of those degrees. But when it stands between these places—for example, at the aforementioned longitude of **Aries**—we will first take the times of the difference of one to the other, namely that which is due to each of the two angles which are formed on either side of Aries. Because the beginning of Aries is between the angle of the Midheaven and the angle of the West (for the position of its beginning was placed after the Midheaven, which is above the earth), we will take the times <note>degrees of the equator</note> that are due to the sign of **Gemini**: if Aries were in the Midheaven, they are 58; if Aries were in the West, they are 70. And when this is done, we will take their difference; and then, based on the length in temporal hours <note>units of time equal to 1/12th of the day or night</note> of the preceding point found from each of the two angles positioned within it, we will observe what part it is of the 6 temporal hours <note>the total time between an angle and the horizon</note>, and we will take that amount from the difference we found between the two angles. We then decide whether that which was taken from the angle to which we made the relation should be subtracted or added.

For example: Since the increase that occurs through these 6 hours was 12 times <note>degrees</note>, and because we have placed the longitude of the preceding place at three temporal hours from each of the two angles—which is half of 6—we take half of 12, which is 6, which we add to 58 or subtract from 70; we find the increase to be 64 <note>The text reads 60, but the math 58 + 6 = 64 is implied by the logic of the example</note>. But if the longitude of this place from either of the two angles was two temporal hours, which is the third part of those 6 hours, we take a third part of 12 (the difference), which is 4. If those hours of longitude were from the Midheaven, we add those 4 times to 58. If, however, they were the longitude from the West, we will subtract those same 4 from 70. It is proper, therefore, that by this method we learn the quantities of the times of the aforementioned longitudes, just as is fitting and necessary.

<margin>Otherwise: of the climate <note>original: "climatis"</note></margin>
It remains for us to make known each type of circumstance encountered by the **Hyleg** <note>original: "alhileg"; the planetary point that signifies life and vitality</note>: which of those of shorter time shall be the "settings" <note>points of descent or endings</note>, and which shall be from those which are called the **killing points** <note>original: "felimecaturam"; a corruption of an Arabic term referring to the "cutter" or "interfector" planet that ends life</note>, and other things also which are said to "meet" it. The knowledge of this matter will come from the science of the unfavorable encounter which hinders, and the good encounter which helps, which are said to happen according to the manner predicted above, as well as from the beginnings of subsequent years, over which that place which met the **Hyleg** is not doubted to have significance. For when the places of encounter are unfavorable and unfortunate, and the places of the stars at the beginnings of subsequent years are hindering the dominant places, it is not improper for us to know that what results from this is truly death. But if only one of these two things is present, we do not doubt that what happens from it will be a great misfortune <note>original: "felicaturam"; here used to mean a significant 'event' or stroke of fate, usually negative in this context</note>, which are large impediments of great fear. But if both should be good, it is manifest that laziness and weakness, or an impediment, or exile, or travels result from it. We shall perceive the specific types of things occurring in each of these matters from the similarity of the place of the encounter to the matters of the **nativity** <note>the birth chart</note>. And when we sometimes doubt which of their places ought to be the "slayers" <note>interfectors</note>, nothing can prohibit us from considering and observing the things that happen to the **Hyleg** in each matter of the person born; and in what is to come, we will follow that which is similar to it, which has already happened and appeared from accidents, and we will consider the manner of them all, because the manner of their perfection in what happens through them is of equal strength in all things. According to this, therefore, we shall establish our investigation, and their increase and decrease.

# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM

...proper to themselves, as they are born with the individual. In the soul, however, these traits do not appear except as those which, through the first occasion after birth and creation, develop step by step. Those things which are outside the body <note>referring to external fortune or events</note> occur much later in the future time following these. It is appropriate for us, in the universality of the matter, to observe the eastern horizon <note>the Ascendant</note> and the planets that follow it among the wanderers <note>the planets</note>, or the masters of the disposition <note>the planetary rulers</note> from among them in the manner we have previously described.

<margin>Where the form of man comes from.</margin>
In the particularity of the matter, it is fitting for us to consider here again the state of the Moon, because the form and manner of bodies is perceived only from the nature of the configurations of these two places <note>the Ascendant and the Moon</note>, and from the configurations of the planets which are their dispositors, and from the mixture of those things which are in each species of them, as well as from the configuration of the fixed stars rising with them. Indeed, those whose powers precede the powers of others are the ruling stars of the disposition, which the quality proper to those same places then assists in turn. The particular matter, which can be stated lightly and absolutely from their modes, is that which follows.

<margin>Saturn’s complexion.</margin>
The first thing we say regarding the stars is that when Saturn is oriental <note>meaning it rises before the Sun</note>—and understand this to be when he is the sole ruler—his nature in the person's form will be of a honey-colored complexion <note>original: *mellini coloris*, a sallow or yellowish-dark skin tone</note>, of moderate thickness, his hair will be black and the hair of the head curly, with thick hair on the chest, medium eyes, a body of temperate size, and coldness and moisture will prevail over his complexion. When he is occidental <note>setting after the Sun</note>, the person born will be blackish, lean, of a small body, having straight and sparse hair, well-proportioned, his eyes black, and dryness will prevail in his complexion.

<margin>Jupiter’s.</margin>
When Jupiter is the master of the disposition of the aforementioned places and is oriental, the person born will be of a white color, with suitable and moderate hair, medium eyes, of a fitting stature and moderate size; heat and moisture will prevail in his complexion. But if he is occidental, he will be white, except that he will not be of such a "fitting" whiteness as we said above. His hair will also be straight, and he will be bald on the front part of the head, with medium eyes, and of a medium body; moisture will prevail in his complexion.

<margin>Mars’s.</margin>
And when Mars is oriental, his form will be of whiteness and redness <note>a ruddy complexion</note>, possessing a good size and a healthy fleshiness; his eyes will be variegated, his hair thick and moderate. Heat and dryness will prevail in his complexion. If he is occidental, however, the person born will be only of a red color, and of moderate body size, having small eyes and sparse, straight, and yellowish hair; dryness will prevail in his complexion.

<margin>Venus.</margin>
Indeed, the works of Venus are similar to the works of Jupiter, except that those things which occur through her are more beautiful and more pleasing; her beauty is more similar to the beauty of women. He will also be of a better figure, of a more agreeable quality of soul, and of a softer body. Also, among her properties is to make the eyes brownish-red <note>original: *subruffos*</note> and attractive.

<margin>Mercury.</margin>
When Mercury is likewise oriental, the person born is likened to the color of honey; he will be moderate in body size, well-proportioned, with small eyes and moderate hair, and heat will prevail in his complexion. But if he is occidental, the person born will be somewhat blackish, sharing in a saffron-yellow color, lean, having a thin voice and hollow sockets; the pupil of his eyes will be like the pupil of a goat's eye <note>a common historical description for light-colored or "piercing" eyes</note>, leaning toward redness. In his complexion, there is no doubt that dryness prevails.

<margin>Moon, Mars, Sun</margin>
The Sun and the Moon assist each of these stars when they are associated with them in the configuration. For the Sun assists in the figure and beauty, and in the fatness of the body. The Moon generally assists in the temperament and in leanness or moisture, especially when she is separating from him <note>the Sun</note>. Her assistance will also be particular according to her properties, which reside in her light, just as we described in the beginning of this book. Furthermore, generally, when stars are in their morning rising and appear, they make large bodies; and when they are in their first station, they grant vigor and strength to them; and when they precede, they temper them; and when they move in their second station, they make them weaker; but when they set, they bring about misery, impediments, and heaviness. Again, those same places in which they reside will assist the form and figure of the one born, and his complexion, as we said before. Generally also, the quarter <note>the season</note> which is produced from the vernal equinox to the summer solstice will demonstrate the person born to be of good color, fitting stature, healthy fleshiness, and good eyes, and in him heat and

Likewise, Virgo, Libra, and Sagittarius produce a temperate and well-proportioned body. But Scorpio, Pisces, and Taurus remove them from that balance. It is fitting for us to observe the qualities of other figures in a similar way, comparing them to one another, and to deduce the properties of the body's form, the complexion <note>the biological temperament</note>, and the mixture of all these things together.

## ON THE IMPEDIMENTS AND INFIRMITIES OF THE BORN
### occurring to the body. Chapter 12.

For when both, or one of them, are in that same place or in its square or opposite aspect with respect to the degrees rising at the predicted places, we will not doubt that infirmities and impediments will occur in the body of the person born. This is especially true when either or both luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are in the angles in the manner we previously described—that is, when both are in the second angle or in the two opposite angles. For then not only is one of the misfortunes strengthened when it rises after the luminaries and is in an angle, to cause some of the predicted infirmities—such as the infirmities signified by the places of the hemisphere, the places of the signs, and the natures of the malefic stars—but the stars which are associated with them in figure are also strengthened. Furthermore, it is strengthened again when it rises before the luminaries, because the parts of each sign surrounding the receiving part signify the light from the parts of the hemisphere. I say the part receiving impediments signifies that part of the body in which the future event will happen. ...because Saturn possesses, among the more noble parts of man, the right ear, the spleen, the bladder, and phlegm <note>In ancient medicine, phlegm was one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids thought to regulate health</note>. Jupiter, however, governs touch, the lungs, the ribs, the cartilages, and the seed. Mars governs the left ear, the kidneys, the veins, and the testicles. The Sun governs sight, the heart, the brain, the nerves, and all the members of the right side of the body. Venus governs the sense of smell, the liver, and the flesh. The Moon governs taste and swallowing, the stomach, the belly, the private parts of women, and all the members of the left side of the body. Physical impediments <note>In this context, "impediments" refers to permanent physical disabilities or birth defects</note> will generally occur for the most part when the malefic stars <note>original: "infortunatrices stellæ," referring to Mars and Saturn</note> that cause them are oriental <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note>. However, illnesses will happen when these same stars are occidental <note>setting in the west after the Sun</note>. This is because there is a distinction between these two states: for physical impediments occur only once and do not last long <note>likely meaning they are fixed conditions from birth rather than progressing diseases</note>, whereas illnesses either last forever or occur in recurring cycles. Regarding the specific ways these accidents are determined, through experience and observation of the figures and qualities found to signify illness and impediments, we have learned from the outcomes that they follow the positions of the stars. For instance, the sight in one of the eyes will be lost when the Moon is alone in the aforementioned angles <note>The four "cardinal" houses of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</note>, and at that hour there is a conjunction or a full moon, or when it is in another configuration with the Sun and has an aspect <note>original: "alictifal," a Latinized Arabic term for a specific astrological connection</note> with any of the nebulous stars <note>original: "alaceha," referring to star clusters that appear cloudy</note> which are in the zodiacal circle. Examples include the cloudy star in Cancer <note>The Praesepe or Beehive Cluster</note>, the Pleiades <note>original: "athoraie," from the Arabic Al-Thurayya</note> in Taurus, the tip of the arrow in Sagittarius, the sting of the Scorpion, the cluster near the "braid" <note>original: "aldhafera," likely referring to the Coma Berenices or a part of the Lion’s mane</note> in Leo, and the "urn" <note>original: "calbez," a corruption of an Arabic term likely referring to a star in the stream of Aquarius</note> of Aquarius. Furthermore, when the Moon is in one of the occidental angles and Mars alone is oriental, or Mars and Saturn are both oriental and approaching the Moon from a distance—or if the Sun is in one of the angles and these two stars rise before it, or if they are associated with the two luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> in a figure where both luminaries are in the same sign or in opposite signs, and they are morning stars in relation to the Sun but evening stars in relation to the Moon—then the affliction will affect both eyes. Mars will cause the loss of sight we mentioned through some action, such as by iron or by burning. If it is associated with Mercury in the figure, this will happen from wrestling, or sport, or by the actions of criminals. Saturn, however, will cause this through cataracts <note>original: "albugine," literally "whiteness" in the eye</note>, or by cold, or by a discharge <note>original: "iaculatione"</note>, and things of this sort. Likewise, when Venus is in one of the aforementioned angles, specifically the occidental one, and is with Saturn or associated with him in a figure, or has exchanged places with him, and Mars is elevated above her or in opposition to her, it will result in men being unable to have children, and in women having abortions or premature births. Sometimes it also results in the "cutting off" of children <note>This could refer to infant mortality or physical deformities at birth</note>, especially in Cancer, Virgo, and Capricorn; and when the Moon has an aspect <note>original: "alictifal"</note> with Mars from the east. If Venus is associated with Mercury and Saturn in this same way, and Mars is elevated over her or in diametrical opposition, the child will be born without testicles, or as a hermaphrodite, or "closed" <note>likely referring to an imperforate condition or lack of external genitalia</note>. If this is the case and the Sun is also associated in the figure, and the luminaries and Venus are masculine while the Moon is occidental and the malefic stars are in the following degrees, if the child is male, he will be castrated or suffer impediments in his testicles. This is most likely when it occurs in Leo, Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn, or Aquarius. If the child is female, she will be sterile, and perhaps one of these will not escape impediments of the eyes.

If, however, they are in the mid-heaven <note>the highest point of the sky in a birth chart</note> and positioned above the luminaries, and their locations are aligned with them in longitude, these impairments will arrive through great and terrifying accidents: such as a plunge from a height, falling into the hands of robbers, or through four-legged animals. And if Mars is elevated and dominant, these impairments will happen from the burning of fire or from great wounds, or because the person falls into the hands of robbers. But if Saturn is elevated and dominant, these same accidents happen from a fall, or drowning, or from paralysis. The impairments that occur most frequently when the Moon is in the two equinoctial points and the two solstitial points are these: When the Moon is in the vernal equinox point <margin>The Moon in the equinoctial points.</margin> the resulting impairment will specifically be morphea <note>a skin condition causing localized hardening</note>; if it is in the summer solstice point, it will be impetigo <note>a contagious skin infection</note>; in the autumn equinox point, it will be white leprosy <note>original: "albaras," a term for vitiligo or skin patches</note>; but if it is in the winter solstice point, the most frequent result will be freckles <note>original: "lentigo"</note> and similar things.

Furthermore, illnesses happen when the aforementioned malefic stars are associated in the chart with the Sun or Moon, but in a contrary way—that is, when they are associated with the Sun and are rising in the morning, or associated with the Moon and are setting in the evening. That which generally happens from these illnesses is added below. Saturn will make the constitution of the person’s belly cold and very phlegmatic <note>having an excess of phlegm, one of the four humors</note>; or, from humors flowing to the limbs, it will make them lean, sickly, and jaundiced; it also causes sores in the intestines, coughing, spitting, catarrh <note>original: "caule," likely a respiratory discharge</note>, and leprosy; and with all these, pain of the womb happens to women. Mars, however, causes the spitting of blood and melancholy <note>a condition caused by "black bile"</note> which comes from dark colors, abscesses in the lungs, and the itch. When these happen, the person always suffers impairments from incisions and cauterizations <note>burning of the skin for medical treatment</note> performed on them because of illnesses suffered in hidden places, such as piles <note>original: "ficus," referring to hemorrhoids</note> and fistulas, and that which grows and spreads in the body, or things like hot, fiery ulcers, and even ulcers that grow by corroding the flesh. For women, these also cause the abortion of children and their mutilation.

The aforementioned natures of the stars, when associated with one another in the chart, sometimes cause specific illnesses in the limbs of the body, which Mercury helps to increase in malice. For he assists Saturn in cooling, and specifically in the flow of humors to the limbs and in their harm, especially in those things that flow to the palate, the chest, and the stomach. But he assists Mars in drying, and in those things that result from drying: such as the crusts of ulcers, scabs, boils <note>original: "dubailet," a Latinized Arabic term for a tumor or boil</note>, erysipelas <note>a skin infection</note>, foul impetigo, melancholy, frenzy <note>inflammation of the brain</note>, epilepsy, and similar things. These again sometimes have properties according to the differences of the signs in which their association occurred in the aforementioned chart, which was over the two angles <note>the Rising and Midheaven points of the zodiac</note>. For Cancer, Capricorn, and Pisces, and all signs whose figures resemble wild animals or fish, specifically generate illnesses that grow by corroding, as well as impetigo, skin-stripping, scrofula <note>swelling of the lymph nodes</note>, fistulas, leprosy, and similar things. Sagittarius and Gemini, however, cause falls and epilepsy, and similar things. And when the stars are in the final parts of the signs, the resulting illness will specifically appear in the extremities of the body; this happens because of the impairments occurring to it, and because of the flow of humors through which leprosy arises, and for the most part, gout in the feet and hands <note>original: "podagra & chiragra"</note> happens from this.

When these things are so, if the benefic stars <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> are not associated in the chart with the malefic stars that are the cause of these things, nor with the luminaries existing in the angles, the illnesses and the resulting impairments will be very heavy and incurable. The same will happen again when the benefic stars are associated with them in the chart, but the malefic stars are elevated over them or are stronger. But when the benefic stars are in their more dignified positions and are stronger than the misfortunes which are the cause of these works, then the impairments will not be shameful nor lead to disgrace. The illnesses will also be light and will quickly subside. This will similarly happen when the benefic stars are oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note>. For Jupiter hides impairments and makes the illnesses of others subside, with help attributed to him by reason of money or excellence. And when he is with Mercury, he will erase illnesses with medicines, or through the mediation of righteous...

## ON THE QUALITIES OF THE SOUL OF THE NATIVE.
### Chapter XIV.

The method by which bodily accidents are predicted is that which we have previously stated. Regarding the qualities of the soul, however, that which properly pertains to the intellect and reason is always recognized through the qualities of Mercury. But that which pertains to the irrational part <note>the "animal soul" or emotional nature</note>—the height of irrationality—is perceived from the one of the two luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> nearest to the heavy bodies, which is called the Moon, as well as from the stars associated with her in the figure <note>the birth chart</note>, and those having <term>alictisal</term> <note>original: "alictisal," from the Arabic for "application," when a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</note> and <term>alinchiref</term> <note>original: "alinchiref," from the Arabic for "separation," when a planet moves away from an aspect</note> with her.

Therefore, since the movements and qualities of the soul are of many types, it is not at all appropriate that their investigation proceed along a single, flat path; rather, it should be attended to with many observations and diverse considerations. This is because the differences in the signs where the Moon, Mercury, and their lords are located greatly assist in determining the qualities of the soul's properties. Furthermore, the configurations of the stars mentioned above—in respect to the Sun and the angles having a part—also assist the qualities of the soul's movements according to the individual natures of each of the stars.

From the signs, therefore, the **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note> generally make the soul inclined toward unity and universality, and cause it to love civic life. Likewise, they compel the soul to seek praise, to think on divine matters, and to be of sharp wit, a researcher of praiseworthy movement, liberal, held in good opinion by others, and skilled in the judgments of the stars. 

**Common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> make the soul multiform, prone to easy change, difficult to know, agile, loving, unstable, crafty, desiring many things, a lover of music, clever, of clear intellect, and prone to regret. 

**Fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note>, however, make the soul upright, without deceit, steady, of good wit, quiet, intelligent, patient in labor, tolerant, rigid, restraining of pleasures, envious of will, effective, imitative, a seeker of honor, contentious, prone to transgression, and unchangeable.

Regarding the qualities of the stars and their figures: that which is oriental <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note> and ascending, and especially that which is in its own <term>almiua</term> <note>an Arabic-derived term referring to a planet's specific dignity or "face" where it has strength</note> proper to itself, will make the soul free, capable, and confident in its own counsel, rigid, of sharp wit, generous, and open.

When the morning stations of the stars occur, and when they are in the mid-heaven, they make souls that are thoughtful, steady, possessing a good memory, quiet, intelligent, magnanimous, immobile, unchangeable, without deceit, knowledgeable, industrious, investigative, and skilled in the true sciences.

The rising of stars at the beginning of the night, and their setting, make souls that are light, agile, weak, unable to tolerate labor, easily moved by passion, unfortunate, small-souled <note>original: "pusillanimes," meaning lacking in courage or ambition</note>, yet effective in small ways, trying many things, weary, slow to move, and solitary.

The stations of the evening stars, and when they are in the mid-heaven which is under the earth <note>the Imum Coeli or lowest point of the chart</note>, as well as the evening setting of Venus and Mercury during the day, and the morning setting of these same stars during the night, will render the soul clean, pure, and sensible, but with an unreliable memory. Such a soul is not a lover of labor, but a researcher of secret things and an inquirer into the hidden, such as the secret arts <note>original: "nigromantiae," literally "black prophecy" or necromancy, but here implying the occult sciences</note>, hidden matters, the highest subjects, the instruments and machines of science, marvelous works, and the judgments of the stars. It also makes the soul prophetic, an improver of the arts, an interpreter of dreams, and similar things.

Likewise, the stars which dominate the disposition of the soul, when they are in their own places and their own <term>haiz</term> <note>original: "haiz," an Arabic astrological term for a planet being in its preferred "home" environment (e.g., a masculine planet in a masculine sign above the earth by day)</note> suited to them—as we have explained in the preceding sections—make the properties of the souls clear. The effects of these properties nothing can hinder, and each part will remain alone and prosper. This is especially true when one and the same star is the ruler of two places: that is, when it is associated in some way with the place of Mercury in the figure and is separated from the Moon, or has *alictisal* <note>application</note> with her.

### BOOK THREE.

But if it is not as has been said, or if their proper natures manifest in places not suitable to them, they will make the qualities of the soul not open, but hidden, imperfect, and unsuccessful. Indeed, the natures of the stars dominating them, or those elevated above them, make the works of human souls rigid and harmful to their subjects—just like unjust and unfair men, to whom these things happen because of their likeness to misfortune. When these stars dominate, they make their movements toward others light and unhindered; there will be no prohibition or difficulty in this. But when those stars which are from their <term>haiz</term> <note>original: "haiz," an Arabic astrological term referring to a planet's "dignity" or "honor" based on whether its gender and the time of day match its position in the sky</note> are dominated by stars contrary to their <term>haiz</term>, they cause the individuals to be of weak reputation; they will not prosper, and they shall suffer punishments. 

Likewise, just as with just and equitable men—to whom this happens through the likeness of their fortunes—when nothing is elevated above them, they will rejoice in doing good to others and will be praised for it, and no harm shall come to them from it; rather, their own goodness will be the occasion of their own profit. But when stars contrary to them are elevated above them, the opposite of what was said will happen: because of their softness and quietness, and even their love and piety toward men, they will be little valued by people; they will be blamed, and violence will be brought upon them. This, therefore, is the general way in which the qualities of the sensory and rational souls are foretold. However, the properties of specific cases—which happen according to the natures of the stars and their dominion—we shall teach through general discourse, until we arrive at the mixing of influences, which is grasped through a general path.

<margin>Saturn alone as lord of the disposition.</margin>
Therefore, when Saturn alone dominates the disposition of the matters of the soul, and is the lord of the Moon and Mercury, if its position is favorable with respect to the world and the <term>angles</term> <note>the four primary points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli</note>, the native <note>the person born under this alignment</note> will love just men. He will be of a rigid but profound mind, and he will remain firm in his own counsel; he will be hardworking and a debater. Sometimes, however, he will decline slightly from the truth; he will be wealthy, a seeker of power, a shifty person <note>original: "versipellis," literally "one who changes skin," meaning a deceptive or adaptable person</note>, a hoarder, secretive, and envious. 

But if he stands in the contrary of what we have said—that is, if he is in an unfavorable position—the native will be filthy, base, small-souled, ignorant, remaining only in his own counsel, envious, and cowardly. He will be separated from other men, deceitful in his words, a lover of concealment and mourning, shameless, unfortunate, a lover of toil, loving no one, a deceiver of friends, never rejoicing, and malevolent toward good people. 

If he is joined <note>original: "assimiletur," meaning the planet takes on the qualities of or is in aspect with another</note> to Jupiter according to what we said before, and his quality is commendable, the native will be just and will honor his elders. He will be of sound counsel, a helper of the kingdom, a man of understanding, magnanimous, of good reputation, a lover of friends, quiet, intelligent, patient, and a philosopher. 

But if the quality of this star is contrary to the aforementioned, the native will be ignorant of how to do good and senseless. He will occupy himself with diabolical matters <note>original: "diabolica," referring to demons or malevolent spirits</note> and frequent places of prayer. He will predict the future, abhor having children, and have no friends. He will dwell in crypts and caves and will not associate with men; no one will trust him. He will be foolish, wicked, weak, and without love for honor; he will be regretful, unwelcome, prone to bad choices, and long-suffering in his labor. 

If he is joined to Mars, and he himself is of good and laudable quality, the native will be unobservant but very hardworking. He will be wretched and weak, yet harmful; he will attempt great things with fear. He will be a heavy brawler <note>original: "barator," a troublemaker or a cheat</note>, not pious, and will value everything little. He will be immoderate and warlike, putting his own life in fear; he will love disturbances. He will be a traitor, a disturber of others, and possessed of the worst envy. His soul will change based on every event; he will make men labor so that he may rule over others. He will be a transgressor and will hold kings and princes in hatred. He will love hypocrisy and victory; he will be envious and of a wicked depth of character. He will be hard to tolerate, full of rusticity, unbearable, a boaster of himself, and unjust. He will harm men, vilify them, and hate them; he will neither change nor be altered. He will involve himself in many matters and then abandon them lightly. He will be a craftsman and generally studious, and he will even prosper. 

But if this star is in the contrary of the aforementioned, it will make the native a plunderer, a violent cutter of limbs, wretched, of bad quality, and of evil gain. He will not fear God, nor love anyone; he will be a blasphemer, a disturber, a thief, a deceiver, a traitor, a slayer, incestuous, wicked, impious, a murderer, a necromancer <note>original: "nigromanticus," one who communicates with the dead or practices dark magic</note>, a plunderer of places of prayer, a fornicator, a violator of tombs, and generally wicked in all things. 

If Saturn is joined to Venus, and she is of good quality, the native [will love] women...

They will commit injustice and, in general, practice great deception. 

While these things are so, it is also necessary for us to know that the quality of the Moon, as we have described it, will assist in some way. 

<margin>The Moon.</margin> For when the Moon is in the positions of its nodes <note>original: "locis anecaf"; likely a corruption of the Greek 'anabibazon' or 'katabibazon', referring to the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic.</note>, at its northern or southern limits, it will help in the variations of the soul's qualities, causing them to change suddenly. But if it exists in either of the two [favorable] modes, it will assist the sharpness of the soul's qualities and cause the person to act with haste. 

Likewise, when the Moon is ascending and increasing in light <note>Waxing.</note>, it will increase the significations, making them clearer and more essential. But if it is decreasing in light <note>Waning.</note> or stays under the rays of the Sun <note>Combust, or hidden by the Sun's glare.</note>, it will cause the qualities to be more hidden and will not operate with such strength. 

The Sun also assists in some way in these matters described above, provided that it is similar to the stars that rule the soul's disposition. For when it is assimilated to them, if its quality is favorable, the qualities of the soul will be more direct, and the person will be more remote from [evil], as well as more powerful, generous, faithful, and of a better law. But when the Sun is in a state contrary to the above and is not assimilated to the ruling star, the qualities of the soul will be worse; the person will be more miserable and low, and will persist with greater labor in their own counsel. They will be foolish, of a more difficult will, and generally hard to improve.

## ON THE IMPEDIMENTS OF THE SOUL.
### Chapter XIV.

Since the descriptions of the soul’s own impediments <note>In this context, 'impedimenta' refers to mental illnesses, disorders, or "afflictions" of the mind.</note> follow the account of its properties, it is generally appropriate for us to know and observe the qualities of Mercury and the Moon in relation to one another, and their positions relative to the "angles" <note>The four cardinal points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> and the unfortunate stars <note>The "malefics," typically Mars and Saturn.</note>. For when the Moon and Mercury are not connected to each other, or when any of the stars whose qualities cause hindrance are elevated above them or surround them on the eastern horizon, or if they remain in opposition to them, these positions signify that many modes of impediments will come to the qualities of the soul. We will be able to recognize and explain this quite aptly from the aforementioned specific qualities of the stars which are assimilated to those places. However, in our previous demonstrations of the soul's properties, we have already explained many of the weaker impediments of the soul, and perhaps their increase and strength come from an overabundance...

### BOOK THREE

...the abundance <note>The first word "dantia" is the end of "abundantia," meaning abundance or overflow, continued from the previous page.</note> of the works of the unfortunate stars <note>In astrology, the "unfortunate stars" or malefics are Saturn and Mars.</note>, because if anyone calls the qualities of the soul that cannot be restrained "hindrances"—whether they are intensified or relaxed around a balanced temperament—he will name them correctly and properly. However, that which is less overflowing, and is like a weakness, and which entirely exceeds nature and occurs partly in the understanding of the soul and partly in the body receiving the impression, will be identified as I shall describe.

<margin>Epileptics.</margin>
Those who are most frequently **epileptics** are those in whose nativities <note>A nativity is a birth chart.</note> the **Moon** and **Mercury** are not connected to each other (as we said before) nor to the eastern horizon; and along with this, in daytime births, **Saturn** is in the angles <note>The "angles" are the four most powerful points in a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>, or in nighttime births, **Mars** is in the angles, provided that this planet dominates the quality of the soul.

However, the **insane** are those in whom this occurs in the opposite way to what we just described: that is, the lord of the quality is **Saturn** by night or **Mars** by day, especially when they are in the signs of **Cancer**, **Virgo**, or **Pisces**.

<margin>The Possessed.</margin>
The **possessed**, and those called *hydrocephalics* <note>Original Latin: "aurotafelis," a corruption of a term for hydrocephalus, which the text explains as having "excess humidity in the head."</note> (that is, those in whose heads there is an excess of moisture), are those in whose nativities the quality of the unfortunate stars exists as we said, and they dominate the **Moon**. This occurs when the **Moon** is rising just under the sun's rays, and its lord is **Saturn** in conjunction, or **Mars** in "prevention" <note>An astrological term for a planet preceding another in the zodiac.</note>, especially in **Sagittarius** and **Pisces**.

If both unfortunate stars prevail in this quality, the diseases of the soul will be incurable, yet they will not be violent and may go unnoticed. But if both fortunate stars (that is, **Jupiter** and **Venus**) are similar to them, and both unfortunate stars remain in the western angle while the fortunate ones are in the eastern angle, they will produce diseases that, although very violent, are nevertheless curable.

If **Jupiter** is the one that is favorable, the weaknesses will be cured by medicines, either through diets or antidotes. If **Venus** is favorable, the sicknesses will be driven away by prophecies or divine help. However, if the unfortunate stars are in the eastern angle and the fortunate ones are in the western angle, the sicknesses will be incurable, violent, and less obvious; the weakness of epilepsy will always endure with shouting and a fear of death. 

The insane and those lacking sense will be impossible to restrain; they will hinder their own kinsmen and speak foul things. Similar things happen to the possessed: their weaknesses and the overflow of moisture that harms the head cause *enthusiasm* <note>Original: "entusiamesmus," referring to a state of being possessed by a spirit or divine frenzy.</note> and excessive exposure, as well as impulsive jumping toward people, whom they will strike, and other such behaviors.

Certain places in which that quality exists will sometimes help by their own nature. For the places of the **Sun** and **Mars** specifically contribute to insanity. The places of **Jupiter** and **Mercury** contribute to the weakness of epilepsy. The place of **Venus** assists through prophecies and the speaking of hidden things. The places of **Saturn** and the **Moon** assist the possessed and the hindrances caused by fluids.

Therefore, these are the many species of sicknesses occurring in the active part of the soul, which generally arrive through these qualities according to their nature. However, the differences that specifically occur in the "receiving part" <note>The body or the physical manifestation of the gendered soul.</note> regarding the increase or decrease of natural things in males and females will be very apparent. We shall reach their prognosis by a path similar to the one already described. We place the **Moon** with **Mercury** as we did there, and observe the likeness of **Venus** and **Mars** to them.

After the explanation of these things, we shall show that if the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> alone are in masculine signs, they will cause men to perform those things natural to them, but women will act excessively against their own nature, and their natural qualities will be converted into the strength and masculinity of the soul. 

Likewise, if **Mars** and **Venus** (or one of them) are masculine, men will be very involved in the natural affairs of **Venus** and will be overly concerned with that vice. From the matters of intercourse, they will hastily desire to do shameful things that are against the law. Women, however, will perpetrate unnatural acts of desire more than is right, and will be *tribades* <note>Original: "thahaherat," an unusual term explained by the text as women who "mix with one another in action."</note>, that is, they will mingle with one another in their actions. If **Venus** alone is masculine, what they perpetrate will be hidden and unknown. But if **Mars** is masculine, it will be so manifest that sometimes the women they live with will be treated as if they were their own wives.

# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY'S QUADRIPARTITE <note>original: "Quadripartitum," also known as the Tetrabiblos, the foundational text of Western astrology.</note>

<margin>Venus alone feminine.</margin>
But if these same stars are in the opposite of the aforementioned condition—that is, if only the luminaries <note>The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.</note> with the described qualities are found in feminine signs—women will act according to what is natural to them. Men, however, will commit acts that are against their nature, and with a softness and femininity of soul, they will overstep what is natural. Likewise, if **Venus** alone is in a feminine state, women will indulge excessively in illegitimate acts of Venus <note>Meaning sexual acts or desires.</note>; yet they will more frequently lean toward natural acts, and will do so with anyone, to the point that they will deny sexual intercourse to no one, whether it concerns physical beauty or is against the law. Men, however, will be effeminate and soft, and more inclined to the natural acts of Venus <note>In this context, it suggests a passive role or a focus on pleasure over traditional "masculine" vigor.</note>. They will not prohibit anyone from illicit intercourse, except that they will perform it in secret. 

Likewise, if **Mars** is in a feminine state, they will perform both of these things—that is, fornication and shameful acts—and illicit acts will be done openly and without a blush on the face, so much so that because of this excessive openness, they will be blasphemed and disgraced. The **oriental** <note>Rising before the sun.</note> and morning qualities of Venus and Mars in masculinity aid in this openness. However, their **vespertine** <note>Setting after the sun.</note> and western quality in femininity aids in concealment. Similarly, if **Saturn** is with them, he will help them incur horrors, foulness, and defilements, as well as great shame, because his nature typically assists in each of these things. But if **Jupiter** is with them, he will increase the beauty and grace of things, as well as a proper sense of modesty. And if **Mercury** is with them, he will assist in the public exposure of matters, the haste of future events, and the multitude and increase of their various kinds.

## CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY'S QUADRIPARTITE WORK, BOOK IV. INTRODUCTION.

Regarding those things in which the conditions before birth, those which occur at the very hour of birth, and also all those things which occur after birth can be observed, we have demonstrated to the greatest extent that which is proper and natural to the individual, and by which their entire natural being is proven. Now we turn to those things which happen from the outside—specifically, those whose explanation follows opportunely from what was previously sent. The first task is to judge the prosperity of the newborn in **substance** <note>Meaning material wealth or possessions.</note> and health, and to describe his prosperity in substance collectively with matters pertaining to the body, as well as to explain his prosperity in health together with matters pertaining to the soul.

### ON THE PROSPERITY AND WEALTH OF THE NEWBORN.
->Chapter I.<-

<margin>Which path of becoming rich each planet signifies.</margin>
In what manner the quality of a person's substance <note>wealth</note> arrives, we must grasp knowledge from the **Part of Fortune** <note>A mathematical point in a birth chart calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant.</note> alone. We shall always learn this by observing the distance between the **Sun** and the **Moon**, and by projecting that distance from the **ascendant** in both day and night births, for the reasons we showed in the discussion on life. The way of this observation is as follows. 

We shall observe the stars that rule the disposition of that sign [where the Part of Fortune falls]. We will consider what their strength and similarity are, as we said before. Likewise, we will observe the stars that are associated with them in the figure <note>the chart layout</note>, or which rise above them, whether they are from their own <term>haiz</term> <note>A technical term for a planet being in a favorable condition regarding its gender and the time of day (sect).</note> or from the opposite <term>haiz</term>. For when the rulers of the aforementioned Part are strong, the newborn will be of great wealth. This is especially true if the luminaries testify to its similarity. 

Furthermore, **Saturn** will signify that the wealth of the newborn comes from buildings, the cultivation of land, or from navigation. **Jupiter**, however, will designate that his riches will be gathered from trusts, or from stewardship <note>original: "baiula," referring to the office of a guardian or tutor</note>, or from any kind of uprightness. **Mars** will signify that his riches come from the command and governance of armies. **Venus** will announce that they are gathered from the gifts of friends or from women. **Mercury** will signify that wealth flows from the industry of trade. ### CHAPTER II: ON THE PROSPERITY AND STANDING 
### OF THE NATIVE.

<margin><unclear>whether in signs or the position of angles</unclear></margin>
The matters of standing <note>original: "valetudo," which usually means health, but in this astrological context refers to the native's "strength" or "validity" in the world—their social power and status.</note> and the prosperity of that same standing are observed from the qualities of the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> and the stars surrounding them; it is necessary for us to observe their similarity in this regard as well. For when both luminaries are in masculine signs, and both or one of them is located in the angles <note>The four "cardinal" points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>—especially that one which is the lord of the *haiz*—and the five wandering stars [planets] surround them, and if those surrounding the Sun are rising in the morning and those surrounding the Moon are rising in the evening, we will not doubt that the native shall be a king. But if the stars that surround them are likewise in the angles, or share a relationship with the angles existing above the earth, the native will be of great standing, most powerful, and a king of the world. His fortune will also be increased when the surrounding stars are on the right <note>original: "dextre," referring to the dexter aspect, considered more powerful than the sinister aspect.</note> and are associated with the angles above the earth.

However, when the qualities of the other stars are like this, but only the Sun revolves in a masculine sign while the Moon is in a feminine one, and only one of them is in the angles, the native will be a man of sole rule and a killer <note>original: "interfector," suggesting a ruler who maintains power through force or a tyrant.</note>. But if, along with this, the surrounding stars do not appear in the angles nor testify to them, the native will be of great name only, and his standing will appear like that of one who rules only one part—such as the rule of a governor or the rule of an army—and not like the rule of an **Alcaidis** <term>Alcaidis: a Latinization of the Arabic 'al-qā'id', referring here to a supreme magistrate or high official who manages the affairs of an entire kingdom</term>. But if the luminaries are not in the angles, but several of those surrounding stars are in the angles or share a relationship with them in the figure, he will not be of such great standing, nor even of a great name, and he will be unknown. Nevertheless, he will prevail in managing cities, and in the matters of managing life, he will be mediocre. 

If, however, the stars that surround the luminaries have no similarity with the angles, the native will appear wretched and unhappy in his works. And if the luminaries are neither in the angles nor in masculine signs, nor even surrounded by the "fortunes" <note>The "fortunes" or benefics are usually Jupiter and Venus.</note>, he will be in the extreme of misery and lack of prosperity. Therefore, the path that must be walked in the investigation of these matters is this one which we have shown regarding the increase and decrease of standing. We must observe many qualities that exist between increase and decrease through those things found in that species of particular alteration which the luminaries and the stars surrounding them possess, and which they have assigned to the attendants. For when the dispositors <note>The planets that rule the signs where other planets are located.</note> are the lords of the *haiz* or the fortunes, the native will endure longer in his standing. But if those contrary to the *haiz* dominate, or if they are "infortunes" <note>The "infortunes" or malefics are usually Saturn and Mars.</note>, his standing will appear weak and will pass away lightly. 

The matters of future standing are to be observed from the specific qualities of the stars that surround the luminaries. For when **Saturn** is the dispositor of this matter, the strength of the standing will consist in a multitude of substance [property] and the gathering of money. But if **Jupiter** or **Venus** is the dispositor, his strength will be in pleasures and gifts, and in honor and magnanimity. If it is **Mars**, it will be in the command of expeditions, in victories, and in the fear of his subordinates. And if it is **Mercury**, it will be in intellect and discipline, and in the management of affairs.

<margin>Mercury as the author of professional skill.</margin>
For if Mercury is the author of the work and professional skill <note>original: "magisterii," referring to one's trade, craft, or vocation</note>, the native will be a negotiator <note>original: "barator," often implying a clever speaker or someone involved in legal disputes</note>, an accountant, a teacher, a merchant, a scribe, a researcher of things, or a priest. <margin>Venus.</margin>
If the authority of the work and professional skill belongs to Venus, the native will concern themselves with the scent of flowers and spices, or with wine, dyeing, pigments, or things pertaining to ornamentation. For example, they might trade in spices and medicines, arrange various flowers, be an innkeeper or a weaver, trade in pigments, or paint and vary colors, or weave silk. <margin>Mars.</margin>
But if Mars is associated with the Sun in the figure <note>The birth chart or horoscope</note>, their work and skill will involve fire—such as the work of a cook, a metal-smith, or work with herbs and gold mines. If he is not associated with the Sun, the native’s skill will be practiced with iron—such as building ships, plowing, architecture, cutting stone, carving seals into the stones of rings, hewing trees, and similar tasks. If Saturn testifies to him, he will be a sailor, a swimmer, a water-carrier, a cook, a painter, or someone who works in bath-houses. But if Jupiter testifies to him, he will be a soldier, an officer of punishments <note>an executioner or jailer</note>, a tax collector, an innkeeper, or a butcher.

Likewise, if two planets have lordship over the professional skill, and they are Venus and Mercury, the native will practice music, games, singing, or the invention of songs, or any kind of composing. If Jupiter testifies to them, he will be a lawyer <note>original: "placitator"</note> and an accountant, and will always be in places where people gather, or near the gates of royalty; he will teach children and be occupied with the affairs of the common people.

But if Mars and Mercury have lordship over the work and professional skill, he will be learned in the making of statues and weapons; he will be a sculptor of things used in sacred houses, and will make figures of animals. He will be a wrestler, a doctor, a surgeon, a sorcerer, a fornicator, and a forger of documents. But if Saturn testifies to them, the native will be a killer, a thief of others' clothes, a highwayman, and will live in caves, and be a deceiver. But specifically, the differences of professional skill <note>original: "magisterij," referring to one's trade, craft, or vocation</note> are influenced in various ways by each of the figures of the signs in which the stars that dominate are moved to their work. <margin>The power of the figures of the stars.</margin> For signs whose figures resemble human shapes help to perfect every professional skill of the sciences which men need. But if she is in Virgo or Scorpio, he will be a necromancer and an astrologer; he will reveal hidden things and predict the future. If she is in Leo, Aries, or Libra, he will be a prophet, an interpreter of dreams, and a wise man. 

This, therefore, is the path which we ought to observe to rationally understand the qualities of professional skills and their types. However, the quantities of their powers are to be observed through the strengths of the stars which dominate the disposition. For when they are oriental <term>oriental: rising before the sun, usually a position of greater strength and activity</term> or positioned in the angles <term>angles: the four pivotal points of a chart—Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli—associated with high visibility</term>, his professional skills will be of dignity, dominance, and strength. But if they are western or falling <term>cadent: positions away from the angles, usually signifying a weaker or more subservient social role</term> from his angles, the professional skills will be established under the power of others. But if the fortunes <term>fortunae: the "benefic" or lucky planets, Jupiter and Venus</term> prevail over them, his professional skill will be suitable, commendable, and peaceful, nor will he ever be deceived in it. But if the infortunes <term>infortunae: the "malefic" or difficult planets, Saturn and Mars</term> prevail over them, they will be base, despicable, and harmful, and he will be deceived in them. If Saturn is the impeder, coldness, delay, and laziness will happen there. If Mars is the impeder, fear and destruction will occur there. And if both are impeders, there will be many inconveniences in the whole time of his life. Moreover, their increase and decrease will be perceived from the qualities of the stars which are the causes of things to come, according to their habit toward the angles, whether they are morning or evening stars...

<margin>On wives.</margin> If the Moon has application <term>ictisal: an Arabic-derived term (al-ittisal) used in medieval astrology to describe "application," where a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one</term>, the man will betroth many wives. For if the Moon has an application to Saturn, his wife will be hardworking, but her character will be wild and harsh. If it has an application to Jupiter, she will be fitting and suitable, possessing a learned disposition. But if to Mars, she will be bold and untamable. And if to Venus, she will be beautiful and very cheerful. If, however, to Mercury, she will be of good intellect. Likewise, if Venus is joined with Jupiter, Saturn, or Mercury, she will be beneficial to him in matters pertaining to life, and she will greatly love both him and their children. But if Venus is with Mars, she will be destructive, unstable, and lacking in understanding.

In the marriages of women, the qualities of the Sun at the hour of the woman's birth must be observed. For when the Sun is in the two eastern quarters—that is, in the orientation of the chart—she will be betrothed in her youth, or in her old age she will take a young man as a husband. But if the Sun is in either of the two western quarters, she will be joined to a husband late in life, or in her early youth she will be betrothed to an old man. If the Sun is in a sign of a single form and we find a morning planet <term>matutinalem: a planet that rises before the sun</term> within it, she will be given to only one man. <margin>The husband.</margin> And if it is in a double-bodied sign <note>signs like Gemini, Pisces, or Sagittarius which represent dual natures</note> or one of multiple forms, or if the Sun is associated with more than one morning planet in the figure, she will have many husbands. 

Likewise, if Saturn is associated with the Sun in the figure, her husband will be upright, just, and hardworking. If Jupiter has fellowship with the Sun, he will be humble and magnanimous; but if Mars, he will be cruel, without affection, and will not humble himself; and if Venus, he will be upright and handsome; but if Mercury is associated, he will be successful in the affairs of life and hardworking. But if Venus is with Saturn, her husband will be weary and will restrain himself from sexual acts; and if she is with Jupiter, her husband will be good, just, and modest; and if with Mars, he will be of a sharp temperament, very preoccupied with sexual acts, and will be a fornicator; but if she remains with Mercury, he will be very devoted to his own children.

What we said above regarding the two eastern quarters of the Sun should be understood as referring to the two quarters where one precedes the point of the ascendant and the other precedes the point of the descendant of the zodiacal circle. In the case of the Moon, we must understand this to refer to the two quarters between the conjunction <note>New Moon</note> and the opposition <note>Full Moon</note>, until half of that light is reached. From the two western quarters, we understand those which are opposite to these aforementioned ones.

When the luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are suitably associated with each other in both births <note>the charts of both the man and the woman</note> through an aspect—that is, if they regard each other by a trine or sextile—and especially when this occurs through "reception" <term>tabdil: from the Arabic al-tabdil, meaning mutual reception, where two planets occupy each other's home signs</term>, and most of all when the Moon in a man's birth is suitably associated with the Sun in a woman's birth, their marriage will never be dissolved. It will, however, be dissolved on any occasion when the aforementioned places of the luminaries are in signs that are not connected to each other, or which are diametrically opposed to each other, or regard each other through a square aspect. 

If the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets</note> direct their rays toward luminaries that are joined in a suitable figure, the marriage will remain in mutual affection, joy, and health. But if the "infortunes" <note>malefics</note> regard them, it will indeed remain, but in strife, hatred, and loss. A similar thing happens regarding their incompatible qualities. For if the fortunes bear witness to the luminaries, a total separation is not denoted; instead, they will be reconciled after a separation and will remain together lastingly with affection. But if the infortunes bear witness to them, the separation will be very litigious <margin>Divorce.</margin> and full of ferocity. But if Mercury alone is with them, they will be clearly separated with accusations and complaints. If Venus is with them, this will happen because of adultery, or sorcery <note>original: "nigromantiam," referring here to love charms or dark arts used to influence relationships</note>, or things similar to these.

The manner in which a marriage is formed will be demonstrated through the qualities of Venus, Mars, and Saturn. For if these are suitably positioned with the luminaries, the marriage will be fit and legitimate. For there is, as it were, a certain disposition held between Venus and each of the aforementioned planets. ### ON FRIENDSHIPS AND ENMITIES, Chapter VI.

Indeed, the qualities and friendships—of which those that are more durable are called friendships and enmities; while those which are truly less durable are called, in another sense, "common applications and repulsions"—it is fitting to investigate in such a manner. Therefore, in those qualities which we consider in major matters, it is necessary for us to observe the places which, in the birth chart of each person, most agree in dominion and power: that is, the places of the Sun and Moon, and of the Ascendant, and of the Lot of Fortune <note>original: "partis & fortunae"; a calculated point in a horoscope representing prosperity and fate.</note>. For when all these have been in the same sign, or have exchanged places either partially or universally—but especially when there are about seventeen degrees between both Ascendants—we shall say that there will be a fixed love between them, which will neither be separated nor disturbed. If, however, they have rotated in places which are not gathered together, or which are diametrically opposed to each other, they will be extremely discordant, or will oppose each other for a long time. 

But if they are in neither of those ways, but only in signs which are associated in turn—if they regard each other by trine <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered harmonious.</note> or sextile <note>An aspect of 60 degrees, also considered harmonious but weaker.</note>—the affection between them will be lesser. If, however, they see each other from the fourth <note>A "square" aspect of 90 degrees, traditionally associated with tension.</note>, we do not doubt that there will be minor discords between them. So that sometimes, in their affection, interruptions of words <note>Meaning quarrels or breaks in communication.</note> will occur, and they will value each other little by turns; these things, however, will happen when the malefic planets <note>original: "infortunae"; specifically Saturn and Mars, which were thought to bring challenges.</note> pass through the locations of the figures. In discord, however, peace and concord will be interposed even when the benefic planets <note>original: "fortunae"; specifically Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring luck.</note> run through the locations of the figures. 

Wherefore, since the mode of friendship and enmity exists in three ways: that is, because the lords of these two qualities are forced to do this either from the birth, or for the sake of gain and loss, or on account of anger and joy. When all these aforementioned places, or as many of them as possible, are similar to each other, friendships will be gathered from all these kinds; but if they do not agree with each other, enmities will be collected from them. But if their affection or agreement—or the opposite of agreement—should be between these two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> alone, a necessary affection will be procreated from it, which is called true and supreme friendship, in which one must trust most of all; truly, a necessary enmity, and as bad as can be, which will never cease, will be born from it. 

Likewise, when their agreement, or its opposite, is between the two locations of the Lot of Fortune for each person, what will be perfected from it will proceed from the cause of gain or loss. But if it should be between the two Ascendants, we shall say that what is brought about happens on account of anger and joy. It is fitting for us to observe also the modes of the places in which this association of the figure exists, and also that which is elevated above them, as well as the planets which regard them. For in births in which the planets that are elevated above the places of the common figure were in almost the same sign, or in that which is elevated above it, it is fitting for us to assign the occasion of friendship and enmity to those elevated planets in their strength, durability, and sincerity. In births, however, in which the aspect of the planets appears fruitful and suitable, it is not unfitting to attribute the occasion of the fruit of friendship and the improvement of enmity to the planets regarding them.
