# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITE

It is not useless to observe the times in which the Hyleg <note>original: "Alhileg"; the planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life" or "releasor."</note>, moving away from the stellar locations of one nativity <note>A "nativity" refers to an individual's birth chart.</note>, passes through the stellar locations of another's nativity; for according to this, there will be particular friendships and enmities. Those friendships which have not known a shorter limit of their permanence before this separation will find no end to their long duration of time until the Hyleg is joined to another star.

**Saturn and Jupiter**, therefore, when one of them reaches the location of the other, will judge friendship between them to arise from agriculture and inheritances. **Saturn and Mars**, when one occupies the location of the other, will generate spontaneous quarrels and discords between them. But from **Saturn and Venus**, fellowship and affection will be produced for the sake of kinship, though it will be terminated very quickly. **Saturn and Mercury** will signify their fellowship and association in the affairs of life, as well as in giving and receiving, and in trade and similar matters.

Through **Jupiter and Mars**, fellowship and love between them will be produced by the occasion of riches, or by any dominion or management. Through **Jupiter and Venus**, they will love each other mutually because of women, or for the sake of divine service, or through houses of prayer, or from prophets, or similar things. **Jupiter and Mercury** will indicate spontaneous fellowship by the occasion of the dialectical sciences and prophecy.

**Mars and Venus**, so to speak, will associate them together through dalliance <note>original: "drueria"; refers to love-affairs, illicit romance, or courtly gallantry.</note> or adultery, or fornication, or the Sodomitic crime <note>A historical legal and religious term for same-sex acts or non-procreative sexual behavior.</note>; however, they will have brief durability in this, because one of them is a "fortune" <note>A "fortune" or benefic planet, like Venus, brings positive outcomes.</note> and the other is an "infortune" <note>An "infortune" or malefic planet, like Mars, brings challenge or strife.</note>. **Mars and Mercury** will signify enmities, deceptions, and quarrels between them by the occasion of incantations and necromancy <note>original: "nigromantiæ"; black magic or divination through the dead.</note>. **Venus and Mercury** will bring about fellowship between them in the affairs of life, or because of craftsmanship <note>original: "magisterij"; refers to mastery of an art or trade.</note>, music, books, or women.

It is fitting for us to know that the increase and decrease in the vigor of common friendship and enmity is found from the qualities of the places in which they exist with respect to the four primary places <note>Likely referring to the four "Angles" of the chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> where dominion and power reside. For if they are in the angles, or with the Part of Fortune, or with the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>, that which they signify will be clearer and more apparent. But if they remain far removed from these, it will by no means appear. The health and harms of this friendship are perceived according to the property of the favorable or unfavorable quality of the stars looking upon the aforementioned places.

Indeed, to treat of servants regarding their affection or hatred for their masters: the planets will indicate this from their own sign, which is in the place of misfortune <note>Usually the 12th House, associated with enemies and slaves.</note> by natural similarity. This is found among the planets who look upon that place at the hour of birth, or who were in that same place or its opposite. Especially, those planets which rule that sign will indicate it when they agree with the places of their dominion and power in the association of the figures, or if they are of the same kind as them.

## ON TRAVELS
## Chapter VII.

**The matter** of travel <note>original: "peregrinationis"; refers to journeys to foreign lands or living abroad.</note> is perceived from the qualities of the luminaries with respect to the angles, but especially from the qualities of the **Moon**. For when the Moon is occidental <note>Setting in the West.</note> and removed from the angles, she will judge travels and changes from place to place. Similarly, **Mars** will also sometimes operate this way when he is occidental, or when he has declined from the zenith <note>The point directly overhead.</note> of the heads, provided his distance from the luminaries is the distance of opposition or the aspect of the quartile <note>A 90-degree angle, considered a stressful aspect.</note>.

If the **Part of Fortune** again falls in the signs that signify travel, his whole life, works, and acts will be in foreign places. If the fortunes <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus.</note> look upon the aforementioned places of travel, or proceed toward them, or follow them, those things he does in his travels will be successful and easy, nor will he ever be contradicted in anything. But if the infortunes <note>Malefic planets like Saturn and Mars.</note> look upon them, those works of his will be laborious and harmful, full of fear, and he will return slowly from his travel. ### BOOK FOUR

In these places, they are associated within the chart <note>The "figure" or "nativity," meaning the birth chart.</note>, as we have shown in the preceding sections, and will always be apparent. And whenever the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> are in either of the two eastern quarters, the person will more frequently undertake journeys toward the eastern and southern parts. But if they rotate in either of the two western quarters, or in the West itself, their journey will appear to be toward the north and west. Furthermore, if the signs themselves which signify pilgrimage—or their planetary lords—are of a single form, the journey will happen occasionally. But if they consist of two bodies or two figures <note>original: "duum corporum"; referring to bicorporeal or "double-bodied" signs like Gemini, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note>, the journey will be continuous and endure for a long time. 

However, if **Jupiter and Venus** rule over the places signifying travel and the locations of the luminaries, there will be no fear in the journey; instead, it will be desired by the person, because he will carry out diplomatic missions for the rulers of lands for the sake of his friends. This will be aided by a favorable temperament of the air and an abundance of things beneficial to him. If **Mercury** is with them on this aforementioned occasion, he follows with great profit, and he will lead his mission to a successful conclusion; gifts will even be given to him, and he will be honored. 

If **Saturn and Mars** rule the places of the luminaries—especially when they are in opposition by distance—what happens to him will be called an infirmity, and he will be greatly hindered. If both stay in humid <note>Water</note> signs, this hindrance will happen to him from the infestation of a sea journey, and from drowning, or because of misfortune; a journey of a dry life will occur through the crossing of desert places. But if they are in fixed signs, this will come from falling from heights <note>original: "praecipitatione"</note> and from powerful blasts of wind. If indeed they are in the solstitial or equinoctial signs, we will not doubt that this happens to him through the lack and deprivation of those things which they need, and through the qualities of corrupted air bringing on sickness. Furthermore, if they are in signs of human form, we shall say it happens from highway robberies, or betrayals, or lootings; but if they are in signs whose forms resemble the forms of wild animals, it will happen from the greed of wolves or from an earthquake. But if **Mercury** is among them, it will proceed from attacks that bring fear, or from the bites of beasts, or by the occasion of venomous animals. 

In the properties of accidental things—that is, in the differences of future occasions, whether they help or hinder—it is fitting for us to observe the occasions according to the aforementioned circumstances from the places of dominion, which relate to works, substance, and matters of the body and health. Indeed, the knowledge of the hours <note>The specific timing or seasons of life.</note> in which these future things will happen will be detected from the qualities arriving at the beginnings of subsequent years. In this chapter, therefore, let it suffice for us to have treated this.

# ON THE QUALITY OF DEATH
## of the native. Chapter VIII.

Since after this brief explanation of the preceding matters, the qualities of death must be observed by us from those things which we predicted in life, it is fitting for us to know whether death comes from the "projection of rays" <note>An astrological technique involving the aspects or "glances" cast by planets.</note> or from the arrival of the significator <note>The planet or point representing the life force.</note> at the western angle <note>The Descendant, or the western horizon, traditionally associated with the end of life.</note>. For if death should intervene from the projection of rays, or because of any conjunction of that planet to which it is joined, it is not improper to consider the places of those planets to which it is joined when we wish to know the qualities of death. 

But if death should be present because of the application of the planet to the angle of the west, the western angle itself must be observed. This is because the quality of death will be detected according to the planets which follow those aforementioned places, or according to the planets which first reached them (if the planets which follow them are not found), provided we have accepted the properties with their natures in the science of the differences of the accidents of the stars in the chart. We shall specifically consider the qualities of the aforementioned western place which they hold from the signs and from the natures of the "terms" <note>original: "terminorum"; specific subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by different planets.</note>. 

<margin>Saturn as the lord of death,</margin>When **Saturn**, therefore, is the lord of death, it occurs by the occasion of a long infirmity, or phthisis <note>A historical term for tuberculosis or a progressive wasting of the body.</note>, or catarrh <note>Inflammation of the respiratory tract.</note>, or because of the dissolution of the body, or a hectic fever <note>A fever typical of chronic diseases like consumption.</note>, as well as from ileus <note>A painful obstruction of the bowel.</note>, or dropsy <note>original: "hydropisi"; the modern term is edema, an accumulation of fluid in the tissues.</note>, or a loosening of the belly <note>Diarrhea or dysentery.</note>, or...

For those whose death nature has decreed in the manner aforesaid, when the planets which have the disposition of death are according to their own proper and natural qualities, or similar to them, and no planet whose occasion brings a bad and heavy death rises over them, they shall depart from life.

<margin>Death beyond the law of nature.</margin> 
However, death which is brought by force and not by the law of nature <note>i.e., a violent death</note> will happen when both malefics <note>Saturn and Mars, the planets traditionally associated with hardship</note> fall into the place of death, so that they stay in that same place, or in its fourth aspect <note>A "square" aspect of 90 degrees</note> or opposite, or if any of them has lordship and power over the Sun and Moon, or over the place of both. A bad and unjust death happens because of the conjunction of the two malefics, and its magnitude will come through the testimony of the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note>. But the quality of the death itself arrives according to the aspects of other planets and the signs in which the malefics are found. 

For when **Saturn** is in the fourth aspect of the Sun, or in its opposite, and in a contrary *alaiz* <note>original: "alaiz"; a medieval astrological term for a planet’s condition or "sect" relative to the horizon and the Sun</note>, if he remains in fixed signs, the person will be crushed by the bonds of death by the hands of a stoning crowd, or by strangulation, or will be afflicted by deadly punishments. And when he is western <note>Setting in the west</note> and the Moon follows him, we know the same happens. But when he is in signs whose figures resemble the forms of wild beasts, he will perish by the diseases of beasts <note>Or attacks by them</note>. 

If Jupiter testifies to him and is unfortunate <note>afflicted by bad aspects</note>, he will be condemned to be thrown as food for wild beasts in an assembly of men on a well-known and solemn day. If he stays in opposition to the place of the other luminary holding the ascendant, he will be endangered by death in prison. 

But if Mercury is joined to him in the figure, especially in the figures of serpents of the celestial sphere, or in signs whose forms are of predatory beasts, he will be torn by the bites of venomous animals. If Venus be with them, he will die by a deadly drink given through the fraud of women. If he claims a place for himself in Virgo or Pisces, or in humid signs, and is associated with the Moon in the figure, he will end his life by drowning. But if he be in a ship <note>Likely referring to the constellation Argo Navis</note>, he will be deprived of life by the stormy tossing of the sea. And if he be in any of the solstitial signs, or in quadrupedal signs with the Sun, or remains in the opposition of Mars in place of the Sun, he will be destroyed by the fall of a ruin. If however he is in the mid-heaven or its opposite, he will be cast down from a height and die. 

**Mars**, however, when he is in the fourth or opposite aspect of the Sun or Moon, and in his contrary *alaiz*, if he revolves in signs of human form, he will perish by the cutting off of his head because of wars and civil disturbances occurring among his kindred, or by fighting; or he will lay his own hand upon himself because of women, or be killed by the hands of women. That will happen when Venus again testifies to him. 

If Mercury is associated with him in the figure, he will be torn apart by the hands of thieves and pirates or ambushers. But if he be in signs of severed limbs or imperfect fortunes, or in the "head of the chain" <note>Likely referring to a specific star or point in a constellation like Andromeda or Perseus</note> with its iron lord <note>referring to Mars as the planet of iron</note>, he will pass away by the cutting off of his head or limbs. But if he remains in the mid-heaven or in its opposite, he will be hung on a cross; especially so if he is with *Ficare* <note>likely "Phicare," a star in the constellation of Leo or a similar stellar reference</note> and Andromeda.

->ON THE DIVISION OF TIMES IN<-
->the life of the native. Chapter 9.<-

<margin>Chapter 9.</margin>
After we have generally explained the mode of predicting in each of these species—reaching toward the perfection of knowledge of these universal matters as has been shown—it is naturally fitting that we add those things which are to be observed in the partition of nativities <note>birth charts</note> through the times of life, and in the particular matters to be attended to by the aforementioned modes. Therefore, just as the judgments and estimations of particular things, which are taken from the aforementioned places in the narration of nativities, are set forth—and even if the greater part of them are judgments and estimations taken from those same regions <note>general climates or ethnicities</note>—these are the judgments in which the particular details observed in individual births are generally contained, such as the forms and figures of bodies, the qualities and properties of souls, as well as the differences in customs and laws. It is also fitting for those who observe this naturally to adhere to the first occasion <note>the most general context</note>, which is more suitable than the others, so that they are never deceived by mere similarity in nativities. 

For instance, one would be deceived if they said a person born in **Ethiopia** was adorned with whiteness and straightness of hair, or that the qualities of their souls were more domestic, or more inclined to reason, or that they were investigators of things <note>Ptolemy argues that the general environment/race overrides the individual chart's specifics</note>. Or if they affirmed that the inhabitants of **Germany** had wild souls, were borrowed, and disagreed with reason; or again, if they were deceived regarding the customs and laws proper to each of these nations. Just as in marriages, if they decreed that **Italians** might marry their own sisters; for it would have to be added to the judgment if they were born in **Egypt**, or that they might marry their mothers without this addition being a problem if they were born in **Persia**. 

It is fitting first to observe the universal qualities in one's judgments and estimations generally, and then to add the particular quantities through which they will judge, so that they may grasp the increases and decreases occurring in them from this. 

<margin>The ages of man</margin> 
Similarly, in the division of the times and hours of the person born, one should first set forth the temporal differences of the years and their similarities with each following future event. They should inspect their qualities so that they are in no way deceived in the general accidents observed in the birth; for it is necessary that we do not judge that a child should work or marry, or do that which can be done by no one except those of a greater age, or that a man of decrepit age should beget offspring or perform acts possible only for youth. Rather, it is generally fitting for them to add those things which they have grasped through the observation of times, matching the years that are suitable to those things which are similar to them and which can happen in them. For the same path, the same mode, and the same single order is held for all temporal differences, embracing the universal nature that contains all men, and obtaining a similarity with the order of the seven planets. This path or order begins from the first years and from the sphere closest to us, namely the **Lunar** sphere, and unfolds in the final years to the last sphere of the planets, which is called **Saturn's**.

### CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S QUADRIPARTITUM

...is explained. It must also be understood that in individual years, events occur that share a likeness with the nature of the planet that has direct rule over that year. The observation of this matter is necessary for understanding the general quality of each of these periods of time.

<margin>The Moon rules over Infancy.</margin>
The particular differences between these ages will be recognized from their inherent properties. Because the **Moon** rules the disposition of the infant for the first 4 years—which corresponds to the number associated with her—the infant undergoes a rapid growth due to the tenderness and weakness of its body. During this time, there is a greater and more frequent need for "watery" nourishment <note>referring to breast milk and the "moist" nature of the Moon in ancient medicine</note>, and a constant, slight alteration of its form. Furthermore, the soul is held in a weak and imperfect state, as is fitting for those matters which occur because of the part of the soul that governs physical formation.

<margin>Mercury rules over Childhood.</margin>
And since the second planet, which is called **Mercury**, is the master of the disposition for the ten following years—which are the years of childhood and are called the "second age"—he is the master of half the number of twenty years <note>original: "numeri medietatis uiginti annorum"; an arithmetic way of saying 10 years</note>. During this space of years, the child enters into the manifest effects of the intellect and the reasoning of the soul, as if the "plant of education" and the roots of the soul’s qualities were being planted within him. In these years, through the properties of those things that are being adapted, discipline and learning begin to shine, and the child rises up, awakened to the initial modes of exercise and study.

<margin>Venus rules over Adolescence.</margin>
But because **Venus** presides over the disposition of the following eight years—which are the years of adolescence and are called the "third age"—she rules for a number of years equal to her own orbital period <note>original: "circuuolutionis"; refers to the 8-year cycle of Venus</note. At this time, the movement of the flow of seed begins, along with the gathering of its abundance, and the adolescent himself is moved toward the acts of Venus <note>sexual activity</note>. This is the time, we say, in which the soul is gripped by a likeness of voracity <note>original: "bolismi"; from the Greek for "intense hunger" or "bulimia," here meaning insatiable desire</note>; touching barely a small portion of restraint, they reach the greatest impulse of desire in all things possible through the affairs of Venus. They run into tempestuous luxury, deception, and a blindness of mind in all they wish for.

<margin>The Sun rules over Youth.</margin>
And because the **Sun**, the ruler of the middle sphere, is said to preside over the disposition for nineteen years <note>the Metonic cycle of the Sun and Moon</note>—which are noted in the fourth place, are in the middle of the order, and are assigned to youth—we decree that the soul now takes on a youthful concern for works of power and the fruitful arrangement of life, as well as its direction. We say that the soul turns from those qualities that were mocking, playful, and deceptive toward the health of the soul, the preservation of shame, and the pursuit of honor.

<margin>Mars rules over Virile Age.</margin>
After the Sun, because **Mars** rules for fifteen years—placed in the fifth position—which are the years of strength and vigor and are equal to the number of his own rotation, the gravity and the obstacles and the adversity of life weigh down upon the man. The soul, along with the body, sustains anxieties and impediments, and the decline of the body is finally felt and understood. The man will also perform great works, from which extreme labor will come to him, the completion of which he seeks before the approach of his death.

<margin>Jupiter rules over Old Age.</margin>
Thereafter, to **Jupiter**, claiming the sixth place and the old man, we assign the twelve years of old age—equal to his own orbital period. In these years, a man withdraws from the labors of the body and from heavy tasks, as well as from the anxiety of working with his hands, and thereafter does not commit his soul to danger. In exchange for all these things, putting on a sound habit of mind, he will study good preservation; through his magnanimity, he will neglect base things. He will be considered prudent in desiring all things, as well as a speaker and a comforter.

<margin>Saturn rules over Decrepitude.</margin>
In this time also, he will be most concerned with liberty, honor, and a good reputation, along with shame and reverence. After these, the years of **Saturn** follow in order, placed as if at the extreme, which are the years of "senium" <note>extreme old age or decrepitude</note>, not ending until the vital spirit departs. These years are changed by a colder motion of the body, a heaviness of pleasure, a diminishment of appetite, and a rapid natural decline. This quality strips the life from the man, impressing upon him impediment, sadness, and a meager sustenance of things, because of the weakness of his movements. These, therefore, are the properties of the qualities of the times of life, which appear according to the general matters of nature. However, the particular properties of the times—since we ought not to observe them except from the properties of the birth—we have considered based on what appeared universal from the *hyleg* <note>original: "alhileg"; the "giver of life," a specific point in a horoscope used to determine longevity</note> mistress. Our observation in these matters, however, has brought knowledge not from any one of them individually, but from all of them together, just as in the space of life...

### BOOK FOUR

<margin>Contrary events.</margin>
...is complete. For that **alhyleg** <term>alhyleg: a term derived from Arabic meaning the "giver of life," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine vitality and lifespan</term>, which is taken from the **ascendant** <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, is used for events happening to the body and for travels. However, that which is considered from the **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "parte fortunae"; a calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and fate</note> is used for matters of substance and wealth. We observe the **alhyleg** taken from the **Moon** for the qualities of the soul and for marriages. That which is discerned from the **Sun** we use for matters of power and high status. Finally, we follow the one found at the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio coeli"; the highest point of the path of the stars</note> for all other particular qualities of life, such as one's work, friends, and children. By doing this, we understand that only one single planet—whether it be a fortune <note>a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> or an infortune <note>a "malefic" planet like Saturn or Mars</note>—is the ruler of a specific matter, which we believe to be a just and proper method. It often happens that contrary events occur at the same hour: for instance, someone might lose a relative but become their heir, or fall ill yet become wealthy, or live idly while fathering children. Such frequent events happen in the body and the soul, in riches and power, as well as in other good or bad circumstances. One and the same quality arises by necessity so that a person may encounter good or bad in all these things. At times of intense good or bad fortune, it is perhaps possible for similar things to happen simultaneously when all or most of the **alhylegs** encounter fortunes or infortunes together. This clearly happens in succession, as human nature—due to sudden decline and a departure from balance—cannot easily endure the simultaneous intensity of both good and bad alterations.

Therefore, the matters of all the **alhyleg** locations are discerned in this predicted manner. From the locations meeting the **alhyleg**, we judge that one must not only consider those signifying the end of life or the lifespan itself, but everything must be examined. Likewise, we should observe not only their physical meeting, or their opposition or square <note>astrological "aspects" or angles of 180 and 90 degrees, often considered difficult</note>, but also their meeting through the trine and sextile <note>angles of 120 and 60 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note>. We shall first attribute the periods of time in each **alhyleg** to the planet existing in that same degree as the **alhyleg**, or to the planet associated with it in the chart. If no planet remains in that degree, and none is associated with it in the chart, it is fitting that we assign that degree to the nearest planet preceding it, until we reach the one which regards the following degree; the aspect of the latter toward the former should follow the succession of the signs. After that, the following times are given to the one who follows it, until we are applied to the next one in sequence. We decree that this should be done similarly in all cases. We shall also establish the planets existing in their own "terms" <note>original: "terminis"; specific subdivisions of zodiac signs ruled by different planets</note>, some of which we have observed and placed as dispositors. It is fitting that the number of years be given by the number of degrees of longitude. Therefore, the number of years for an **alhyleg** taken from the **ascendant** will be assigned equal to the number of times of the "ascensions" <note>the time it takes for a sign to rise over the horizon</note in which the birth occurred. For an **alhyleg** found from the **Midheaven**, the years should be provided in a number equal to the times of transit through the Midheaven. In other **alhylegs** taken from elsewhere, we proceed in this order, taking the number of ascensions or settings or transits through the Midheaven according to their proximity to the "angles" <note>the four most powerful points in a chart: East, West, Top, and Bottom</note>, just as we explained in the narration of the span of life.

In this aforementioned manner, the rulers of universal times and matters are discerned. The rulers of the matters of the years will be known when we take the number of years from the birth and, beginning from each of the **alhyleg** locations, project one year for each sign according to their succession; the ruler of that sign where the number ends shall be set aside. We shall do the same for months; by taking the number of months that have passed since the birth, we project 28 days for each sign, starting from the locations of the yearly rulers. We shall do the same for days. Taking the number of days from the day of birth, we project two and one-third days to each sign from the locations of the months. Furthermore, it is fitting for us to observe the existence of the planets in the locations of these times. This provides no small help in knowing future events that occur in those times. Thus, we shall observe the presence of **Saturn** in the locations of universal times, **Jupiter** in the locations of years, the **Sun** or **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** in the locations of months, and the **Moon** in the locations of days. <meta>This page concludes Book IV of Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos* (The Four Books on the Influence of the Stars) and begins the *Centiloquium* (The Hundred Aphorisms). The previous page established how different planetary points govern specific life areas like health, wealth, and the soul.</meta>

...increase or decrease according to the similarity of the things existing in those locations. For this will provide the occasion for the strength or weakness of the accidents <note>accidents: in historical philosophy and astrology, these are specific events or outward occurrences that happen to a person, as opposed to their essential nature</note>. For the location of the **alhyleg** <term>alhyleg: a term derived from Arabic meaning the "giver of life," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine vitality and lifespan</term> is the indicator of universal quality and the span of time; the lord of the universal times, who is the lord of the **terms** <term>terms: also known as "bounds," these are specific subdivisions of each zodiac sign ruled by different planets, affecting how a planet in that sign behaves</term>, is cited for this reason: because each of these stars in that very same birth chart had a similarity with the locations of the stars that governed them previously. 

But whether a happening is good or evil is discerned from the properties of the qualities of the nature of the lords of the times, and their combination in producing good or evil, as well as from their similarity or opposition at the start with the ruling matter. In what specific times an event might occur is judged from the qualities of the signs ruling the year and month of the matter, based on the positions they will occupy, as well as from the qualities that arise when the planets, the Sun, and the Moon are in the signs of the rulers of the year and months. For planets that agreed with the aforementioned places from the hour of the beginning—which is called the birth—and were appropriately associated with them in the arrangement of the hour of existence, will signify good in the future matter. When they are in a contrary position, they will announce evil. 

Those, however, who are inappropriately associated with them—such as being in direct opposition <note>original: "oppositione per diametrum," meaning 180 degrees apart</note>, or in a square aspect <note>90 degrees apart</note>, and in a contrary **alaiz** <note>original: "alaiz"; likely a corruption of an Arabic astrological term referring to a planet's strength or its "disposition"</note>—will be the cause of adversity. In other qualities, they will produce nothing. But if the same planets have power both in the timing and in their essential state, the person will feel an abundance and increase of future good or evil. This necessarily happens more when they have power over the occasion, even if they lack ruling power over the times alone; rather, it is because they themselves were the disposers at the start of the birth. 

And so that good or evil may happen equally to the person born in all his affairs, it sometimes occurs because all types of the **alhyleg**, or many of them, have met in one and the same place, or because they were separated from one another, and at the same time the factors meeting them—or all of them, or many of them—were fortunes <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> or infortunes <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, agreeing with each other. In this way, according to the natural method suitable to the matter, we predict the nature of the times. 

As for the particular ways by which the qualities of the temporal future are predicted: because the variety of things arising from them is so complex and the explanation is burdensome, we have judged it suitable to conclude the explanation here. For from the beginning of this book, we proposed to explain the general nature of the stars and their similarity with particular things, as is proper, according to a rational estimation of how these things mix. Thus, with the general matters of birth charts explained, we do not think it inappropriate to bring this book to an end at this point.

# CLAUDIUS PTOLEMY’S CENTILOQUIUM,
-> OR THE HUNDRED APHORISMS, <-
-> interpreted by Giovanni Gioviano <-
-> Pontano. <insert>but by another</insert> <note>This insertion suggests the reader or a later scholar doubted Pontano was the true translator of this specific version</note> <-

1 **A**te and from knowledge <note>The Latin "A te & à scientia" means "From you and from science/knowledge," implying that the skill of the astrologer and the system itself must work together</note>. For it is impossible for one who is knowledgeable to predict the particular forms of things; just as the senses do not perceive a specific individual form, but rather a general form of a sensible thing, so it is necessary for the practitioner to use conjecture. Only those inspired by the divine predict particulars.

2 When he who consults the stars examines the matter itself better, there will be no difference between the matter and its form.

3 He who is suited to any particular task will certainly have a star of that kind of significance very powerful in his birth chart <note>original: "genitura"</note>.

4 A soul suited to knowledge attains more of the truth than one who has merely exercised himself in science in a supreme manner.

5 He who is knowledgeable can avert many effects of the stars when he knows their nature and prepares himself before they happen.

6 The choice of days and hours is only beneficial when the time of the birth chart is well-constituted. For if the birth chart is contrary, the choice will not profit at all, even if it seems to look toward a good outcome.

<meta>This page transitions from the theoretical foundations of the *Tetrabiblos* to the *Centiloquium*, a series of one hundred practical astrological axioms. The previous page discussed the "giver of life" and the timing of events; here, the text provides concise rules for daily application and medical astrology.</meta>

->### THE HUNDRED APHORISMS###<-
<note>original: *Centiloquium*. Historically attributed to Ptolemy, these one hundred "sayings" served as a practical handbook for medieval and Renaissance astrologers.</note>

7 No one can perceive the mixtures of the stars unless they have first learned their natural differences and their combinations.

8 A wise soul aids the celestial operation, just as a very good farmer aids nature by plowing and weeding.

9 In the process of birth and decay, physical forms are affected by celestial forms. For this reason, those who create talismans <note>original: *imagines*. These were astrological charms or "images" engraved at specific times to capture planetary power.</note> make use of them, observing when the stars have entered certain positions.

10 In choosing days and hours for actions, use the **malefic planets** <term>malefic planets: traditionally Saturn and Mars, which were thought to cause difficulty or destruction unless channeled carefully</term> just as a very good physician uses poisons moderately for healing.

11 Do not choose a day or hour before you understand the quality of the matter you have proposed.

12 Love and hatred prevent true judgments from occurring, for they diminish the greatest things and amplify the smallest.

13 When the celestial configuration signifies something, use the assisting or even the "corrupting" stars—that is, the secondary ones.

14 Consider how many errors an astrologer may fall into when the **seventh house** and its lord are afflicted <note>In a consultation, the seventh house represents the client; if it is poorly positioned, the reading is likely to be inaccurate.</note>.

15 The **Ascendants** <term>Ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</term> of a kingdom’s enemies are the signs falling away from that kingdom’s own Ascendant. However, the Ascendants of friends are the **angles** <term>angles: the four most powerful points in a chart—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> and the **succedent houses** <term>succedent houses: the houses that follow the angles (the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th), thought to provide support</term>. The same applies to schools of thought.

16 When the **benefic planets** <term>benefic planets: Jupiter and Venus, associated with luck and harmony</term> rule in the eighth house, they bring loss from good men; if they are well-positioned, they will avert that loss.

17 When you judge the life of an old man, do not offer a judgment until you have measured how many years he is naturally capable of living.

18 When both **luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> are at the exact same minute of a degree, if the Ascendant is a benefic planet, the person born will be equally fortunate in all things that happen to them. It is the same if they are in opposition from the rising and setting. But if a malefic is in the Ascendant, you should judge the opposite.

19 The power of a medical purge is weakened when the Moon is joined with Jupiter.

20 Do not <term>pierce</term> <note>original: *ꝑcutito* / *percutito*. This refers to surgery or bloodletting.</note> a limb with iron when the Moon holds the zodiac sign that rules that limb.

21 When the Moon is in Scorpio or Pisces, and the lord of the Ascendant is joined to a star positioned below the earth, it is good to use medical purges. But if it is joined to a star positioned above the earth, whoever takes the potion will vomit it up.

22 Neither put on a garment for the first time, nor cut it, when the Moon is placed in Leo. It is even worse if the Moon is poorly positioned at that time.

23 The Moon's relationship to the stars makes the person born quite agile; if the stars are powerful, they make them effective in action; if they are weak, they indicate an inert or sluggish impulse to act.

24 An eclipse of the luminaries in the **angles** of a birth chart or in the annual revolutions is harmful; the timing is taken from the interval between the Ascendant and the location of the eclipse. Just as you take years from the hour of a solar eclipse, you take months from the hours of a lunar eclipse.

25 Calculate the progression of the ruler when it is positioned in the middle of heaven by the ascensions of the sphere; but when it is positioned in the Ascendant, do so by the ascensions of the specific climate.

26 A matter remains hidden when the star signifying it is joined to the Sun either underground or in a foreign place; conversely, it is revealed when it is raised from depression to height and placed in its own home.

27 Venus brings pleasure to the person born in the limb ruled by the sign in which she is located. The same applies to the other stars.

28 When you cannot manage to join the Moon to two planets, manage this: join it to a fixed star that possesses the mixture of those planets.

29 The **fixed stars** <note>The distant stars that do not move like planets; they were thought to give sudden, "irrational" bursts of fate.</note> bring about irrational and wonderful successes; however, they usually mark these with calamities unless the planets also agree to that success.

30 Look at the coronations of the first kings of a lineage. For if the Ascendant of the coronation agrees with the Ascendant of the birth of the king's son, he will be the successor to the kingdom.

31 When the ruler of a kingdom falls into a **climacteric place** <note>A critical or "dangerous" turning point in a cycle of years.</note>, then either the king or someone great among the leaders of the kingdom will die.

32 A favorable configuration of stars signifying the nature of the matter creates harmony between two people, based on the goodwill established in both of their birth charts.

33 Love and hatred are detected both from the harmony and discord of the luminaries, and from the Ascendants of both birth charts. However, **obedient signs** <note>Signs that have equal "power" because they are equidistant from the equinoxes.</note> increase goodwill.

<note>The insertion of "Not" reflects a long-standing historical debate; while these aphorisms were attributed to Ptolemy in the Middle Ages, later scholars realized they were likely written by a later Arabic or Greek author.</note>

34 The ruler or "host" of the **interlunium** <note>original: *interluniij*. The period of the new moon when the moon is invisible.</note>, if it is in a **cardinal sign** <term>cardinal sign: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, which represent the beginnings of the seasons and indicate strong, direct action</term>, signifies whatever events are to happen in that month.

35 When the Sun reaches the position of any particular star, it arouses the power that the star possesses over the air.

36 In the founding of cities, make use of the **fixed stars** <note>Stars that do not move relative to one another, unlike planets.</note> which are beneficial; but in the building of houses, use the **planets** <note>original: *erraticis*, meaning "wandering stars."</note>. The kings of any city who have Mars **culminating** <term>culminating: located at the highest point in the sky at the moment of birth, known as the Midheaven</term> usually perish by the sword.

37 Those who have Virgo or Pisces as their **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth.</note> will be the cause of their own power; however, those whose ascendant is Aries or Libra will be the cause of their own death. You shall reason in the same way regarding the other signs.

38 When Mercury is positioned and powerful in a house of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius.</note>, it gives the person born an intuitive intellect and a drive to search into the nature of things; but in a house of Mars, and especially in Aries, it grants eloquence.

39 An **affliction** <term>affliction: a state where a planet's influence is weakened or made harmful by its position or its relationship to "malefic" planets like Saturn or Mars</term> of the **eleventh house** in the birth chart of a king signifies the loss of both his household and his money. However, an affliction of the **second house** signifies the loss of his inherited wealth.

40 When the ascendant is oppressed by **malefics** <note>Saturn or Mars.</note>, the person born takes delight in filthy things and approves of foul-smelling odors.

41 Beware of an affliction of the **eighth house** and its lord at the time of departure; but beware of the second house and its lord at the time of return.

42 A disease that begins when the Moon is in the sign held by a malefic planet in the birth chart—or in a **square or opposite** position to it—will be very grave. If the malefic planet is "looking" at it <note>making an aspect</note>, it will be dangerous. But if the Moon is in the place where a **benefic** <note>Jupiter or Venus.</note> was at the time of birth, it will be without danger.

43 Contrary timings of events intensify the figures of an evil race.

44 It is harmful when the ascendant of a sick person conflicts with the figures of their own birth chart, and no benefic influence has arrived at that time.

45 Anyone who does not have the rulers of their birth chart or their ascendant in **human signs** <term>human signs: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius—signs depicted as human figures</term> will be a stranger to humanity, even to themselves.

46 Great strokes of luck are granted in birth charts by the fixed stars, the angles of the new moons, and the locations of the **Part of Fortune** of the kingdom, when the ascendant is found among them.

47 In a birth chart, when a malefic planet falls into the place where another person’s birth chart has a benefic, the one who has the benefic will be harmed by the one who has the malefic.

48 When the "summit" <note>the Midheaven</note> of a master (that is, a prince) is the ascendant of a subject, or if the rulers form a favorable configuration, they will remain inseparable for a long time. The same is true when the **sixth house** of a servant is found to be the ascendant of the prince.

49 When the ascendant of a subject is the "summit" <note>Midheaven</note> in the birth chart of the master, the master will place such trust in that subject that the master is actually commanded by him.

50 Do not overlook the **one hundred and nineteen conjunctions**. For in them is placed the knowledge of those things which happen in the world regarding both birth and decay.

51 Use the sign the Moon is in at the time of birth as the ascendant for the moment of conception. And the sign it was in at conception (or its opposite) should be the ascendant at birth. <note>This is a famous rule known as the Trutine of Hermes, used to rectify birth times.</note>

52 The rulers of the birth charts of tall people are in "heights" <note>high degrees of ascension</note>, and their ascendants are at the beginnings of the signs. However, the rulers of short people are found in "depths." Beyond this, inquire whether the signs are **straight or oblique**. <term>straight or oblique signs: signs that rise at different angles relative to the horizon, affecting the perceived physical proportions of the person</term>

53 The rulers of the birth charts of thin people have no **latitude** <note>distance from the ecliptic</note>, while those of fat people do. If the latitude is Southern, they will be agile; if Northern, they will be sluggish.

54 In construction, when "subterranean" stars <note>planets below the horizon, specifically near the 4th house</note> are joined, the rulers hinder the raising of the building.

55 The harmful power of Mars against ships is diminished when it is neither in the Midheaven nor in the eleventh house. In those places, it destroys the ship through violent seizure by pirates. However, a ship will catch fire if the ascendant is afflicted by any fixed star of a "Mars-like" nature.

56 When the Moon is in the first quarter—that is, from the time it leaves its conjunction with the Sun—the moisture of bodies flows out until the second quarter; in the remaining quarters, it decreases.

### ->CENTILOQUIUM<-

57 When you see the **seventh house** <term>seventh house: in medical astrology, this house represents the physician or the treatment</term> and its ruler afflicted during a sickness, change the doctor.

58 Inspect the place of the **conjunction** <note>original: *Coniunctionis locum*. Likely referring to the most recent New Moon or planetary meeting</note> and where it falls in relation to the **annual ascendant** <term>annual ascendant: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the exact moment the Sun returns to its birth position each year</term>: for when the **profection** <term>profection: a symbolic timing technique where a point is moved forward by one sign per year</term> reaches that place, the event will occur.

59 Do not pronounce what has happened to an absent person until you have seen whether he has become drunk: nor that he has received a wound until you have investigated whether he has been **bled** <note>original: *sanguis ei missus*; bloodletting was a common medical practice</note>: nor that he has found treasures before you have scrutinized whether he has perhaps received a **deposit** <note>original: *depositum*; something held in trust for another</note>, since the astrological figures for all these are similar.

60 For the sick, inspect the **critical days** <term>critical days: specific days in the course of a disease, often tied to the Moon's cycle, where the patient's condition is expected to significantly change</term>, and the Moon's passage through the angles of a sixteen-sided figure; for where you find those angles well-disposed, it will be well for the patient; conversely, it will be ill if you find them afflicted.

61 The Moon signifies those things belonging to the body, as its movements are similar to the body's motions.

62 When you act at the beginning of a **minor conjunction** <note>original: *minuti coniunctionis*. Likely a reference to the monthly New Moon cycle</note>, you can judge the change of weather for that month. For the judgment will be according to the ruler of the angle of each figure; for this ruler overcomes the nature of the air, also taking on the quality of the present season.

63 When Saturn and Jupiter are in conjunction, see which of them is **higher** <note>original: *sublimior*; likely referring to northern declination or being closer to its apogee</note>, and pronounce according to its nature. Do the same for the other stars.

64 When you have inspected the ruler of the inquiry, look at what power it holds in the **annual revolution** or in the **ascendant of the new moon**, and pronounce according to these.

65 In the **minimum conjunction**, use the difference of the **middle conjunction**, and in the middle, the difference of the **maximum conjunction** <note>These terms refer to the Great Conjunctions of Jupiter and Saturn, which occur in cycles of roughly 20, 200, and 800 years</note>.

66 Do not use **profection** alone, but also the attributions and adaptations of the stars.

67 The years of life are diminished on account of the weakness of the recipient.

68 A **malefic planet** <note>Saturn or Mars</note> signifies a fall when it is rising in the morning; but when it is rising in the evening, it signifies disease.

69 There will be a defect in the sight of the newborn when the Moon is opposite the Sun and is joined with **nebulous stars** <note>Clusters or nebulae that appeared as faint "misty stars" to ancient observers, often associated with blindness</note>. Likewise, when the Moon is in the western angle and both malefic stars are in the eastern angle, and the Sun is also at an angle, the person born will be blind.

70 In those who are raving mad, the Moon is not joined to Mercury, and neither is joined to the ascendant; in **demoniacs** <note>those believed to be possessed by spirits or suffering from severe epilepsy/psychosis</note>, in this figure Saturn will hold the angle by night, but Mars by day, especially in Cancer, Virgo, or Pisces.

71 In the births of males, when both **luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> are in masculine signs, their actions will be according to nature. But in the births of women, their actions will be intensified <note>or "bold/masculine"</note>. The same applies to Mars and Venus; for as morning stars they become masculine, and as evening stars they become feminine.

72 Take those things which pertain to education from the rulers of the **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water)</term> of the ascendant; those which pertain to life, from the rulers of the triplicity of the luminary in charge.

73 Where the Sun is found with the **head of the Gorgon** <note>original: *capite Gorgonis*; the star Algol, historically considered the most "evil" star in the sky</note>, if it is neither aspected by a beneficial star, nor a beneficial star rules the eighth house, and the ruler of the luminary in charge is opposite Mars or in **square aspect** to it, the person born will be beheaded. If the luminary is at the **Midheaven**, his body will be wounded. But if the conjunction is in Gemini or Pisces, his hands and feet will be cut off.

74 Whoever has Mars in the ascendant will certainly have a scar on the face.

75 When the Sun is joined with the ruler of the ascendant in Leo, and Mars has no power over the ascendant, and no beneficial planet is in the eighth house, the person born will be burned to death.

76 When Saturn holds the **Midheaven** <note>original: *coeli medium*</note>, and the luminary in charge is opposite it, and an **earthen sign** is at the bottom of the sky, the person born will perish by the ruin of buildings. If it is a **watery sign**, he will be suffocated by water. If it is a **human sign**, he will be strangled by men, or perish by the noose or lashes. But if a beneficial planet is in the eighth house, he will be near these things, but will not die.

77 Take the profection of the ascendant for things of the body, the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and fate</term> for external things, the Moon for the connection of body and soul, and the Midheaven for actions.

78 A star often exercises its powers in a place where it has no formal strength, bringing unexpected gain to the person born.

<meta>This page continues the "Centiloquium" (The Hundred Sayings), concluding the list of 100 astrological aphorisms traditionally attributed to Ptolemy. ### ->ON THE CENTILOQUIUM OF PTOLEMY<-

79 When Mars is in the eleventh house, which is situated here, it does not dominate its own lord. <note>The eleventh house is typically the house of "Good Spirit," associated with friends and hopes.</note>

80 When Venus is joined with Saturn and has any host <note>original: *hospitatorem*; refers to the planetary ruler of that sign</note> in the seventh house, the native will engage in shameful sexual encounters.

81 The timing of events is determined in seven ways: by the interval between two rulers; by the interval of configurations between them; by the approach of one planet to another; by the interval between one of them and the place signifying the matter in question; by the setting of a star with addition or subtraction; by the change of a ruler; and by the entry of a planet into its own place.

82 When the charts for the New Moon or Full Moon are equal, inspect the **horoscope** <term>horoscope: here meaning the Ascendant, or the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>: if that is also equal, do not be in a hurry to deliver your judgment.

83 The time of a petition indicates the affection between the petitioner and the king. The **Throne** <note>original: *Cathedra*; likely referring to the Midheaven or tenth house, the seat of power</note> indicates those things which pertain to action.

84 When Mars is the lord of the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising in the east at the start of an event</term> at the time property is taken into possession, and it presides over the second house or is joined to the lord of the second house, it will bring much loss.

85 When the lord of the Ascendant is configured with the lord of the second house, the prince will voluntarily take on many expenses.

86 The Sun is the source of vital power, and the Moon is the source of natural power.

87 Monthly revolutions <note>original: *conuersiones*; the lunar cycle</note> occur over twenty-eight days, two hours, and about eighteen minutes. However, some judge by the transit of the Sun when it is exactly equal in degree and minute to the position it held at the beginning.

88 When we wish to calculate the **profection** <term>profection: a technique where a point is moved forward by one sign per year or month</term> of the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and health</term> for the entire year of a revolution, we take the distance from the Sun to the Moon and project the same distance from the Ascendant.

89 Look for things concerning the grandfather from the seventh house; but for things concerning the paternal uncle, look to the sixth house.

90 When the ruler of the Ascendant aspects the Ascendant, the hidden matter will be according to the nature of the Ascendant; but if it does not aspect it, the matter will be according to the nature of the place in which that ruler is located. The lord of the hour demonstrates its color, while the location of the Moon shows the time: the thing will be new if the Moon is above the earth, but old if it is below the earth. The Part of Fortune shows its quantity, whether it be long or short. The lord of the **terms** <term>terms: specific degrees within a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term>, of the bottom and middle of heaven <note>The 4th and 10th houses</note>, as well as the Moon, show its substance.

91 It is an evil sign when the ruler of a sick person is **combust** <term>combust: a planet is 'combust' when it is so close to the Sun—usually within 8.5 degrees—that its power is weakened or "burnt up"</term>, especially if the Part of Fortune is also afflicted.

92 Saturn in the east does not harm the sick man as much as Mars in the west.

93 You shall not judge from the charts before you have considered the **conjunction** <note>original: *coniunctionem*; the meeting of planets or the New Moon</note>. For the beginnings are transformed in every conjunction; therefore, mix both, and you will not err.

94 The place of the more powerful of the rulers indicates those things which are in the thoughts of the person asking the question.

95 Those things which rise with each decan <note>original: *decursis*; referring to the 10-degree subdivisions of zodiac signs</note> confirm the native's will toward the craft they practice.

96 The decrees of an eclipse are signified by those planets near the **angles** <term>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</term>. Consider also the nature of the stars standing together—both the wandering stars <note>planets</note> and the fixed stars—as well as the constellations rising with them, and pronounce your judgment according to these.

97 The matter about which a question is asked is completed quickly when the lord of the New or Full Moon is in an angle.

98 Meteors <note>original: *Traiectiones*; literally 'throwings-across'</note> and comets <note>original: *crinitæ*; literally 'hairy stars'</note> hold a secondary place in judgments.

99 Meteors indicate dryness of the air: if they are carried toward one part, they indicate wind from that corner; but if they are carried toward different parts, they indicate a decrease in waters, disturbances of the air, and invasions by armies.

100 Comets whose distance from the Sun is eleven signs: if they appear in the angles, the king of some kingdom or one of the princes of the realm will die. If they appear in a **succedent** <term>succedent: the houses following the angles (2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th)</term> place, the treasury will be in good condition, but it will change its governor. If they appear in a **declining** <term>declining: also called 'cadent' houses (3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th)</term> place, there will be diseases and sudden deaths. If they move from the west to the east, a foreign enemy will invade the regions; if they do not move, the enemy will be from within the province.

<summary>This final page of the Centiloquium provides specific aphorisms for horary and mundane astrology, ranging from identifying hidden objects and medical outcomes to predicting political instability and weather through comets and meteors.</summary>

### January.

<margin>K.</margin> <note>The Kalends (January 1st).</note> The Sun begins to be elevated, the days become somewhat longer, the Eagle <note>original: *Aquila*</note> and the Crown <note>original: *Corona*; refers to Corona Borealis</note> set, and they produce storms.

## XXX.
## *July.*

<margin>K.</margin> <note>July 1st; the Kalends.</note> The air is disturbed by the North wind <note>original: *Aquilo*</note>.
<margin>6</margin> <note>July 2nd.</note> An obscure star <note>likely referring to a faint star or nebula not clearly named</note> appears; the South wind <note>original: *Auster*</note> or the West wind <note>original: *Fauonius*</note> blows.
<margin>5</margin> <note>July 3rd.</note> A southerly day and a disturbance of the air.
<margin>4</margin> <note>July 4th.</note> Orion rises, the Stork <note>original: *Ciconia*; possibly referring to the constellation Cygnus or the literal arrival of the bird</note> sets, and the West wind breathes.
<margin>3</margin> <note>July 5th.</note> The middle of the Crab <note>the constellation Cancer</note> rises.
<margin>Pr.</margin> <note>July 6th; the day before the Nones.</note> The Trade winds <note>original: *Etesiæ*; seasonal Mediterranean winds</note> blow, along with North winds and the South wind.
<margin>Non.</margin> <note>July 7th; the Nones.</note> The Crown <note>original: *Corona*</note> sets in the morning; the South wind blows.
<margin>8</margin> <note>July 8th.</note> Cepheus rises, and there is a southerly disturbance of the air.
<margin>7</margin> <note>July 9th.</note> All of Orion emerges; the South wind blows.
<margin>6</margin> <note>July 10th.</note> The "Forerunner" winds <note>original: *prodromi*; winds that precede the main Trade winds</note> begin to blow.
<margin>5</margin> <note>July 11th.</note> Rains with thunder; the North wind blows.
<margin>4</margin> <note>July 12th.</note> All of Orion rises in the morning, and the Forerunner winds grow stronger.
<margin>3</margin> <note>July 13th.</note> The Southwest wind <note>original: *Africus*</note> blows turbulently.
<margin>Pr.</margin> <note>July 14th; the day before the Ides.</note> The North wind blows.
<margin>Id.</margin> <note>July 15th; the Ides.</note> The Little Dog Star <note>original: *Canicula*; likely Procyon or Sirius</note> rises; the Trade winds grow stronger.
<margin>17</margin> <note>July 16th.</note> Orion rises, and a violent North wind blows.
<margin>16</margin> <note>July 17th.</note> The midpoint of summer; the day is colder due to the blowing of the North wind.
<margin>15</margin> <note>July 18th.</note> The West wind, and sometimes the South wind, breathes. The Dog Star rises in the morning, and the Trade winds grow even stronger.
<margin>14</margin> <note>July 19th.</note> Orion rises, the Northwest wind <note>original: *Corus*</note> blows, and all of Orion is visible.
<margin>13</margin> <note>July 20th.</note> The Sun is in Leo; the Northwest wind breathes, and the Dog Star rises.
<margin>12</margin> <note>July 21st.</note> The Trade winds, along with other winds, blow for twenty-one days.
<margin>11</margin> <note>July 22nd.</note> The Forerunner winds blow widely.
<margin>10</margin> <note>July 23rd.</note> All of the Crab rises with the Lion <note>Leo</note>, and the Eagle <note>original: *Aquila*</note> sets.
<margin>9</margin> <note>July 24th.</note> The Lion rises with the Sun and the Dog Star; the Crab descends.
<margin>8</margin> <note>July 25th.</note> The Twins <note>original: *Gemini*</note> begin to set, the Dog Star emerges, and there are southerly winds.
<margin>7</margin> <note>July 26th.</note> A sandy mist; the Eagle sets, the Lion rises, and the South wind blows.
<margin>6</margin> <note>July 27th.</note> The heat of the Dog Days <note>original: *Canicularis æstus*</note>.
<margin>5</margin> <note>July 28th.</note> Vehement heat; the Trade winds blow strongly.
<margin>4</margin> <note>July 29th.</note> The bright star in the chest of the Lion <note>Regulus</note> rises; the North wind is chilly despite the heat.

## XXXI.
## *August.*

<margin>K.</margin> <note>August 1st; the Kalends.</note> The Eagle sets in the morning; the Southwest wind blows, and the heat is parching.

<margin>3</margin> <note>August 3rd.</note> A southerly day.

<margin>7</margin> <note>August 7th.</note> The middle of Orion is hidden; the day is misty and sultry from the South wind.
<margin>6</margin> <note>August 8th.</note> The Lion rises; the heat is intolerable, and the air is cloudy. The middle of Orion rises.
<margin>5</margin> <note>August 9th.</note> An obscure star; the North wind <note>original: *Septentrio*</note> breathes gently; the heat is moderate.

<margin>3</margin> <note>August 11th.</note> The Lyre sets in the morning; Autumn begins, and a meeting of the winds occurs.
<margin>Pr.</margin> <note>August 12th.</note> A conflict and battle of the winds.

<margin>15</margin> <note>August 17th.</note> The Lyre sets, and the North wind blows.
<margin>14</margin> <note>August 18th.</note> The Dolphin is hidden; moderate heat.
<margin>13</margin> <note>August 19th.</note> The Lyre sets in the morning; the Sun is in the Virgin <note>Virgo</note>; the South wind blows, it rains, and it thunders.
<margin>12</margin> <note>August 20th.</note> The Sun is entirely in the Virgin.
<margin>11</margin> <note>August 21st.</note> The Virgin rises.
<margin>10</margin> <note>August 22nd.</note> The North wind breathes gently; all of the Virgin rises; there is serenity in the air.
<margin>9</margin> <note>August 23rd.</note> The Virgin rises; the North wind blows.
